The draft stores the `vat_on_debits` its plan was computed with; the job sends a draft with documents back (`vat_option_changed`) when the servicer's setting differs, and `private.issue_commission_documents` books the invoices on the draft's value (a new parameter), so the invoice and the settlement plan book the VAT on the same account (44571 or 44574), never twice. pgTAP `023`: the setting flipped after prepare → back to draft with that reason; once it matches, booked on the account the draft assumed.
- **The proceeding date the plan assumed** (money#2, C1). The draft stores the `proceeding_opened_on` its plan used; when the plan has compensation or advance settles and the current date is distinct, the job sends it back (`client_status_changed`), so no document dated before an opening recorded meanwhile is netted (design §9.6). pgTAP `023`.
- **A late N = 0 approval** (money#3, C1). The command and the job ask the reason when nothing is transferred and today (Paris) is after the run's earliest latest execution date, and store it; the sheet shows « Motif du retard » for such a run (`lateReasonRequired`, vitest). The late lines are recorded in `remittance_late_approval` with the settlement date, and get their breach row when none exists yet (`private.remittance_late_lines`, used by both branches of the job). pgTAP `023`: a run 40 days old refused without a reason, queued with one, refused by the job if the reason is gone, then booked.
- **Deadlines outside the calendar never stop the checks, the schedule or the overview** (numbering-concurrency#0, C2). The set-based readers take the deadline through a total wrapper; an item or a payment whose encaissement date is outside the seeded calendar raises the alert `remittance_deadline_not_computable` with its ids. The worker isolates the hourly schedule: the stuck-job recovery, the candidates' read and each client's draft run in their own savepoints, so a client's data error is logged and recorded and the others (and the recovery) still commit, while a transient error still fails the job for the queue to retry. A client's data error and a schedule job that dies are recorded (`private.remittance_schedule_failure`) and raised by the nightly checks as `remittance_schedule_failed` on « Contrôles » (pgTAP `024`; integration `test_one_failing_client_never_stops_the_schedule`). Left as is: the prepare still turns such an E into `prepare_failed` (the calendar is seeded from 2026; seeding it back is rule-pack work), which `remittance_deadline_not_computable` and `draft_waiting` now show.
- **An approval that crosses Paris midnight** (numbering-concurrency#1). The issue date is the transaction's Paris day (`private.paris_today()`), checked against the clock read under the counter lock; a mismatch raises 40001, which the queue retries and the cancel command shows as « réessayez » (`run_retry`), instead of failing with LG006 and sending the run back to draft. The counter is one insert-on-conflict for that year, which locks it; the year loop, which could never commit, is gone (pgTAP `023`).
- **One locked run never fails the batch** (numbering-concurrency#2 = tests-ui#5, C1). Each run is locked `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` in its own sub-block after an unlocked read (so `unknown_run` keeps its reason); a run a job or another command holds is refused alone, `busy` (« traitement en cours sur ce reversement : réessayez »), the others are queued. A lock timeout that still reaches a remittance command, and the `allocation_busy` refusal (55P03) that cancel, « Actualiser » and « Abandonner » raise when the allocation lock waits too long (`private.remittance_command_locks`), read « Un traitement est en cours sur ce reversement ou pour ce cabinet … » (`run_busy`), not the payments' matching text (vitest; integration `test_a_run_a_job_holds_is_refused_alone_and_the_others_are_queued`, `test_a_command_waiting_too_long_on_the_allocation_lock_says_so`).
- **The E2E spec no longer expires** (tests-ui#0). Its statement is dated the latest business day on or before yesterday (Paris), read from `public.business_calendar`, instead of 2026-11-02 (whose latest execution date, 01/12/2026, would have made the default date late and the chip « Délai dépassé »); it accepts a draft the hourly schedule prepared first, and fills « Motif du retard » if it ever shows.
- **The guard test picks its day** (tests-ui#1): walking back from the latest execution date to a business day that is not a run day of the terms and on which the guard is due, instead of a fixed offset that failed on about 12 % of calendar days; `test_the_guard_day_is_never_a_scheduled_day` checks every business day to 2028.
- **A late approval's record** (tests-ui#2 = legal#8, C3). `remittance_deadline_breach` keeps one row per entry and never changes, and the nightly checks usually write it first, without the reason; the approval now writes `remittance_late_approval` (run, entry, latest execution date, requested execution date or settlement date, the reason, the approver; unique per (run, entry); append-only; read like the breach rows, the client its own) for every line whose latest execution date is before the requested or settlement date, whether or not a breach row exists. The integration breach test asserts the reason and the requested date are there and that the nightly row stays without reason; pgTAP `023` covers the table's RLS (staff, client A and B, restricted viewer, collector, another servicer) and that the API cannot write it.
- **A failed preparation** (tests-ui#3, C4: status `draft`, no job, never prepared, last failure at the prepare step). The pages show « Préparation échouée — actualisez » (error) and « Préparation échouée : … — « Actualiser » la relance » instead of « Préparation en cours », and stop refreshing themselves (`prepareFailed`, `runBusy`, vitest); the nightly checks raise `draft_waiting` for such a draft at once, with `prepare_failed` and the failure's code in the details (pgTAP `024`).
- **Every refusal in French** (tests-ui#4). `unknown_run`, `not_draft`, `preparing`, `approval_in_progress`, a bare `payout_blocked`, `busy`, `vat_option_changed`, `client_status_changed`, `late_reason_required` have French words; the result line counts the refused and is orange when some were, red when all were (`summaryTone`, vitest).
- **The counter lock is tested without the advisory locks** (tests-ui#7, `test_the_counter_row_alone_serialises_two_issuers`: a held counter row makes a direct issuer wait, two issuers behind a barrier take consecutive numbers), and **the stale-page integration case is refused as stale** (tests-ui#8: a third client's draft with a wrong hash, no job, no `approve` message).
- **Death, guardianship and mandate end** (legal#0): documented as an interim fail-closed state (decisions above); payee confirmation after the event and the final run are listed for M2c-7.
- **Unmeetable short delays escalate** (legal#1, C2): such an item raises `remittance_delay_unmeetable` while its one-month dates (`remittance_deadline(E, 30)`) run (the alert carries them), then `remittance_due_soon`, `remittance_due_critical` on them and, once passed, `remittance_deadline_breached` with a breach row (no reason of its own: the nightly no longer writes an `unmeetable_delay` row at the mandate's date; nor, since round 2 below, does the approval). In-flight lines are held to the same month (pgTAP `024`).
- **No `has_terms` exclusion** (legal#2): see the decision above; pgTAP `024`: a collection dated before the first version, past one month → breach row and violation; a portfolio under no mandate, or under one that never had terms, is not monitored.
- **Approved runs not debited are checked** (legal#3, C2): `remittance_payout_overdue` (violation per run, and breach rows naming the run, its requested date and reason) and `remittance_payout_not_executed` (alert), read by `private.inflight_overdue_lines`; CPCE-08 no longer says an approved run's collections cannot be breaches. Death, guardianship, mandate end and liquidation each block the payout today, proceedings do not (pgTAP `024`, legal#0).
- **The invoice payload freezes the mentions that change** (legal#4, C5): `penalty_text`, `flat_indemnity` (40 € for a professional buyer, L441-10 II and D441-5 as design §14.2 cites), `due_date`, `payment_reference` and, when an amount is due, the own account {iban, bic, holder}, all before hashing. The indemnity is not claimed while a client proceeding or liquidation is in force (L441-10 II); `payment_reference` is set on an approval's documents (round 2 below: on netted documents only, and on a cancellation's corrective invoice); the holder is the servicer's legal name (a bank account has no holder of its own). M2c-5 renders from these keys (pgTAP `023`).
- **« Avoir remboursé » only once booked** (legal#5): until then the run's page reads « remboursement d'avoir inclus dans le virement : X € » (`refundNote`, vitest).
- **A re-tiering credit says so** (legal#6, C6): « Régularisation de paliers (changement de conditions) »; reversal credits keep « — encaissements annulés ». Golden case `retiering-credit-descending` (a descending grid; the golden harness now checks each credit's cause).
- **`unallocated_deadline` on the mandate's delay** (legal#7): the file's terms version on E, one month without one (`private.unallocated_payment_deadlines`).
- **Performance** (performance#0–#7): the money waiting on files read per payment by keyed lookups whatever the statistics, the deadlines once per distinct (E, delay) (#0; integration `test_unallocated_money_is_read_by_key_without_statistics`); the cancellation of a 50,000-line run under the API's 8 s (#1, above: 3.97 s); `settlement_ledger` and `vat_pending_ledger` on their indexes, `run_remittance_checks` with `enable_seqscan = off` (#2); the reservation's first-run bound computed only for a first run, an EXISTS for nothing pending, « Actualiser » reserving only the new items (#3); the approval job's allocation-lock hold cut to the checks, the numbering, posting and the payout, the lines, repricings, tier history and charges written before it and `commission_invoice_charge.invoice_id` checked at commit (#4: 0.16 s at 5,000 lines, about 1.6 s at 50,000 by extrapolation, under the 2 s of the M2b commands but close to it; the job itself 7.9 → 6.3 s at 50,000; commands that wait too long say `allocation_busy`); I16 in one pass per run, over runs changed since the previous check run, all of them on Sundays (#5); the overview and the schedule read only unreserved items (`pending_item_deadlines(org, true)`, #6); the prepare reads one key state per (file, tier key) its terms can price (`private.remittance_key_states`, #7; integration `test_the_prepare_reads_one_history_state_per_key`). Figures in `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md`.
- **Round 2 (skeptics' verification, 2026-11-10).** Four first-round fixes were rejected with reproductions (`real_round.py`, `run_round.sql`, `p1.sql`); fixed again, each with a test that failed before:
  - **The corrective invoice bears the VAT of its own HT** (money#0, regression of the first fix): it was given the sum of the VATs the run's credit notes gave back, each a cumulative difference on its own invoice, which is not R(HT × rate) whenever the run credited two or more invoices of one mandate and rate, or one already partly credited (about 6 cases in 25 at 20 %): 300,04 € HT with 60,00 € of VAT, which the re-run, crediting it in full with the engine's R(300,04 × 20 %) = 60,01 €, could not approve (23514, the client's runs stuck in draft), or at 150,03 € twice 0,01 € of VAT pending for ever. Now VAT = R(HT × rate) half up, as `vat_of` (242 nonies A 11°; documents rule 5 then credits it exactly); lines and charges unchanged. Between the cancellation and the re-run the net VAT differs from the pre-run state by at most one cent per earlier invoice credited (one cent for one invoice, or two not credited before), exact after the re-run (CALCULATION_RULES §7 « Cent-level effect of a cancellation »). The corrective invoice is dated over the service periods of the invoices it charges again (min start, max end), not the cancelled run's. Integration `test_a_corrective_invoice_bears_the_vat_of_its_own_ht` through the real prepare and approval job (2 × 150,02 €, 2 × 150,03 €, one invoice credited by a live run first): open 0, pending VAT 0, the re-run approved, no violation; pgTAP `023` (service period).
  - **The corrective invoice's payment date** (legal#4): it froze none (netted, so no due date, and no payment reference), yet L441-9 asks for « la date à laquelle le règlement doit intervenir » and invoices are append-only. The settlement plan reads every open invoice of the client whatever its settlement column (`load_facts`' open documents; `_plan` sets off a netting mandate's open invoices oldest first), so a netted invoice with a date is carried as is: under a netting clause it stays netted, set off on the next run, at the latest on issue + the mandate's `invoice_payment_days` (30 without, ≤ 45, L441-10 I as the design cites) — `due_date` set, `payment_reference` {`mode`: `next_run`, `latest_date`}, no own account; the table's check allows a netted `due_date` on such an invoice only. `invoice_late` is the approval's lateness (K + 2 business days) and cannot carry a document's date, so the date is checked by the design's `invoice_overdue` (§15), now built: an alert per invoice still open after its `due_date` (a due invoice too), with its open TTC and date (« Facture de commission non réglée à sa date », vitest). The rule is OQ-72 for the founder. Also `payment_reference` is set on netted documents only — {`mode`: `run`, run number, execution date} for an approval's —, a due document's date being its `due_date` (pgTAP `023`).
  - **Unmeetable delays at approval** (legal#1): `private.remittance_late_lines` holds an unmeetable line to `remittance_deadline(E, 30)`, as the nightly checks do: its late approval is still recorded against the mandate's date, its breach row is written only when it is paid after the month, with the month's deadline and latest execution date; no `unmeetable_delay` row is written any more (the column stays for the payments L722-5 or L622-7 hold, design §9.2). So a line approved within the month and not debited, or sent back to pending by a cancellation, gets its breach row from the nightly checks the day after the month (it was blocked by the approval's « délai intenable » row before). pgTAP `023` through the real approval job (Pin's and Cyprès's 1-day mandates).
  - **One deadline per distinct (E, delay), whatever the statistics** (perf#0): the deadline CTEs are `materialized` in `private.unallocated_payment_deadlines` (`dl`), `private.pending_item_deadlines` (`dl`, `m`) and `private.inflight_overdue_lines` (`m`), and the late lines' month in `remittance_late_lines`; inlined, the planner joined them first and computed a deadline per payment, item or line when the tables had no statistics (ARCHITECTURE §4). pgTAP `024`: ten payments, ten waiting collections and ten frozen lines on one E — each reader probes `business_calendar` twice per distinct (E, delay) (24, 44 and 20 probes before; 6, 10 and 2 now).
  - **The scheduler property CPCE-08 promised** (legal#8), written: `test_schedule.py` simulates days over the pure schedule functions (`is_scheduled`, `guard_due`, `remittance_deadline`, the calendar) with random collections, run days, frequencies and delays (1–5-day unmeetable ones included); a run cut on every scheduled day and whenever the guard is due, paying out the next business day, pays every collection that reached the queue on its E or by its J-5 date by its latest execution date, an unmeetable one by the month (no miss in 290,000 collections checked offline). Modelling one live run per client, as `private.create_remittance_run` holds, the property found a gap that is not the guard's: a collection that arrives while a payout is in flight waits for its debit, and under a 2- to 5-day delay misses its date (1,493 of 294,622 collections with the debit booked on its execution day, all with E on a closed day; 2,558 of 143,071 on business days when it is booked the next business day; 23 of 189,392 at 6–8 days). Not fixed here: it needs a second live run per client whose plan leaves aside what the run in flight sets off, or same-day execution — M2c-6's, with the debit booking (OQ-73); the property holds with one live run from 6 days or for business-day encaissements, and the gap is pinned by a strict xfail.
  - **Round 3 (verification of round 2).** The skeptic showed the property could not see the J-5 margin: it approved each run the day it was cut, so any margin of one business day passed. `test_the_guard_leaves_room_for_ops_to_approve` approves each run 0 to 4 business days after it is cut (the J-5 … J-1 window) and pays the next business day; it fails with the guard at 4 or 3 business days (mutation check), passes at 5. The other three round-2 fixes were confirmed (money#0 across 20 scenarios and three VAT rates, legal#4, legal#1, perf#0 under five statistics states).
- **Schema changes beyond the contract** (perf#1, perf#4): the foreign keys `remittance_line.organization_id`/`client_organization_id`, `remittance_key_state.organization_id`/`client_organization_id` and `commission_credit_alloc.credit_note_id`/`original_invoice_id` are replaced by statement-level `AFTER INSERT` guards with one keyed lookup per run or pair, which check more (a line's currency = its run's; a credit note on an invoice of its own client); `commission_invoice_charge.invoice_id` is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`; new index `commission_credit_alloc (entry_id)`; `private.issue_commission_documents` takes `p_vat_on_debits`; `private.pending_item_deadlines(uuid, boolean)` reports `monitored`, `max_days`, the `check_*` dates and `out_of_horizon`; `private.run_remittance_checks(uuid, uuid, date)` takes an optional day for tests.

## M2c-5: documents (M2-14 statement, M2-15 PDF; design §10, §14, §16, §17, §19, §21)
Migration `20261113090000_remittance_documents.sql` (forward-only; since the review it redefines three M2c-4 functions,
`private.issue_commission_documents`, `private.run_remittance_checks` and `private.queue_remittance_schedule`, with
their settings and grants restated, and relaxes the constraint `commission_invoice_due`); worker
`remittance.statement`, `statement_csv`, `statement_pdf`, `invoice`, `invoice_pdf`, `pdf`, job `remittances.documents`
(`jobs.remittance_documents`, on the existing `remittances` queue: no new queue).
- **What is due** (`private.remittance_document_todo`): a statement for every run whose approval is recorded (trigger on
  `remittance_run.approved_at` null → set: approved, or booked at approval when N = 0), a PDF for every invoice or
  credit note (statement trigger on `commission_invoice`: the approval's, a cancellation's credit notes and corrective
  invoice, and any later issuer). Each trigger also queues `documents {organization_id}`; the job draws what is due for
  that servicer, oldest first (200 invoice PDFs and 1 statement a job, the rest queued again), under the servicer's
  documents lock. Runs and invoices issued before the migration were queued by it (none in production).
- **The statement payload** (`private.remittance_statement_build`, §10): built once, in SQL, by the job right after
  the approval commits, from the run's frozen facts — its lines and the earlier lines it priced (`remittance_line_
  repricing`), each line's file, borrower, mandate, portfolio, the items and components its entry's 1100 postings
  moved, the notification's reason code (bank return, recalled file…), its invoice, its payment's receipt number and its
  late approval (`remittance_late_approval`) —, the run's documents and settlement plan, its payout as ordered (IBAN
  masked), the previous run's payout, and the identities (`private.invoice_party`). Every lookup is keyed from the
  run's lines (ARCHITECTURE §4). Amounts are text in minor units, dates ISO, lines as arrays in the order
  `line_columns` names (a 50,000-line payload stays ≈ 10 MB). It is stored with its SHA-256 (`remittance_statement`,
  append-only) and never rebuilt: the files are rendered from the stored payload. Sections: header (issuer block
  R123-237/238 « agissant en qualité de mandataire de recouvrement amiable », client, mandates with their R124-3 3°/4°,
  netting and claw-back clause references, period, K), « Récapitulatif », « Sommes encaissées pour votre compte »
  (natures, per-file table), « Retenues et compensations », « Reversement », « Suivi de vos reversements précédents »,
  « Sommes reçues sur vos dossiers et non reversées », « Position ».
- **Decisions where the design was open:**
  - **The PDF shows the per-file table, the CSV every line.** §10 asks both « one row per line » and « a per-file table
    up to 2,000 files »; the PDF carries the summary, the natures and one row per file (≤ 2,000, else the CSV's
    SHA-256 for the detail), the CSV one row per line — so a 50,000-line statement's PDF stays short. The PDF always
    names the CSV's SHA-256 (CSV = PDF), and its footer the first 16 characters.
  - **CSV columns**: the design's list plus `hors_delai` (« oui » and a cause category for a line approved after its
    latest execution date, §10.2 « hors délai with its cause » — never the approver's free-text reason since the review,
    K5 below); several items or components of one line joined with « ; » in
    `piece` / `composante`; `regle` / `taux` the rules and band rates of the line's parts (« Commission en attente »
    when pending); `base_commission_centimes` the basis its parts priced. **Dates ISO** (AAAA-MM-JJ) in the CSV
    (§10's « ISO and French dates » read as ISO dates and French amounts), French in the PDF. Amounts « 1 234,56 »
    with a no-break space (U+00A0, what French spreadsheets read) and in integer cents.
  - **Earlier lines priced by this run** (commission left pending by an earlier run, §9.1) are CSV rows of amount 0
    (« Commission sur un encaissement du relevé RV-… ») so the CSV's commission adds up to the documents' HT.
  - **Position**: owed to the client at K = the run's gross (every item pending at K is the run's: one live run per
    client and currency, I14; the integration test checks it equals −4670 known at K), 0 after the payout; what the
    client owes the servicer (4111, 4112) known at K, and after this statement's documents and the settlement the plan
    posts at the payout's debit. Worded « Les compensations sont réalisées au débit du virement … jusque-là elles
    restent à régler »; since the review, a run that transfers nothing (N = 0, settled at approval) reads « Les
    compensations ci-dessus ont été réalisées le …, sans virement », and a cancelled run's position after equals its
    position before plus the TTC of all its documents (legal#2, legal#5 below).
  - **Section 5 before M2c-6**: the previous run's payout as its transfer stands (ordered → « son débit n'est pas encore
    constaté », booked → « débité de notre compte dédié le … », returned, cancelled; N = 0 → « aucun virement »).
  - **Section 6**: per (file, reason, currency), the money waiting on 4710 at K (since the review, figures#2: it said
    « when the statement is drawn »; `payment.review_reason` worded: paiement bloqué, trop-perçu, avoir à imputer…,
    « à restituer au payeur » for a refund requested) and the refunds whose cash-out was posted between the previous
    run's K and this K and not sent back by K, with their dates; no payer data (OQ-40).
  - **A run cancelled before its statement is drawn** still gets it, saying so (« Reversement annulé le … ») and,
    since the review (legal#2), presenting no payout or set-off as happening; one drawn before the cancellation keeps
    its bytes (append-only) and the client space reads the run's live status beside it (K7); the cancellation's
    documents get their PDFs.
- **Files**: reportlab pinned with its own defaults (the receipts' `reportlab_defaults`, imported first by every PDF
  module — a finding of the environment test: a module importing reportlab before it made the renderer refuse under
  `RL_*` variables), invariant mode, no compression, DejaVu Sans; the statement dated K, an invoice its issue date at
  00:00 UTC; templates `releve-reversement-fr-2` and `facture-commission-fr-2` (the review's; `fr-1` never left the
  slice), `RENDERER_VERSION`
  `reportlab-4.4.10/dejavu-2.37/d1`, stored on each row. Keys in the private bucket `documents`:
  `statements/<servicer>/<client>/<year>/<RV>.pdf|.csv`, `invoices/<servicer>/<client>/<year>/<FC>.pdf`; the bucket
  accepts `text/csv` (config). A failed attempt removes what it uploaded; a retry renders the same bytes at the same
  keys. Golden SHA-256 for fixed payloads (`tests/test_statement_docs.py`), the same bytes in another process
  whatever `RL_*`, `reportlab_settings.py`, `TZ` or `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.
- **Invoices** render the payload M2c-4 froze at issue, never the current settings (C5): seller and buyer blocks, «
  Prestations de services », the service period, lines (quantity 1, unit price HT, rate), « Aucun rabais, remise ni
  ristourne », HT, VAT per rate (a credit note: per rate of the invoices it rectifies), TTC, « Option pour le paiement
  de la taxe d'après les débits » when opted, the payment line from `payment_reference` (`run`: « À régler par
  compensation sur le reversement RV-… (exécution demandée le … ; mandat …, art. …) »; `next_run`: « … sur le prochain
  reversement, au plus tard le … »; a due invoice: « À régler au plus tard le … par virement sur le compte … (BIC …),
  titulaire … » from `own_account`), « Pas d'escompte pour paiement anticipé », `penalty_text`, the 40 € flat
  indemnity when `flat_indemnity.applies`, `po_number` when present (review below: the 40 € for every professional
  buyer, the buyer's two addresses, the amount set off and the remainder's date, N = 0, template `fr-2`; no
  purchase-order number is captured yet, OQ-77); a credit note names each invoice it rectifies
  (number and date read from the append-only invoice rows, 289 I 5) and carries no payment mentions. No CGI article
  number is printed (§3.1).
- **Electronic delivery (CGI 289 VI)**: `commission_invoice_document.electronic` = the buyer's
  `invoice_acceptance_ref` frozen in the payload at issue. Without it, neither the document row nor the object is
  readable by the client, the client space says « PDF non disponible en ligne : vous n'aviez pas accepté la facture
  électronique à son émission. Demandez-la au cabinet. » (it said « Adressée par courrier » before the review, K6) and
  the back office flags « À envoyer par courrier » (OQ-74).
- **Read access** (OQ-48): `remittance_statement` and the statement documents — money staff (aal2) and the client's
  members with access to the whole client; `commission_invoice_document` and the invoice PDF — money staff, and the
  client's whole-client members when electronic. A restrictive policy on `document` narrows `document_read` for the
  three kinds; the storage policy on `statements/%` and `invoices/%` asks the same of the object's document (keyed by
  bucket and path). Collectors, portfolio-restricted users, other servicers and aal1 staff read none (pgTAP `025`).
  Downloads are served after the bytes are checked against the recorded SHA-256 (CGI 289 V).
- **Client space** (§17.7): `/client/reversements` (`public.client_remittance_summary`: owed today from the running
  4670 balance, the payout in flight « ordonné », the next run day `private.next_scheduled_run_day` — the 1st and 16th
  or the mandate's weekday moved to the next business day, checked against `remittance.schedule` over 60 days in
  integration; the statements with PDF and CSV), `/client/factures`. Restricted users read « Vos accès ne couvrent
  pas … ». Nothing says « payé » or « réglé » before the bank's debit.
- **Accounting export** (§14.2): `public.accounting_export_documents(from, to)` (invoices and credit notes of the
  period: client, SIREN, mandate, run, HT/VAT/TTC, VAT book, settlement mode and due date, invoices rectified, settled
  amount and its rows, open amount) and `public.accounting_export_entries(from, to)` (postings of 7060, 44571, 44574,
  6270, 6780, 4111, 4112, 5122 with their entry, type, document reference and client), money staff at aal2, one year at
  most; `/backoffice/reversements/comptabilite` writes them as CSV (BOM, `;`, CRLF, French headers, amounts twice,
  deterministic order). Not a FEC: the servicer's general ledger is out of scope (§1, OQ-76). Read in keyset pages of
  1,000 rows at most and text cells neutralised since the review (K1, K3 below).
- **Left for later slices:**
  - **`issue_credit_note` (the manual credit note, §14.1, risk R2) is not built.** It needs a change of the commission
    engine's contract, not a document: the engine requires each (file, tier key)'s invoices' open charges to add up to
    the commission it charged (`commission._key`, `CommissionInputError` otherwise). A manual credit either lowers the
    key's state (then the next collection on that file re-charges what was given back: telescoping) or does not (then a
    later reversal credits the invoice LIFO beyond what is left of it, and `issue_commission_documents` refuses the
    approval with 23514). It needs a waived amount per key (`KeyState.waived_minor`: open charges + waived = K; LIFO
    credits capped by each invoice's remaining HT and absorbed by the waiver first), with its Hypothesis properties —
    the engine's slice, before go-live. Meanwhile R2's mitigations stay the draft's lines, the golden cases and the
    approval sheet; a wrong invoice is corrected by cancelling the run before its file (M2c-4). **Review M2c-5: it
    moves to its own slice, M2c-5b** — the engine's waived amount per (file, tier key) with its Hypothesis properties,
    then `issue_credit_note` on top — so no document of this slice waits for it.
  - ~~The nightly `document_missing` alert~~ — wired by the review (K4 below): `remittance_document_failed` and
    `remittance_document_missing` in the nightly checks.
  - **The production `documents` bucket must allow `text/csv`** (a manual step on the Supabase project before the
    merge reaches production; `supabase/config.toml` allows it locally): without it every statement's CSV upload is
    refused. Since the review that failure no longer blocks other documents (K4) and raises
    `remittance_document_failed`, but no statement is drawn until the bucket accepts it.
  - Postal dispatch of invoices without electronic acceptance (ops' record of the sending), the orphan-object sweep for
    statements and invoices (`private.remittance_document_orphans` is ready; the job removes its own uploads on
    failure), the Factur-X / UBL mapping of the payload (OQ-44), the statement's « Suivi » once M2c-6 books debits.
- **Tests:** pgTAP `025_remittance_documents` (42: the queue, the payload = the run, CSV = PDF = run in SQL, the
  position = −4670 at K, idempotent record, append-only, RLS on rows, documents and objects for staff, clients A/B,
  a restricted viewer, a collector, another servicer and aal1, the summary and the export); pytest
  `test_statement_docs` (18: CSV format and amounts, CSV = payload totals, natures, text snapshots, the invoice
  mentions with their bases, frozen mentions, credit notes, golden hashes, environment-proof bytes),
  `test_statement_scale` (50,000 lines over 2,000 files: CSV 1.3 s, PDF 1.6 s); integration
  `test_remittance_documents_integration` (6: the worked example's statement and invoice stored = recorded =
  re-rendered, CSV = PDF = run, another process, a due invoice's own account frozen at issue, a cancelled run's credit
  note, a failed upload leaves nothing — replaced by the review's K4 test —, the next run day = the schedule; the review
  adds pgTAP `026` and the tests named below); the 50k scale run draws its statement; vitest
  `documents.test.ts`; E2E `remittances` (documents downloaded by ops and the client, the export).

## M2c-5 review fixes (2026-11-10)
Confirmed findings of the five-lens review (legal, figures, security, performance, tests and UI), fixed in this slice by two fix branches (database and worker; pages and docs) and integrated. The migration `20261113090000_remittance_documents.sql`, not yet applied in production, is edited in place; the M2c-4 functions it must change (`private.issue_commission_documents`, `private.run_remittance_checks`, `private.queue_remittance_schedule`) are redefined in it with `CREATE OR REPLACE`, their `SET` clauses, `SECURITY DEFINER` and grants restated, and it relaxes the constraint `commission_invoice_due`; no earlier migration file is edited. The legal texts were read on LibreJustice (C. com. L441-9 I in its versions of 2019 and 2027, L441-10 II from 2026-09-01, D441-5); no rule was added beyond them, and the remainder's term reuses OQ-72's default. The database, the worker and the pages follow one contract:
- **K1 export paging** (perf#0 = tests-ui#0, perf#1): `public.accounting_export_documents` and `public.accounting_export_entries` take `(p_from, p_to, p_after text default null, p_limit integer default 1000)`, the limit capped at 1,000, and return keyset-ordered pages whose rows each carry `page_key` (opaque, rising in the export's order in C collation): documents by (year, seq, id), key `YYYY:SEQ10:uuid`; entries by (effective date, posted at, entry, line), key `date|posted_at UTC to the µs|uuid|line6`; a malformed key is refused (22023 « accounting export refused: page »). PostgREST cut any answer at `max_rows` (1,000), an RPC's too, and answered 206 as a success: a year of postings (≈ 4–6 per run) silently lost its later rows. The route (`lib/remittance/accounting-export.ts`) asks page after page with `p_after` = the last row's `page_key` (omitted on the first page) until a page is shorter than the limit; a failing page, or a full page whose last key does not move on, refuses the whole file (« Export refusé. »), never a CSV cut short. The entries' document references are looked up by key (`id = source_id::uuid` under a `CASE` on the source type: no per-row scan of every servicer's invoices or runs), the account filter adds `claim_item_id is null` so the pooled index serves it, and the entries function runs with `enable_hashjoin` and `enable_mergejoin` off (ARCHITECTURE §4); the statement build's earlier-settlement lookup is keyed the same way. pgTAP `026`: 1,001 extra invoices and more than 3,000 postings paged to completion (every row once, in order), `p_limit` 5,000 answers 1,000, a bad key refused, no new sequential scan of `commission_invoice` or `remittance_run` during an entries export (`pg_stat_xact_user_tables`). Vitest `accounting-export.test.ts`: a fake RPC answering 1,000 + 1,000 + 3 rows gives 2,003 CSV rows for both exports with `p_after` chained; an exactly full last page; an empty period; a failing second page; a key that does not move on.
- **Settled and open amounts as of the period's end** (figures#7): `accounting_export_documents` counts only the settlements dated by `p_to`, so `regle_centimes` and `reste_du_centimes` are those of the period's last day; the page says « Règlements et restes dus arrêtés au … ». pgTAP `026` (a settlement dated after `p_to` left out, then counted once the period covers it); E2E.
