## M2c-5b: the manual credit note and the waiver (design §4, §8.3–§8.4, §14.1, §16, §20 R2)
Migration `20261114090000_manual_credit_note.sql` (forward-only; it redefines, with their `SET` clauses, `SECURITY DEFINER` and grants restated, `private.remittance_key_state_insert_guard`, `private.remittance_key_states` — dropped and created: its return type gains `waived_minor` —, `private.remittance_approval_refusal`, `private.approve_remittance_run`, `public.cancel_remittance_run`, `private.run_remittance_checks` and `private.remittance_statement_build`, and relaxes the constraints `commission_invoice_reason_check` (+ `manual`) and `remittance_key_state_cause_check` (+ `credit_note`), `remittance_key_state.run_id` nullable); worker `remittance.commission`, `documents`, `run`, `statement`, `jobs.remittances`; pages `/backoffice/reversements/factures/[id]` and the client « Factures ». M2c-5 had left it out (« Left for later »): the engine required each (file, tier key)'s invoices' open charges to add up to the commission K it charged, so a manual credit either lowered the key's state (the next collection re-charged it: telescoping) or did not (a later reversal credited the invoice beyond what was left of it, and the approval failed with 23514).
- **The waiver** (`remittance.commission`; CALCULATION_RULES §7 « The waiver »). A manual credit note moves part of what an invoice charges a (file, tier key) from its open charge to a **waiver on the same (invoice, file, tier key)** (`OpenCharge.waived_minor`; the key's total `KeyState.waived_minor`; in the database `public.commission_waiver`, signed movements, and `remittance_key_state.waived_minor`). For every key at every moment Σ open charges + Σ waivers = V, the commission charged; the engine refuses a history that breaks it (`CommissionInputError`: the run keeps the commission pending) and the nightly checks flag it (I22). The engine reads each invoice's **capacity** (open + waived) wherever it read its open charge before — V, the cap, the rounding reserve's n and TTC, the allocation of credits — so the waiver is invisible to what it charges: V after any runs is what it would be without the manual credit note, and **no later collection re-charges a waived amount**. Only the documents differ: when a run credits an invoice for a key (its original's invoice first, then LIFO, unchanged), the take is **absorbed by that invoice's waiver for the key first** (`KeySide.absorbed`, `documents.WaiverAbsorption`: no document, recorded at approval as `commission_waiver` rows `absorbed` with the run and the line) and only the rest is credited — never beyond the invoice's remaining HT.
- **Decisions where the design was open:**
  - **The waiver is held per (invoice, file, tier key), not per key** (the slice's brief said « KeyState.waived_minor … absorbed by the waiver first »). Held per key, the first reversal of the key would absorb it whatever invoice charged the collection: with A on FC-1, B on FC-2 and a manual credit note on FC-2, undoing A would leave FC-1 charging A's undone collection and bill the client again, through FC-2, the amount it was given back (`manual-credit-per-invoice`). Per invoice, a reversal meets only the waiver of the invoice it is credited on; `KeyState.waived_minor` is their sum.
  - **Waiver first within an invoice** (the brief's rule; OQ-78 for counsel): a collection undone on an invoice partly rectified gives back only what the rectification did not already give back. It never credits a disputed collection twice (rectified, then undone); when the rectification concerned another collection of the same file on the same invoice, that amount is billed again. Neither reading is exact without knowing what the rectification concerned; the difference is at most that (invoice, file, tier key)'s waiver.
  - **The spread over the invoice's keys: in proportion**, to what the invoice still charges each (file, tier key), integer shares and the cents left to the largest remainders, ties by file then tier key in code-point order (`documents.manual_credit`; SQL twin `private.manual_credit_plan`, parity on 60 random amounts in integration) — or over **one file's keys** when the admin names the file (the page lists the invoice's files). A file is what a client disputes; a key (the tier key of a rule) is the engine's, never shown.
  - **The reversal's invoices as a chain**: `line_invoices` may give a tuple — after a cancellation, the corrective invoice that charges the reversal again first, then the original line's own invoice, where the cancellation restored what the run's credit had absorbed — so a re-run after a cancellation of the same lines at the same VAT rate issues the same documents (`manual-credit-cancelled-run`; integration; review round 2 below for another rate or new lines). Without waivers nothing changes (the corrective invoice takes everything first, as before).
  - **The reason**: three categories on the document (« rectification d'une erreur de conditions de rémunération (taux, paliers ou minimum) », « … d'assiette (encaissement non commissionnable) », « … de facturation »), in the credit note's one line after the invoice it rectifies and its date (CGI 289 I 5); the admin's free text stays in `public.manual_credit_note`, money staff only (as the late approvals' reasons, review M2c-5 legal#6). No payload key was added (the renderer prints the line; `private.issue_commission_documents` is reused as is, `p_run_id` null, reason `manual`). *Review M2c-5b (legal#1): redefined so that every credit note freezes `ht_after` / `vat_after`, below.*
  - **Refused**: a credit note on a credit note (`credit_note`); more than the invoice still charges, or than the file chosen still owes (`more_than_remaining`); a file the invoice does not charge; **an invoice a run in flight sets off** (`in_flight`: approved or sent, its payout not debited — the stored settlement plan, posted at the debit by M2c-6, would set off more than the invoice owes; cancel the run before its file or wait for its debit; OQ-78 (c)); *review M2c-5b:* **an invoice whose own run is approved or sent** (`run_in_flight`: the run can still be cancelled, which would credit the invoice in full and let the re-run bill the rectified amount again; ledger-vat#0). A cancelled run's invoices are credited in full: `nothing_left`. A corrective invoice (`run_cancelled`) can be rectified like any invoice.
- **`public.issue_credit_note(key, invoice, amount_ht_text, reason_code, reason, expected_remaining_text, account?)`** (an admin of the invoice's servicer at aal2; another servicer's invoice is « not allowed »): idempotency key and request hash; the amount as typed in euros (`private.euros_to_minor`, two decimals at most); under the servicer's allocation and remit locks (`private.remittance_command_locks`, 55P03 « réessayez »), so with an approval's lock order — allocation, remit, then the counter, locked last by `private.issue_commission_documents` —; the plan (`private.manual_credit_plan`: the spread, VAT = R((credited + X) × rate) − R(credited × rate) at the invoice's own rate, v₁ = min(VAT, its pending VAT) on 44574 and the rest on 44571, applied = min(TTC, what the invoice owes), the rest a refund owed); compare and set on the invoice's remaining HT the page read (`invoice_changed`); the document numbered in the gapless series, dated today, its entry −4111 TTC / +7060 HT / +44574 v₁ / +44571 v₂ (design §5.2 row), applied at once (`commission_settlement` kind `credit_note`); the waiver rows and one key state per key credited (cause `credit_note`, V unchanged, waived grown), then the engine's input check per key (`private.commission_key_open`); the staff record. Its PDF is queued by the M2c-5 trigger and drawn by the documents job (`facture-commission-fr-2`: « Avoir », the invoice it rectifies with its date, VAT per rate of the invoice; `fr-3` since the review, F3). A refund owed is paid by the client's next run (the plan's refunds, M2c-4); *review M2c-5b (legal#0):* with no later run, by a transfer from the own account (`record_client_refund`, design §16, M2c-7), the alert `credit_refund_owed` naming it after 30 days.
- **Approval, cancellation, history** (redefinitions): the approval writes each key state's waiver and the `absorbed` rows its draft's key states carry (`run.prepare_run`: `key_states[].waived` and `.absorbed`); a manual credit note's key state has no run and counts in the history a draft assumed (`history_changed`: `is distinct from` where the refusal compared run ids), and changes the invoice's open part (`documents_changed`) — a draft prepared before one is sent back. Cancelling a run clears the waivers of its own invoices (they are credited in full on what they still charge: `run_cancelled`), restores what its credits absorbed (`restored`; *review math#0: as the waiver of its corrective invoice of the absorbing invoice's rate, below*), and writes each key back to its state before the run with the waiver its invoices hold now (manual credit notes issued since included); its input check covers the keys whose waivers moved.
- **Checks** (`private.run_remittance_checks` redefined): I16 counts what a run's credits absorbed (documents' HT + absorbed = the lines' commission); **I22 `commission_key_state`** (new, violation): per (file, tier key) whose state changed since the previous check run (with a day's margin; `remittance_key_state (organization_id, created_at)` indexed), open charges + waivers = the commission charged, the waivers its state's, none below 0. I17 (numbering) and I18 (4111 = open documents, 44574 = pending VAT) hold unchanged with manual credit notes (pgTAP `027`). « Contrôles » labels I22.
- **Statement**: `private.remittance_statement_build` adds `waived_absorbed_minor` and the invoices it was on to its totals when a run's credit was absorbed (absent otherwise: statements drawn before keep their bytes); the PDF says « Dont … de commission sur des encaissements annulés, déjà rendus par avoir manuel sur la facture … : aucun nouvel avoir pour ce montant » (the lines' commission and the documents then differ by that amount; reworded by the review, legal#4, below). Template name unchanged (no stored payload carries the key).
- **Pages**: `/backoffice/reversements/factures/[id]` (`public.commission_invoice_detail`, money staff at aal2: HT, TTC, what it still charges and owes, its files with what each still owes and what manual credit notes rectified, its credit notes — a manual one's category and, for staff, its reason; « Émettre un avoir » for an admin when the invoice can take one, else why not): the amount, the file or the whole invoice, the category, the internal reason, « Voir l'effet » (`public.credit_note_preview`, the command's own plan: HT, VAT, TTC, what it takes off what the invoice owes, the refund owed, what the invoice still owes and charges after, where the VAT comes off), « Émettre l'avoir »; refusals in French (`credit-notes.ts`). The run page links each document to it. Client « Factures »: « rectifie la facture FC-… du … » and a manual credit note's category, never the reason.
- **Read access**: `commission_waiver` and `manual_credit_note` are money staff's (RLS); the credit note itself is a `commission_invoice` row the client reads like any (its whole-client members; its PDF once electronic acceptance was frozen). No write policy.
- **Left for later**: re-invoicing under corrected terms (design §20 R2: undercharging stays the servicer's loss); a manual credit note while a payout is in flight, or on an invoice whose own run can still be cancelled (refused until M2c-6 books debits, OQ-78 (c)); the refund of a credit note's amount owed when no later run comes (`record_client_refund`, M2c-7; `credit_refund_owed` makes it visible, OQ-78 (e)); the waiver per collection rather than per (invoice, file, tier key) (would need the manual credit note to name collections; OQ-78 (b)); a manual credit note issued between a cancellation and the run again on an invoice the cancelled run took from keeps its waiver there while the run again credits the reversal on the corrective invoice — the client billed less than in the run never approved, by at most that credit note, V unchanged (review round 3, there since the waiver; OQ-78 (f), CALCULATION_RULES §7).
- **Tests**: Hypothesis in `test_commission.py` — against a twin without manual credit notes, with mixed clauses, two keys, versions and small amounts: Σ open + Σ waived = V at every step, V and tier positions the twin's, invoices the twin's to the cent, each credit the twin issues absorbed first then credited on the same invoice and key, never beyond its remaining HT, and for `credit` clauses the schedule's K that of one run over the lines (partition); inside one version a run of collections charges only what it adds, keeps every waiver, issues no credit note, in any order of its lines; everything undone: every invoice credited in full with exactly its VAT, no waiver left; a cancellation with manual credit notes before and after the run restores the state before it and the re-run charges what the run charged; the spread (proportion, Σ, each within a cent, never above a key's charge, cumulative VAT); input errors. Golden cases (TO VALIDATE): `manual-credit-waiver`, `manual-credit-per-invoice`, `manual-credit-two-files`, `manual-credit-cancelled-run`. pgTAP `027_manual_credit_note` (70). Integration `test_manual_credit_note_integration` (the real prepare and approval jobs: no re-charge, absorption, FC-1 closed with its VAT, the statement's sentence, cancellation and re-run, the checks clean; SQL = Python spread). Vitest `credit-notes.test.ts` (11). E2E `credit-notes` (desktop, mobile; screenshots `m2c5b-*`).

## M2c-5b review fixes (2026-11-10)
Confirmed findings of the five-lens review (math, ledger and VAT, legal, security and concurrency, tests and UI), fixed by two branches (database and worker; pages and docs) that follow one contract (F1–F5), then integrated. The migration `20261114090000_manual_credit_note.sql`, not yet applied in production, is edited in place: it now also redefines `private.issue_commission_documents` (its settings and revoke restated; F3), adds `public.commission_invoice_files` (F4) and `private.absorbed_credit_notes` (legal#4), the indexes `commission_waiver_entry_idx` and `commission_invoice_credit_note_idx`, and relaxes `commission_invoice_charge_charged_minor_check` to `>= 0` (math#0); the functions of merged migrations it changes are redefined in it with `CREATE OR REPLACE`, their `SET` clauses, `SECURITY DEFINER` and grants restated; no earlier migration file is edited. Texts read on LibreJustice on 2026-11-10: CIBS L212-9, L214-6, L214-9 and L214-18 in their versions from 2027-01-01 (ordonnance n° 2026-671, art. 19 I), CGI 272 and 283 (repealed from 2027-01-01 but for 272 1 al. 2 and 283 2 septies, ordonnance n° 2025-1247), BOI-TVA-DECLA-30-20-20-20 §260 (2022-01-19) and BOI-TVA-DED-40-10-20 §80 (2017-04-05).
- **F1 No manual credit note on an invoice whose own run can still be cancelled** (ledger-vat#0). The refusal only looked at the settlement plans of runs in flight, so an invoice its own approved run did not set off (a due invoice, a netted invoice the plan deferred) took a manual credit note; cancelling that run then cleared the waiver, wrote each key back to its state before the run with no waiver, and the re-run billed the rectified amount again in full (30,00 € HT + 6,00 € VAT in the reproduction). `private.manual_credit_refusal` now returns **`run_in_flight`** when the invoice is a run's own (`reason = 'commission'`) and that run is approved or sent, checked before `in_flight` (a plan in flight sets it off); `issue_credit_note`, `credit_note_preview` and `commission_invoice_detail` all read it. A corrective invoice (`run_cancelled`, carrying the cancelled run's id) stays creditable, a booked run's invoices too, so a cancellation never meets a manual credit note on its own invoices. pgTAP `027`: Martin's r1 invoice refused `run_in_flight` (command and effect sheet), then r1 booked (standing in for M2c-6's debit) for the « creditable » fixture; Cyprès's invoice `run_in_flight`, the `in_flight` branch through `pg_temp.refusal_as_debited`; the block cancelling a run with a manual credit note on its own invoice removed. Integration: RV-2's invoice refused `run_in_flight`. The Simulator and the Hypothesis properties draw manual credit notes only on invoices of runs no longer in flight. Pages: the refusal in French on the invoice page and from the command (`credit-notes.ts`; `forms.ts` `credit_note_run_in_flight`, matched before `in_flight`); E2E `credit-notes` checks it while the run is approved, then stands in for M2c-6's debit booking (the service role sets the run `booked`) before issuing the credit note. Not chosen: carrying the waiver across the cancellation (a run cancelled to be re-run under corrected circumstances would be corrected twice).
- **F2 A refund owed that no run settles is visible** (legal#0). A manual credit note on a paid invoice leaves a refund owed (`excess`) that only a later run's payout paid; with no later collection nothing paid it, nothing alerted, and « Préparer maintenant » refused (`nothing_pending`). The nightly alert **`credit_refund_owed`** (alert, in `private.run_remittance_checks`; design §15's `refund_owed_to_client`): a credit note that owed a refund at issue (a correction with `excess` > 0) still open more than 30 days after its issue date — an operating threshold, not a legal deadline —, its details {`number`, `client_id`, `reason`, `issue_date`, `planned_run`: a run in flight whose plan pays it}, read by `commission_invoice_credit_note_idx`. « Contrôles » labels it « Avoir à rembourser au client depuis plus de 30 jours » and opens the credit note's page (`checkSubjectLink`, `invoice_overdue` too). The refund by transfer from the own account is `record_client_refund` (design §16, M2c-7). The effect sheet reads « À rembourser au client (avec son prochain reversement, sinon par virement du cabinet) », the PDF (F3) « l'excédent éventuel vous est dû : il vous sera versé avec un prochain reversement, ou par virement s'il n'y en a pas »; nothing says « remboursé » before money moves. pgTAP `027`: Lilas's 3 600,00 € owed alerted 31 days on, not on the day; none for the notes applied in full. Vitest `debits.test.ts`. OQ-78 (e); « Left for later » above.
- **F3 A credit note states the invoice's totals after it** (legal#1). BOFiP asks a credit note by which the issuer means to recover the VAT to mention « le montant du total hors taxes et de la TVA due après application de la réduction de prix »; no credit note did (run, cancellation or manual: the template's gap, not only this slice's). `private.issue_commission_documents` freezes, per correction, **`ht_after`** and **`vat_after`**: the corrected invoice's HT and VAT less every credit note on it — earlier ones, those issued before it in the same call, and this one. Template **`facture-commission-fr-3`** prints « Après cet avoir, la facture FC-… du … s'élève à X € HT, TVA Y € (taux). » and words the excess as owed, not refunded (F2); `fr-2` stays in `TEMPLATE_VERSIONS` and renders its old bytes (its golden PDF hashes unchanged), and a payload without `ht_after` prints no after-line. `test_statement_docs.test_a_credit_note_states_each_invoice_after_it` (the mentions under `fr-3`, `fr-2` and an old payload), `fr-3` hashes pinned; pgTAP `027` (`ht_after` / `vat_after` on three credit notes); integration (RV-2's credit note payload). The back-office page of a credit note does not repeat the after-line (the PDF carries it). Design §14.2, FAC-05.
- **F4 Every file in « Sur », and a credit note's own page** (tests-ui#2, tests-ui#3). « Sur » offered only the 200 files `commission_invoice_detail` lists (by what is still open), so a file ranked past 200 could not be chosen and the pro-rata spread put the waiver on the wrong (invoice, file, tier key). **`public.commission_invoice_files(p_invoice_id, p_after text default null, p_limit int default 200)`** (money staff at aal2, 42501 otherwise) returns the invoice's open charges per (file, tier key) — `file_id`, `file_ref`, `tier_key`, `open_minor` (> 0), `page_key` — in primary-key order (`account_id`, `tier_key`) after `p_after`, at most 1 000 a page; `page_key` is `account_id/tier_key`, opaque to the page; there is no search in the database. The sheet reads it a page at a time through the typed client (« Charger les dossiers suivants », after the last row's key; a short page or a key that does not move stops), lists each file once, and « Chercher un dossier (référence) » narrows what is loaded; if the read fails, it falls back to the detail's 200 files and says the list is incomplete. A credit note's own page showed an empty « Avoirs qui rectifient cette facture » and never named what it rectifies: `commission_invoice_detail` now also returns, for a credit note, `corrects` [{`id`, `number`, `issue_date`, `ht`, `vat`}], `reason_code`, `reason_fr` and `reason_text`, and the page (`creditNoteFacts`) names each invoice it rectifies, linked, with what it took off (HT, VAT), a manual one's category and staff reason; the empty section is hidden, and with no run (a manual credit note) the back link goes to the invoice. pgTAP `027` (three pages of one row each, the last empty; another servicer refused; a credit note's detail names FC-…-000001); vitest `credit-notes.test.ts` (paging, merge, search, `creditNoteBack`, `creditNoteFacts`); E2E `credit-notes` (the credit note's page, screenshot `m2c5b-avoir-page`).
- **F5 A draft computed from mixed snapshots is never approved** (security-concurrency#0). The prepare read the key states, then the history's high-water mark, then the charges with their waivers, each statement in its own snapshot (READ COMMITTED); a credit note committing between the first two reads gave a draft whose every line's commission was pending (`commission_input_error`) and which the approval accepted (`history_changed` compared two values read after the commit). `jobs.remittances.load_facts` reads `private.remittance_history_seq` first, right after the run head: a credit note committed after it raises the mark and the approval sends the draft back (`history_changed`); one committed before is seen by every later read. `private.remittance_approval_refusal` refuses a draft whose `commission_blockers` carry `commission_input_error` (**`engine_error`**, « la commission de certains encaissements n'a pas pu être calculée : actualisez le brouillon »), and « À valider » leaves it unselectable (`commissionNotComputed`). REPEATABLE READ is not used: the queue's transaction has already run statements when the prepare starts. Integration `test_a_credit_note_committing_mid_prepare_never_gives_an_approvable_draft` (a second connection commits a manual credit note mid-prepare: after the history read → `history_changed`; after the key states → `engine_error`, approved before the fix); pgTAP `027` (`pg_temp.refusal_with_input_error` → `engine_error`); vitest `runs.test.ts`. Design §9.4. *Round 2 below: `engine_error`, its label and the draft hiding removed; the history read first is the fix.*
- **Cancellation of a run whose credits absorbed a waiver, and the run again** (math#0, math#1). With two reversals of one key in the run (the absorbing one first) and a newer invoice still live on the key, cancel then re-run left the waiver on the original invoice (whose collection was undone) and credited the live invoice instead (40,00 € HT under-billed for good in the reproduction). `public.cancel_remittance_run` step 3 now puts what the run's credits absorbed back as the **waiver of its corrective invoice of the absorbing invoice's mandate and VAT rate** — with a 0 charge row there for a key the run only absorbed (`commission_invoice_charge.charged_minor` may be 0, on a corrective invoice only) —, one `restored` row per absorption with its line (`entry_id`); where the cancellation issued no corrective invoice at that rate, back on the absorbing invoice. The waiver guard lets a corrective invoice hold up to Σ `restored` for the key and requires a charge row for every waiver. In the engine a link of a reversal's chain can be a **`commission.Retake`** (invoice, caps per key): run again, the reversal takes from each invoice that holds what the cancelled run took for it at most that much per (file, tier key), the cap shared by all the line's credits on the key, then its original's own invoice, then LIFO; `jobs.remittances` (`_line_invoices`) loads the caps from the latest cancelled run that credited or absorbed something for the reversal, `inputs_hash` includes them, and `Simulator.cancel_last` mirrors the SQL (*round 2 below: in the order the cancelled run took them, every cancelled run replayed*). The same caps fix an M2c-4 C7 defect the fuzz found with no manual credit note (8 of the 1 900 seeds the review ran: a reversal's credit spanning two VAT rates or two keys drained another's pooled share, 1 to 511 cents of HT per invoice). math#1: fixed wherever a corrective invoice exists at the absorbing invoice's rate; when every take of the run at a rate was absorbed, no corrective invoice is issued and the file is exactly as before the run, while the twin without manual credit notes keeps one more open invoice — its reserve and, under mixed rates with the cap binding, its LIFO order can differ: documented in CALCULATION_RULES §7 (« Cent-level effects »), not fixed (a 0 € corrective invoice was rejected). Goldens `manual-credit-cancel-two-reversals`, `cancel-credit-across-rates`, `manual-credit-cancel-all-absorbed`, and `manual-credit-cancelled-run` (the absorption now on FC-6); Hypothesis `test_with_waivers_a_cancellation_then_the_run_again_is_the_run_never_approved` (mixed VAT rates; the waivers and each earlier invoice's (open, waived) against the run never approved; fails on the build and when the caps are ignored); integration `test_a_cancelled_run_again_gives_each_reversal_its_own_share`, and the existing cancellation test asserts the waiver restored on the corrective invoice. The reviewers' fuzz harness with the math#1 allowance: 0 failing over seeds 0–29 999 (183 under the allowance) and 0 over 0–9 999 with manual credit notes disabled (database branch); on the integrated branch, seeds 0–1 899: 0 failing, 7 under the allowance (1 cent), the same 7 the unpatched harness reports.
- **The statement's absorbed sentence** (legal#4). « déjà rendus » read as money returned beside a refund only « ordonné », and named the corrected invoice, not the credit note. It now reads « Dont -X € de commission sur des encaissements annulés, déjà crédités par avoir manuel (avoir n° FC-… rectifiant la facture FC-…) : aucun nouvel avoir pour ce montant » (« avoirs » when several; a payload without the credit notes: « sur la facture / les factures … »). `private.absorbed_credit_notes(run)` follows the run's `absorbed` rows back through `restored` rows on corrective invoices (recursive, keyed per movement) to the manual credit notes issued before the run's approval; `private.remittance_statement_build` freezes them as `totals.waived_absorbed_credit_notes` [{`number`, `invoice`}] beside `waived_absorbed_minor`, present only when something was absorbed (statements with no absorption keep their bytes). `test_statement_docs.test_what_a_manual_credit_notes_waiver_absorbed_is_named` (one note, two notes, an old payload, never « rendu »); integration (RV-2, and RV-3 traced back through the corrective invoice; rv5 in the two-reversal test).
- **VAT timing and the 2027 texts** (legal#2, legal#3; docs and pack). OQ-78 (d) asks the accountant whether, under the encaissement regime, the VAT on a refunded part is reduced at the credit note (as built: 44574 first, then 44571, at issue) or at the refund (CIBS L214-6 al. 2; L214-9 on the option), with the remedy if « at the refund »; the `vat/fr` pack's 2027 review covers it (M2c-3 block above). FAC-05 and OQ-78 (a) cite the CIBS successors of CGI 283 3 and 272 1 — L212-9 2° and L214-18 1° —, and the pack's `credit_note` texts carry them (quoted, each with its review due 2026-12-01); its « non identifié » note now says which 2027 rule covers which case (L212-9 2° / L214-18 1° for VAT invoiced in error, L214-6 / L214-9 for a price given back) and that no article repeating the « justification … de la rectification préalable » was found. `test_vat.test_the_review_tripwire_logic` names both among the texts due and refuses a « Non identifié » note there.
- **Tests the review asked for** (tests-ui#0, tests-ui#1, tests-ui#5). pgTAP `027`: Martin's draft r5 prepared, a manual credit note on its earlier invoice, the approval job sends it back (`back_to_draft`, `history_changed`), no key state, no document, the run a draft again; integration `test_a_credit_note_between_prepare_and_approval_sends_the_draft_back` through the real jobs, then « Actualiser » and the approval: the latest key state's waiver equals Σ `commission_waiver` for the (file, tier key). `test_a_manual_credit_note_never_changes_what_the_engine_charges` draws the VAT rate per run (0 %, 5,5 %, 10 %, 20 %) for both simulators, and golden `manual-credit-rate-fall` (1 % flat, 20,00 € minimum per file, 20,01 € at 20 %, a manual credit of 10,00 €, the rate down to 5,5 %, then 0,01 €: no document, V 16,66 €); the mutation `capacity(ch)` → `ch.open_minor` in the mixed-rate TTC now fails both. `test_the_inputs_hash_names_every_input` covers the state's and a charge's waiver, a line's own invoice against a chain, a `Retake`'s cap and key, `('FC-1',)` hashing as `'FC-1'`, and pins the digest of a fixed input without waivers to the value computed on main (478b641). Counts after the review: pgTAP `027` 77 tests, vitest `credit-notes.test.ts` 21.
- **Docs**: COMPLIANCE FAC-05 and OQ-78 (a), (c) widened, (d), (e); design §9.4, §14.1, §14.2 (the after-line, the excess owed), §15, §16; CALCULATION_RULES §7 (the cancellation, the run again, the M2c-4 defect, the cent-level exception, five golden rows); DOMAIN; the `vat/fr` pack.
- **Round 2 (skeptics' verification, 2026-11-11).** Two first-round fixes were rejected as regressions (`verify2.md`: math#0's chain order, security-concurrency#0's `engine_error`); fixed again on `m5b-fix2`, each with tests that fail on the integrated build (98f3388):
  - **math#0 — the order of a reversal's links.** Round 1 sorted a reversal's `Retake` links by their invoices' numbers, so the corrective invoice of the lower VAT rate, or an older invoice whose waiver was restored, came before the share of the reversal's own invoice. With the same lines at the same rate every link is taken in full and the order is moot; when the run again credits less (another VAT rate, through the cap and the reserve, or new lines), the shortfall fell on the wrong invoice and rate (reviewers' gen2 seed 1896 at realistic rates: V 15,39 € against 15,84 € never approved, 2,64 € more of a live invoice's waiver consumed; seed 3967 at a 100 % rate: −37,15 €). **`commission.retake_links`** (pure, called by `Simulator.cancel_last` and by `jobs.remittances._line_invoices`) orders them as the cancelled run took: first what it took from the invoices of the chain it ran with — its original's own invoice; for a run cancelled again, the earlier cancellation's links first (a second cancellation otherwise put the own invoice's share ahead of the corrective invoices the run had taken first: 11 cents in gen2 seed 3037) — in that order, then the rest LIFO, newest first; a link pooling several takes comes where its first came. The prepare's takes CTE carries each take's original invoice and its (year, seq) — a credit's `original_invoice_id`; an absorption's `absorbed` row's invoice, its destination recomputed as the cancellation did (the corrective invoice of the absorbing invoice's mandate and rate, else that invoice) — and replays every cancelled run that took something for the reversal in approval order, the latest giving the links. The wording is restricted to what holds (engine docstring, CALCULATION_RULES §7, DOMAIN, design §9.7): **the same lines at the same VAT rate give the documents of the run never approved**; after a change of rate or with new lines the run again is within the reserve when each key has at most two invoices and one reversal, and otherwise within a measured bound (n + 1 + ⌈D·s⌉ cents of V, D the credit moved between the key's lines — after repeated cancellations summed over each cancelled run and the next, D = Σᵢ |tookᵢ − tookᵢ₊₁| (round 3 below) —, s the spread of its VAT rates), the split between open and waived possibly differing more after repeated cancellations with new lines (« a waiver left on an earlier corrective invoice »), Σ open + Σ waived = V throughout. Not done: exactness there (a link per take with its credited and absorbed parts, an engine change). Tests: Hypothesis `test_with_waivers_a_cancellation_then_another_vat_rate_stays_within_the_reserve_of_the_run_never_approved` (≤ two invoices and one reversal per key, the rate changed: |ΔV| ≤ n + 1, |ΔW| ≤ |ΔV| plus D when both invoices bear one rate; it fails under the number order in 8 of 10 random seeds, and always on its pinned example — a 5 000,00 € minimum on a small file, 89,54 € against 91,99 €; 91,98 € now), `test_retake_links_come_in_the_order_the_cancelled_run_took`; golden **`cancel-retiering-two-credits`** (a reversal's own band and its regularisation of the later tiers on one key, the 20 % corrective invoice pooled with another reversal: with the Retake cap per credit instead of per line — the reviewers' mutation mutL, caught by no test before — the second credit takes the other reversal's share, which falls on D's live invoice, and FC-5 is left open); integration `test_a_reversal_run_again_after_its_cancellation_takes_back_its_own_invoices_share_first` (the chain `_line_invoices` builds, cancelled and run again twice; `own-at-20`: the reversal's own invoice at 20 %, LIFO at 10 % — the 10 % corrective invoice is numbered first, the chain starts with the 20 % one; fails with the integrated `_line_invoices`; `own-at-10`: after the second cancellation the chain follows the first one's links, the older invoice first — fails when only the latest cancelled run is read, LIFO putting the 20 % one first). Reviewers' generators on the simulator, re-run on the final commit (`verify2/math`, first divergence per history): gen2 with the same lines at the same rate (`CYCLE_VAT=0 EXTRA=0`, up to three cancellations), 1 500 seeds each with and without manual credit notes, at its rates and at realistic ones (`REALISTIC=1`): 0 failing in 6 000. At realistic rates with new lines and up to three cancellations (4 000 seeds each): with VAT changes (`CYCLE_VAT=1`) max |ΔV| 3 cents with manual credit notes and 2 without (integrated build: 69 and 151 cents; ff90db8: 3,16 € and 22 cents), without them (`CYCLE_VAT=0`) 1 cent either way; seed 1896 now exact. One cancellation, the rate always changed, the same lines (`EXTRA=0 MAXCYC=1`, the rate forced to change; 4 000 seeds per setting): max |ΔV| 51 cents with manual credit notes and 1 without at realistic rates (integrated: 85 cents and 2,19 €), 35,83 € and 43 cents at the generator's 100 % rates (integrated: 35,83 € and 3,95 €); |ΔV| ≤ n + 1 + ⌈D·s⌉ and |ΔW| ≤ D + |ΔV| in all 16 000. With new lines and repeated cancellations the V bound held in all 24 000 (max 3 cents at realistic rates, 43,52 € at 100 %), the W one failed in 25 of the 12 000 with manual credit notes (up to 5,97 € at realistic rates, 34,27 € at 100 %; none without) — the « bounded, not exact » wording above. *Round 3 below: these are gen2's histories, D measured against the latest cancelled run; on gen5 that D does not bound V after two cancellations with a change of rate between them, D summed over the steps does, and the maxima are larger.* gen3 (7 000 seeds): 0 failing, V differing only in the documented math#1 case (185 seeds, up to 197,86 € at 100 % rates, 60 and 77 cents at realistic ones; integrated: 187 and 197,86 €, now recorded in CALCULATION_RULES §7); gen4 (4 000): 0 failing (3 624 compared to the end); the DB agent's patched fuzz, seeds 0–1 899: 0 failing, 8 under the math#1 allowance (1 cent). Mutants: the number order fails the property in 8 of 10 random seeds (its example always) and `test_retake_links_come_in_the_order_the_cancelled_run_took`; mutL fails `cancel-retiering-two-credits`.
  - **security-concurrency#0 — option (a): no `engine_error`.** With the history's position read first, `history_changed` already refuses every draft prepared across a credit note's commit (both interleavings of the integration test, now refused by it: the draft read across the key states carries `commission_input_error` and is still sent back as stale). `engine_error` only added a refusal of drafts whose input error persists — a key I22 flags: every « Actualiser » read the same data, so the client's run could never be approved and no gross payout left, against M2c-4 « The commission kept pending » (the run remits gross) and CPCE R124-6 al. 2 (remittance within one month of the effective collection, unless agreed otherwise). Removed from `private.remittance_approval_refusal` (the migration's comments say why); on the pages the `engine_error` label, the « actualisez ce brouillon » card and the draft hiding (`commissionNotComputed`) are gone — the card says again « Commission en attente : … (reversement brut) » and the run is selectable —, and I22's help says « … laissera sa commission en attente (reversement brut) ». `run.py` and `load_facts` say why no refusal is needed; design §9.4. Tests: integration `test_a_draft_the_engine_cannot_price_for_good_is_approved_gross` (a key state one cent above its invoices, as pgTAP `027` builds for I22: the draft carries `commission_input_error`, is approved, net = gross = 1 000,00 €, no document, its line `pending`, I22 flagged; refused `engine_error` under the integrated function); the race test also asserts which draft carries the error; pgTAP `027` (78 tests): the input-error draft refused `history_changed` when its history is stale, and approvable (no refusal) when it is current — `engine_error` before; vitest `debits.test.ts` (I22's help: commission pending, gross).
  - **Round 3 (verification of round 2, 2026-11-11).** Both fixes confirmed in the code — no change to `retake_links`, `_line_invoices` or `Simulator.cancel_last`, `engine_error`'s removal right (three wording nits, done: `run.py` « e.g. a key I22 flags »; design §9.4 and the migration's comment: the gross remittance *can* leave within R124-6's month, its approval is not guaranteed by then) — and three gaps in docs and tests, closed on `m5b-fix3` without a code change. (1) **D after repeated cancellations.** The docs gave D against the cancelled run; after two cancellations with a change of rate between them that D does not bound V: an approval at another rate freezes what the cap allowed at that rate, and the next approval, taking exactly as much (D = 0), keeps the drift (the reviewers' gen5 seed 9572, realistic rates, no manual credit note: +31 cents with D = 0, n = 4; seed 599 at 100 % rates: +3,20 €; 22 of 8 781 histories). D is now Σ over the run's lines of Σᵢ |tookᵢ − tookᵢ₊₁| over the consecutive cancelled runs and the run again (CALCULATION_RULES §7, the engine docstring); with it |ΔV| ≤ n + 1 + ⌈D·s⌉ and |ΔW| ≤ D + |ΔV| held in all 8 781 and in all 40 491 gen5 histories with a changed rate or new lines (re-run on this code: 20 000 seeds in each of four settings, every mode). (2) **The measured maxima are gen5's, not bounds**: at realistic rates a run re-approved at another rate and then run again at the first reaches 1,47 € of V (1,39 € without manual credit notes), one cancellation with a fall of the rate 26 cents without manual credit notes, |ΔW| 8,23 € after one cancellation — against the « 3 cents », « 1 cent » and « 6,50 € » of gen2 above; restated in CALCULATION_RULES §7 with the other modes. (3) **LIFO beyond the chain was pinned by no test**: ordering the links beyond the chain oldest first passed all 66 commission and golden tests, while gen5 seed 9967 (realistic, manual credit notes, the rate down), exact on this code, gives −1,36 € of V and −18,76 € of waiver with it. `test_a_smaller_credit_run_again_comes_off_the_oldest_invoice_the_cancelled_run_took_from` — the reversal's credit on its own invoice at 2,1 %, then LIFO on FC-2 at 5,5 % and the older FC-1 at 0 %, cancelled, run again at 10 % instead of 20 %: the run never approved takes the 81,81 € shortfall off FC-1, the run again off FC-1's corrective FC-5 — fails with that order (FC-5 takes the whole credit left and FC-7 is never credited: 23,67 € HT and 1,30 € of VAT still billed at 5,5 %, V 981,79 € against 981,80 €), and passes here. Also recorded, not fixed: a manual credit note between a cancellation and the run again (pre-existing; OQ-78 (f), « Left for later » above).

## M2c-6a: transfers and files (M2-14 cash-out, first half; design §6.1, §9.7–§9.9, §11, §15–§17, §21)
Migration `20261115090000_transfers_files.sql` (forward-only; redefines `private.bank_transfer_guard`, `private.remittance_run_guard`, `private.remittance_payout_blockers`, `public.request_refund` and `public.cancel_remittance_run` — the last two gain a defaulted last argument, so their old signatures are dropped — with their settings and grants restated; renames `private.run_remittance_checks` to `private.run_remittance_runs_checks`, its body unchanged, and a new `private.run_remittance_checks` calls it then the transfers' checks; a later slice redefines the runs' part under the new name); worker `remittance.pain001`, job `remittances.transfer_file` (`jobs.transfer_files`, on the existing `remittances` queue: no new queue); bucket `transfer-files` (`supabase/config.toml`; hosted: `supabase config push`). **No ledger entry is posted**: §0 and §5.2 date the remittance, the settlement and the sweep at the bank's debit; generating, downloading or uploading a file is no bank fact (M2c-6b books the debits).
- **Files** (`transfer_file`, `transfer_file_item`, `transfer_file_download`): `public.generate_transfer_file(key, bank_account, late_reason?)` (admins and ops managers at aal2, idempotency key and request hash) builds **one live file per paying account**: it supersedes the account's files not downloaded yet (their transfers come in the new one, new MsgId) and takes every `ordered` payout and file-mode refund of the account that passes the checks, plus the sweep. Only an active `client_funds` account in EUR pays a file; the own account's top-up files are M2c-7's (design §21). File number `TF-AAAA-NNNNNN` (a sequence: unique, not gapless, §3.2 #4) is the MsgId; one PmtInf per (group, execution date), `<number>-<n>`, the sweep in its own; `CreDtTm` frozen at generation (Paris time with its offset); the debtor (servicer's legal name, IBAN, BIC or `NOTPROVIDED`) frozen on the file. States `pending → generated → downloaded → sent`, or `superseded | rejected | failed` (the design's list plus `pending`, while the job writes it, and `failed`).
- **Transfers** (`bank_transfer`): `in_file` names its file (`transfer_file_id`); a transfer goes back from `in_file` to `ordered` only when its file is superseded, rejected or failed (the guard checks it), so it goes in the next file; a sweep is cancelled instead and recomputed (ledger critique #16). The file's items keep which file held each transfer (and the PmtInfId M2c-6b matches batch debits with).
- **The sweep** (§11, §13 #8; founder #9): S = max(0, −Σ4679 − Σ sweeps ordered or in a file), read under the remit lock, to the servicer's active own account named in « Facturation » (none: no sweep, the page says so). Until M2c-6b books sweeps, a sweep stays `in_file` and S nets it.
- **Checks at generation** (§11), under the allocation then remit locks: **cash** — the closing balance of the account's last imported statement that has one, less the debits on statements for later days (credits left aside), less the transfers in a downloaded or sent file whose debit no statement shows yet (by our end-to-end id, or by PmtInfId for a batch), less the refunds ops execute by hand still pending, ≥ CtrlSum; when short the sweep is left out first (clients are paid first), then the file is refused (`cash_not_covered`; none imported: `no_closing_balance`). **Per transfer** (`private.transfer_hold_reason`): a payout's run still approved or sent; today's payout blockers (M2c-4's, plus `payee_name_mismatch`); the payout account unchanged since approval froze it (`payout_account_changed`); the per-client cap N + D ≤ −4670[c] − c's other runs in flight (`payout_not_covered`: a collection reversed since approval, ledger critique #1); its execution date — the later of its requested date and the account's next execution day (today only before its cut-off, as at approval) — after the run's earliest latest execution date only with a late reason (the run's, or one given with the file: kept on the file, the item marked `late`). A transfer that fails is **held out** with its reason (`transfer_file.held`) and stays `ordered`.
- **The job** (`transfer_file {file_id, token}`): `private.transfer_file_begin` returns the frozen facts (null when superseded meanwhile or another job's), the writer renders deterministic bytes (`pain.001.001.09` default, `.03` per `bank_account.pain_version`, `public.set_bank_account_pain_version` admins only), `pain001.check` verifies every field §11 lists (element order, lengths, the EPC charset, NbOfTxs and CtrlSum from integer minor units, unique ids ≤ 35, IBANs, BICs), the ISO 20022 XSD validates them **when vendored** (`docs/reference/iso20022/README.md`; the files could not be downloaded in this session: `www.iso20022.org` was refused; the file records `xsd_validated`), the bytes go to `transfer-files/<servicer>/<file>/<number>.xml` and `private.transfer_file_record` stores their SHA-256 (refused if NbOfTxs or CtrlSum differ from the file's). A data error (`Pain001Error`, SQLSTATE 22/23/LG) fails the file at once (`private.transfer_file_failed`: its transfers back to ordered, the alert says why); other errors are retried, then the dead-letter hook fails it.
- **Download** (§11, ops critique #33): the web route reads the file with the caller's session (RLS, the bucket policy `private.can_read_transfer_file_object`: money staff at aal2, the file's own path only), checks the bytes against the SHA-256, then `public.transfer_file_download(file, sha256, acknowledged)` records the download (refused when the hash differs, before the job wrote it, or a second time unless the warning is acknowledged), and only then serves the bytes — **not a signed URL** (deviation from §11's wording: a URL the browser fetches would skip the hash check; the route serves them as M2c-5's documents). Every download is a row (`transfer_file_download`), so the command takes no idempotency key. The file's runs become `sent` (§9.8). `public.mark_transfer_file_sent` (« Marquer comme transmis ») records who uploaded it.
- **Cancellations** (§9.7; risk R4; after download replaced by review T1 below, then off until M2c-6b (ADR-0014 M2c-6a round 5; OQ-81): `bank_booking_required`): `public.cancel_transfer_file(key, file, version, reason, attestation?)` — before download the file is superseded; after download only with the attestation `not_uploaded` or `rejected_by_bank` (status `rejected`), and never once a statement shows a debit of one of its transfers; its transfers back to ordered, its runs back to `approved` (`remittance_run_guard`: sent → approved only with its transfer ordered). `public.cancel_remittance_run(…, p_attestation)` — approved or sent: a transfer still ordered is cancelled; one in a file not downloaded supersedes that file first; one in a downloaded or sent file only with the attestation `not_executed` (the file not uploaded, rejected, or this transfer refused — a payee mismatch), once a statement of the paying account covering its execution date is imported, and never with its debit seen; then M2c-5b's credit notes and corrective invoices as before. The file of an executed batch stays as it is.
- **Refunds in the file** (§6.1, M2b-6 #13; founder #15): `refund_request.execution_mode` (`manual` for the rows before, `file` by default from now on when the payment's account is the servicer's active dedicated account in EUR) and `transfer_id`: a file-mode refund has a `refund` transfer with the refund's own RFD id, never executed by hand. Its booking stays the M2b-6 RFD link; the trigger `private.refund_transfer_follow` keeps the transfer in step (executed → booked, the refund's `cash_out` as its entry — a pending or generated file holding it is superseded first, so it is never uploaded already paid; cancelled → cancelled, refused while a downloaded file holds it; bounced → returned).
- **Verification of payee** (Reg. 260/2012 art. 5 quater; founder #15, OQ-50): `payee_name_check` (`no_match` / `close_match`, the bank's suggested name, a note) recorded on a payout by ops blocks the client's payout account (`payee_name_mismatch` in the payout blockers: drafts, approvals and files) until **another person** clears it (`clear_payee_name_mismatch`, four eyes, a reason), or a new payout account is confirmed under M2c-2's dual control (since the review's round 2, S1: only one with another IBAN — the check follows the IBAN, see below).
- **Nightly alerts** (§15): `transfer_not_filed` (an ordered payout, refund or sweep more than one business day old), `file_not_downloaded` (generated more than one business day ago), `file_not_marked_sent` (downloaded, not marked once its first execution day's cut-off has passed — checked by the nightly run, so it fires the next night), `transfer_not_debited` (in a downloaded or sent file, no debit seen more than two business days after its execution date), `transfer_file_failed`, `payee_name_mismatch`. I21 keeps running over approved and sent runs (M2c-4).
- **Lock order** (ADR-0014): run rows (id order) → allocation lock → remit lock → file rows → transfer rows; every writer of a transfer's or a file's status holds the remit lock (generation, download, « transmis », cancellations, the refund trigger, the failed job). The job holds only its file row while it writes (the failure path rolls back its savepoint before taking the locks).
- **Reads**: `public.transfer_overview()` (per paying account: the cash position, the transfers to file with why each would be held today, the sweep a file would carry, the last 20 files; the open payee checks), `public.transfer_file_detail(file, after_seq, limit)` (header, cash check and held at generation, downloads, items a page at a time). Pages `/backoffice/reversements/virements` and `/[id]` (« Générer le fichier » with an effect sheet, « Télécharger », the second time past the warning, « Marquer comme transmis », « Annuler le fichier », « Nom non concordant », the pain version); the run page names its file and asks the attestation after download; the refund sheet asks how it is executed.
- **Plan robustness** (ARCHITECTURE §4): keyed probes for our debits (`bank_transaction (bank_account_id, end_to_end_id)` partial index on debits; PmtInfId by `(bank_account_id, payment_info_id)`), laterals with `OFFSET 0` for the files' status, `enable_seqscan = off` in the cash position, the overview and the checks. Measured at 5,000 transfers with their statistics forgotten (`docs/benchmarks/remittances.md`).
- **Left for M2c-6b**: booking the debits from the statement (§12: payout + settlement + booking-time cover, batch debits by PmtInfId, the sweep's debit, returned payouts and charges on return, unplanned payouts, `transfer_booked_once` I20), the top-up booking from its file, the statement's « Suivi », I9/I19 with payouts, the §7 example end to end with synthetic camt.053. The hooks are in place: transfer states and ids, `transfer_file_item.pmt_inf_id`, `bank_transaction.payment_info_id`, the debit lookup index, `private.transfer_debit_seen`.

## M2c-6a review fixes (2026-11-11)
Confirmed findings of the five-lens review (pain.001, money, security, concurrency and performance, tests and UI; 28 findings), fixed by two branches (database and worker; pages and docs) that follow one contract (T1–T8), then integrated. The migration `20261115090000_transfers_files.sql`, not yet applied in production, is edited in place; nothing in this slice posts a ledger entry (booking debits is M2c-6b).
- **T1 — a downloaded file is re-issued only on evidence and by four eyes** (money#1 high, security#1, money#2, pain001#1; off until M2c-6b (ADR-0014 M2c-6a round 5; OQ-81): `bank_booking_required`). `cancel_transfer_file` re-queued a downloaded or sent file's payouts and sweep on one person's attestation alone, the same day, before any statement could show a debit: a colleague's upload and the regenerated file both executed (a double payout, or a double sweep). A downloaded or sent file is now cancelled in **two steps**: `public.request_transfer_file_cancellation(key, file, version, reason, attestation)` by one admin or ops manager at aal2, then `public.confirm_transfer_file_cancellation(key, file, version)` by **a different one** at aal2 (`same_person`), each with the **statements' evidence** (`private.transfer_cancel_evidence`, re-checked at the confirmation): every business day from the file's first requested execution date to the business day after its last is in an imported statement of the paying account (`private.statement_covers`; `no_statement_evidence` — the execution day alone is not enough: the debit may be booked the next business day), no debit carries one of its PmtInfIds, nor one of its end-to-end ids unless the bank returned that transfer, and none of its transfers is booked (`debit_seen`). Requests are kept in `public.transfer_cancellation_request` (RLS; four eyes as a constraint; one open request per file version, `already_requested`; a download after the request makes it stale — the confirmation then answers `not_requested` and a new request may be made; `version_changed`, `attestation_required`). On confirmation the file is superseded (`not_uploaded`) or rejected (`rejected_by_bank`): a transfer the bank debited then returned is cancelled (never re-issued under the same end-to-end id), the others go back « à mettre dans un fichier » and the sweep is recomputed. `cancel_transfer_file` keeps only the file not downloaded (`cancellation_request_required` after download). **One transfer** the bank refused inside an executed file (a refund or a sweep had no exit at all; pain001#1) is cancelled the same way, `public.request_transfer_cancellation(key, transfer, reason)` / `public.confirm_transfer_cancellation(key, transfer)` (`transfer refused: …`, `not_in_downloaded_file`), its evidence being that transfer's over its execution day and the next business day: no debit of its end-to-end id unless returned; a batch debit of its PmtInf (no end-to-end id) counts only when its amount is exactly the sum of the PmtInf's other transfers neither cancelled nor debited on their own (it then left this one out), any other is `debit_seen` (two refused transfers of one batch-booked PmtInf: OQ-80). The rest of the file stays; a downloaded file holding a cancelled transfer is never served again (`holds_cancelled_transfer`; « Marquer comme transmis » stays possible: the executed file was uploaded); a refund is then cancelled (`cancel_refund`, refused before: `refund refused: in_downloaded_file`), a sweep recomputed at the next file. **A run** whose payout is in a downloaded file is cancelled only once that transfer is (`payout_in_downloaded_file`; money#2: the run's cancellation used to leave its RMT in a live, re-downloadable file the cash check no longer counted) — `cancel_remittance_run` is back to M2c-5b's four arguments, with no attestation. Pages: the file's page shows what the statements prove (« Relevés importés jusqu'au … : aucun débit de ce fichier », or what to import), who asked and when, « Confirmer l'annulation » to anyone else and « une autre personne doit confirmer » to the requester; each transfer of an executed file has « Virement refusé par la banque ? »; the run page links to the file instead of asking an attestation. The window is OQ-80.
- **T2 — the generation's checks are re-run at download** (pain001#0, money#0, concurrency-perf#0, tests-ui#1, security#0). A generated file could be downloaded days later — its date passed (R124-6's late check skipped, no item marked late), a reversal since leaving a payout uncovered, an IBAN retired or a payee name mismatch recorded since — and the runs moved to `sent`. The first download of a `generated` file now re-runs, under the generation's locks (the file's runs, the paying account's row `FOR SHARE`, the allocation then remit locks), the date rule (the requested date against the paying account's next execution day now, its cut-off), every payout's and refund's hold reason (the payout blockers, a payee check, the payout account changed or retired, the per-client cap, T3's reasons) and the cash check against the file's CtrlSum; a file that fails is **superseded and not served**, the command returning — not raising, so the supersession stays — `{refused: 'file_stale' | 'file_blocked', blocked: [{transfer_id, reason}], …}` (the cash check as a reason with no transfer id), and the next generation takes its transfers again. The web route calls the command first; a refusal (and every other one: a second download without the warning, the file being written, a hash mismatch) sends the browser back to the file's page (303) with the reasons and « Régénérer le fichier ». « Virements » shows a generated file whose date passed as « Date d'exécution dépassée — à régénérer » (no « Télécharger »), and « Générer » replaces it there (« Régénérer le fichier » with its effects).
- **T3 — what a SEPA file cannot carry is held out, not failing the file** (pain001#4, concurrency-perf#1, pain001#2). A payee name with no EPC basic Latin character once transliterated (Cyrillic, Greek, Chinese…) raised `Pain001Error` in the job, failed the whole file and came back at every generation (a poison transfer blocking every payout of the account); `private.transfer_hold_reason` now holds it out (`payee_name_not_epc`, `private.epc_name_empty`, the SQL twin of `pain001.epc_text(…) == ''`, with a parity test). A creditor IBAN outside the SEPA schemes' countries (TN, TR, BR, AE… passed `iban_valid`) went into an SCT file the bank rejects; the countries are kept as data with their source (EPC409-09 v8.0 of 24/12/2025, `private.sepa_scheme_country` and `private.iban_in_sepa`; the writer's `SEPA_COUNTRIES`, which `render` and `check` enforce too), and such an IBAN is held out (`iban_not_sepa`; for a payout, after the per-client cap). A refund to such an IBAN or name defaults to `manual`; an explicit `file` is refused (`refund refused: iban_not_sepa`, `refund refused: payee_name_not_epc`). The nightly checks raise both as alerts, one per ordered transfer (subject the transfer) and at once; both have French reasons on the pages, in « Contrôles » and in the alerts (OQ-79: the list to check against the EPC's PDF, the FR-prefixed territories outside SEPA, the non-EEA countries' address).
- **T4 — the bucket is read only after the download command** (money#3, security#2). The storage policy let money staff read any file's bytes directly — superseded, rejected or failed ones (re-filed under a new MsgId: uploading one pays twice), and live ones with no recorded download or second-download warning. The bucket's one policy (`private.can_read_transfer_file_object`) now opens a file's object only to the money-staff member at aal2 who has a `transfer_file_download` row for it from the last 60 seconds, and only while the file is `downloaded` or `sent`: a superseded, rejected or failed file is never readable, and the download log cannot be skipped. The route calls `transfer_file_download` first (its checks, the download recorded), then reads the bytes with the user's session and serves them only if their SHA-256 is the one the job recorded; a read that fails after the download was recorded says so (« le téléchargement est enregistré »). Deviation from the contract's « no storage policy, a signed URL from the command »: SQL cannot mint a Storage signed URL and the service role never reaches `apps/web` (ARCHITECTURE §2, §13), so the narrow policy stands in for it (integration: the web branch's service-role read, `transfer-file-bytes.ts`, was dropped for it).
- **T5 — the payee check's four eyes exclude the flagged IBAN's parties** (security#3, tests-ui#7). `clear_payee_name_mismatch` now refuses (`same_person`) who recorded the mismatch and who proposed or confirmed the flagged payout account; the overview gives `can_clear` and the page hides « Nom vérifié » from them. A check on a payout account retired since (a replacement confirmed) closes itself: no nightly alert nor « bloqués » banner for an IBAN no longer used.
- **T6 — the alerts in time** (concurrency-perf#2, tests-ui#5, tests-ui#10). `file_not_marked_sent` is raised from the account's cut-off on the execution day (`private.transfer_file_cutoff_at`: that day at the cut-off, 00:00 without one); `private.transfer_checks_due(org, now)` is true once such a cut-off has passed or a file is still pending 15 minutes after its generation with no check run since, and the hourly `private.queue_remittance_schedule` (redefined) then queues the payments `invariants` job, so « Contrôles »' latest run stays complete (it used to fire only the night after, the execution day lost); `transfer_file_pending` flags such a file (a dead-lettered job is tested through `remittances.record_dead_job`: its file failed, its transfers back); `file_not_downloaded` is tested and 028's `count(*) >= 0` replaced by an assertion on `remittance_payout_not_executed`. French labels and links in « Contrôles ».
- **T7 — file numbers never truncate** (concurrency-perf#3): past 999,999 `lpad(…, 6)` cut the number and duplicated the MsgId; the width grows (`greatest(6, length(…))`, as the receipts' numbers).
- **The cash check and batch debits** (pain001#3): `private.transfer_debit_seen` counted every transfer of a PmtInf as debited once any debit carried that PmtInfId (blocking the not-executed exit of the one the bank refused, silencing `transfer_not_debited`, overstating the cash in flight); a batch debit with no end-to-end id now explains a PmtInf's transfers only when its amount equals the sum of those neither cancelled nor debited on their own (`private.pmt_inf_batch_seen`, design §12's rule); the cash position and the alerts read the transfers in flight in one pass with one test per PmtInf (`private.transfers_in_flight`).
- **Tests the review asked for** (tests-ui#0, tests-ui#2, tests-ui#3, tests-ui#4, tests-ui#6). The review's cases are in the new pgTAP `029_transfer_files_review` (96 tests; 028 keeps the slice's own, rewritten for T1, 116): 42501 for 12 commands and reads — `mark_transfer_file_sent`, `cancel_transfer_file` (generated and downloaded), `clear_payee_name_mismatch`, the four cancellation commands… — each called as a collector, a client admin, another servicer's ops manager and an ops manager at aal1, and the RLS of `transfer_cancellation_request`; a confirmed replacement retiring the frozen IBAN (`payout_account_changed`, held at generation); the per-client cap counting the client's other runs in flight (a second live run set up by dropping `remittance_run_pending_uq` in the test's transaction, OQ-73); a later statement with no closing balance carrying a 5 000 € debit (`debits_since_minor` 500000, the file blocked at download, generation refused with `cash_not_covered`). pytest `test_pain001.py`: `test_each_check_catches_its_tamper` (one tamper per check, each with its own message: SvcLvl, both IBANs, a non-SEPA creditor, Nm > 70, Ustrd > 140 and its charset, BIC/BICFI per version, a bad BIC, NOTPROVIDED, ReqdExctnDt (.09 `Dt`) and CreDtTm, InitgPty and Dbtr names, the MsgId, PmtInfId, InstrId and EndToEndId ids, the PmtInf CtrlSum, a PmtInfId twice, a 0.00 amount, a foreign namespace, a repeated element, the XML declaration), `test_remittance_info_is_cut_at_140_characters` and the writer's pins; integration `test_transfer_files_parity_integration.py` (the EPC test's SQL twin on curated names and by Hypothesis, the SEPA lists). Each fix was shown by a mutant its test kills (34 SQL, 36 pain001). The XSD's « vérifié / non vérifié » assertions follow whether the schemas are vendored (`test_a_file_of_two_payouts_written_by_the_job` asserts `xsd_validated is pain001.xsd_available(…)`; `docs/reference/iso20022/README.md`).
- **The refund's execution** (tests-ui#8): the sheet sent `execution_mode = 'file'` whatever the payment's account, so `request_refund`'s default (by hand when the account cannot pay a file) was unreachable and a non-EUR or closed account's refund was refused; it now defaults to « Dans le prochain fichier si le compte le permet, sinon à exécuter dans la banque » and sends the mode only when ops choose one. The payment's page then says which the database chose (integration: its banner told ops to « exécutez le virement dans la banque » for every pending refund, one in the file included — paid twice, risk R4; now `pendingRefundInstruction`, « ne l'exécutez pas dans la banque » for a refund in the file; vitest `debits.test.ts`, E2E `payments-debits`).
- **The download link** (tests-ui#9): « Télécharger » was a plain link to an attachment, so the page stayed stale (no warning, no « Marquer comme transmis ») and a second tap landed on a bare `text/plain` 409; the link now refreshes the page after the download, and every refusal is a 303 to the file's page (the warning sheet open for a second download), its `Location` a path the browser resolves against its own origin (integration: built from `request.url` it named `localhost`, the host `next start` binds, and the browser, on another origin, lost its session). The two probes (`private.transfer_own_debit_seen`, `private.transfer_return_seen`) now hold only the end-to-end id, in a subquery that cannot be pulled up, and check the account, direction and kind on the lines found; their indexes lead with the id and are no longer partial on the direction or kind (`bank_transaction_end_to_end_idx`, `bank_transaction_return_e2e_idx`), so no other index can serve them (ARCHITECTURE §4). The scale test asserts what the cash check reads (`pg_stat_xact_user_tables`: at most one line per transfer; it read 12,502,500 before, 5,000 after, in three cold runs).

- **Round 5 — fail-closed** (founder-level decision, already announced to the founder; pgTAP `033_transfer_files_fail_closed`, 26 tests, plus one in `030`, 72; 12 SQL mutants — the five gates, `switch_on` answering true, the two guards and the two reads killed by `033`, the two payee mutants by `030` — and 2 of the reader, each killed):
  - **Why.** Four review rounds kept finding ways a transfer cancelled out of a file the bank already has could be paid late and then paid again — round 4's verifiers still found three (below). Bank statements alone can never prove that a transfer will not be executed later: a cancellation on the statements' evidence is a bet on the bank's timing, and each fix narrowed the bet without closing it. So M2c-6a fails closed: **once a file is downloaded, nothing in it is cancelled, re-issued or re-queued until M2c-6b books its debits from the statements.** Slower money, never double money.
  - **What is off.** `private.feature_switch` (`key`, `enabled` default false, `note`; RLS on, nothing granted to `anon` or `authenticated`, change-logged), seeded by the migration itself with `downloaded_file_cancellation` off (production needs the row, not `seed.sql`); `private.switch_on(key)` (stable, definer, false for an unknown key; executable by the worker only). No public function writes it: M2c-6b's migration switches it on. While it is off, `request_transfer_file_cancellation`, `confirm_transfer_file_cancellation`, `request_transfer_cancellation` and `confirm_transfer_cancellation` refuse `bank_booking_required` right after the permission check and the idempotency replay (a French hint: keep the file as it is, check the statement, contact the bank) — a request opened while it was on is never confirmed —, and `cancel_transfer_file` refuses a downloaded or sent file `bank_booking_required` (in place of `cancellation_request_required`). In depth, `private.transfer_file_guard` refuses closing a downloaded or sent file and `private.bank_transfer_guard` refuses taking a transfer of a file downloaded at least once out of it (to `ordered` or `cancelled`; `booked` by its debit stays), whoever writes them — `private.transfer_file_release`, the only re-issue and re-queue, included. The audit of every path that can move a payout, refund or sweep of a downloaded or sent file out of `in_file`, change such a file's status or put its item back in a queue is the migration's « Round 5: fail-closed » header: each is refused for such a file or reachable only through the five gated commands (`cancel_remittance_run` → `payout_in_downloaded_file`; `cancel_refund`, a payment's full return and the M2b links → `private.refund_transfer_follow`, `in_downloaded_file`; the payee checks, generation, download, « transmis », the checks and the worker's jobs move no such transfer).
  - **What stays live.** Everything before download (a pending or generated file is superseded, its transfers back to « à mettre dans un fichier »; a run whose payout is not in a downloaded file is cancelled as before); generation and its checks; the download and its re-checks (`file_stale`, `file_blocked`, `holds_cancelled_transfer`, `holds_debited_transfer`); « Marquer comme transmis »; the payee check; a refund booked by its own debit (M2b's link); the alerts. The rounds 1–4 machinery stays in the code and is still tested: pgTAP `028`–`032` switch it on in their own transaction.
  - **The pages.** `transfer_file_detail` and `transfer_overview` give `cancellation_after_download`; while it is false they read no cancellation card (no evidence computed) and the file's page hides « Demander l'annulation », « Confirmer l'annulation » and « Virement refusé par la banque » and says: « Un fichier téléchargé ne peut pas encore être annulé dans Collectoo : ses virements restent « en cours » jusqu'à ce que leurs débits soient lus sur le relevé bancaire… » (E2E `remittances`, screenshot `m2c-virement-telecharge`). `bank_booking_required` has its French words; every refusal, hint and alert help that sent ops to a cancellation after download (`cancellation_request_required`, `file_not_marked_sent`, the payee-mismatch sheet, `payout_in_downloaded_file`, `in_downloaded_file`, `reissue_in_downloaded_file`, `holds_cancelled_transfer`, `file_not_executed`, the run's page…) now says what to do now — keep the file, check the statement, contact the bank —, the SQL hints by the switch, the pages' texts written for it off (M2c-6b rewords them when it switches it on). vitest `transfers.test.ts` sweeps them.
  - **Prerequisites to switching it on (M2c-6b), with round 4's verifiers' remaining fixes.** (1) **G2, the batch-line variant** (high): a predecessor file's batch line linked to a refund while its re-issue sits in a downloaded file books the re-issue there — refunded twice; `private.refund_transfer_follow` must accept `executed` for a refund whose transfer is in a downloaded or sent file only by that transfer's own end-to-end id, or by a batch line (no end-to-end id) whose `payment_info_id` is that transfer's PmtInf **in its current file** (`transfer_file_item.pmt_inf_id`), anything else `reissue_in_downloaded_file`; M2c-6b's booking of a payout by an old RMT id the same — **met for refunds in round 6** (below). (2) **SW2/SW3** (medium): a sweep in a generated or downloaded file when a sweep cancelled **before it was created** is debited late — the servicer's share leaves twice; the generated file is superseded at its first download (a blocked row `cancelled_sweep_debited`), a downloaded one refused at a re-download (`holds_debited_transfer`), and such an in-file sweep alerted (`transfer_already_debited`, kind sweep, status in_file), comparing the cancelled sweep's `cancelled_at` with the new sweep's `created_at` — pgTAP `034` (todo) since round 6. (3) **G1c** (medium): a refused transfer executed late as a batch line after its run or refund was cancelled — the client paid again through a new run, no alert; M2c-6b's `cancelled_transfer_debited` must cover batch lines that can contain a cancelled transfer (`private.transfer_debited_before`'s rule), not only RMT and RFD ids, and the G1 alert must not be keyed on live runs and refunds — pgTAP `034` (todo) since round 6. **Switching it on is done when `034` passes with its `todo()` lines removed** (round 6).

The G3 reader regression: without FrToDt, a PRCD dated on the closing day gave a period starting the day after the closing; a period never starts after the closing balance's date (that day alone, shown whole on no day: OQ-80 (f)'s default; pytest `test_camt053.py`, two mutants killed). Round 4's verifier nit (c): the refusals, hints and alert name « une ligne groupée de son lot ».
  - **Consequence** (COMPLIANCE OQ-81, founder to confirm): a payout the bank refuses, or a file never uploaded, stays « en cours » until M2c-6b — a client's remittance may then pass R124-6 al. 2's month; default: accepted, no live payouts before M2c-6b. And (OQ-81 (b)) `cancel_refund` refused once the refund's transfer was debited (pgTAP `015` #144, a change from M2b): kept, an exit such as a four-eyes link decided in M2c-6b.
  - **Docs**: design §9.7 (the switch), COMPLIANCE SEPA-01, OQ-80 (f), (n) and its round-5 paragraph, new OQ-81; DOMAIN; ROADMAP M2c-6b (« switch on cancellation after download » and its prerequisites).
- **Round 6 — round 5's verifiers' remaining items** (pgTAP `033` gains 11 tests, 37, 11 of which fail on round 5's code; new `034_transfer_files_switch_on_prerequisites`, 15 tests of which 6 `todo()`; vitest +6; 14 SQL mutants, 11 killed and 3 shown equivalent; each changed web source put back alone fails the new vitest cases — the runs are not kept in the repository):
  - **The run guard, in depth.** `private.remittance_run_guard` refuses an approved or sent run going to `cancelled` while its payout is `in_file` in a file downloaded at least once and the switch is off, whoever writes it: a direct `update` as the owner or as `service_role` (the worker's role, which can write runs) is refused, as `cancel_remittance_run` already refused (`payout_in_downloaded_file`). Alone it paid nobody twice (no function re-queues a cancelled run's lines), but with the worker's access to `private.ledger_post` it was one forged write away. Mutants: guard removed, `approved` only (killed by `033`); without the download condition, or whatever the switch (equivalent: every legitimate path — `cancel_remittance_run` before download or with the switch on — takes the payout out of `in_file` before the run is cancelled).
  - **No re-download of an executed file** (round 5's verifier, `p_redl`). `transfer_file_download`'s downloaded/sent branch refuses a new download with **`file_executed`** (« La banque a déjà exécuté ce fichier, en tout ou partie : ne le déposez plus ») when `private.transfer_file_executed(f.id)` — a debit of one of its PmtInfIds or of its transfers' end-to-end ids, or a return of one of them — or one of its payouts, refunds or sweeps has its own debit seen (`private.transfer_debit_seen`: its id, or a batch line of its PmtInf); acknowledged or not, **whatever the switch**. Before, a file executed in full was served again past the « ne le déposez pas deux fois » warning, sent or not: uploaded again it paid everything twice (unless the bank refused the duplicate MsgId). The web maps it (`DownloadRefusal`, `REFUSALS`, `refusalText`, `transferErrorCode` → `transfer_file_executed`, French words).
