## M2c-6b-1: bookings core — our payouts' and sweeps' debits booked from the statement (plan docs/design/m2c-6b-plan.md §1.2, §2.1–§2.5, §4; design §5, §7, §12, §13, §15)

Migration `20261116090000_debit_bookings.sql` (forward-only; it redefines what it changes), pgTAP `035`, worker
`decide_bookings` and the debit job's funds pass, `synth camt053 --debits-of`. The cancellation after download stays
**off** (`downloaded_file_cancellation`); it is 6b-3's. Decisions:

- **What the job books by itself** (plan §2.3): a debit carrying a payout's RMT id or the sweep's SWP id, of the
  transfer's paying account and amount, whose transfer is `in_file` in a file downloaded or sent (or its batch line:
  no end-to-end id, the PmtInfId of the transfer in its current file, Σ of the PmtInf's `in_file` members = the line,
  one kind, no cancelled member); its return (a credit with the RMT/SWP id as original id, line ≤ amount: the booked
  entry reversed in full, the difference a `bank_fee` booked on the line, the payout account `returned`, one
  `payout_returned` item of the payout's amount back in `remittance_pending`); each booked payout's run settlement
  (`private.post_run_settlements`, the set twin of `post_run_settlement`); a cover advance (`client_advance`, cause
  `payout_overrun`) when the remittance would put the client's 4670 in debit (I13). Batch lines stay `batch_unsplit` /
  `other_debit` as the import read them; the PmtInf decides.
- **Never automatically** (P0 reviews, alerts): a debit of a cancelled transfer (`cancelled_transfer_debited`), a second
  debit of a booked one (`transfer_debited_twice`), a transfer never handed out (`transfer_not_handed_out`), an RMT/SWP
  id or a PmtInf we do not know (`transfer_unknown`); and to ops with why: `transfer_differs`, `run_not_in_flight`,
  `batch_partial`, `batch_mixed`, `return_differs`, `return_before_debit` (a return whose debit is not booked yet — the
  same chunk's included: it is reviewed so and booked by the job's next run, at the next import — or dated before its
  debit, never booked; review legal-texts#3, T4/K5). Our RMT/SWP debits, our batch lines and their returns are never
  linked to a payment or a refund nor explained (`own_transfer_line` since the review, money-1/K1; `not_explainable`
  before) and are never fees (`not_a_fee`). 6b-2 adds ops' `book_transfer_line`.
- **One PmtInf per kind** (plan §2.1): `generate_transfer_file` groups payouts, refunds, then the sweep, so a batch line
  is one kind. A PmtInf holding one refund alone is that refund's debit, linked by the M2b pass (`debit_candidates`).
- **The funds pass runs in its own transaction** (plan §2.5 [critic]): the debit job's first message runs the M2b pass
  and queues `{"funds_after": null}`; the funds pass takes runs FOR UPDATE → payout accounts → bank accounts → the
  allocation lock → lines → the remit lock → files → transfers, so it never deadlocks with a run's cancellation or a
  file's download (integration test on two connections). The import queues the job for a batch line naming a PmtInf.
- **Signed checks**: I19 `bank_cash_identity` sums the bookings' and links' 5120 postings; `bank_line_booking_check`
  checks a line against its signed movement once its last booking is in; I20 `transfer_booked_once` (a booked payout,
  sweep or top-up has exactly one debit booking, a returned one one return; a booked run its transfer); new alerts
  (`payout_returned`, `sweep_returned`, `payout_overrun`, `bank_line_unbooked`, `servicer_funds_unswept`,
  `top_up_pending`, the P0 ones). The accounting export names the debits' documents (the end-to-end id, the bank's
  reference, the advance's cause) and reads them by key under `enable_seqscan = off`.
- **R124-6** (Q7's default, OQ-36): a returned payout's item keeps the R124-6 date of the run line it came from (the
  returned run's positive, live, dated line with the earliest latest execution date), in the queue and — since the
  review (legal-texts#1, money-2) — in the next run's line, its approval's late reason and its breach rows; a breach of
  it is recorded `blocked_reason = 'payout_returned'`. An in-flight line is proven unpaid, and its breach row written,
  only when its transfer never left (never handed out — still ordered or in a file never downloaded — or the paying
  account's statements cover its latest execution date without its debit, nor — since the review, legal-texts#2 — an
  unbooked, unlinked line that could still be it); until then the alert only; a late debit writes the row at its
  booking (review legal-texts#5: this sentence said the opposite).

**Deviations from the plan, recorded:**
- **Round-7 SQL hints and 033 kept** (plan §4.2 rewords six SQL hints and updates 033's hint assertion): this slice must
  leave 033 and 034 as they are, so the SQL hints that say a payout's debit « ne peut pas encore être comptabilisé »
  keep their wording until 6b-3 (which inverts 033); the web texts are reworded now (« automatiquement à l'import quand
  la ligne porte sa référence RMT ou celle de son lot » since the review, legal-texts#3). The pages never show the
  hints' raw text. Founder question.
- **Tests changed and why** (each assertion kept unless named): 017 — an RMT debit can no longer be « explained »
  (`not_explainable`) nor booked as a fee (`not_a_fee`): plan §2.3; 031 — the N1 fixture's batch line split per
  PmtInf (one PmtInf per kind: payouts, refund, sweep), assertions unchanged; 026 — unchanged, the export now reads by
  key whatever the statistics (it failed once autovacuum had marked `remittance_run` empty); worker `test_funds_integration`
  — an unknown RMT id is `transfer_unknown`, and is refused « explained »; the M2c-4/5 integration tests' emulated payout
  booking (`book_payout`) now goes through the real path (file, download, a statement of its debit, the job), because I20
  flags a payout booked without its debit. 034's TODO 16 (G1c alert) passes now; its TODO markers stay (6b-3).

## M2c-6b-1 review fixes (2026-11-12)

Confirmed findings of the four-lens review (money, concurrency, legal texts, tests and scale; 17 findings), fixed by
three branches (database, worker, pages and docs) that follow one contract (K1–K6), then integrated. The migration
`20261116090000_debit_bookings.sql`, not merged yet, is edited in place; the cancellation after download stays **off**
and pgTAP `033`/`034` keep their assertions and TODO markers.

- **money-1 (high; K1) — our payouts' and sweeps' lines are booked, never linked.** `private.post_debit_links` refused
  only « explained » on them, so one ops manager could link our payouts' batch line as a payment's return (its payouts
  stuck `in_file`, the funds candidates and the P0 alerts gone), a payout's return as a refund come back (the client
  never paid again, every check clean), or a manual refund on our batch line. Every link kind — return (its loss
  included), refund, refund come back, explained — is now refused on a debit carrying our RMT/SWP id, a batch line of
  one of our PmtInfs, and a credit return carrying our RMT/SWP id (`own_transfer_line`, `check_violation`, a French
  hint: booked from the statement, automatically or by ops in 6b-2). The one link kept on our batch line: a refund
  whose transfer is in a file handed out (downloaded or sent), the refund's own trigger then admitting only its own
  PmtInf in that file — the M2b pass's single-refund batch link among them; never a manual refund. `debit_queue` returns
  each line's `payment_info_id` (dropped and created). Pages: `isOurTransferLine` (`lib/payments/debits.ts`, the
  database's reading), `offersPaymentLinks` false on such lines (no « Retour du paiement … », « Retour au-delà du
  paiement … », « Remboursement … », « Remboursement revenu … »), `explainable` false, `own_transfer_line` worded
  (vitest `debits.test.ts` « our payouts' and sweeps' lines are booked, never linked »). pgTAP `035`: « Retour du
  paiement » on our batch line, a manual refund on it, a return or a refund on an RMT debit, « Remboursement revenu »
  on the return of our RMT payout — each `own_transfer_line`. Contract deviation: K1's exception named
  `private.pmt_inf_single_refund`; the database's is « a refund whose transfer is in a file handed out », wider (ops may
  link one refund of a PmtInf of refunds) but bounded by the refund trigger's G2 rule (033's test of ops linking a refund
  to a batch line of its own two-refund PmtInf, and 034's `reissue_in_downloaded_file`, must stay). Integration: the
  page follows the database, not the contract's letter — on our batch lines (no end-to-end id, one of our PmtInfIds) it
  offers the refunds of the line's amount only (`offersOwnBatchRefunds`: « Remboursement … », as M2c-6a's page did for
  such a line), never a payment's return, its loss or an explanation; on our RMT/SWP debits and their returns, nothing
  (vitest « offers our batch line the refunds of its amount only »; mutants: the PmtInf test, the end-to-end test, the
  whole predicate — each killed). `own_transfer_line`'s words name that one link.
- **money-2 (medium) and legal-texts#1 (high; K2) — a returned payout re-proposed keeps its R124-6 date.** The
  prepare's facts gave a `payout_returned` item no encaissement date, so its draft line, the run header, the approval's
  late reason, `remittance_late_lines`, the in-flight check and the booking-time breach all saw a null date: once in a
  run the returned money left R124-6 tracking. `jobs/remittances.py` `load_facts` now resolves each such item by
  `private.pending_item_deadlines`' chain (reversal → reversed remittance → its transfer → its run → that run's positive,
  live, dated line with the earliest latest execution date: its E and its mandate terms), and `remittance/run.py`
  `prepare_run` dates the positive `payout_returned` line from it (never commissioned). The breach rows of such lines say
  `blocked_reason = 'payout_returned'` (« bloqué : virement revenu impayé ») at approval (`private.remittance_late_lines`
  redefined), at the booking (`private.bank_booking_post_rows`) and in flight (`private.run_remittance_runs_checks`).
  Tests: pytest `test_a_returned_payout_keeps_the_deadline_of_the_line_it_came_from`; integration
  `test_a_returned_payout_re_proposed_keeps_its_r124_6_date`, `test_a_returned_payout_s_breach_row_says_why_it_was_held`;
  pgTAP `035` (late_reason_required without a reason, the late approval and the `payout_returned` breach row with one;
  at the booking; in flight). Integration (the worker's K2 deviation): the re-proposed line has no mandate (no file, so
  no mandate's gross or netting), only the terms version it is held to; a payout returned a **second** time was then
  held by `private.pending_item_deadlines` to one month and left unmonitored (no J-5/J-1 alert, no waiting breach row).
  Its `payout_returned` branch now takes, for a line without a mandate, its terms version's delay and mandate, as the
  worker's `_held_to` does (pgTAP `035` « a payout returned twice »: the new item held exactly as the first, monitored;
  red before). Docs: COMPLIANCE CPCE-08, OQ-36 (the note for counsel kept), DOMAIN « Revenu impayé » and « Manquement au
  délai ».
- **concurrency-1 (medium) and T1 (medium) — the deadlock test stages the cycle it guards.** The build's test called a
  three-argument `cancel_remittance_run` that does not exist, swallowed the error and ran after the funds pass had
  booked everything. `test_the_funds_pass_and_a_command_holding_the_run_never_deadlock` (cancel, download): a statement
  with the RMT debits and a payer's return (so the M2b pass takes the allocation lock), its message taken off unrun; a
  third session holds the allocation lock; the job's first message queues on it; the other side (the four-argument
  cancellation, or an acknowledged re-download) locks the run and queues behind; only the expected refusals are caught
  by SQLSTATE and message. Mutant: the funds pass in the M2b pass's transaction — DeadlockDetected. The plan's
  `generate_transfer_file` and `request_refund` variants and 035's dblink lock-order item: deferred (recorded).
- **concurrency-2 (low) — the payments of late lines locked before the allocation lock.** A booking's breach row's
  foreign key took a key-share lock on its payment under the allocation lock, a cycle with `request_refund`,
  `link_debit`, `reverse_allocation` and `forward_payment` (which hold the payment FOR UPDATE and wait for that lock).
  `private.post_bank_bookings` now locks FOR KEY SHARE, in id order and before the allocation lock, the payments of the
  payout runs' lines that can be late at this debit (a superset of the breach rows'); lock order: runs → payout accounts
  → bank accounts → those payments → `payments:<org>` → lines → remit lock → files → transfers. pgTAP `035` checks that
  the set of payments the step selects (`pg_temp._bb_pay_locks`) covers the breach rows' (mutant: the whole step removed
  — killed). It reads that set only, not the lock: the verifier's two lock mutants survived it (95/95 each) — the `for
  key share` statement deleted with the set kept, and the lock moved after the allocation lock — so « killed » held for
  the whole step, not for the lock. No two-connection test (a request_refund or reverse_allocation waiting on the
  allocation lock against the funds pass booking a late debit): deferred, recorded; round 2 adds it and both lock
  mutants fail it (below).
- **legal-texts#2 (medium; K3) — no permanent breach row for a payout whose debit the job cannot book.** A CSV line
  without the end-to-end id, or a batch line short of one member, left a payout paid on time « proven unpaid » and an
  append-only breach row written. The in-flight proof now also needs no unbooked, unlinked debit line on the paying
  account, booked from the transfer's requested execution date to its latest execution date, that could hold it (its
  e2e id; a batch line naming its PmtInf in its current file, whatever the amount; a line with neither reference of
  exactly its amount) — `private.transfer_debit_may_be_seen`, keyed by (account, booking date); until then the alert
  only. The `remittance_payout_overdue` help says « … son débit n'est pas comptabilisé … » and where such a line waits
  (vitest). pgTAP `035`: a reference-less line or a batch line of its PmtInf keeps the alert only; a line of another
  amount is no evidence. Contract K3 kept the requested execution date as the lower bound (the verifier suggested the
  download date). COMPLIANCE CPCE-08, OQ-83.
- **legal-texts#3 (medium) — no text promises a « rejection » read from the statement.** The payee-mismatch sheet, the
  run's page and `run_payout_in_downloaded_file` said a payout stays « en cours » until « son débit, ou son rejet » is
  booked « automatiquement »: a payout the bank does not execute (refused, or not authorised after « Nom non
  concordant ») leaves no statement line, and a line without the RMT reference is not booked by itself. Those three now
  say its debit is booked « automatiquement à l'import quand la ligne porte sa référence RMT ou celle de son lot ; sinon
  la ligne attend dans « Débits et retours » sa comptabilisation par l'équipe, à venir », then its return if the
  payee's bank sends it back, and that a payout the bank does not execute « n'apparaît sur aucun relevé » and stays « en
  cours » until the cancellation after download is available; `run_already_sent`, the four credit-note texts,
  `DOWNLOADED_FILE_NOTE`, `transfer_bank_booking_required`, `transfer_cancellation_request_required` and the
  `file_not_marked_sent` alert carry the same qualifier (`PAYOUT_BOOKED_WHEN`, `FILE_BOOKED_WHEN`,
  `PAYOUT_NOT_EXECUTED`, `FILE_TRANSFER_NOT_EXECUTED` in `lib/boarding/forms.ts`; vitest `transfers.test.ts`
  « no text promises that a payout the bank does not execute is read from the statement », `credit-notes.test.ts`).
  COMPLIANCE SEPA-01 reworded (a return after execution is read and booked; a return before its debit goes to ops; a
  payout not executed leaves no line and stays « en cours » until 6b-3) and OQ-81 (6b-1 does not close (a)). The
  verifier's adjacent point — a return on the same statement as its debit is reviewed `return_before_debit` and booked
  at the job's next run, not by a follow-up pass — is corrected in the M2c-6b-1 body above. Not changed: the refund
  texts' « son débit, ou son rejet, soit lu sur le relevé » (M2c-6a round 6, outside this finding).
- **legal-texts#4 (low) — `top_up_pending` said who owes whom backwards.** It now says a top-up of the dedicated account
  from the own account was asked more than a business day ago, its credit not on the imported statements yet, and that
  it covers « ce que le cabinet doit au compte dédié (frais bancaires, avances) » (vitest pins « depuis le compte
  propre », « le cabinet doit », never « Le compte dédié doit »).
- **legal-texts#5 (low) — this ADR's in-flight sentence said the opposite of the code.** The M2c-6b-1 body's R124-6
  bullet now reads: proven unpaid, and its breach row written, only when the transfer never left; until then the alert

  counterparty IBAN — `client_transfer_in` from the client's payout IBAN, `own_transfer_in` from our own — and « À
  classer » offered « Paiement d'un débiteur relayé par le client / par le cabinet » on it: a debtor's file credited
  with money the debtor never paid, commission charged on it and remitted again, the run left booked with no
  `payout_returned` item (the verifier's `sql/l4.sql`: `{"status":"unmatched"}` on both shapes).

  ''`, the grants) refuses, after its `not_own_credit` check, a credit whose end-to-end id or original end-to-end id is
  `^(RMT|SWP)[0-9A-F]{12}$`, or which has no end-to-end id and names one of our files' PmtInfIds (`^TF-…`: a lot of ours
  coming back as one line), with « own credit release refused: own_transfer_line » (check_violation; its hint: one of
  our own transfers coming back, booked from the statement — automatically when the bank flags it as a return, otherwise
  by ops with M2c-6b-2's line booking — never a debtor's payment nor a top-up). pgTAP `035` test 120 (`sc_relay_own`: a
  client's credit carrying our RMT id — with the exact hint —, an own credit carrying our SWP id, a client's credit
  returning our RMT id and an own credit naming our PmtInfId are refused; an ordinary relay is still `unmatched` and
  makes one payment); mutants without the end-to-end arm, the original arm or the PmtInfId arm each fail it. Pages
  (`lib/payments/debits.ts`): `relayable` and `clientRelayable` are false on `isOurTransferCredit(row)` — a credit
  `isOurTransferLine` reads as ours (it already read a credit's own and original ids, either direction) or one naming
  our PmtInfId with no end-to-end id, exactly as the database reads it (integration, below); the refusal maps to its own

- **M2 (L4) — nor a top-up; the fee exception.** `private.post_bank_bookings`' `top_up` rule refuses our lines with
  `own_transfer_line` before `already_linked` and `not_an_own_credit` (the `loss` rule's order): own or original id
  `^(RMT|SWP)[0-9A-F]{12}$`, or no end-to-end id and one of our PmtInfIds (our batch line, or — integration — a credit
  naming it, as `release_own_credit` reads it): an `own_transfer_in` credit carrying our SWP id was booked as a top-up
  with no transfer, the sweep left booked and its return counted as the servicer's own money. This covers ops'
  `link_debit` `own_credit` (strict: « bank booking refused: own_transfer_line ») and the job's top-up row (skipped
  `own_transfer_line`, reviewed `changed`). pgTAP `035` test 121 (`sc_top_up_own`: an own credit carrying our SWP id as
  its own id, and as its original, refused by ops; the job's top-up row skipped `own_transfer_line`, nothing booked; an
  ordinary own credit still `own_credit`, one top-up of 5,000) and test 125 (`sc_top_up_own_pmt`, the integration's: an
  own credit naming our PmtInfId with no end-to-end id refused by ops and by the job; with an end-to-end id not ours
  still a top-up); mutants — the rule unguarded, or testing the own id only — fail 121; round 3's database branch's arm
  (our debit batch line only) fails 125, and one ignoring the end-to-end id errors it. Pages: « Approvisionnement par le
  compte propre » only when `offersTopUp(row)` (a credit from the own account that is not `isOurTransferCredit`); the
  refusal, « bank booking refused: own_transfer_line » as for the loss, is worded by the kind ops asked for
  (`linkDebitErrorCode`, the `linkDebit` action passing its kind: on `own_credit` the credit's words of M1, on `loss`
  the line's). **The fee rule tests the line's own end-to-end id, never its original id**, and keeps booking a bank
  charge whatever its original: it refuses a line whose own end-to-end id is our RMT/SWP id and our TF- batch line
  (`not_a_fee`), but not a debit `other_debit` whose original id names our payout or sweep. Recorded as an exception
  rather than closed, because such a line is a **bank charge of ours**: the bank's fee for handling our payout or its
  return (e.g. the payee's bank's charge on a payout it sent back, on a separate line), which names the transfer it
  charges for. Bank fees on the dedicated account are the servicer's cost (OQ-47's default, 6270; « Frais bancaires (à
  la charge du cabinet) »), and it is not money leaving for a payee: it moves no client's money and no transfer's
  status, and hides neither its debit nor its return (those lines carry the RMT/SWP id as their own id, or are the payee
  bank's credit, and stay refused). Refused, it would be a real charge nobody could book before M2c-6b-2 (an I9 gap).
  The debit job books the same line automatically by its charge code (CHRG/FEES) whatever its original id (`decide_line`
  tests only a debit's own end-to-end id), so ops' path agrees with the job's. pgTAP `035` test 122
  (`sc_fee_naming_ours`: `other_debit` lines whose original is our RMT or our SWP id booked as fees by ops and by the
  job, `bank_fees` postings) pins it; a mutant testing the original id too fails it.
- **M3 (P1, a regression of round 2's rewrite) — the re-check linear in time and memory.** Round 2's batch rule read
  each member once but grouped by the array of every transfer id the line holds: each of N rows carried an N-element
  array into the sort (392 MB of temporary files and 1.8 s per 5,000-member line, 882 MB at 7,500), and « one kind per
  line » and `transfer_twice` were n² semi-joins over the unanalysed `_bb` (about 5.7 s at 5,000 members together). Now:
  (1) a `MATERIALIZED` step `a` aggregates each line's members once, grouped by the line and its amount only (count, the
  flags, the in-file kinds and sum, `live_ids` ordered), and `w` compares `live_ids` with the line's ids one row of `a`
  to one row of `r` — no array in a group or sort key; (2) « one kind per line » is a join to a per-line aggregate
  (`count(distinct kind) > 1` and a payout, sweep or return kind among them: the same lines as the EXISTS); (3)
  `transfer_twice` is a window over the accepted rows (more earlier rows of the same transfer, debit or return, than
  earlier rows of the same transfer, debit or return, and line), and (4) `analyze pg_temp._bb` follows its CTAS (the
  verifier's two alternatives, both kept); (5) a quadratic the verifier did not list, found by the new probe: `_bb_keys`
  read a batch line's PmtInf items once per row of the line (N² rows into a `distinct`: 16 million rows and 98,070
  temporary blocks, ~770 MB, at 2,000 members) — now once per distinct line. Tests that fail on the quadratic:
  `worker/tests/test_debit_bookings_batch_rules_integration.py` (the `db` job; a 2,000-sweep batch line and the
  individual debit of its first member re-checked in one call, under auto_explain: the second line `transfer_twice`, no
  statement writing a temporary block, none handling more than 40 rows per job row + 2,000) — round 2's whole function
  fails it (`_bb_keys` 117,624 temporary blocks and 16 million rows, the batch rule 78,730 blocks, `transfer_twice` 8.0
  million rows, « one kind » 4.0 million), so do the build's (`_bb_keys`) and the single-statement mutants (the keys per
  row, round 2's batch rule, « one kind » as the EXISTS, `transfer_twice` as the EXISTS without the analyze); and the
  payout scale test: both batch passes assert `pg_stat_database`'s `temp_bytes` unchanged, and (b)'s 5,000-member pass
  runs a second time under auto_explain (the superuser's connection, the pass as `postgres`) asserting no spilled
  statement and each re-check statement within 40 rows per member + 50 (the plans' rows as `checks_work` counts them,
  `worker/tests/explain_helpers.py`). `ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 records the rules (no growing value in a group or sort key; a
  key read once per group; a temporary table analysed before it is joined to itself; temporary files bounded too).

  (x01, x03: a payout the bank had just debited, set `returned`). The parser stored a single-detail entry with
  NbOfTxs absent or 1 as a line of its own already, and an entry kept unsplit had a « sole consistent detail » only in
  name: so the simplest encoding is the parser's. `payments.camt053` gives a detail of ours a line of its own only when
  it is the whole entry (`_Reader.whole`: the entry's direction, its own Amt absent or the entry's; NbOfTxs absent or 1
  as before) and keeps the entry unsplit otherwise; a line kept unsplit takes its line ids from its one detail only
  when that detail is of the entry's direction, and its original id only from a detail of ours of that direction
  (`alike`), counting every detail of ours (`unsplit_ours`, so every refusal still sees it). The synthetic ground truth
  agrees (`Entry.adds_up`). Both twins then refuse every such line: `payments.debits._transfer_return` and

## M2c-6b-2a: foundations of ops' booking of our transfer lines (plan docs/design/m2c-6b-2-plan.md §2, §6, §7.1, §8, §9)

Migration `20261117090000_transfer_line_foundations.sql` (forward-only; it redefines what it changes, each function
copied from the migration named in its comment with its settings and grants restated), pgTAP `036`, the camt.053
parser's unsplit details and charges, the job's two new return rules and their worker twin, `unique_subset` and its
Python twin, and the page texts. No screen books a line yet (6b-2b's command, 6b-2c's pages); the cancellation after
download stays **off**; `033` and `034` are unchanged. The founder answered none of the plan's §10 questions: every
default below is built and each question stays open. Decisions:

- **The statement's own detail of an entry kept unsplit, kept on its line** (plan §2.1–§2.2; critic F8, L11; critic2
  ML-5, ML-6, ML-10, CSO2-8, CSO2-9). `bank_transaction` (and the stage) gain `unsplit_details` (the details of ours,
  `{id, direction, amount_minor}` in the file's order — the id as `_our_ids` reads it, own or original; the amount read
  as `split()` and `whole()` read it, `Amt` first, then `AmtDtls/TxAmt/Amt`, in the statement's currency, else null),
  `unsplit_detail_count` (every `TxDtls` of the entry, ours or not), `unsplit_batch_count` (`NbOfTxs`) and
  `charges_minor` (the charges the statement records for a line that is its entry's only line: `Ntry/Chrgs` and its one
  `TxDtls/Chrgs`, `Rcrd/Amt` from v04, each record a `DBIT` in the account's currency with `ChrgInclInd` absent or
  true; null when there are none or when one record cannot be read so — a record without `CdtDbtInd`, the entry's and
  the detail's totals disagreeing, or an entry of several details one of which records a charge; a v02 `Chrgs`, its
  `Amt` with no direction nor inclusion indicator, is never read: review fixes, M3). The worker stages them as `Jsonb` (`jobs.payments.stage_row`). `private.ingest_statement` refuses a malformed
  one `line_invalid` (`private.unsplit_details_valid`: exactly `unsplit_ours` details of ours, our id shape, `debit` or
  `credit`, the amount digits or null; the count at least `unsplit_ours`; `NbOfTxs` only beside details; a charge
  positive, on a camt.053 line only) and, on a re-import, refuses `entry_detail_differs` a known line whose stored
  details, counts or charges differ from the file's; a stored null (a line imported before this slice) is neither
  compared nor filled. A CSV line keeps none. What 6b-2b's booking of such an entry rests on: the bank's file, never one
  person's transcription.
- **A return the job never books** (plan §2.3; critic F1, L5; critic2 ML-3). In `private.post_bank_bookings`, right
  after `return_before_debit` and before `already_returned`: a return of a transfer that has an open unplanned booking
  (`unplanned_payout` / `unplanned_sweep` whose entry is not reversed, `private.transfer_unplanned_open`) is reviewed
  `unplanned_payout_return`; one whose second or late debit is on a statement and not booked
  (`private.transfer_late_lines`; never a line ops decided is a duplicate: review fixes, M1) `return_debit_pending`. `private.bank_booking_candidates` hands the worker the same two
  facts (`unplanned_open`, `debit_pending`), the twin (`payments.debits._transfer_return`) has the same rules at the same
  place, and the SQL re-check under the job's locks catches a fact that changed after the candidates were read.
  `private.apply_bank_bookings` reviews both under their own reason (not `changed`). Booked as the planned payout's
  return, such a copy would queue the client's item again — the client paid twice. Once the unplanned booking is reversed
  the next return is the planned payout's, as before.
- **A generated file's sweep re-checked at its first download** (plan §2.4; critic CSO-2, F10, CSO-10; critic2
  CSO2-4). `public.transfer_file_download` compares the file's `in_file` sweep with the servicer's share read under the
  remit lock it already holds (every writer of 4679 holds it), by `generate_transfer_file`'s own formula (−Σ 4679 of the
  servicer and currency, less the other sweeps ordered or in a file). A sweep above it is a blocked entry
  `{transfer_id, kind: 'sweep', reason: 'sweep_exceeds_share', sweep_minor, share_minor}`: the file is refused
  `file_blocked` and superseded, its sweep cancelled, its payouts ordered again with their dates, and the next file
  recomputes the sweep. A file still `pending` is never served (`not_ready`). « Virements »: the hold's label, and, when
  the sweep is the only blocked entry, a refusal text of its own (`refusalText(code, blocked)`): the payouts go back in
  at the regeneration and their deadline still runs.
- **`private.unique_subset`** (plan §2.5; critic2 CSO2-2, CSO2-11), for 6b-2b's lots: the 1-based indexes of the only
  subset summing to the target, or null (none, several, past a bound). A dynamic programme over partial sums with a count
  capped at 2 and the path for count 1, on the smaller side t' = min(t, Σ − t) (answering the complement), amounts above
  t' skipped, the items visited in the order given; bounds: more than `private.transfer_line_lot_cap()` (500) amounts →
  null at once, 10,000 partial sums, 200,000 stored path entries, 1,000,000 work (Σ over the items visited of the sums
  kept). Two representations, the same answer and the same trace (`private.unique_subset_trace`: where and which bound
  tripped): a bit string of the reachable sums when t'' (t' over the amounts' gcd) is below 2¹⁸ (262,144), sorted rows
  otherwise. Measured on 500 amounts (corrected by the review fixes, CS-2 and T7): the worst input of the bit
  representation (5–90 €, t' = 8,000) trips the work bound in 0.07–0.19 s; the worst of the row representation — its
  partial sums saturating just under the 10,000-sum bound, so that only the work bound or the last item stops it — runs
  1.8–2.5 s; that is the figure 6b-2b's command budget and lot cap read. The Python twin
  `payments.debits.unique_subset_trace` has the same bounds, order and trace. Execute revoked from `public`, `anon` and
  `authenticated` (with `private.transfer_line_lot_cap` and `private.own_transfer_line_hint`).
- **Alerts and reviews** (plan §2.6; critic L10, L14). New: `transfer_unknown` (P0) on every line the job reviewed so,
  debits and credits; `double_payout_open` on a `double_payout` advance, open = amount − settlements, none once its entry
  is reversed; `own_transfer_payment` (P0) on an unassigned payment made of a line carrying our RMT/SWP id (own or
  original) or naming one of our lots, after one business day — one of our transfers come back, on 4710 with no R124-6
  clock. Extended: `payout_returned` also on an unplanned payout's return (`unplanned_payout_returned`, keyed by the
  booking whose entry queued the item), the planned branch only for the transfer's own payout (so it is never counted
  twice); `sweep_returned` also on an `unplanned_sweep_returned`; `bank_line_unbooked` also counts an entry kept unsplit
  holding ours, a credit naming our lot, an own or client credit carrying our id and (review fixes, M2) the lines
  reviewed `unplanned_payout_return` or `return_debit_pending`, a held line read as the kind ops released it as. `bank_line_booking`'s kinds gain
  `unplanned_payout_returned` and `unplanned_sweep_returned` (6b-2b books them; the booking guard admits no row of them
  before 6b-2b defines their rule). `private.apply_debit_decisions` reviews a link refused on our own line
  `own_transfer_line` (OQ-84 (i)). The worker's `P0_REVIEWS` include `transfer_unknown`.
- **Texts** (plan §2.6; S23, Q13's default). `public.assign_payment`'s and `public.resolve_duplicate`'s hints and their
  page twins (`payment_own_transfer_line`, `duplicate_own_transfer_line`, `OUR_TRANSFER_PAYMENT_NOTE`) no longer promise
  a screen: Collectoo cannot book such a payment as that return yet (a recorded payment is never undone; M2c-7) — tell
  support; a held line stays in « Doublons possibles » (build check: « Libérer » cannot release it as a return —
  `resolve_duplicate` takes no such kind). The funds pass's own-line hint comes from one place,
  `private.own_transfer_line_hint('bank_booking')`, unchanged in wording (6b-2c rewords it with the screen). The review
  labels `unplanned_payout_return` and `return_debit_pending` say nothing is booked automatically and to tell support
  (the latter, since the review fixes, also to decide first a copy held in « Doublons possibles »), and
  `own_transfer_line` promises no screen (review fixes, T6).
- **CI** (plan §2.6; critic2 CSO2-5): the `db` job fails when a migration file the branch adds sorts at or before the
  latest on `origin/main` (`scripts/check-migration-order.sh`): production applies migrations in merge order and

## M2c-6b-2a review fixes (2026-11-17)

The review of 6b-2a (three lenses: money, concurrency and security, tests and texts; 14 findings, one medium, the rest
low) checked against the build; each finding below was confirmed on the stack. The migration
`20261117090000_transfer_line_foundations.sql`, not merged yet, is edited in place; the cancellation after download
stays **off**; `033`/`034` unchanged. No §10 question answered: each default stays open.

- **M1 (medium) — a debit decided a duplicate kept a return of ours waiting for good.** The job's new fact
  `debit_pending` is `private.transfer_late_lines`, which counted every unbooked, unlinked debit carrying the transfer's
  id — a CSV line held as a suspected duplicate of the booked debit too, even once ops decided it is a duplicate (a
  final decision: that line is never booked). The CSV safety net holds such a line on an ordinary overlapping export.
  Every return of the payout was then reviewed `return_debit_pending` on every pass: the client's returned money never
  owed nor paid again (before 6b-2a it was booked `payout_returned`). Fix: `private.transfer_late_lines` (redefined from
  20261116090000, settings and grants restated) never counts a line decided `duplicate` (`bank_duplicate_resolution`,
  by its key), in both its branches — so the candidates, the SQL re-check and the worker twin (which reads the
  candidates) stay in parity; 6b-1's P0 `cancelled_transfer_debited`, which reads the same function, no longer names
  such a line either (not exercised by a test here). A held line not decided yet still counts (it may
  be released as a second debit: the conservative side), and the `return_debit_pending` label now says to decide it
  first in « Doublons possibles ». `public.resolve_duplicate` queues the debit job (`process_debits`) when it decides a
  debit is a duplicate, as a release as a return already did, so the return is read again at once (without it, only
  the next import holding debits or returns queued the job; the label's « repris automatiquement » would not have been
  true). This restores 6b-1's booking of that return; it books nothing 6b-1 did not. Tests: pgTAP `036` B
  « (review M1) a debit held as a suspected duplicate keeps a return waiting … » (held: `return_debit_pending`; decided:
  the job queued, `1 payout_returned 82000`, the transfer `returned`, its item queued again; the other servicer's ops
  refused — user 05, unused before, CS-4); integration
  `test_a_return_waits_while_its_debit_is_held_as_a_duplicate_then_is_booked` (a real CSV export overlapping the
  camt.053 debit, held by the safety net, the return reviewed, ops' decision through the API's session, the queue
  drained: booked); vitest « return_debit_pending says a held copy is decided first … ». Each failed on `b0a1747`.
- **M2, T1 (low) — `bank_line_unbooked` missed a held line released by ops.** A released held line keeps the kind
  `suspected_duplicate` (its kind is the resolution's `released_kind`, as the job reads it); the check read the raw
  kind, and the build had dropped the plan's « reviewed `unplanned_payout_return` or `return_debit_pending` » clause as
  equivalent. Fix (`private.run_transfer_checks`): the kinds read as released (a keyed lateral on
  `bank_duplicate_resolution`) and the plan's clause restored; the deviation above is withdrawn. pgTAP `036` E
  « (review M2, T1) a held line released by ops is read as the kind it was released as … » (a return reviewed
  `return_debit_pending` or `transfer_unknown`, our debit, a client's credit carrying our id; failed on `b0a1747`).
- **M3 (low) — the v02 charges branch read a shape v02 does not give.** v02's `Chrgs` carries its `Amt` with no
  `CdtDbtInd` nor `ChrgInclInd` (as we read ChargesInformation6; no XSD vendored, `www.iso20022.org` refused), while the
  parser asked for a `CdtDbtInd` `DBIT` on it and the test fixture and the synthetic statements wrote one. Default (no
  direction invented): a `Chrgs` without `Rcrd` is seen and never read — `charges_minor` null, the conservative side
  (6b-2b refuses or holds such a fee). The fixture and `synth camt053` write v02's shape; the ISO-shape tests use v08
  (`--version 08`). Tests: `test_camt053_details.py::test_a_v02_charges_block_is_never_read` (failed on `b0a1747`),
  `test_synth_debits.py::test_a_debit_charge_in_the_iso_shape_is_kept_unsplit_with_its_charge[02]` (charge null) and
  `test_the_command_writes_the_new_shapes`. COMPLIANCE OQ-84 (j) and DOMAIN say so.
- **T6 (low) — the `own_transfer_line` review label promised « écran à venir ».** Reworded: « Collectoo ne peut pas
  encore la comptabiliser depuis cet écran : prévenez le support » (vitest « … promises no screen »).
- **T2–T5, CS-4 (low) — rules no test pinned; now each killed by a named `036` test.** T2: « (review T2) a return of a
  sweep with an open unplanned sweep booking is reviewed unplanned_payout_return … » (the `unplanned_sweep` arm). T3:
  `a_reimport`'s NC4 (a stored null charge neither compared nor filled; the import kept in a subtransaction, so a
  mutant fails the assertion, not the file) and « (T3) a CSV line staging a charge refuses the file line_invalid ». T4:
  « (review T4) an open unplanned booking comes before a pending debit, and before already_returned (S03r …) ». T5:
  `e_unplanned_returns`' `swept_again` (a newer sweep ordered ends the unplanned sweep's alert). CS-4: the privilege
  assertion covers `private.unsplit_details_valid`, `private.transfer_unplanned_open` and `private.transfer_late_lines`.
- **T7, CS-2, CS-3 (low) — texts.** The bit representation switches at t'' < 2¹⁸ (262,144), as the code does, not 2²³;
  the worst case is the row representation with its partial sums saturating just under the 10,000-sum bound — 500
  multiples of 10 € for 26,000.01 € runs all 500 items in 1.8–2.1 s, 500 multiples of 1 € for 9,999.99 € trips the
  work bound at item 151 in 1.8–2.5 s (this VM) — not the 1.4 s given; 500 lots of 10–4,000 € for 50,000 € run the
  row representation when their gcd is 1 (t'' = 5,000,000; a random such input trips the partial-sum bound at item 14
  in 0.1 s). Default: 6b-2b's scale run times the row-mode saturating input and sets the lot cap
  from it (2× headroom under the API's 8 s still holds at 2.5 s); no pgTAP timing of it (a 2 s assertion on CI hardware
  would be noise). `unsplit_detail_count`'s comment and the deviation above say what is true: the count never
  overflows, `unsplit_ours` (6b-1's `smallint`) still bounds an entry kept unsplit to 32,767 details of ours
  (COMPLIANCE OQ-85, known limit).
- **CS-1 (low) — recorded, not rewritten.** The two-connection tests beside the first download run the first command to
  its end before the second starts: they show the wait and each outcome, not the lock order; an inversion would pass.
  The reviewer's static reading finds today's orders consistent (the download: runs by id, the debtor account, then
  `payments:`, `remit:`, the file; the cancellation: its run, `payments:`, `remit:`, transfers, file; the funds pass: runs,
  accounts, payments, `payments:`, lines, `remit:`, files, transfers). The test and its docstring now say what it
  shows (renamed `test_the_download_and_a_regeneration_or_a_cancellation_one_waits_for_the_other`). Default: the
  interleaved test (the first connection holding only the run row the second needs, then calling the command; a mutant
  of `transfer_file_download` taking `payments:`/`remit:` before its runs must fail it with 40P01) is written with
  6b-2b, whose command adds its locks to this order (plan §3.8) and must be proven against it anyway.

**Mutants (SQL: one function redefined after `036`'s `begin`, through `psql` in one rolled-back transaction, the
no-op control 44 of 44; worker: a scratch copy of `worker/src` first on `PYTHONPATH`, its no-op control passing; web: the
build's labels).** Killed: `transfer_late_lines` without the duplicate exclusion, and with it widened to every held line
(B 30); `resolve_duplicate` queueing nothing (B 30, and the integration test with that definition committed, then
restored); `bank_line_unbooked`'s raw kind for a return, a transfer out, an own or client credit, and the build's version
(E 39); the `unplanned_sweep` arm dropped (B 32); the two rules swapped, and both after `already_returned` (B 31); the
newer-sweep clause dropped (E 38); a stored null charge compared (A 3); a CSV charge accepted (A 4); the three helpers
granted again (10); the v02 block read as a record (`test_a_v02_charges_block_is_never_read`); the build's three labels
(vitest, 3 failures). Equivalent, kept: the duplicate exclusion in `transfer_late_lines`' batch-line branch (only a CSV
line is ever held, and none carries a PmtInfId; kept so both branches read the same) and the restored plan clause
(every line the job reviews `unplanned_payout_return` or `return_debit_pending` is a return credit carrying our id, which
the released-kind clause counts; kept as the plan's membership).

## M2c-6b-2b: the ops command — ops book our transfer lines (plan docs/design/m2c-6b-2-plan.md §3, §6, §7.2, §8, §9)

Migration `20261117100000_transfer_line_ops.sql` (forward-only; every redefinition copied from the migration its comment
names, its settings and grants restated), pgTAP `037`, the worker's `_held_to` third branch, the parser's two « given »
flags (COMPLIANCE OQ-84 (j)), the pure twin of P, and the web's refusal and decision labels. **No page books a line in
this slice** (6b-2c): the command, its preview and its options are reachable by the API only;
`lib/payments/transfer-lines.ts` is imported by no page yet, but `lib/payments/debits.ts`'s `decisionLabel`, changed here,
is rendered by « Traités » (`app/backoffice/encaissements/debits/page.tsx`): the job's own bookings now read
« Débit d'un reversement », « Reversement revenu » and the other `DECISION_LABEL` texts (review LT-8). The cancellation after download stays **off**; `033` and `034` are unchanged. The founder
answered none of the plan's §10 questions: each default is built and stays open. Decisions:

- **One command, three reads** (plan §3.2, §3.9, §3.11). `public.book_transfer_line(p_idempotency_key, p_bank_transaction_id,
  p_parts, p_expected_text, p_reason)` (`security definer`, `search_path = ''`, `lock_timeout = '2s'`; executable by
  `authenticated`, the role checked inside: admin or ops manager of the line's servicer). Its order: the role; the
  command key's advisory lock under 7 s (a second call with the same key waits beyond the command's 2 s and replays the
  first result: critic2 CSO2-6); `private.command_replay`; the motif (1–2,000 characters); the parts' shape
  (`private.transfer_line_parse`: kinds, amounts ≤ 10¹⁵, no transfer twice, at most one fee, at most one part without
  a transfer); the expected text; the tenant filter (`private.transfer_line_tenant`: any id of another servicer, or none,
  is `transfer_unknown` / `client_unknown`, the same code whatever the id names: critic CSO-5); the pre-read of the
  line's lot (`private.transfer_line_pre`, `lot_too_large` above `private.transfer_line_lot_cap()` before any subset);
  the locks (below); the check under the locks (`private.transfer_line_check(line, true)`); the compare-and-set of the
  expected text against the text the check builds now (`split_changed` when it moved); the posting
  (`private.transfer_line_post`; a ledger refusal → `posting_failed`, nothing kept); the drafts re-prepared; the funds
  pass queued when the line moved what it may net (`funds_after` null); `private.command_record`. `public.transfer_line_preview(line,
  parts)` runs the same check without the locks and returns `{ok, why, detail, parts, drafts, supersedes_file,
  expected_text}`; `public.transfer_line_options(line)` gives the line's class, its proposals (each with its request and
  its preview), the lot's members (at most 50 listed, `member_count` always) and the refusal when none can be proposed.
- **Line classes, read under the lock** (plan §3.3): U (an entry kept unsplit holding ours, booked only from the
  statement's own details), E (our end-to-end id on the line, of a transfer of the servicer: on another account it is
  `transfer_differs`, never a line without reference), B (the line names our lot: a debit with no end-to-end id by its
  `payment_info_id`, a PmtInf of a file of the line's account; a credit by `names_our_lot` when its ids name nothing of
  ours), E0 (an RMT/SWP-shaped id, or a TF PmtInfId, naming nothing of ours), N (neither an end-to-end id nor a
  PmtInfId: a CSV feed without the reference column; its counterparty IBAN, when given, is read by rule 3b), O
  (anything else: a foreign end-to-end id or PmtInfId). `private.transfer_line_class` (wording corrected, review
  LT-8).
- **Part kinds and their acceptance rules in the plan's order** (§3.4; the first failure is the refusal): `payout`,
  `sweep`, `unplanned_payout`, `unplanned_sweep`, `payout_returned`, `sweep_returned`, `unplanned_payout_returned`,
  `unplanned_sweep_returned`, `fee`. Rule 3b (`private.transfer_line_candidates`): a line without our reference is a
  transfer's only when that transfer is the only candidate of its amount to that IBAN among (i) live transfers handed
  out to the bank, (ii) refunds in a file, (iii) cancelled or returned payouts (ML-8: a returned payout is not a
  candidate while its return item is held by a live line of a run whose payout is a (i) candidate of this line — that
  run re-pays it to the same IBAN), its execution date not after the line, an IBAN required on class O; several →
  `line_ambiguous`. A client part (an unplanned payout to a client's registered payout IBAN with no transfer, Q8) is
  refused while a transfer of that amount to that IBAN is in flight (`payout_in_flight_matches`), cancelled or returned
  (`cancelled_payout_matches`), or not yet handed out (`payout_not_handed_out_matches`; critic F12, F13). A fee only on
  our transfer's own line (its debit, class E, or the ISO shape on U; its flagged return), equal to the statement's
  `Chrgs` when it records one, and, with none, never the amount of one of our transfers (`fee_unexplained`; critic L2,
  critic2 ML-6, ML-10).
- **The only subset** (§3.5): a lot line books exactly the members of the only subset of its lot (every member, whatever
  its status) that makes its amount (`private.unique_subset`, 6b-2a); several or none → `batch_ambiguous`; a lot
  holding refunds or transfers of several kinds → `batch_mixed`; a lot credit re-reads the lot's credit universe under the lock (`split_changed`).
- **P per item** (§3.6.1; Q4's default, COMPLIANCE OQ-82; critic F2–F5, L1; critic2 ML-1, ML-9). The pool of an
  unplanned payout of x: x cancelled → its run's released lines; x returned → its return item; otherwise none (P = 0).
  Eligible: the pool's items with a pending row, less the pool's own unplanned rows and their advances
  (`private.unplanned_own_item`), a reversal folded into the item it reverses (one level: a reversal is never
  reversed). net = pending + its reversal's pending, signed; paid = what unreversed unplanned bookings attributed
  (`private.unplanned_paid_item`) + what earlier parts of the call did; cap = greatest(0, Σ net − Σ paid), floored
  once; queue = greatest(0, Σ the client's pending) − the earlier parts' P; P = greatest(0, least(A, queue, cap)),
  attributed in (posted_at, id) order, each item up to what it can still take; `p_bound` ∈ none / amount / items /
  queue. Since the review fixes (money-2, LT-1), the cap is also at most A less what the earlier unreversed unplanned
  bookings of the same transfer netted (« M2c-6b-2b review fixes » below). The Python
  twin `payments.transfer_lines.unplanned_p` has the same rules; its properties (Hypothesis) bound P by A, the queue and
  the cap, the attribution by each item's net, and the queue's move by −P.
- **The entries** (§3.6.2–§3.7, all at the line's booking date): an unplanned payout posts its remittance
  (+4670[c] A / −5120 A, key `remit:line:<line>:<n>`, reason « Virement exécuté hors reversement (relevé du …) ») and,
  when A − P > 0, the client advance (+4679 X / −4670[c] X ‖ +4112[c] X / −4689 X, `adv:line:<line>:<n>`, cause
  `double_payout`) after it (LG008 at `private.ledger_check_now()`); a −A pending row (the 4670 trigger skips remittance
  entries), so the queue moves by −P; one `private.unplanned_paid_item` row per attributed item. An unplanned sweep
  posts `servicer_sweep` (`sweep:line:<line>:<n>`). A return reverses the planned remittance (`return:<line>:<transfer>`)
  or the unplanned one (`return:<line>:<n>`, and its advance `return:adv:<line>:<n>`; the reason of an unplanned
  sweep's return, « Virement au compte propre hors ordre de Collectoo revenu », is ours — the plan names none). The
  planned parts go through `private.bank_booking_begin` and `private.bank_booking_post_rows` with the job's own
  `pg_temp._bb` columns (CSO-1, parity: a payout's remittance entry has no reason; the motif is on the booking row,
  and — as `public.link_debit`'s fees, top-ups and losses — the reason of the servicer's own fee and sweep entries,
  which no client reads: review LT-7).
  `private.unplanned_paid_item` is append-only, RLS on, every privilege revoked.
- **Locks, the job's order plus the drafts** (§3.8; `private.transfer_line_locks`): the runs of the named transfers
  and the clients' live runs `FOR UPDATE` → the payout accounts a return marks → the bank accounts `FOR SHARE` → the
  payments the payout parts' breach rows may name `FOR KEY SHARE` → `payments:` → the bank lines `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` →
  `remit:` → the files `FOR SHARE` → the transfers `FOR UPDATE`. A 55P03 is re-raised with the step it waited at:
  `allocation_busy` on the servicer-wide advisory locks, `busy` elsewhere (critic2 CSO2-6). A live run found under the
  locks that step 1 did not lock is `split_changed`, never locked late (critic CSO-12).
- **The draft re-prepared, not cleared** (§3.6.5; critic CSO-6, CSO-7): `private.remittance_draft_requeue(run)` reserves
  the client's unreserved items, sets a new prepare token (`known_at`, `service_to`, `prepared_at`/`inputs_hash`/
  `line_count` null, `item_count` recounted, the approval's request and `last_failure` null, `version + 1`) and queues
  the prepare job; the job's `remittance_prepare_begin` clears the old draft under the run lock.
- **Redefinitions** (§3.12): `private.bank_line_booking_guard` (the fee on our debits, the returns on own and client
  credits, the unsplit lines in either direction, the two unplanned return kinds on a reversal of an unplanned booking's
  entry); `private.pending_item_deadlines` (the planned `payout_returned` branch for a transfer's own planned remittance
  only — `bt.entry_id` = the reversed entry, critic F11, L4 — and a third branch, critic2 ML-2: the item re-owed when an
  unplanned payout comes back after a run froze the items its P paid is held to the earliest latest execution date of
  those items' live lines; the worker's `jobs/remittances.py` `_held_to` has the same branches);
  `private.bank_booking_post_rows` (a payout's remittance entry carries no reason); `private.ingest_statement` (OQ-84
  (j), below).
- **OQ-84 (j), the 6b-2a known limit, fixed**: `bank_transaction` and the stage gain `charges_read` (for a line that is
  its entry's only line: true when the statement had no charges or every record was read, false when a block was seen
  and not read; checked: never false beside a charge) and `unsplit_direction_given` (per detail of ours, whether its
  `CdtDbtInd` was given; its length that of the details). The parser sets both (its `charges` returns `(read, charges)`;
  `jobs.payments.stage_row` writes them). A re-import compares the stored values with every value the new file
  gives, and only with those (`private.unsplit_details_differ`; the charges when the new file read them — corrected by
  the review fixes, CSR-4: the build compared a value only when both files gave it); a stored null flag (a line
  imported before) is read as « given ».
- **The pg-safeupdate guard** (found by the integration test through the API session): two `UPDATE`s of the check's
  temporary tables had no `WHERE`; an API session (the `authenticator` role preloads `safeupdate`) refuses them (`UPDATE requires a WHERE
  clause`), which pgTAP does not load. Both carry `where true`; the test that books through `debit_helpers.api` kills
  the mutant that drops it.
- **Web (pure, no page)**: `lib/payments/transfer-lines.ts` — the French label of every refusal of §3.10, `busy`,
  `allocation_busy` and `timeout`; `transferLineErrorCode` (the command's code, 55P03 → `busy`, 57014 → `timeout`, « not
  allowed », the motif); `lib/payments/debits.ts` `DECISION_LABEL` (the booking kinds of §3.13; `decisionLabel` says each
  part of a line booked in several, joined by « + »).

**Deviations from the plan, with why**:
- A client part with a fee is refused `bad_request` at parse (at most one part without a transfer: the fee is one),
  not `fee_not_allowed` — §3.4.0's shape rule comes first.
- Class E is any transfer of the line's servicer named by its id; on another account it is `transfer_differs` (the plan
  leaves the case open between E and E0). A lot credit whose ids name nothing of ours is class B by `names_our_lot`.
- `client_ambiguous` counts every registered payout account of the IBAN, proposed or active (the plan says
  « registered »).
- A U line (an entry kept unsplit) is exempt from the line-kind checks (`wrong_direction`, `not_a_transfer_line`): its
  direction is the net of its details, and its parts are the statement's own details.
- The reason of an unplanned sweep's return is ours (above).
- The stateful `ledger_machine` rules of §8.2 are replaced by the pure twin's properties (P's bounds, the attribution,
  the queue's move, each entry's balance) and the SQL scenarios of `037`; the stateful machine over a bank model
  (`test_transfer_line_machine_integration.py`) is not built.
- pgTAP `037` covers groups A–L of §8.1, not every case. The first build left F5, ML-1's signed pool in SQL and ML-8
  to the review, saying the twin covered the first two — it did not (the twin never runs against the SQL): since the
  review fixes they are SQL cases of `037` (« M2c-6b-2b review fixes »). S02/S04, the lot variant of F1, M (the funds
  pass after an ops booking, CSO-11, CSO2-7, beyond G's and the sweeps') and J (every read's tenant isolation beyond
  A's) are still left.
- `exec_on` (test only) disables `transfer_file_item`'s append-only trigger inside the test's transaction to move a
  file's execution dates back (a file generated today executes on the next business day, and a statement line is never
  dated in the future).
- `DECISION_LABEL` is a new constant beside `LINK_KIND` (none existed under that name); the fee keeps M2c-1's label
  « Frais bancaires (à la charge du cabinet) ».

**Tests** (each red before its code): pgTAP `037_transfer_line_ops.test.sql` (51 assertions, groups A roles, refusals,
tenants, privileges and OQ-84 (j); B the line's state and replay; C planned payouts, rule 3b, fees, lots, late, parity;
D unplanned payouts and P; E sweeps; F returns; G unplanned returns and ML-2; H unsplit entries; I compare-and-set; K the
guard; L alerts); worker `tests/test_transfer_line_ops.py` (P's examples and properties, the entries' balance, the
parser's flags and the stage), `tests/test_transfer_line_ops_integration.py`
(`test_a_payout_returned_then_executed_again_then_returned_again` through the real camt.053 import, the debit job, the
command as an aal2 API session, the prepare and approval jobs and `_held_to`; `test_a_second_debit_booked_by_ops_is_the_servicer_s_advance`;
`test_cs1_the_download_waits_on_its_run_holding_nothing`; `test_cs1_the_command_waits_on_the_client_s_draft_holding_nothing`;
`test_the_same_key_twice_at_once_returns_the_first_result`; `test_a_command_waiting_on_the_allocation_lock_is_allocation_busy`),
`tests/test_transfer_line_scale_integration.py` (the lot cap); web `lib/payments/transfer-lines.test.ts`.

**CS-1, the interleaved order** (review M2c-6b-2a, left to this slice): the first connection holds only the run row the
second needs, then calls its own command. The download waits on its run holding nothing and the cancellation commits;
the command waits on the client's draft holding nothing and the draft's refresh commits. Mutants: the download taking
`payments:`/`remit:` before its runs, and the command taking `payments:` before its runs — each deadlocks, 40P01, the
named test fails; both controls pass.

**Mutants** (each a scratch redefinition of one function, killed by the named test; a no-op control passes `037`):
the only subset removed (C S09); P's reversal fold (D F2/F3); P = 0 for a returned x (D F2, G ML-2); earlier bookings'
attributions ignored (D S01, F4: another collection waiting); `client_run_cancellable` (D F6); `unplanned_open` (F F1);
the fee rule widened (C L2, F S20, H); the unsplit identity by count only (H); the pending row −P instead of −A (B, D,
C); the draft requeue removed (D S01); the key without the part index (E, B, D); the motif as the payout's entry reason
(C CSO-1); the tenant filter after the status rules (A CSO-5, CSO2-10); the third held-to branch (G ML-2); the planned
return branch on any remittance (G F11); `debit_pending` (F ML-3); `run_still_live` (D ML-4); the U count (H ML-5);
S08-on-U (C ML-6); the fee check and the charges compare (C ML-10); the re-import comparing every stored value, or
ignoring the directions given (A OQ-84 (j)); rule 3b's IBAN on class O and its execution date (C); the client part's
in-flight refusal (C F13); `client_ambiguous` (D); `advance_settled` and the largest-advance rule (G); an unreferenced
credit as an unplanned return (G L3); the funds pass not queued (G); the guard's unplanned return on any reversal and
payout on any credit (K); the key lock under 2 s, the allocation wait as `busy`, the `UPDATE` without `WHERE` (the
integration tests); the attribution of earlier parts of the same call dropped (D F4: one item released by two
cancelled runs, both payouts executed late in one entry kept unsplit). None survives. The plan's « the line not locked → booked twice » is equivalent here: the servicer-wide `payments:` lock serialises two
commands on one line, and the check re-reads the line under the locks (`already_booked`).

Suites on the final code, after `supabase db reset`: pgTAP 37 files, 2,600 tests (`037` 51; `034`'s TODO markers
kept); the worker's ruff, format and mypy (174 files), 1,055 unit tests passed (5 xfailed) and 202 integration tests
(the scale files apart); the evals unchanged — mapping 167/167 (threshold 0.980), reconciliation 0.9600 automatic
(95,997/100,000), 0 wrong, 0 policy violations; on a fresh reset, the payouts scale test once (5 of 5) and the new
lot-cap test (2 of 2; timings in `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md`) — the download did not change, so the transfer-files
scale test was not run again; the web's lint, types and 358 vitest tests; the E2E's 54 tests — no screenshot
committed: no page the E2E shows changed (the decision labels appear in « Traités » only for bookings the fixtures do
not hold), and the image diffs are dates, ages and ids. `database.types.ts` regenerated (the command, its two reads,
`charges_read`, `unsplit_direction_given`).

## M2c-6b-2b review fixes (2026-11-17)

**Round 1.** The review of 6b-2b (four lenses: money, legal texts, concurrency and security, tests; 23 findings — money-1,
TESTS-1 to TESTS-4 medium, the rest low) checked against the build `1f8ea8f`; each finding below was confirmed on the
stack (none rejected). The migration `20261117100000_transfer_line_ops.sql`, not merged yet, is edited in place (its
redefinitions copied from the latest definition, settings and grants restated); `20261117090000` and every earlier file
unchanged; the cancellation after download stays **off**; `033`/`034` unchanged. No §10 question answered: each default
stays open. Every fix only narrows what is booked or netted.

- **money-1 (medium) — an entry kept unsplit holding none of ours was booked as one movement.** `transfer_line_class`
  reads a line as U only when `unsplit_ours > 0`; an entry the parser kept unsplit with no detail of ours (two `TxDtls`
  that do not add up, or one detail under an `NbOfTxs` of 2) fell to N, O or E0, and rule 3b's only candidate, the
  client part (S13) and the IBAN-matched unplanned return (ML-11) each took the entry's total — one ops confirmation of
  the proposal booked a run paid, a 50 000 double-payout advance, or an advance reversed and a payout account marked
  returned, where the job says `batch_partial`. Fix (`private.transfer_line_check`, after the line-state rules): a line
  kept unsplit (`unsplit_ours` not null) that is neither U nor B is refused `unsplit_not_bookable` (the options inherit it
  through their preview); our lot kept unsplit (B) is booked only when the count of transactions the statement gives —
  `NbOfTxs` (`unsplit_batch_count`), or its details' count when it has details — is the only subset's (deviation, the
  narrower side: the review asked for `NbOfTxs` only). Tests: pgTAP `037` H « (review money-1): an entry kept unsplit
  holding no detail of ours is never booked as one movement … » (the reviewer's three shapes: x2's payout, a client
  part, an unplanned return; options and command; x2 stays `in_file`) and « (review money-1): our lot kept unsplit whose
  NbOfTxs, or whose details' count, is not its only subset's → unsplit_not_bookable … » (equal: booked).
- **money-2, LT-1 (low) — a second late execution of one payout netted the commission share.** P counted a cancelled
  run's released item at its gross, so once a first execution of x (24 600) had paid the 30 000 item's net, a second
  got P = 5 400 — the commission the run had set off, which the next run then takes on the item from the client's
  unrelated collections: a hold-back without a claw-back clause (Q4, founder #7, OQ-38). Fix (the reviewer's
  alternative, per transfer): the cap is also at most A less what the earlier unreversed unplanned bookings of the same
  transfer netted (their amount less their advance) — x's amount is all its run would have paid the client of its
  items, their gross less the commission. The twin's `UnplannedAsk.prior` has the same rule. Known limit, recorded in
  COMPLIANCE OQ-82 with its default: an item released by **two** cancelled runs whose two payouts are both executed late
  can still be netted twice up to its gross (each transfer is bounded by its own A) — unreachable while the switch is
  off; before 6b-3 turns it on, P must count a released item net of the commission its cancelled run set off on it.
  Tests: `037` D « (S01, Q4; F4, CSO-6, CSO-7; review money-2, LT-1) … » (second execution `["0", "24600", "items"]`,
  was `["5400", "19200", "items"]`); worker `test_money2_bookings_of_one_transfer_never_net_more_than_its_amount` and
  the property `test_p_bounds_and_attribution` (`prior`). Deviation: no case with a real commission invoice (the bound
  reads only x's amount and the earlier bookings, never the run's documents; `037`'s 24 600 on a 30 000 item stands
  for the 18 % set-off, as the reviewer's reproduction).
- **LT-2 (low) — the return of an unplanned payout read « reversé à nouveau ».** Brought forward from 6b-2d (plan §5,
  critic L4): `private.remittance_statement_build` (redefined from `20261116090000`, settings and grants restated)
  marks a `payout_returned` line whose reversed entry is an `unplanned_payout` booking's (`nature_reason` `unplanned`,
  late cause `unplanned_payout_returned`); the renderer's `NATURE` reads « Virement exécuté hors reversement revenu »

**CI scale fix (2026-11-17).** The dispatched `scale` run of PR #33 failed three cases of
`test_transfer_line_scale_integration.py` at the API's 8 s, in `private.transfer_line_locks` step 4 (the payments of the
lot's runs' late lines); the CI order on a third local stack failed the same three, at the same line. Not CPU: plans
chosen from the statistics the 50,000-line runs leave — two runs hold 100,000 of remittance_line's lines, n_distinct of
`run_id` 2, so a run's key is estimated at 50,000 rows. Each member's run was read with the run's conditions next to its
key, three times per member:
- the lock step's lateral (`amount_minor > 0 and not released … < booking_date` inside it, and the function without
  `enable_seqscan = off`) by a sequential scan of remittance_line per member — 500 × 101,000 rows, 21 s instrumented;
- the posting's late lines (`private.bank_booking_post_rows`' `late` CTE, the same lateral) the same — 20.9 s;
- the check's late flag (`private.transfer_line_check`, enable_seqscan off) by a whole scan of the partial index
  `remittance_line_account_idx`, its `not released` predicate implied by the condition — 499 × 51,000 rows per check:
  the options' 1.6 s in CI (the preview's check), 6.5 s instrumented, and as much again in the command's check.

Fix, in place in `20261117100000` (the same rows read, the same locks in the same order and strength — §3.8; CS-1's
tests unchanged and passing): each of the three reads the run's lines by its key alone, its conditions outside an
`offset 0` subquery, under enable_seqscan off — the locks now `set enable_seqscan = off`; the posting's late lines through
`private.remittance_run_late_lines(run, date)` (new, its own `enable_seqscan = off`: `bank_booking_post_rows` keeps its
callers' settings). The same pass over every other statement of the command, its preview and its options whose plan the
statistics chose: the id probes of `transfer_line_class`, of the options' classes E and U and of the check's and the
locks' unsplit details hold the end-to-end id alone, the servicer compared outside (a second condition lets stale
statistics read the servicer's transfers through `bank_transfer_org_idx`); the options' member list reads a member's
file items by the member, the PmtInf compared outside; the tenant filter reads each id's row by key in a lateral (as
`not exists (… and organization_id = p_org)` it hashed every transfer of the servicer on each call);
`transfer_line_pre` and the tenant filter set enable_seqscan off; the posting's client balances, runs booked and payout
accounts returned are reached by the arrays of their keys, as its transfers were (P2); the command's copy of the job's
`pg_temp._bb` build runs in `private.transfer_line_bb` (new) under enable_seqscan off (with bank_line_booking estimated
small, a lot read it whole about 2,000 times). Left as they are, outside the command's own statements: the booking
guard's and the posting's `max(seq)` lookups of bank_line_booking and bank_debit_link, once per booking (a booking may
read them whole while their statistics call them small), the ledger's set-based joins, and the job's own `_bb` build
and payments lock in `private.post_bank_bookings` (its lateral has the lock step's old shape; the db suite's
2,000-member batch test reads bank_line_booking per row there when the transfer-line integration tests ran before it,
at `c581a8b` as now — it passes in the CI order). Test: `test_the_command_reads_a_lot_by_key` (the scale file's first
case, rolled back): no sequential scan of remittance_line, remittance_run, bank_transfer, transfer_file or
transfer_file_item, the lot's runs' lines read at most 10 times per member (before the fix, at the failing point, the
lock step alone scanned remittance_line 500 times). Timings in `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md` (« The ops command »,
CI scale fix).

**Bugs found and fixed** (each test red on `c581a8b`, green on the fix; severity by the slice's rule):
- **Cross-tenant lock (low).** `private.transfer_line_locks` step 8 took `FOR SHARE` on every `transfer_file` holding an
  item of the line's `payment_info_id`, whatever its account. The PmtInfId is the bank's data: a line of one servicer
  whose PmtInfId equals another servicer's lot (TF numbers are one global sequence, so only a bank-given or mistyped
  id collides) made that servicer's file locked for the command's duration — its download or regeneration waited,
  then `busy` (critic CSO-5: « no row of another servicer is ever locked »). No money, no data shown. Fix: the PmtInf's
  files of the line's account only, as every read of the lot already filters them (`transfer_line_class`,
  `transfer_line_pre`, `transfer_line_members`). Test:
  `test_transfer_line_concurrency_integration.py::test_another_servicer_s_rows_are_never_locked_by_the_command` (the
  command booking such a line holds its transaction open while a second connection probes the other servicer's file,
  transfers, runs and account `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`: on `c581a8b` the file is held, 55P03; and a command naming the other
  servicer's transfer, refused `transfer_unknown`, holds none of its rows). Mutant: the fix reverted → the test fails.
- **A misleading refusal (low).** `public.transfer_line_options` answered `bad_request` for an entry kept unsplit
  whose stored detail has no amount (its proposed part carried no amount; the preview's parse refused it) — the sheet's
  label « La demande est incomplète ou mal formée : rouvrez la ligne et recommencez. », false — where the check and
  plan §3.11, §3.4.12 say `unsplit_detail_missing` (« Le relevé ne détaille pas assez cette écriture … »). Nothing was
  booked either way. Fix: such an entry is refused `unsplit_detail_missing` with no part proposed. Test:
  `test_transfer_line_ops_more_integration.py::test_the_iso_charged_debit_without_chrgs_and_an_unsplit_entry_without_amounts_stay`
  (`--unsplit-details no-amounts` through the real camt.053 import). Mutant: the fix reverted → the test fails.

**Deviations, with why**:
- `037b` is a new file beside `037` (track A appends 6b-2c's group P to `037`); its fixtures are `037`'s, copied.
- The M2b pass's `post_debit_links` is not run against the command: `request_refund` holds the late line's payment
  `FOR UPDATE` and then waits for the allocation lock exactly as it does (6b-1's concurrency-2 staging), so the pair
  is the same lock shape.
- The 5,000-member lot is not the payout scale fixture's (5,050 runs through the jobs, ≈ 14 minutes, in the
  `scale-payouts` job): the file of two payouts is made through the jobs and its PmtInf filled to 5,000 members in a
  rolled-back transaction. What the test measures — the keyed count answering before any member is read — reads only
  `transfer_file_item` and `transfer_file`, which these rows populate as the jobs do.
- The 50,000-item draft is not the remittance scale fixture's (50,000 files boarded): 50,000 advances are posted
  set-based (each a pending item of the client's queue), then the draft is requested by the command (its 50,000 items
  reserved). The requeue reads only the queue and the run.
- The `_hold` pairs of the concurrency file let the first call finish before committing; a lock-order mutant (the
  payments' key share after the allocation lock) is killed by the three-session refund staging (above), not by those
  pairs.
- The P parity examples shape the pool's facts with the guards off inside their rolled-back transaction (the
  transfer's and the line's amount, the pending amounts, the attributions); every fact is then read back from SQL for
  the twin, as `_pool_item` reads it for 6b-2b's single parity point.
- Three test defects the runs found, fixed in the tests (no product change): the machine first picked payouts and
  files by their random ids and gated rules on preconditions read from the database, so a replayed choice sequence
  could enable other rules (Hypothesis `FlakyStrategyDefinition` in a full run): the picks now follow the model's own
  order and no rule has a precondition; the machine took the file's `cash_not_covered` refusal for an error (now
  modelled, above); the parity test's « fifth item » was the client's first other pending row by id, which an
  example's reversal row could precede (its `extra` then landed on that row: a zero amount, refused by the check
  constraint, found while the per-item floor mutant ran) — now pinned by the fixture.
- Not changed (6b-1's): `test_debit_bookings_batch_rules_integration.py`'s row budget is met on a fresh database (the

## M2c-6b-2c: the pages — ops book our transfer lines from « Débits et retours » (plan docs/design/m2c-6b-2-plan.md §4, §6, §7.3–§7.5, §8, §9)

Migration `20261117110000_transfer_line_pages.sql` (forward-only; every redefinition copied from its latest definition —
6b-2b's `20261117100000` treated as merged — with `SECURITY DEFINER`, every `SET` clause, `search_path` and its grants
restated; no earlier file edited), pgTAP `037` group P (10 assertions), the web's pages and texts, the E2E. The
cancellation after download stays **off**; `033` and `034` keep their assertions and TODO markers. The founder answered
none of the plan's §10 questions: each default is built (Q14's five business days included) and stays open. Decisions:

- **The guards of « Lier »** (plan §4.1; critic F9, L8). `private.link_debit_guard(line, kind, refund)`, called by
  `public.link_debit` once its own request checks pass, on a debit of class N, O or E0 only (our own lines keep
  `post_debit_links`' `own_transfer_line`): « Frais bancaires », « Classer sans comptabiliser » and the refund link are
  refused `payout_candidate` while rule 3b (`private.transfer_line_candidates`) finds a transfer of ours the line may be
  — for the refund link, a candidate other than that refund's own transfer and other than a sweep; `client_payout_line`
  on a debit to a client's confirmed payout IBAN (an unplanned payout, or its run's payout without its reference);
  the explanation `own_transfer_out_line` on a transfer out to one of our own accounts. The error is `debit link
  refused: <code>` (`check_violation`); the web labels each (`errorText`), and the page no longer offers « Classer sans
  comptabiliser » on such a line (`linkGuarded`).
- **The queue's cheap facts** (plan §4.1; critic CSO-4, critic2 CSO2-13). `public.debit_queue` (dropped and created:
  its row type changes) gains `bookable_as` (`private.transfer_line_bookable_as`: `e`, `b`, `u` from the line's class;
  `n` for a reference-less debit of kind `transfer_out`, `other_debit` or `batch_unsplit` with a rule-3b candidate or to a
  confirmed client payout IBAN or one of our own accounts, and for a return credit from a client's payout IBAN; null
  otherwise, and for an entry kept unsplit holding nothing of ours), one keyed read per row shown — the options are
  read only when a line's sheet opens. « À classer » lists the other debits without our reference that
  `private.transfer_line_queue_reason` names (`payout_amount_match` with its candidates, `client_payout_iban`,
  `own_transfer_out`), except those of a requested refund's amount (`refund_amount_match` as before); « Frais » no longer
  lists them. Each candidate is enriched with its run's status and number by a fenced keyed lookup (`cancelled_transfer_debited`
  is worded by it: a run still approved or sent is that payout's, never « Virement hors reversement », critic2 ML-4).
- **The bounded suppression** (plan §4.2; Q14's default; critic L8, critic2 ML-7). `private.transfer_debit_suppression(transfer,
  to, today)` reads the lines 6b-1's `private.transfer_debit_may_be_seen` read (now its wrapper: `= 'waiting'` at
  `private.paris_today()`), newest first: `waiting` while a line is younger than `private.transfer_debit_bound_days()`
  (5) business days (`private.business_days_between`) or offers a booking containing that transfer
  (`private.transfer_line_offers`: the options' own proposals, `private.transfer_line_options_of`, so the alert and the
  sheet agree by construction); `expired` once every such line is past the bound and offers none; null without any.
  `private.run_remittance_runs_checks` writes the in-flight breach row with `blocked_reason = 'debit_unbooked'` when the
  only lines left are expired (the check constraint gains the value); `private.run_transfer_checks`' `bank_line_unbooked`
  extends to reference-less other debits with a rule-3b candidate (reason `payout_amount_match`; P0 when a candidate's run
  holds a positive live line past its latest execution date).
- **Plan robustness** (pgTAP `037` P `p_queue_reads`, 300 cancelled payouts of the account in a file, 40 reference-less
  debits): `private.transfer_line_candidates` reads its line by key in a fenced subquery and probes the new non-partial
  index `bank_transfer_account_amount_idx (debtor_bank_account_id, amount_minor)` — the partial
  `bank_transfer_filed_amount_idx` let the planner imply its predicate and scan the account's transfers on stale

  (as PR #33's CI scale fix already does in `20261117100000`: at integration this file's redefinition of it, the same

  `debit_link`, `own_credit`), which `post_debit_links` and `release_own_credit` call; the job's reviews
