- **Reads** (plan §4.4; critic CSO-6, CSO-9, L6; critic2 ML-12), money staff of the servicer at aal2 only, keyed:
  `private.transfer_chain(transfer)` (itself, then each `replaces_transfer_id`, depth < 50);
  `public.remittance_run_payout(run)` (the chain's transfers with their debit and return dates and lines, the run's
  set-off date and amounts, its overrun advances, the unplanned bookings of its transfers, a draft's unplanned items);
  `public.transfer_bookings(ids)` (≤ 500 ids; another servicer's ids are ignored); `client_remittance_summary`'s
  `unplanned_runs` (a cancelled run any transfer of whose chain the bank executed all the same).

  refusal with its run; « Motif (ce que montre le relevé ou la banque) » is required; an entry kept unsplit is checked

  hors reversement » (`transfer_bookings`); « Virements » says when the last nightly check found the servicer's share
  unswept; the client space says the debit's date and the cancelled run's truth (`runStatusText(status, net, bookedOn,
  unplannedOn)`).

**Deviations from the plan, with why**:
- The refund link is not refused `payout_candidate` for a sweep of its amount (the plan: any candidate but the refund's
  own transfer): review round 7's founder decision N1 (b), pinned by `033` (a reference-less line executes a refund in a

**A test adapted to 6b-2c's guards.** B's `test_link_debit_and_the_command_on_one_line_never_deadlock[fee|explained ×
link first]` failed: on the reference-less line a payout may be (rule 3b's candidate, to its payee IBAN), A's

**Known limits found, not fixed (low).**

  explanation, on a `transfer_out`): the page offers no « Frais bancaires » there (the line is in « À classer »,
  `own_transfer_out`, not « Frais »), so only a direct call of the command books it.
- `private.post_bank_bookings`' own `_bb` build, its booking guard and `_bb_pay_locks` (6b-1's, outside this slice) as

## M2c-6b-2c review fixes (2026-11-18)

**Round 1.** The review of 6b-2c (five lenses: money, legal deadlines, concurrency and security, tests, pages and texts;
26 findings — money-1 high; money-2, money-3, money-4, legal-deadlines-1, legal-deadlines-2 and pages-1 medium; the
rest low) checked against the integration `fea2a19`. Each finding was confirmed on the main stack; none rejected
(money-3 and legal-deadlines-2 are one defect, T1 and pages-2 another). `20261117110000_transfer_line_pages.sql`, not
merged yet, is edited in place (`20261117105000` unchanged); each function it now redefines is copied from its latest
definition (`private.transfer_line_check` from `20261117100000` as PR #33's CI scale fix left it,
`public.debit_link_options` from `20261116090000`), `SECURITY DEFINER`, every `SET` clause and the grants restated; no
earlier file edited. The cancellation after download stays **off**; `033`/`034` unchanged; no §10 question answered
(Q14's five business days included). Every fix narrows what is booked, linked or netted, but one: legal-deadlines-1
widens which lines hold an in-flight breach row back, because plan §4.2, Q14's default and CPCE-08 require that a line
ops can book as the payout's debit holds it back (the system wrote a false R124-6 row otherwise); it stays bounded
the same way.

- **money-1 (high) — a payout's debit could be linked as a debtor payment's return.** The lines 6b-2c moved into « À
  classer » (`payout_amount_match`, `client_payout_iban`) were offered « Retour du paiement de … » and its loss, which
  `private.link_debit_guard` let through (it checked fee, explanation and refund only): one click returned a debtor's
  payment by the client's payout amount, hid the payout's on-time debit from the suppression and, once its date
  passed, the nightly check wrote a false breach row. Fix: the guard refuses `return` and `loss` on a debit of class N,
  O or E0 as it refuses a fee (round 2 below: of a kind « Comptabiliser… » books) — `payout_candidate` while rule 3b
  finds a transfer of ours it may be,
  `client_payout_line` on a debit to a client's confirmed payout IBAN (active, returned or retired);
  `public.debit_link_options` (redefined) lists no payment there and only the refunds the guard lets through; the page's
  `linkOffers` offers no return, loss or refund on a guarded row (`linkGuarded`, which now also reads `bookable_as`).
  Tests: pgTAP `037` « P (§4.1; critic F9; review 6b-2c money-1, money-2, T4) … » (`p_guards`: return and loss refused on
  lines 1, 2, 3 and 8, `debit_link_options` empty there, a debit to no one we know still a payment's return); vitest
  `transfer-line-review-fixes.test.ts` « the links « Comptabiliser… » replaces (money-1, money-2; T5) ».
- **money-2 (medium) — the return of an unplanned payout could be classified without booking.** A credit the bank flags
  as a return from a client's payout IBAN (critic2 ML-11's shape, « Virement revenu ») took « Classer sans comptabiliser »
  and « Remboursement revenu »: 5120 left unequal to the bank and the double_payout advance open, no check flagging it.
  Fix: the guard refuses `explained` and `refund_returned` on such a credit of class N, O or E0 (its kind, or a held
  line released as one), `client_payout_line` — whether or not an unplanned payout of that amount is open (deviation,
  the narrower side: the review asked at least while one is; without one, it is Q13's « a client's money that waits »,
  never explained); an entry kept unsplit is left out (its total is not one movement, « Comptabiliser… » is not offered
  on it: it keeps the explanation). The page hides both (`linkGuarded` on a credit with `bookable_as` n, the same lines).
  Tests: `037` `p_guards` (`explain_return_credit`, `refund_back_credit`, `explain_unsplit_credit`); vitest (same
  describe).
- **money-3, legal-deadlines-2 (medium) — the sheet said a breach was recorded that the booking does not record.** The
  part's `late` flag and its `latest_execution_date` compared the run's lines' short date with the line's date; the
  booking (`private.bank_booking_post_rows`) holds a line whose mandate's delay cannot be met (`unmeetable`, OQ-71) to
  its one-month date. Fix: `private.remittance_run_late_on(run, date)` (new, internal) gives the date the booking would
  record a breach against — per late live line, its one-month date (`remittance_deadline_or_null(encaissement, 30)`)
  when unmeetable, else its own, the earliest, read by the run's key (`remittance_run_late_lines`); the check
  (`private.transfer_line_check`, redefined) sets `late` and `late_date` from it and the parts carry that date. Test:
  `037` « P (review 6b-2c money-3, legal-deadlines-2; R124-6, OQ-71) … » (`p_unmeetable`: before the one-month date no
  late, no date, no row; after it the one-month date and the row).
- **money-4 (medium) — the draft's run page said it deducted A.** `draft_unplanned` returned the −A row; the draft also
  holds the booking's +(A − P) advance row, so it deducts P. Fix: per booking, the net of its own rows the draft holds
  (−A and its double_payout advance, by their entries), a booking netting 0 not listed; `runPayoutNotes` words what SQL
  returns. Tests: `037` « P (review 6b-2c money-4; critic CSO-6) … » (`p_draft_net`, P = 0: nothing listed) and « P
  (review 6b-2c money-4): … says it deducts P (31 000), never A » (`p_draft_partial`, 0 < P < A; the mutant that
  restores −A dies only here); P = A stays `p_unplanned_runs`; vitest « the run page (pages-1, money-4) ».
- **legal-deadlines-1 (medium) — lines the options book as the payout's debit did not hold its breach row back.** A
  debit of its amount to its payee's IBAN with a foreign end-to-end id or PmtInfId (O, E0) and an entry kept unsplit
  whose stored details name its debit (U, netted) were not counted by `private.transfer_debit_suppression`: the first
  nightly check after the date wrote a plain breach row though the bank debited on time. Fix: both shapes counted (the
  unsplit one by its stored detail `{id, direction: debit}`), keyed and bounded as before (five business days unless
  the line offers the booking). The WIP's first version left the « not booked nor linked » filter on the unsplit branch

## M2c-6b-2d: « Suivi » — the statement follows the earlier payouts as of K (plan docs/design/m2c-6b-2-plan.md §5, §6, §8.1 038, §8.2, §9)

Migration `20261117120000_statement_suivi.sql` (forward-only; `private.remittance_statement_build` copied from its latest
definition, `20261117100000` — not `20261116090000` — and `private.remittance_statement_line_columns` from its only one,
`20261113090000`, each with `SECURITY DEFINER` where it had it, every `SET` clause, `search_path` and its grants
restated; 6b-2c's `20261117105000` and `20261117110000` treated as merged; no earlier file edited), template
`releve-reversement-fr-3` (`remittance/statement.py`, `statement_pdf.py`), pgTAP `038_statement_suivi` (14 assertions),
the renderer's pytest and the documents integration test. No page reads the payload's `follow_up` (the web is
unchanged: no screenshot). The cancellation after download stays **off**; `033` and `034` keep their assertions and TODO
markers. The founder answered none of the plan's §10 questions nor COMPLIANCE OQ-83/OQ-86: each default is built and
stays open; the defaults this slice adds are COMPLIANCE OQ-87. Decisions:

- **The payload** drops M2c-5's `follow_up` (the previous run's transfer as it stood when the statement was drawn, not
  as of K) and adds `previous_payouts` `{since, events}` (`private.remittance_statement_previous_payouts`, internal,
  keyed, sequential scans off). `since` is the client's previous **approved** run of the currency (`approved_at` set,
  `known_at` below this run's — critic L7: a draft discarded with its RV number neither bounds the window nor is listed)
  with its K; the window is (since's K, this run's K] on `ledger_entry.posted_at` and `remittance_run.cancelled_at`
  (ADR-0012; critic L17: never the statement's drawing time). The events are those of the client's earlier approved
  runs that ordered a payout (N > 0), read on each run's chain (`private.transfer_chain`, critic2 ML-12), one per event,
  ordered by effective date, then run number (nulls last), then kind: `debited`, `returned` (`repaid` here / run /
  pending, `repaid_by`), `cancelled`, `executed_after_cancellation`, `debited_again` (`unplanned_minor`,
  `advance_minor`, `p_bound` from the booking's `double_payout` advance — critic2 ML-9 — `amount` when there is none),
  `unplanned_returned` (`owed_minor` = P = A − advance) and `executed_outside` (`iban_last4`). Amounts as text, dates
  the entries' effective dates (the cancellation's Paris date).
- **`here`** is « this run holds the event's entry in a live line » (`remittance_line_live_uq`): the payout_returned
  item of a return, the −A line of an unplanned booking, the re-owed +A of its return. A run cancelled before its
  statement is drawn holds nothing live, so its statement says « vous sera reversé / sera pris en compte dans un prochain
  reversement » — true, and drawn as the run stands like the rest of a cancelled run's statement (OQ-87 (b)). `repaid`
  `run` (a run approved by K holds the return's item) is built as the plan says, but with the window bounded by the
  previous approved run it cannot occur (such a run would be approved with a K inside the window): no test reaches it.
- **Late cause `paid_by_unplanned`** (critic L9, critic2 ML-9): a late line whose item an unplanned payout's P paid —
  `private.unplanned_paid_item` of a booking whose remittance entry is posted at or before K and has no reversal posted
  by then (`private.remittance_statement_paid_by_unplanned`, read for the late lines only, keyed) — takes that cause
  first, with the amount attributed (`paid_by_unplanned_minor`, summed over the bookings) and the latest such booking's
  date (`paid_by_unplanned_on`), the two line columns appended to `line_columns` (the CSV's columns unchanged; the
  renderer reads by name). The renderer words it « versé le … par un virement exécuté hors reversement » when the amount
  covers the line, « dont … versés le … » when it covers part of it; a payload with the cause and without either field
  is refused.
- **The renderer** (`releve-reversement-fr-3`; `TEMPLATE_VERSIONS` = fr-3 only: stored statements are never
  re-rendered): `_previous_payouts` in place of `_follow_up`, every sentence of plan §5; a payload carrying `follow_up`,
  missing `previous_payouts`, or holding an event it does not know is refused `StatementPayloadError`
  (`payload_version`) — never drawn with a section missing (the documents job records the failure and retries). The
  advance clause is worded by `p_bound` (`items`/`none`: « elle dépassait ce qui restait à vous reverser des sommes de ce
  reversement »; `queue`: « vos sommes en attente à cette date ne permettaient pas d'en déduire davantage »; no advance,
  no clause). An IBAN is printed « IBAN …1234 » from its last four characters (`masked_iban_end`, the pages' format of
  review 6b-2c T1/pages-2), never « FR76 •••• ». The CSV is unchanged (its golden hash too); the statement PDF's golden
  is regenerated and a second golden pins one sentence of each event.
- **Read cost** (plan §5): the client's runs by `remittance_run_client_idx`, each chain and transfer by key, the
  bookings by `bank_line_booking_transfer_idx`, entries and advances by key, live lines by `remittance_line_live_uq`;
  the transfer-less unplanned payouts by a new small partial index `bank_line_booking_unplanned_client_idx
  (organization_id) where kind = 'unplanned_payout' and transfer_id is null` (the mirror of 6b-2a's
  `bank_line_booking_unplanned_return_idx`, which reads their returns), each entry by key for its client and time.
  The late cause's lateral carries `offset 0`, like the build's other laterals: without it the planner pulls the
  subquery up, the « is this line late » test becomes a filter on the helper's rows, and the helper (SQL with `SET`
  clauses, never inlined) is called for every line. The 50,000-line scale run found it (the documents job's build
  7.4 s against 6.1–6.2 s in `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md`): 50,000 calls (0.68 s) for a run with no late line, the
  build 6.5–6.9 s against 5.5–5.8 s for `20261117100000`'s on the same run. With `offset 0` the late test is a
  one-time filter: no call, the build 4.8–5.5 s against 4.8–5.3 s for the previous one (each timed four times,
  alternately, on the second stack's scale run), the documents job's 5.9 s and 6.2 s in the scale file; `038`'s second R
  asserts the calls (one per late line, none for the others).

Deviations from the plan, each with its reason:
- **`unplanned: true` is the existing `nature_reason` `unplanned`** (plan §5 critic L4). 6b-2b's review LT-2 brought the
  unplanned return's nature forward as `nature_reason = 'unplanned'` on the payout_returned line, worded « Virement exécuté
  hors reversement revenu » by the renderer's `UNPLANNED_RETURN`; a second flag would say the same thing twice. Kept;
  `038` C2 and F assert it on lines this slice's scenarios build.
- **`executed_after_cancellation` vs `debited_again` keyed on the run, not the transfer** (plan §5: « x cancelled / booked
  or returned »). An unplanned booking of a transfer of the chain is `executed_after_cancellation` when the run was
  cancelled by the booking (`run.status = 'cancelled'` and `cancelled_at <= posted_at`), `debited_again` otherwise. They
  differ only when a re-issued payout's old (cancelled) transfer is executed while the run was paid by the new one: « Reversement
  … annulé » would then be false (the run was booked; the client received its amount twice). OQ-87 (c).
- **`unplanned_returned` also for a payout outside any run** (plan §5 lists it after the run events only). The return of
  an S13/S07 unplanned payout is the same fact (its advance reversed) and would otherwise be told never; it is listed
  with `run_number` null. OQ-87 (f).
- **`unplanned_returned` says « l'avance du cabinet correspondante est annulée » only when there was an advance**, and
  « … vous sont de nouveau dus » only when P > 0 (plan: the first always). With P = A there is no advance to annul.
- **« Rien à signaler … (encaissements connus au 20/10/2026 à 17:30) »**: the header's own wording of K (`_paris`, « à »)
  rather than the plan's « jj/mm/aaaa hh:mm » placeholder.
- **A new index** (the plan's read cost lists none for `executed_outside`): above.
- **Not in this track** (track B of the 6b-2d workflow): 6b-2c's « Left open after round 3 » items and the E2E flows

after download stays **off**; `033` and `034` keep their assertions and TODO markers. No founder question (plan §10,

**Medium.**
- **statement-money (`debited_again` before the first debit).** The window is read on `posted_at` and the events are
  listed by effective date, so a debit the bank made first but that was booked after the planned one (the d-1
  statement imported before the d-2 one; or, switch on, a re-issued payout's old transfer executed the day before the
  new one and refused `run_still_live` until the new one's debit booked the run) was worded « une seconde fois le 16/11 »
  and listed before the « débité … le 17/11 » it was said to repeat. Fix: `private.remittance_statement_previous_payouts`
  reads the bookings of each run's chain posted by K whenever posted (`ab`), ranks the chain's executions — its
  `payout` booking and every `unplanned_payout` one — by date, then posting (`xn`), and gives each `debited_again` the
  planned debit's date (`debited_on`, the chain's `payout` booking, `bank_line_booking_debit_uq`'s) and
  `before_debit` (its rank below the planned debit's). The renderer then says « la banque a exécuté son virement le
  16/11/2026 (820,00 €), en plus de son débit du 17/11/2026 ; ce virement en plus, que vous avez reçu, figure … ».
- **legal-texts-1 (a third execution « une seconde fois »).** Each unplanned booking of a chain carries its rank
  (`execution_no`, the same ranking): the renderer says « une seconde fois » / « ce second virement » only of the
  second execution, « de nouveau le … (… ; 3e exécution) » / « ce nouveau virement » after it. A cancelled run's
  payout executed more than once is « a néanmoins exécuté » the first time and « a de nouveau exécuté … (2e
  exécution) » after (`executed_after_cancellation` carries the rank too: two identical sentences would read as one
  event told twice). A payload without the rank, a `debited_again` without its planned debit, or one ranked first but
  not before it, is refused `payload_version` (never drawn with a guess; the SQL always gives them: an unplanned booking
  of a live run's chain is refused `run_still_live`, so a run not cancelled by its booking was booked by a `payout`).

## M2c-6b-3a: switch-on prerequisites, the switch still off (2026-11-18)

Plan: docs/design/m2c-6b-3-plan.md (revised after its critics; its §10 records each finding). Migration
`20261118090000_switch_on_prerequisites.sql`. **The switch stays off**: no statement writes `private.feature_switch`;
6b-3b flips `downloaded_file_cancellation` with a one-line migration once the founder answers Q1 (COMPLIANCE OQ-81
(a)). Every rule below bites only in states that need a downloaded file's transfer to be cancelled — production has
none, and pgTAP `033` (the switch-off test) is byte for byte unchanged. The three partial indexes are the only change
that is not inert (the plan named two: `refund_request_transfer_idx` was added after the 5,000-refund scale file showed
M's lookup of a refund's request quadratic — generation 2.3 s → 8.0 s, download 0.8 s → 6.3 s — with no index led by
`refund_request.transfer_id`). *Review round 1 (CSC-2) corrects this:* `refund_request_transfer_id_key` (the column's
unique index since `20261115090000`) already led by it; the quadratic plan came from the probe holding the servicer and
the status beside the key, and the probe holding its key alone is the fix — the duplicate index is removed (two partial
indexes now). `034` passes with its four `todo()` lines removed (every assertion kept, no booking added); `039` holds
the follow-ups, each scenario switching the flag on inside its own subtransaction, the file asserting at its end that
it is off.

### Decisions

- **L — a debit carrying none of our references is a cancelled transfer's possible late execution.**
  `private.transfer_unreferenced_lines(t)`: for a transfer that was an item of a file downloaded at least once, the
  debits of its paying account of its currency and amount, from the earliest execution date of such an item, with no
  end-to-end id nor PmtInfId (class N) to its payee's IBAN or none, or with a reference that is not ours (O, E0) to its
  payee's IBAN — never an E0 naming another lot of ours on the account, never a line of an unsplit entry nor a debit the
  bank flags as a return —, not booked, not linked but as `explained`, not a payment, not decided a duplicate. It never
  reads the options nor rule 3b's candidates (a line that offers nothing still counts). `private.transfer_debited_before`
  counts it for a chain member deeper than the transfer, and for the transfer itself once cancelled — never the
  transfer's own execution out of the live downloaded file it is in. Every guard inherits it: the holds, the
  re-download, `cancel_remittance_run`, the refund's cancellation, the alerts. Unlike the own-id arm (any line, booked or
  not), this arm counts unresolved lines only: once ops book or classify the line it has a meaning. **Deviation from
  round 4's « final statement » default** (a batch line imported after the cancellation's window is not read as a late
  execution): a line without our references cannot be told apart, so it counts whenever it is imported, and N refuses
  the cancellation while it is open. `private.transfer_late_debit_open(t)` = an open late line of t (its own id, its
  PmtInf's batch line — `transfer_late_lines`, its chain's — or one without our references) and no return seen.
  `transfer_late_lines` is unchanged: the job's return rule and the P0 `cancelled_transfer_debited` keep reading our
  references only (a debit without them is never booked automatically: no worker twin).
- **K — rule 3b's (iv).** `private.transfer_line_candidates` also gives a refund or a sweep cancelled out of a file
  downloaded at least once (its current file), at the line's amount, its execution date there on or before the line's,
  to the line's IBAN when it has one, its return not seen. Beside another candidate the line is `line_ambiguous`; alone,
  a sweep's line is proposed and booked as that sweep's late debit (`unplanned_sweep` of it) — the unplanned sweep with
  no transfer keeps `sweep_in_flight_matches` —, a refund's is proposed nothing (`cancelled_transfer_matches`: S25's
  twin, no booking kind yet); an unplanned payout or sweep with no transfer is refused `cancelled_transfer_matches`
  beside such a candidate. `link_debit_guard` is unchanged: the fee and the explanation are refused on every candidate,
  the return and the loss keep OQ-86's rule (iv never refuses them), the refund link is D's.
- **N — the evidence sees debits without our references.** `private.transfer_cancel_evidence` refuses
  `unreferenced_debit_open` (after `debit_seen`, before `batch_ambiguous`): for a file, an in-file transfer's
  `transfer_unreferenced_lines`, or a line with no reference at the sum of a PmtInf's in-file transfers (two or more)
  from the file's first execution date (a bank ignoring `BtchBookg false`, OQ-83); for one transfer, its own. The card
  carries `unreferenced_debit` and `unreferenced_from`; the confirmations recompute it. Not
  `transfer_debit_suppression` (critic 1-1's suggestion): its reference-less arm ignores the IBAN and its `'waiting'`
  depends on the options and a day bound. The m2c-6b-plan §3.3 « subsumed » sentence is corrected there.
- **A, A′ — a sweep made after a cancelled sweep the bank debited late.** `private.sweep_after_debited_cancelled(t)`:
  t a sweep ordered or in a file, and a sweep c of the same servicer and currency — on any of its dedicated accounts,
  whatever its status (A′: a sweep of an account closed since can still be executed late) —, in a downloaded file,
  `c.cancelled_at < t.created_at`, its return not seen, and its late debit open or booked (`unplanned_sweep` of c) by an
  entry whose `posted_at` is at or after t's creation. Not `transfer_debited_before(c)`: once c's line without our
  references is booked it no longer counts there, and t, made before that booking, would be released. **Timestamp
  rule:** the new sweep's `created_at` is generation's clock time read under the remit lock (`v_now`), never `now()` (a
  generation that waited for the lock behind a cancellation would otherwise be « earlier » than it), and the booking is
  compared by its entry's `posted_at` (a clock time), never `decided_at` (`now()`). Held `cancelled_sweep_debited` by
  `private.transfer_hold_reason` (generation never asks for its own new sweep; the download's generated re-check now
  runs over the sweep), refused `holds_debited_transfer` at a re-download, alerted by a new `transfer_already_debited`
  branch (`kind` sweep, its status). Generation's D4 and « Virements »' sweep preview read every dedicated account of
  the servicer in the currency (`private.debited_cancelled_sweeps` stays per account).
- **B — the share proposed again.** `private.debited_cancelled_sweeps` keeps a cancelled sweep while its late debit is
  open (no longer once ops booked it: 4679 then shows the share left); a second late line stops the next sweep again.
- **C — G1c.** The G1 branch reads the servicer's cancelled payouts and refunds that were in a downloaded file (a
  materialized set shared with the P0 `cancelled_transfer_debited` branch), `transfer_debited_before` and
  `transfer_late_debit_open`, whatever their run's or refund's state — excluded only while the live end of their chain
  (their run's transfer, approved or sent, ordered or in a file; their requested refund's) is alerted instead by the
  ordered/in-file branch (critic 2-8: not « re-issued by no transfer »). The alert stops once ops book or link the line.
- **D — H-PAY, account-wide.** `private.refund_transfer_follow`'s reference-less arm (a refund in a downloaded or sent
  file, re-issuing none) also requires `private.cancelled_refund_line_may_be(line, request)` null (review round 1: renamed
  `private.refund_line_barred_by` and widened, below): no refund of the
  account cancelled out of a downloaded file at the line's amount (rule 3b's (iv)), of any payment, outside the
  request's own chain. Else `reissue_in_downloaded_file`, its hint by the account's feed (camt.053: wait for the RFD or
  lot reference, see the bank; CSV: ask the bank for the detail, tell support). A refund whose transfer is ordered is
  still executed by the line and its transfer booked (the right outcome if the line is the earlier one's execution; M's
  exit). `public.debit_link_options` no longer lists such a refund; `link_debit_guard` unchanged.
- **M — holds beyond the chain.** `private.transfer_sibling_debited_late(t)`: a payout is held
  `client_payout_debited_late` while a cancelled payout of its client and currency, outside its chain, in a downloaded
  file, its run ended, shows an open late debit; a refund `payment_refund_debited_late` while another refund request of
  its payment has a transfer in its chain cancelled out of a downloaded file with an open late debit. In
  `transfer_hold_reason` after `already_debited`, in the download's two re-checks (the detail names each transfer with
  its reason), in a new `transfer_already_debited` branch (`reason`). Index `bank_transfer_client_cancelled_idx`.
- **`public.cancellation_after_download()`** answers the flag to any member of a servicer organisation (any role, any
  aal: a collector reads the payment page), false to anyone else; granted to authenticated, revoked from public and anon.
- **Texts.** `errorText(code, {cancellationAfterDownload})` and the « on » variants (T1–T7, T9, T11, T12, T15 by case,
  T19, the sweep's hold, the credit-note refusals); the run page, the payment page, the credit-note page, the file page,
  « Virements » and « Contrôles » pass the flag; the new codes (`cancelled_transfer_matches`,
  `client_payout_debited_late`, `payment_refund_debited_late`, `cancelled_sweep_debited` as a transfer's hold,
  `unreferenced_debit_open` and the card's date) have words; « À classer » says, on a debit whose only candidates are
  a cancelled sweep or refund (K), that the sweep's late debit is booked as that sweep's, a refund's not yet. Every
  « off » text is unchanged.

### Founder questions (each default built, each open; COMPLIANCE OQ-80, OQ-81, OQ-82)

1. Switch cancellation after download on (6b-3b)? Default **a**: yes, by its one-line migration once 6b-3a and
   6b-3a-2 are merged; S06, S25 and its twins, and the feed-without-references stuck states (D, N) stay open, held or
   alerted, never booked. (b) no: refused payouts stay « en cours » beyond R124-6's month.
2. A debit without our references and a refund still in a downloaded file (H-PAY)? Default **a**: refused while a
   cancelled refund of the same account and amount, of any payment, was in a downloaded file (built); (b) the same
   payment only.
3. The same sums repaid by two late transfers (J, 6b-3a-2)? Default **a**: not deducted again (an advance).
4. A debit without reference that may be a cancelled refund's or share's late execution (K)? Default **a**: never booked
   as another payout; a cancelled share alone is booked as that share's late debit (built).
5. A debit without our references at a cancelled or in-file transfer's amount (L, N)? Default **a**: it counts as a
   possible late execution until classified (built; OQ-80 (p)).
6. Holds beyond the transfer's own replacement (M)? Default **a**: the client's other payouts and the payment's other
   refunds held (built); (b) alert only.

### Deviations from the plan

- **E–J and their texts are 6b-3a-2's** (the plan's §5 split point): the migration passed 2,500 lines (2,755) with A–D
  and K–N, each redefinition copied whole (`transfer_line_check` alone is 650 lines). Not built here: the late
  predecessor's booking (E) and its readers (F), its return (G), the release's defence in depth (H), the R124-6 rows of

## M2c-6b-3a review fixes (2026-11-18)

### Round 1

Five lenses reviewed `m6b3a` (`fd5556b`): four medium items and nineteen low ones. Each was checked on the main stack
first: the four medium items reproduced (the reviewers' scenarios, inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with the switch on in the
transaction); every low one is real, but L's payment exclusion (tests-2) is unreachable (below). Every medium item is
fixed at its root, tests first; every low one that is a text, a test, a layout fix or a one-line guard is fixed; the
rest is left open below with its default. The migration `20261118090000` is unmerged and was edited in place; one more
function is redefined there, `private.link_debit_guard`, copied from its latest definition (`20261117113000:265`),
`SECURITY DEFINER`, its `SET` clauses, `search_path` and grants restated. **The switch stays off** (no statement writes
`private.feature_switch`); `033` is unchanged; `034` keeps its 18 assertions with no `todo()`. Every fix only narrows
what is linked or booked, but LD-1 and LD-2, where the review shows rule 3b wrongly refusing the ordinary booking of a
re-issue's own debit (plan §3: the re-issue is booked from its line).

**Medium.**
- **DP-1 (a reference-less line executing another payment's refund not handed out).** D tested H-PAY only for a refund
  in a downloaded or sent file; an ordered refund of another payment at the amount was listed and executed by a line
  that may be a cancelled refund's late execution — that payer shown refunded, the first payment's re-issue released
  (L's line no longer open once linked) and its payer refunded twice. Fix: D's reader is now
  `private.refund_line_barred_by(line, request)` (it replaces `private.cancelled_refund_line_may_be`): for a refund
  whose transfer is not handed out (ordered, or in a file not downloaded) a refund cancelled out of a downloaded file
  (rule 3b's (iv)) bars the line unless it is in the chain of a request **of the same payment** (D7, M's exit:
  that payment's money); `private.refund_transfer_follow` refuses `refund refused: cancelled_transfer_matches` (a new
  code, its hint by the cancelled transfer's kind) and `public.debit_link_options` no longer lists such a refund. For a
  refund in a downloaded or sent file the rule is D's (any payment); the request's-own-chain clause is gone — a
  re-issue's own predecessor is refused there by round 7's rule already (mutant DP1_chain: equivalent). S1b (each
  refund to its payer's IBAN, the line naming the first one's) is the same rule: the line's IBAN makes the cancelled
  refund the candidate. The reviewer's « when the line has an IBAN, require the refund's payee IBAN » is not added: a
  general link rule of M2b, beyond this fix (no state it would change here).
- **DP-2 (the refund link beside a payout or a sweep cancelled after download).** `private.link_debit_guard` let the
  refund link through beside a cancelled payout whose run had ended (iii, OQ-86) and beside a cancelled sweep (iv: the
  sweep exemption of round 7), and D read cancelled refunds only: linked as a refund, the line closed that transfer's
  late debit and released M's hold (the client's next payout: paid twice) or A's and B's (the next share). Fix: the
  refund link is refused `payout_candidate` while rule 3b finds a payout cancelled (not only returned) out of a
  downloaded file, whatever its run's state, or a sweep cancelled so (round 7's sweep exemption stays for a sweep in
  flight); `private.refund_line_barred_by` bars them too, so the trigger refuses (`reissue_in_downloaded_file` for a
  refund in a downloaded file, its hint naming « un reversement » or « un virement au compte propre »;
  `cancelled_transfer_matches` for one not handed out) and the options do not list the refund. OQ-86's exemption stays
  for a payout only returned (`037c` `r_returned_twin`). The return and the loss keep OQ-86's rule beside such a
  candidate (COMPLIANCE OQ-86 (b): refused, a debtor's payment taken back by a debit the bank does not flag would stay
  allocated for good; founder Q7 below). The review's S3 shape — the new sweep S2 in the same downloaded file as the
  refund — is LD-2's: S1 is then no candidate beside S2 and the refund link stays allowed beside the sweep in flight
  (round 7's decision; whichever transfer the line is, the other two lines that follow are booked to the others).
  `039` RF3 pins the shape where no sweep was made since.
- **LD-1 (a re-issue's own execution on a CSV feed, ambiguous for good).** On a feed without the end-to-end column the
  re-issued payout's own line had two candidates, the re-issue (i) and its cancelled predecessor (iii): never booked,
  its file not cancellable (N), the run « en cours » past R124-6 (`debit_unbooked` breach rows, every later run
  `run_pending`). Likewise a re-run payout at the same amount after « Virement refusé par la banque ». Fix:
  `private.transfer_line_candidates` leaves out a cancelled payout (iii) beside an in-flight payout (i) that has it in
  its replaces chain, or whose run holds, not released, an item the cancelled payout's run released — as it already
  left out a returned payout whose item such a run re-pays. The line is proposed and booked as the in-flight payout's
  debit. If it was in fact the predecessor's late execution, the re-issue's own execution comes as a second line with
  the predecessor alone, booked « Virement hors reversement » of it (an advance, OQ-82). COMPLIANCE OQ-80 (q).
- **LD-2 (a re-made sweep's own execution on a CSV feed).** K's (iv) made the sweep D4 re-made at a cancelled sweep's
  amount ambiguous with it, its own line unbookable, A holding it and B stopping the next share. Fix: a cancelled sweep
  (iv) is no candidate beside an in-flight sweep (i) created after its cancellation (same servicer, account, currency
  and amount: rule 3b's); the line books as the in-flight sweep, and the share is proposed again. If it was in fact the
  cancelled sweep's late execution, the in-flight sweep's own line comes with (iv) alone and is booked « Virement au
  compte propre » of the cancelled sweep, A's booked arm then holding the next share.

**Low, fixed.**
- **CSC-1.** `private.debited_cancelled_sweeps` probes the account's cancelled filed transfers by
  `bank_transfer_cancelled_filed_idx`'s own key (the servicer, the account), the kind outside the probe, each one's

## M2c-6b-3a-2: switch-on prerequisites, part 2 — the late predecessor, the switch still off (2026-11-18)

Plan: docs/design/m2c-6b-3-plan.md items E–J, texts T13, T14, T16 (the late predecessor's wording), T17, T18, §3, §5,
§7, §8, §10; m2c-6b-plan §3. Migration `20261118100000_switch_on_prerequisites_2.sql`: one new helper,
`private.transfer_late_predecessor`, and 19 functions redefined whole from their latest definitions (each restating
security definer, every `SET`, `search_path ''` and its grants). **The switch stays off**: no statement writes
`private.feature_switch`; `033` is byte for byte unchanged; `034` and `039` keep every assertion. Every rule below bites
only in states that need a downloaded file's transfer to be cancelled — production has none. With this slice **every
prerequisite of the switch is met** (ROADMAP M2c-6b); 6b-3b is the one-line migration once the founder answers Q1.

### Decisions

- **E — the late predecessor (LP), booked as its run's payout.** `private.transfer_late_predecessor(x)`: x is a payout,
  `cancelled`, of a file downloaded at least once, its run `approved` or `sent`, and the chain of the run's transfer
  (`private.transfer_chain`) holds it — x cancelled alone (the chain is x) or cancelled with its file and re-issued.
  When the bank executes x late (its RMT id, a batch line of its PmtInf in the cancelled file, or a line without our
  references that rule 3b names alone), `transfer_line_check`'s payout branch accepts `payout(x)` and the options propose
  it (classes E, B, U and N; `transfer_line_options_of`): `remit:<x>` (source x) and `settle:<run>` at the line's date,
  the run booked (its R124-6 row at the booking when that date is past L, none when on time), **x stays `cancelled`
  with no entry of its own** (its debit is its `payout` booking's; `bank_booking_post_rows`' booked update skips a
  cancelled transfer). The run's live end y (`remittance_run.transfer_id`) is then withdrawn **before the planned parts**
  (`transfer_line_post`): its file superseded when not downloaded yet (`transfer_file_release`: its other payouts and
  refunds back in the queue, its sweep cancelled, recomputed at the next file), then y cancelled when `ordered`
  (« Réémission annulée : le virement … qu'elle remplace a été débité »). Refused **`reissue_in_downloaded_file`** (the
  file's number as the detail) while y is in a downloaded or sent file — the bank confirms which it executed, that file
  is cancelled on evidence by two people (y re-issued as y2, held), then the line is booked and y2 cancelled; refused
  **`already_debited`** once a transfer of the chain has a payout booking or y is booked or returned. **Locks:** after
  the remit lock `transfer_line_locks` re-reads y and locks its not-downloaded file FOR UPDATE, y and that file's
  transfers joining step 9's keys (a generation commits under the remit lock and takes no run lock); the compare text
  appends `:lp:<y>:<status>:<file or ->` (`transfer_line_text`), so a preview taken before y moved is refused
  `split_changed`. The parts carry `late_predecessor`, `cancels_transfer_id`, `cancels_end_to_end_id`,
  `supersedes_file_number` and `replacement_status` on the LP part only (`transfer_line_parts_json`).
- **F — every reader of « booked » takes the LP as the run's paid transfer:** I20 (`run_payment_checks`: a cancelled
  payout with exactly one payout booking (and at most one return) whose run is booked and holds it in its chain; the run
  booked by it), the deadlines (`pending_item_deadlines`' planned branch and the worker's `HELD_TO_SQL`: the reversed
  entry is its payout booking's), the P0 `payout_returned` (`run_transfer_checks`), the run page
  (`remittance_run_payout`: `late_predecessor`, `repaid_by` through its return booking's entry, its advances through its
  payout booking's entry), the client summary's `returned_runs`, the lot's returnable members
  (`transfer_line_returnable`). « Suivi » follows it with no change (040 F7).
- **G — its return.** `transfer_line_check`'s return branch takes a cancelled payout with exactly one `payout` booking
  as that booking's entry reversed (`tr_entry`); `bank_line_booking_guard` widened to it (`reversed_kind = 'payout'`,
  `reversed_transfer` = the booking's transfer, when the transfer has no entry); the returned update skips a cancelled
  transfer (x stays cancelled); the payout account is returned as for any payout.
- **H — `transfer_file_release`** never re-issues a payout whose run is no longer `approved`/`sent` (booked by its LP)
  nor a refund no longer `requested`: each is cancelled with its file, its reason saying why (defence in depth: no
  command reaches it).
- **I — CPCE-08 (R124-6).** `run_remittance_runs_checks`: a run whose transfer re-issues another (chained) or is itself
  cancelled while the run stays approved or sent is proven unpaid at L only once `statement_covers(least(e0, L), L)` —
  e0 the earliest execution date of its chain's transfers that were in a downloaded file — and no such transfer's
  suppression is `waiting`; `expired` writes the row « bloqué : débit possible non comptabilisé » (`debit_unbooked`).
  A predecessor's late debit may have paid the client on time; the row is append-only.
- **J — OQ-82, founder Q3's default (a).** In `transfer_line_check`, an item an unreversed unplanned booking of another
  transfer attributed, or an earlier part of the same call for another transfer, gets `paid := greatest(net, paid)`: P
  counts it 0 (`p_bound` `items`, the whole of it an advance). The twin `unplanned_p` reads `PoolItem.paid_by_other`
  and `UnplannedAsk.transfer` (`min(0, left)`), with its property oracle and a named example.
- **Texts (pages; both ways true):** T13 (« Débits et retours »: the LP proposal hedged, `run_still_live` pointing at
  « Débit d'un reversement », `reissue_in_downloaded_file` with the file, « déjà débité » naming both transfers), T14
  (the `cancelled_transfer_debited` review by kind: a payout's booked as its run's payout while in flight, else « Virement
  hors reversement »; a refund's never booked yet), T16 (the run page: « (virement annulé, exécuté en retard par la
  banque) »), T17 (the client space: a cancelled run whose transfer the bank refused reads « Annulé : la banque n'a pas
  exécuté son virement (les relevés ne le montraient pas débité) » from `client_remittance_summary.cancelled_runs`
  [{run_id, transfer_outcome: not_executed | never_handed_out}], never from the switch), T18 (« Virements »: « Annulé —
  exécuté en retard par la banque le …, comptabilisé comme le débit de son reversement »), J's sentence (« ont déjà été
  déduites »), « Contrôles »' help for a cancelled payout alerted and its held re-issue.
- **6b-3a's lows:** a **manual** refund's link (no transfer of ours) to a debit naming neither an end-to-end id nor a
  PmtInf is refused in `link_debit_guard` (`payout_candidate`) while `refund_line_barred_by` names a cancelled transfer
  it may be — not only hidden by « Lier »; `cancel_remittance_run`'s `transfer_already_debited` hint names the exit
  (« Comptabiliser… » in « Débits et retours »); « déjà débité » names both transfers. Founder Q7 (COMPLIANCE OQ-86):
  default (a) kept — a return or a loss may still take such a debit.

### Deviations from the plan

- **The switch-on E2E project takes the two screenshots this slice names, and builds no late predecessor** (plan §3.7
  listed four, built on an LP): `m2c-virement-telecharge` retaken with the cancellation card offered, and
  `m2c-annulation-fichier` (the request sheet: what it does, and why it cannot be asked yet — the bank may still execute
  the file until the end of the business day after its execution date). An LP needs a cancellation confirmed, which needs
  that window over and a statement produced after it: real dates still to come in an E2E run. pgTAP 040 builds it. The
  project is **one** serial test (`switch-on`, after desktop and mobile) that opens the phone's context itself: two
  projects (desktop, mobile) ran in parallel under `--no-deps`, and one turned the switch off under the other (seen).
  `remittances.spec.ts` keeps its switch-off assertions on that page and no longer takes its screenshot.
- **The scale fixture is its own file**, `test_transfer_cancellation_scale_integration.py` (the scale job runs every
  `*scale_integration.py`): 5,000 refunds in a downloaded file never executed (the large file's evidence at its worst:
  every transfer's own debit, its PmtInf and the N branch read) beside 40 refunds cancelled with their downloaded file
  and re-issued, 20 of them debited late, the switch on inside one forced-rollback transaction; not the 6a file with
  « 5,000 booked and 50 cancelled » (§3.5): a booked file makes the evidence trivial, and the 6a file's timings stay
  comparable across slices.
- **Not built: the LP worker integration file** (§3.5: the LP through the debit job, G4's `return_differs` review by the
  job, `HELD_TO_SQL`'s parity on an LP, the two-connection LP against generation and download). Consequences, each
  recorded: `HELD_TO_SQL`'s LP branch has no test that fails when it is reverted (its SQL twin is killed by 040 F2); the
  locks' re-read of y (`lp_locks_reread`) survives every single-session test (it only orders locks).
- **The cancelled sweep's batch-line review text** (6b-3a review pages-texts-2) needed no SQL: the job's candidates
  already carry the kind (`_signal`), so the sheet words the sweep's text; vitest pins it. `debit_queue` is not
  redefined.
- **040 F1b** was added during mutation testing: the chain-containment clause of `transfer_late_predecessor` is defence
  in depth (a payout's run never changes), so no reachable state killed its mutant; F1b forges one.

## M2c-6b-3a-2 review fixes (2026-11-19)

### Round 1

Five lenses reviewed `m6b3a2` (`1ecf112`): one high item (CSC-1), six medium (DP-1, DP-2, DP-3, LD-1, LD-2, CSC-2) and
fourteen low (CSC-3, tests-1 … tests-7, pages-texts-1 … pages-texts-6). Each was checked on the main stack first, with
the switch on inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`: every high and medium item reproduced. DP-1 and CSC-1 are one root (a late
predecessor executed as a detail of an entry the bank kept unsplit is invisible to the hold), as are DP-2 and CSC-2
(that entry cannot be booked). Every high and medium item is fixed at its root, tests first; every low one that is a
text, a test, a layout fix or a one-line guard is fixed; the rest is left open below with its default. The migration
`20261118100000` is unmerged and was edited in place: three more functions are redefined there, each copied from its
latest definition (`SECURITY DEFINER` where it was, every `SET`, `search_path ''` and its grants restated) —
`private.transfer_debited_before` (`20261118090000:346`), `private.transfer_late_lines` (`20261117090000:825`),
`private.transfer_cancel_evidence` (`20261118090000:1442`) — two helpers are new, `private.transfer_unsplit_debit_seen`
and `private.transfer_named_debit_on` (EXECUTE revoked from every role: only the `SECURITY DEFINER` callers use them),
and one index, `bank_transaction_unsplit_details_idx` (GIN `jsonb_path_ops` on `unsplit_details`, partial). **The
switch stays off** (no statement writes `private.feature_switch`); `033` is unchanged; `034` and `039` keep every
assertion. Every fix only narrows what is generated, downloaded, cancelled, booked or written, but DP-2, where the
review shows the class-U derivation wrongly refusing the late predecessor's booking that plan E.1 requires (classes E,
B, U and N).

**High and medium.**
- **CSC-1, DP-1 (a late predecessor inside an entry kept unsplit; high).** With two or more details of ours the
  parser keeps the entry unsplit with no end-to-end id of its own; with the bank's charge taken from it no subset of
  the PmtInf makes it. `private.transfer_debited_before` read the line's own id, the reference-less lines (which skip
  unsplit lines) and `batch_debit_may_hold` (which the charge defeats): the re-issues y and yl were not held,
  « Générer » filed them, « Télécharger » handed them out, no alert — both clients paid twice. Fix:
  `private.transfer_unsplit_debit_seen(account, e2e)` — a stored detail (`unsplit_details @> [{id, direction: debit}]`,
  keyed by the new GIN index, the account compared on the lines found) — counts as the transfer's own debit wherever
  its id does: `transfer_debited_before` (a deeper chain member, or the transfer not in a live downloaded file; its
  return not seen: `already_debited` at generation, the download's re-checks and the run's cancellation),
  `transfer_late_lines` (a deeper member or a cancelled transfer: the P0 `cancelled_transfer_debited`, A, B, C, M and
  the siblings' holds through `transfer_late_debit_open`, a return's `debit_pending`), and the cancellation evidence
  (`debit_seen` for the file and for one transfer: never cancelled on that evidence). `private.transfer_debit_seen`
  (the plain R124-6 branch of a live transfer) is unchanged: a live transfer's own detail is booked from
  « Comptabiliser… » (class U) and `transfer_debit_suppression` holds its row `waiting` while the page offers it.
- **DP-2, CSC-2 (the late predecessor as an entry's detail cannot be booked).** `transfer_line_check`'s class-U
  derivation made every cancelled transfer's debit `unplanned_payout` while the options proposed `payout`: the
  proposal, the preview and the command were refused (`unsplit_parts_differ`, `run_still_live`), the run stayed
  approved, 5120 above the bank. Fix: the derivation gives a late predecessor's debit detail `payout`, as
  `transfer_line_options_of` does; the late predecessor's rules then apply as for classes E, B and N (the re-issue
  cancelled or withdrawn, `reissue_in_downloaded_file` while it is handed out). New guard: two debit details of one
  run's payout chain in one entry (a payout and its re-issue, both executed) are `unsplit_not_bookable` — never two
  payouts of one run (the bank's detail, then support).
- **DP-3 (a returned late predecessor executed again).** The late predecessor keeps no return entry: an unplanned
  payout of it had P = 0 and the client's next run paid its returned item again. Fix: an unplanned payout's pool also
  holds the payout_returned bookings' entries of its run's payout chain (the late predecessor's return; a re-issue's,
  E4b's chain): P = A against that item, nothing paid twice. The sheet names those sums (the part's new `run_status`:
  « sommes du reversement … remises à reverser par le retour de son virement »); the worker twin takes the pool as
  its input (its docstring says so).
- **LD-1 (CPCE-08: an on-time predecessor's debit waiting on its re-issue's downloaded file).** The chained branch of
  `run_remittance_runs_checks` held the row back only while « Comptabiliser… » offered the debit's booking: once the
  booking was refused `reissue_in_downloaded_file` past the bound days the debit turned `expired` and a false
  append-only row was written. Fix: `private.transfer_named_debit_on(transfer, L)` — the earliest debit naming a chain
  transfer by our references, dated from its execution date to L, not booked nor linked, its return not seen — holds
  the row back however long the booking waits; its booking writes the true row at its own date. « Naming it » is what
  certainly is that transfer's execution: its own end-to-end id, a detail of an entry kept unsplit carrying it, or a
  batch line of its PmtInf **that certainly holds it** (`batch_line_may_hold`, and the PmtInf's other transfers not
  debited on their own cannot make the line's amount without it). A batch line other transfers can make only may be
  its debit: it keeps Q14's rule (`transfer_debit_suppression`, five business days unless it offers the booking) —
  this narrows the reviewer's « its PmtInf's batch line », which would have held such a line's rows back for good. A
  returned transfer paid nothing: its debit names nothing. COMPLIANCE CPCE-08 says so.
- **LD-2 (CPCE-08: the re-issue's later debit booked by the import while the predecessor's on-time debit waits).**
  Fix (the reviewer's minimum): `bank_booking_post_rows` judges the run's R124-6 rows at the earliest debit naming
  another transfer of its chain (`transfer_named_debit_on`, above) when it predates the line booked as the run's
  payout; `transfer_line_check`'s late flag alike (the sheet and the preview say the same). The job's rule is
  unchanged: it books y's own debit as the run's payout (the run booked at y's date, its own transfer's debit), and x's
  line becomes « Virement hors reversement » (P = 0, the servicer's advance: the double payment, shown with its date on
  the run page and the client's statement). If x came back (its return seen) the rows are judged at y's date (040 «
  LD-2 (a returned predecessor) »). Not done, with its reason: holding the job's booking for review and booking x as
  the late predecessor while y is executed — it would widen what is booked (x as the payout of a run whose transfer y
  left the account too) and need a state for an executed y that is not the run's payout; the minimum makes the
  append-only row true and keeps every amount on the ledger. The job's pure rule is unchanged, so the twin has no new
  property; T13 says what ships (below).

**Low, fixed.**
- **CSC-3, tests-6 (scale).** `test_transfer_cancellation_scale_integration.py` now holds a client's approved run
  whose payout x is filed with the cancelled refunds, cancelled with that file and re-issued; SIZE more refunds are
  ordered, so generation files y with them (a 5,021-transfer file, written by the emulated job), x's late debit
  arrives, the nightly checks read the chained run (I's chained branch, the LP probes), and « Comptabiliser… » on x's
  line (the options and the command) books it as the late predecessor — the generated file withdrawn, y cancelled, the
  run booked, 5,040 refunds ordered again — each timed under 4 s.
- **tests-1 … tests-4.** `040` « J2 (tests-1) », « T17d (tests-2) », « tests-3 (a, b; forged) », « tests-3 (c, d;
  forged) » (I20's other-chain clause pinned by a second payout booking that books y whole), « tests-4 (F4, F5) »
  (repaid_by through the return booking's entry).
- **tests-5 (the switch-on E2E).** `switch-on.spec.ts` now plays the late predecessor through the pages: the file
  dated back with psql on the local stack only (as pgTAP's backdate), a statement of its days produced after them
  imported through the page, the cancellation asked (desktop) and confirmed (phone) by two ops managers, x's own debit
  on today's statement, booked from « Débits et retours » « Comptabiliser… » as its run's payout; read back: one
  `payout` booking of x, x and y cancelled, the run booked; the run page names x's reference. Screenshots

**ld2-reissue-return-pays-twice (medium, reproduced).** The run's payout chain executed twice — the re-issue y booked by
the import as the run's payout, the predecessor x booked « Virement hors reversement » (P = 0, the servicer's advance) —
then y came back: `transfer_unplanned_open(y)` read only y's own unplanned bookings, so the return was proposed (and,
when x was booked before the return arrived, booked by the import) as the run's `payout_returned`: the run's sums owed
again while the client kept x's copy and the advance stayed open — the client's next run paid 1 640 € a second time.
The refusal `debit_pending`'s promise (« ce retour sera alors celui du virement hors reversement ») was false.
Fix (the reviewer's first and second options together, critic F1 over the run's chain): the transfers of a run's chain
are copies of one payment; the copy that comes back closes an open « Virement hors reversement » first.
- `private.transfer_chain_unplanned(t)`: the other transfers of t's run chain whose open unplanned payouts a return of t
  closes — t is the run's payout (a payout booking of it, its entry not reversed: the booked re-issue or a late
  predecessor), or its own unplanned copy was closed by another transfer's return (both copies came back); and t has no
  unplanned payout of its own still open (that one closes first, as before).
- `private.transfer_unplanned_open` and `private.transfer_line_open_unplanned` read them: the job's facts say
  `unplanned_open` (the import never books such a return: review `unplanned_payout_return`, its SQL re-check alike), the
  command refuses the run's `payout_returned` (`unplanned_open`), « Comptabiliser… » proposes
  `unplanned_payout_returned` of the return's own transfer closing the other copy (largest advance first, as before);
  the check finds that booking through the chain; `bank_line_booking_guard` accepts an `unplanned_payout_returned`
  reversing an unplanned payout of another payout of the same run. The reversal is the existing one (the copy's entry and
  its advance): nothing is re-owed, the advance closes, the run stays paid.
- Both copies coming back would then have left the second return unbookable (x cancelled, its copy closed, no payout of
  its own: `transfer_cancelled`; 5120 above the bank): `private.transfer_return_partner(m)` names the run's payout p whose
  return closed m's copy while p's payout stands, and m's return is proposed and booked as p's `payout_returned` (on m's
  line, naming m; the class-E check accepts the line of such a partner) — the run's sums owed again, as they are. Read only
  once no other copy is open (a third copy closes first). This widens what is booked only in the states this fix creates:
  before it, the same sequence booked y's return as the run's payout and x's return as x's own copy's.
- Pages (both ways true): the part carries `closes_end_to_end_id` or `returned_end_to_end_id` (keys only then); the sheet
  says « Ce retour du virement y solde le virement x du même reversement, exécuté hors reversement le … : le client garde
  l'un des deux virements et n'a reçu ce reversement qu'une fois », and for the partner « Le virement x du même
  reversement, exécuté hors reversement, revient aussi … ce retour-ci est donc celui du reversement »; the run page's
  unplanned entry carries `returned_by_end_to_end_id` (« Le virement y de ce reversement est revenu depuis : son retour
  solde ce virement hors reversement … »); `unplanned_open`, `debit_pending` and the job's `return_debit_pending` name
  « un autre virement du même reversement ». The job's `unplanned_payout_return` text is unchanged (pinned by
  `transfer-line-pages.test.ts`; still true: the run's payout was executed outside its order).
- Labels, recorded: the books close the unplanned copy even when the bank returned the run's payout's own transfer (y
  came back, the books keep y as the run's payout and close x's copy) — the money is the same either way (two copies of
  one amount to one client), as critic F1 already treated two executions of one transfer; the pages name both transfers.

**ld2-named-debit-returned-after-booking (medium, reproduced; CPCE-08).** Round 1 held a booked run's R124-6 rows to the
earliest debit naming another transfer of its chain when the import booked the re-issue (`bank_booking_post_rows`); when
that earlier transfer came back afterwards (a recall, a return) nothing judged the rows again — the client was paid by y
alone, after L, and no row was ever written. Fix (the reviewer's second option, the nightly I-branch):
`run_remittance_runs_checks` first takes the booked runs whose chain holds a payout cancelled out of a downloaded file
(by `bank_transfer_cancelled_filed_idx`), once a statement shows the return of a transfer of the chain and while the
run's payout stands (its payout booking's entry not reversed: a run whose payout came back has its sums owed again and
their rows are the queue's, « bloqué : virement revenu impayé »), and judges their rows at
`private.remittance_run_paid_on(run)` — the earliest debit of a transfer of the chain that stayed paid
(`transfer_named_debit_on(…, p_booked => true)`: its own id, an unsplit detail, a batch line that certainly holds it, or
the line booked as its payout or « Virement hors reversement » — rule 3b's line included; its return not seen) — the
insert `bank_booking_post_rows` makes (unmeetable delays at their one-month date), `on conflict do nothing`. Every order is
covered: x's return seen after y's booking (l4) and after x's own bookings; and the reverse made by the first item (y on
time, x after L, y's return closing x's copy — the client was paid by x, late: the row). A return carries the fact; the
nightly check writes the row the day after the statement, whether or not ops book the lines. Recorded in COMPLIANCE
CPCE-08 with its default (a recalled or returned transfer paid nothing). **Corrected in round 3** (below): « a batch line
that certainly holds it » did not hold once that line was booked — a batch line booked as the payouts of several of its
PmtInf's members was dropped by the « not booked » filter (another member's booking sits on it), so a re-issue debited
in such a line never counted; and « its return not seen » read only a credit carrying the transfer's id as its own or
original, so « every order is covered » held only for returns on a line of their own — a return kept unsplit (several
of our details, or our lot's PmtInfId) or sent as a lot credit was never seen, and no row was written.

- A return the bank sends without our reference (rule 3b's return to an unplanned payout's IBAN) closes a copy in the
  books but is not a « return seen » for `remittance_run_paid_on` (it reads the transfer's own id): the row may be missing
  (COMPLIANCE CPCE-08).
- Round 1's open lows stay so (pages-texts-2, tests-6's N-runs fixture, 6b-3a's founder Q7).

**paid-on-misses-lot-lines-and-return-shapes (medium, reproduced; CPCE-08).** Two roots, both in what
`remittance_run_paid_on` and the nightly booked branch read.
- *A batch line booked for several members.* `transfer_named_debit_on`'s « not booked » filter kept a line only when
  every booking on it was this transfer's own debit. A batch line of F2's PmtInf booked as the payouts of y and of Lilas'
  yl (a bank ignoring BtchBookg false, OQ-83) holds yl's booking too, so y's debit never counted: in ldl1 (y debited
  after L in that line, x's on-time copy booked « Virement hors reversement » and then returned) the paid date was null
  and no row was ever written, though the client was paid by y alone, late. Fix: with `p_booked`, a line holding this
  transfer's own `payout` or `unplanned_payout` booking counts whatever else is booked on it — the bookings of a line add
  up to its amount (`bank_line_booking_complete`), so none claims the line against this transfer's. Without `p_booked`
  nothing changes (the chained branch, `bank_booking_post_rows`, the check's late flag).
- *A return not on a line of its own.* « Its return not seen » and the nightly's « a return of the chain seen » read
  `transfer_return_seen` only: a credit carrying the transfer's id as its own or original. A return the bank sends as an
  entry kept unsplit holding two of our details, or naming our lot by its PmtInfId (the parser then keeps no original id
  for the others), or as a lot credit of its PmtInf (no end-to-end id), was never seen: in rs5 (y and yl back in one
  entry kept unsplit, y's return closing x's late copy), rs6 (y's return as a lot credit, closing x's late copy) and rs2
  (x's on-time copy back as a detail) ops book the line as proposed and no row was ever written. Fix:
  `private.transfer_return_known(t)` — `transfer_return_seen(t)`; or a stored detail carrying t's id as a credit, on its
  account (by `bank_transaction_unsplit_details_idx`; booked or not: the bank's statement says it came back); or a
  `payout_returned` / `unplanned_payout_returned` booking of t on a credit line that carries no end-to-end id and names
  t's own PmtInf (a lot credit: the booking names the member that came back; a swap's booking — round 2's return closing
  another copy — is the returning transfer's, so its transfer is the one that came back). A partner's booking (the run's
  payout returned on the other copy's own-id line, round 2) is never counted for the booking's transfer: that line
  carries the copy's id (and at most the copy's PmtInf, never the booking's transfer's) — the reviewer's « the line's
  returned id », which `transfer_return_seen` reads (**corrected in round 4**: only when the bank flagged the line a
  `return`; an unflagged one, `client_transfer_in` from the client's IBAN under the copy's id, was never read — round 4
  counts it). A booking on an entry kept unsplit is one of its details
  (`unsplit_parts_differ`): the detail arm reads it. A debit detail is never a return (the detail's direction: rs8).
  It is read by `transfer_named_debit_on` with `p_booked` (`remittance_run_paid_on`) and by the nightly booked branch
  only: the nightly judges the run again once the return is known, at the earliest debit of a transfer of the chain
  that stayed paid, as round 2 does.

**One rule over the run's payout chain (r4-guidance; new:return-known-misses-unflagged-own-id-return,
new:paid-on-ignores-debits-outnumbering-returns, both medium; CPCE-08).**
- *The events* (`private.remittance_chain_events(run's transfer, line, line's transfer)`): every line of the
  statements that executes or returns a transfer of the chain (`private.transfer_chain`: the run's transfer, then each
  transfer it re-issues), once per transfer, at its booking date. Executions: a debit on the transfer's account, dated
  from its requested execution date, carrying its end-to-end id as its own or original; a debit entry kept unsplit
  holding a detail of it; a batch line of its PmtInf in a downloaded file that certainly holds it (round 1's test); a
  line holding its `payout` or `unplanned_payout` booking (round 2's lines booked as its own debit, a rule-3b line among
  them; round 3's batch line booked for several members); and the line being booked or previewed as its payout. Not a
  line booked or linked otherwise, a payment, nor a CSV line held as a suspected duplicate and not released. Returns: a
  credit on its account carrying its end-to-end id as its own or original whose kind is `return`, `client_transfer_in`
  or `own_transfer_in` — the kinds a return part sits on (`transfer_line_check`): **the bank's unflagged return from the
  client's payout IBAN under our RMT id is one** (new:return-known-misses-unflagged-own-id-return) —, a credit detail of
  an entry kept unsplit (round 3), a lot credit of its PmtInf booked as its return (round 3); booked or not, but a
  payment or an unreleased suspected duplicate. A return counts for the transfer whose reference it carries, whatever
  booking it closes (round 2's return closing another copy, its partner booked as the run's payout returned on the
  copy's line): the copy that came back paid nothing. A return carrying none of our references (rule 3b) is not counted
  (it may be either copy's: round 2's default, rs7), nor a lot credit not booked yet (it names no member: round 3).
- *The rule* (`private.remittance_chain_paid`): per transfer, its events in date order (an execution before a return
  on one date — a same-day return undoes that day's execution), counted; a return with nothing outstanding undoes
  nothing (its execution is on no line counted here); the transfer is paid from the first date from which its
  executions outnumber its returns for the rest of what the statements show, never when every execution came back; the
  run is paid from the earliest such date of its chain (`paid_on`, null when no transfer stayed paid); `returned` says a
  return of the chain is on the statements. A transfer executed again after its return (n2a, n2b), or more often than it
  came back (n2d, fr1, n2f's y), stays paid (new:paid-on-ignores-debits-outnumbering-returns: rounds 1–3 dropped every
  debit of a transfer as soon as one return of it was seen).
- *Its readers*: `private.bank_booking_post_rows` judges a run whose chain holds another transfer at the chain's paid
  date with the line being booked counted as its payout's execution — this line's date when no transfer stayed paid, as
  before; a run with no other transfer keeps its line's date (production: inert). The late flag of
  `private.transfer_line_check` reads the same with the previewed line (the sheet and the preview say what the booking
  will write). The chained branch of `private.run_remittance_runs_checks` never proves a run unpaid at L while its chain
  paid the client by L and stayed paid (round 1's « named debit »). Its booked branch judges a booked run whose chain
  holds a payout cancelled out of a downloaded file again at the paid date once a return of the chain is on the
  statements, its payout standing (round 2), `private.remittance_run_paid_on` reading the rule.
- *Per transfer, not over the chain as a whole* (a narrower reading of the guidance's « executions − returns over the
  run's whole transfer chain », which its own constraint settles: « each earlier round's case keeps its expectation »).
  Counted over the chain at once, ldl1 (round 3: x on time, returned; y after L) would read « paid from x's date »,
  since y's execution came before x's return — no row, against round 3's expectation and the fact: x came back, so it
  paid nothing, and the client was paid by y alone, late. So would rs2 and n2f (x paid then returned, y late). Each
  return undoes an execution of the transfer it names; the run is paid from the earliest date one copy stayed with the
  client. The test's oracle and the code read it so.
- *Which execution a return undoes* (default, COMPLIANCE CPCE-08): of two executions of one transfer and one return,
  the earlier execution is the one kept (the duplicate is the one that comes back) — the « stays ≥ 1 from » reading of
  the guidance. pgTAP `040`'s « lifo » case pins it (x on time and after L, one return: no row); its FIFO mutant fails.
- What it changes: nothing is cancelled, re-issued, booked, linked or paid differently; only the append-only R124-6 rows
  of runs whose chain holds a cancelled or re-issued payout (written by the booking, the chained and the booked nightly
  branches) and the sheet's late flag follow the rule. The booking may now judge its rows at a date after its own
  line's — when its own transfer came back and was executed again — the date the client was paid.
