  3. A return without our references (rule 3b) is not a known return.

## M2c-6b-3b part 1: the last switch-on prerequisites, the switch still off (2026-11-20)

Plan: ADR-0014 « M2c-6b-3a-2 review fixes » « Open after round 4 » (its fix and its not-done list), COMPLIANCE CPCE-08's
6b-3a-2 notes, docs/design/m2c-6b-3-plan.md items E (§3.5, the late predecessor's worker integration file) and I.
Migration `20261119090000_switch_on_prerequisites_3.sql`: three internal helpers are new —
`private.transfer_debit_lines`, `private.remittance_chain_holds` and `private.remittance_chain_rows`, EXECUTE revoked
from every role — and four functions are redefined whole from their latest definitions across all the migration files
(each restating `SECURITY DEFINER` where it was, every `SET`, `search_path ''` and its grants):
`private.transfer_debit_suppression` (`20261117113000:175`), `private.bank_booking_post_rows` (`20261118100000:2344`),
`private.transfer_line_check` (`20261118100000:801`) and `private.run_remittance_runs_checks` (`20261118100000:3889`);
`private.remittance_chain_events` gets its comment corrected (`COMMENT ON FUNCTION`, its body unchanged). No public
signature changed (`database.types.ts` regenerated: unchanged); no Python or web code changed. **The switch stays off**:
no statement writes `private.feature_switch`; `033` is byte for byte unchanged; `034`, `039` and `040` keep every
assertion. Every rule below bites only for a run whose payout chain holds another transfer (a payout cancelled out of a
downloaded file and re-issued, or a late predecessor booked while its re-issue exists) — with the switch off no chain is
created, so production has none.

### Decisions

- **booking-rows-skip-chain-coverage-and-waiting-lines (medium once the switch is on; CPCE-08) — the holds at the
  booking.** For a run whose chain holds another transfer, `private.bank_booking_post_rows` writes the R124-6 rows of
  the lines late at the chain's paid date (`private.remittance_chain_paid`, round 4's rule, the line being booked
  counted as the payout's execution) only through `private.remittance_chain_rows`: only for each line whose two holds
  pass at its own date L (its latest execution date, or the one-month date of its collection for a delay that cannot be
  met, as before) — `private.remittance_chain_holds`: (a) *covered*: the paying account's statements cover [least(e0,
  L), L] (`private.statement_covers`), e0 the earliest execution date of the chain's transfers handed out (an item of a
  file downloaded at least once), the nightly chained branch's own reading since 6b-3a-2 (I); (b) *not waiting*: no
  other transfer of the chain handed out (never the one the run is booked by) has a line dated by L that may be its
  debit (`private.transfer_debit_lines`, the very lines `private.transfer_debit_suppression` reads) and that the chain's
  rule does not count yet as one of its executions. Else no row then: the nightly booked branch writes it once both
  hold. A run with no other transfer: as before (the 5,000 payouts of the scale fixture, production).
- **The nightly booked branch judges such a run whenever it has a late line without a row.**
  `private.run_remittance_runs_checks`' booked branch now takes every booked run whose chain holds a payout cancelled
  out of a downloaded file, its payout standing (the transfer of its chain whose `payout` booking's entry is not
  reversed: a run whose payout came back has its sums owed again, their rows the queue's, round 2), at the chain's paid
  date, and writes the rows of its lines late then that have none yet and whose holds pass —
  `private.remittance_chain_rows` with the holds *decided*, as `private.transfer_debit_suppression` decides them (Q14's
  rule): such a line waits while younger than the bound days or while it offers that transfer's booking; past them
  offering none, the row is written « bloqué : débit possible non comptabilisé » (`debit_unbooked`). Rows append-only,
  each item's written once (`on conflict do nothing`; only runs with a late line without a row are judged). Round 2's
  filter « once a return of the chain is on the statements » is dropped: the booking may now leave rows to this branch
  with no return in sight (S1, S2c). Dropping it adds no row for a run the booking judged with both holds passing:
  without a return the paid date only ever moves earlier (round 2's equivalent mutant).
- **The sheet says what the booking writes.** `private.transfer_line_check`'s late flag (`late`, `late_date`) for a
  payout part of such a run reads the same `private.remittance_chain_rows`, the previewed line counted as its execution
  and never as a possible debit of another transfer (once booked it is none): « le dépassement du délai est enregistré »
  only when the booking records it (S1's and S3's sheets say on time while the statements do not cover L; S4's says late
  although the previewed line has x's amount).
- **Uncertain lines only (a narrower reading of the verifier's « no chain transfer other than the line's own is
  'waiting' »).** A line carrying a chain transfer's id, a detail of an entry kept unsplit, a batch line that certainly
  holds it, or a line booked as its payout or « Virement hors reversement » is already one of its executions (or
  returns) in round 4's rule, booked or not: holding the rows back for it would change nothing but their day — and
  `040`'s n1c/n1d, whose booking writes its row while x's on-time own-id debit and its return wait for ops, would no
  longer (house rule R3). The lines that hold are those the rule cannot count yet: a line without our references, a
  batch line other transfers of the PmtInf can make, a line held as a suspected duplicate (`040`'s « dup »), a line of
  its amount to its payee with a reference not ours (`transfer_debit_suppression`'s rule 3b lines).
- **At the booking, a possible debit is never decided (default, recorded).** Telling 'waiting' from 'expired' needs the
  options of each old line (`private.transfer_line_offers` → `private.transfer_line_options_of`, which rebuild
  `pg_temp._tl` and its working tables); the booking runs inside `private.transfer_line_post`, which reads `pg_temp._tl`
  after `bank_booking_post_rows`, so it cannot call them (its mutant raises « cannot DROP TABLE _tl because it is being
  used by active queries »). Any such line therefore holds the booking's rows back, and the nightly check decides the
  next night (S2c's control « expired »: the row `debit_unbooked` from the nightly check). The rows only ever come
  later, never different. COMPLIANCE CPCE-08 records it as a default, not a legal rule.
- **`private.transfer_debit_lines`** is `private.transfer_debit_suppression`'s predicate moved into a helper unchanged,
  so the holds and the suppression read the same lines; the suppression loops over it, newest first, as before (no
  assertion of `037`–`040` moved).
- **The three survivors of round 4 are killed**, each by a `041` case that fails on its mutant: (a) a line naming a
  transfer of the chain booked or linked otherwise counted — « round 4's survivor (a), forged » (x's own-id debit on
  time linked as a payer's return, forged with the link guard off: no command books or links such a line otherwise —
  classes E, B, U, `link_debit_guard`; y after L booked by the import: the row at the booking); (b) the previewed line
  not counted — « round 4's survivor (b) » (reachable: y's on-time execution without our references previewed as its
  payout while x's own-id debit after L is on the statement: the sheet says on time, the booking writes no row); (c) the
  requested-execution-date bound dropped — « round 4's survivor (c), forged dates » (x's own-id debit dated before x's
  requested execution date is not its execution: the row at y's booking).
- **The late predecessor's worker integration file** (`worker/tests/test_switch_on_late_predecessor_integration.py`, 4
  tests, the local stack only). The switch is turned on only inside the one transaction that asks (the ops manager) and
  confirms (an admin) F1's cancellation, and off again before it commits; an autouse fixture turns it off whatever
  happens, and each test asserts it off. F1 is dated back two business days with psql (as pgTAP's backdate), and an
  empty camt.053 of those days, produced by the bank today, goes through the real import. Then: x's late debit through
  the import — the debit job reviews it `cancelled_transfer_debited` (never booked automatically), « Comptabiliser… »
  proposes and books the late predecessor (the run booked, y cancelled, x cancelled with no entry); G4 — x's return
  through the import, reviewed `return_differs` by the job and never booked by it, then booked as proposed (« Virement
  revenu » of x: the run's sums owed again); `HELD_TO_SQL`'s parity on the late predecessor — the item x's return put
  back is held to x's run's line in the worker (`_held_to`), in `private.pending_item_deadlines` and on the draft's
  line; two connections against a generation (a generation holding the remit lock files y and yl into F2 while the
  booking, its sheet read with y ordered, waits; once it commits the booking re-reads y after the remit lock and locks
  every transfer of F2 — it waits on a key-share lock a third session holds on yl — and is refused `split_changed`; a
  fresh sheet books it, F2 superseded, y cancelled, yl back in the queue); two connections against the download of F2,
  each first (the download first hands y out: the booking waits on its run lock and is refused
  `reissue_in_downloaded_file`; the booking first withdraws F2: the download waits and is refused). No deadlock; y is
  never handed out and cancelled.
- **Round 4's low (« Comptabiliser… » proposes nothing for round 2's partner sent as an entry kept unsplit,
  `transfer_cancelled`, rnd08): recorded, not fixed.** The partner (`private.transfer_return_partner`) is accepted on
  the transfer's own line (class E) only. For an entry kept unsplit, the class-U parts are derived detail by detail with
  the detail's own transfer (`_tl_u` in `private.transfer_line_check`, its twin in `private.transfer_line_options_of`),
  so booking the detail as the partner's `payout_returned` needs both derivations widened and the sheet's copy id
  (`returned_end_to_end_id`) carried for class U: not a one-line guard or proposal. Default: the support books it — an
  unusual bank shape on top of a run paid twice and returned twice (round 2's open low); the R124-6 rows still follow
  the rule (the return is counted from the statement's detail), as `040`'s and `041`'s properties check.

### Deviations from the plan

- The holds are the uncertain lines only, and undecided at the booking (above).
- The lock re-read's mutant (`lp_locks_reread`, plan §2 E: y read before the remit lock) is killed by a lock wait, not
  by an outcome: in every interleaving the product can produce, a booking that collected its keys before a generation
  moved y is refused `split_changed` by its compare text whether or not it re-read y — every writer of y's file
  (generation, download, regeneration, cancellation) takes the remit lock or the run locks the booking holds first. The
  re-read orders the locks; the test observes the order (the booking waits on a lock held on another transfer of y's new
  file).
- The integration file builds its late predecessor through the public cancellation commands with the switch on for one
  transaction, not through the pages (the switch-on E2E project does that, without a late predecessor: 6b-3a-2's
  deviation, unchanged); plan §3.7's other switch-on screenshots stay with 6b-3b (no page changed here).

### Assertions whose expected value changed (house rule R3)

None: `015`–`040` unchanged (`033` byte for byte).

## M2c-6b-3b part 1 review fixes (2026-11-21)

### Round 1

The review of `f66b9fc` raised two medium items and five lows; each medium was reproduced first on the main stack, the
switch on inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` only, on `f66b9fc`'s bodies (the reviewer's shapes rebuilt as `041` cases, and a
scratch race script before them). The migration `20261119090000` is unmerged and was edited in place: three internal
helpers are new — `private.remittance_chain_hold_facts`, `private.remittance_inflight_facts` and
`private.remittance_inflight_judge` (EXECUTE revoked from every role) —, `private.remittance_chain_holds` and
`private.remittance_chain_rows` (new in this migration) take the caller's paid date, and the booking, its sheet and the
nightly check pass it. No public signature changed (`database.types.ts` regenerated: unchanged); no web code changed;
only a worker test changed. **The switch stays off**; `033` is byte for byte unchanged; `034`, `039` and `040` keep every
assertion.

**nightly-null-paid-date-skips-standing-run (medium; CPCE-08).** The nightly booked branch judged a run only at the
chain's paid date and dropped it when that date was null, though its booking judges such a run at its own line's date
(`coalesce(remittance_chain_paid(…), line date)`). Since 6b-3b part 1 the booking may leave the rows to the nightly check
(the statements not covering [least(e0, L), L] yet), so a return of the paying transfer reaching the statements before
the cover — y's unflagged return under its RMT id, or the late predecessor x's flagged return, which the debit job only
reviews (`return_differs`) — left a run paid after L, or not at all, with no row, while the other statement order wrote
it. Reproduced (`041` n1r, n3r on `f66b9fc`'s bodies: `[]` at every nightly check, the payout standing; n1c, n3c — the
cover before the return — `["none"]`). Fixed: the
booked branch's standing payout lateral also reads that booking's line date, and the run is judged at
`coalesce(paid_on, line date)` — in the late-lines filter and in `private.remittance_chain_rows` — as the booking judges
it: the same row whichever of the return and the cover arrives first, once (append-only). A payout that came back and was
booked so (`payout_returned`, its entry reversed) still leaves its sums' rows to the queue (S7, unchanged). The test's
rule over time (`pg_temp.pc2_rule`) had the same gap (the booked line's day only at the booking's statement): corrected to
read it whenever the run's payout stands — no expectation of the earlier property cases moved, and with the correction
alone (on `f66b9fc`'s bodies) the new shape and the interleaving rnd03 fail.

**chain-holds-snapshot-race (medium once the switch is on; and, found while fixing it, the same race in the in-flight
branch of every run, the switch off — production since 6b-2c; CPCE-08).** A reader judged the run's paid date in its own
statement's snapshot (`private.remittance_chain_paid` is STABLE) and the holds read the coverage, the counted executions
and the possible debits in later snapshots (`remittance_chain_holds` and `remittance_chain_rows` are VOLATILE: a fresh
snapshot per query under READ COMMITTED): an import of the earlier statement, or ops booking the predecessor's line
without our references, committed in between made the holds pass on facts the paid date did not see, and an append-only
row was written for a run the chain paid on time. Reproduced with the reviewer's rename-and-wrapper injection (A: the
import as the booking's holds start, `["none"]`; C: the same as the nightly check's holds start; D: S2c's shape, ops'
« Virement hors reversement » of x as the nightly check's holds start; each `["none"]`) and, beyond the reviewer's,
three more: D2 (that booking committed as the nightly check asks whether the line offers x's booking, after the holds'
read: the row « bloqué : débit possible non comptabilisé »), IA (the in-flight branch of a chained run, y ordered: ops book x's on-time line as the
late predecessor as the branch's suppression of x starts: `["none"]`) and IB (the in-flight branch of a run with no other
transfer, the switch off: ops book its own payout's on-time line without our references as the suppression starts:
`["none"]` — a false row today in production, its reach one worker and one ordinary ops action during the nightly
check). Fixed with one rule for every reader that writes an R124-6 row from the holds or the suppression, rather than
serialising (the import's advisory lock, the transfers FOR SHARE: the reviewer's alternative, which neither covers a link
or a duplicate's release nor avoids new lock orders inside the booking):
- *One snapshot.* The facts a judgement rests on are read by one STABLE function, whose queries all read the snapshot of
  the query that calls it: `private.remittance_chain_hold_facts` (the coverage, the chain's paid date, and the possible
  debits of the chain's other transfers handed out that its rule does not count yet — read in that snapshot too: read in
  a later one, as the reviewer's preferred fix kept them, a line booked meanwhile would drop out of them uncounted) and
  `private.remittance_inflight_facts` (the run still in flight, its transfer and file, and — chained — the coverage of
  [least(e0, L), L], whether the chain paid by L and stayed paid, the lines that may be a debit of its transfers handed out
  by L; — not chained — whether its transfer is handed out and not seen debited with L covered, and then the lines that
  may be its debit by L).
- *The caller's paid date.* `private.remittance_chain_holds` takes the chain's paid date the caller judged the run at (its
  own statement's read, null when no copy stayed) and waits when the facts' paid date is another: something committed
  since the caller's snapshot; the nightly check judges the run again on facts read together (A, C, D).
- *Read again after the options.* A decision that rests on `private.transfer_line_offers` (VOLATILE: the options build
  their working tables) — 'expired', the row « bloqué : débit possible non comptabilisé », or the in-flight branch's proof
  past the bound days — stands only if the facts read again afterwards have not moved (D2; IA2 and IB2, the same booking
  committed as the in-flight branch asks the options): an import or a booking that lands between the two reads is seen by
  the second.
- *The in-flight branch* (`private.run_remittance_runs_checks`' `olc`): its rule is unchanged — 6b-2c's for a run with no
  other transfer, 6b-3a-2 (I) and round 4's for a chained one — and now judged per run and date by
  `private.remittance_inflight_judge` on `private.remittance_inflight_facts` (IA, IB; `037`'s, `039`'s and `040`'s cases
  of the branch pass unchanged). A run no longer in flight in the facts' snapshot is not proven (defence in depth: a
  booking that makes it so also moves the facts it is judged on).
- What it changes: no row that the facts support is lost — a reader that waits leaves the row to the next nightly check,
  which judges it on facts read together; nothing is booked, linked or paid differently.

**tests-1, tests-2, tests-3 (low): fixed by tests.** `041` « tests-1 »: R-A (y's own debit after L booked before d2 … d3

## M2c-6b-3b part 1 — CI round (PR #38) (2026-11-21)

**The failure.** CI run 44850889494, job « Database (migrations, pgTAP) », step « Worker integration tests »:
`test_a_batch_line_of_2000_members_is_re_checked_in_linear_time_and_memory` failed its bound (40 rows per row of the
job × 2,001 + 2,000 = 82,040 rows per statement), the facts' statement of `private.post_bank_bookings` (`create temp
table _bb …`) handling 338,170 rows. The same commit passed the same job in the dispatched run 44850891917, and a fresh
reset locally (22,012 rows). Nothing in PR #38 touches that function or a table it reads.

**Root cause: the plan, chosen from the statistics the suite leaves.** Reproduced on the main stack in CI's order
(`supabase db reset`, `supabase test db`, the two integration files before the batch test: it passed there, as in the
next CI run), then exactly: `vacuum analyze` of `bank_transaction` and `ledger_entry` gave three of CI's figures
(44,036; 34,015; 32,038), and `vacuum full` of `ledger_entry` (its 144 committed rows in 7 pages) with
`random_page_cost` 5 the fourth (338,170), each to the row. Two keyed reads of the facts ran as
sequential scans once per row of the job: the lateral read of `bank_transaction` by the row's line (15 rows each time,
+28,014) and the correlated read of `ledger_entry` by the transfer's entry (`tr_entry_date`: 144 rows each time, all
removed by the filter — an `in_file` transfer has no entry —, +288,144); the bank-account lock's lateral read
`bank_transaction` the same way (44,036 rows; 16,012 by key). Each table's scan was priced below one probe of its
primary key — tables vacuumed back to a few pages after the pgTAP suite, their keys left bloated by its rolled-back rows
—; with autovacuum at other times the index plan won. « Flake » was the timing of autovacuum, not the cause: every keyed
read of the re-check had the same exposure, the one PR #33's CI scale fix left open (« the job's own `_bb` build and
payments lock in `private.post_bank_bookings` », above). With a probe priced at 1,000 sequential pages, the facts handled
8.3 million rows and the keys, the files' lock and the batch rule 4 million each: the batch line's 2,000 transfers of
`bank_transfer`, and their file items, scanned once per member.

**Fix** (in place in the unmerged `20261119090000`, its last section; behaviour unchanged, only the plans): the re-check —
the keys, the locks, the facts and the rules' verdicts, everything before the posting — moved verbatim into
`private.bank_booking_recheck(org)` (new: SECURITY DEFINER, `set enable_seqscan = off`, EXECUTE revoked from every
role), which `private.post_bank_bookings` (redefined from its latest definition, `20261117100000`, settings and grants
restated) calls first. As `private.transfer_line_bb` (the ops' copy of the same facts) and `private.transfer_line_locks`
since PR #33's CI scale fix, every lateral and correlated read of a stored table by its key is a probe of its index
whatever the statistics; the job's temporary tables are read whole as before; the posting (`bank_booking_post_rows`)
keeps its callers' settings. Same rows, the same locks in the same order and strength, the same verdicts: inlining the
helper back gives the old body line for line. At 2,000 members, under both cost settings: the facts 22,012 rows, the
keys 32,010, the batch rule 40,014, the bank-account lock 24,016 (its union sorted, no longer hashed: 8,004 more, linear).

**Test** (`worker/tests/test_debit_bookings_batch_rules_integration.py`; the existing test unchanged and passing):
`test_the_re_check_reads_by_key_whatever_the_statistics` — the same batch line, verdicts and per-statement bound, with
`random_page_cost` 1,000 (a probe of a key index priced above a scan of any table the re-check reads, as CI's statistics
priced it for its small tables), and no stored table scanned once per row of the job. Deterministic: it fails on the old
body after a fresh reset as after the suite — the facts 8.0 million rows, 16 scans of stored tables repeated once per row
(18 after the suite), those of `bank_transfer` and `transfer_file_item` 4 million rows each — and passes on the new (the
old body applied over the new one in place, then `supabase db reset`). It runs in the `db` job, in a few seconds.

**Suites** (the main stack alone): `supabase test db` after `supabase db reset` — **Files=43, Tests=2,882, PASS**; then,
without a reset (CI's order), the integration tests but the scale files — **242 passed** (241 and the new test);
`database.types.ts` regenerated: unchanged (the new function is internal). Worker: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check
.`, `mypy` (179 files) clean; unit pytest 1,093 passed, 5 xfailed. The payouts' bookings scale file once right after
`supabase db reset`: **5 passed** (782.8 s; the 5,000-member batch line's funds pass 20.3 s, the debit job 19.1 s — within
the earlier rounds' spread, `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md` « M2c-6b-3b part 1 — CI round (PR #38) »). No web code
changed.

## M2c-6b-3b part 2: the held-rows alert and the booking guard's plans, the switch still off (2026-11-21)

Plan: founder question 2 of « M2c-6b-3b part 1 » (its default: « remittance_breach_held » before the switch-on), round 1's
low booked-chained-rows-held-without-alert, and PR #38's known limit on `private.bank_line_booking_guard()` (PROGRESS).
Migration `20261121090000_switch_on_prerequisites_4.sql`: two internal helpers are new —
`private.remittance_booked_chain_runs` and `private.remittance_breach_held`, EXECUTE revoked from every role — and two
functions are redefined whole from their latest definitions across all the migration files (each restating `SECURITY
DEFINER` where it was, every `SET`, `search_path ''` and its grants): `private.run_remittance_runs_checks`
(`20261119090000:1552`) and `private.bank_line_booking_guard` (`20261118100000:2595`). No public signature changed
(`database.types.ts` regenerated: unchanged); no Python product code changed. **The switch stays off**: no statement
writes `private.feature_switch`; `033` is byte for byte unchanged; `015`–`041` keep every assertion.

### Decisions

- **« remittance_breach_held » (CPCE-08; an operational safeguard, not a legal deadline).** Since 6b-3b part 1 the R124-6
  rows of a booked run whose payout chain holds another transfer wait while the paying account's statements do not cover
  [least(e0, L), L] or a line that may be another transfer's debit waits (`private.remittance_chain_holds`). The nightly
  checks now raise an alert of the existing kind on every such run: `payment_check_result` code
  `remittance_breach_held`, severity `alert` (not a violation: nothing is wrong in the books, a record waits), subject
  the run (`remittance_run`, « Ouvrir » leads to its page), currency, the held lines' amount and count, `oldest_days` the
  days since the earliest date they are held to; `details`: the run's `number`, `judged_on` (the date the run is judged
  at: the chain's paid date, or the payout line's date when no copy stayed), `earliest_latest_execution_date`, and why —
  `uncovered_days` (the business days of [least(e0, L), L] no imported statement covers yet, each read by
  `private.statement_covers` of that day; the first 31, `uncovered_count` all of them), `balance_break` (every day covered
  but two statements' balances not following: the window's own break), `waiting` (once the dates are covered, the lines
  dated by L that may be another transfer's debit and that the chain's rule does not count yet: line id, booking date,
  amount, currency, the end-to-end id of the transfer it may be; the first 10, `waiting_count` all of them),
  `bound_days` (`private.transfer_debit_bound_days()`, the page's « N jours ouvrés » — never a number of its own), `ids`
  (the held lines' ledger entries, the first 50). Open/resolved as every check: a check run's results are the open ones;
  the next run raises it again while the row waits and not once it is written.
- **One rule for the rows and their alert.** The booked branch's runs moved verbatim into
  `private.remittance_booked_chain_runs` (its `bc` and `bp` CTEs, the same rows: every booked run of the servicer whose
  payout chain holds a payout cancelled out of a downloaded file, its payout standing, with a late line at the chain's
  paid date — or the payout line's — that has no row yet); the booked branch reads it, and so does the alert. The alert's
  helper takes, per run, the lines due at that date (each held to its latest execution date, or to the one-month date of
  its collection for a delay that cannot be met once that date is before the run's — `private.remittance_chain_rows`'
  own reading) that still have no row, and per date they are held to, the holds' own facts
  (`private.remittance_chain_hold_facts`, one snapshot). It runs in the results' statement, after the booked branch's
  statement wrote the rows that are due: a run whose row the check writes, or whose chain the statements show paid on
  time, raises nothing — the alert resolves itself. A run whose payout came back raises none (its sums' rows are the
  queue's, alerted as such); a run whose chain holds no other transfer raises none (its booking writes its row whatever
  the statements, since 6b-2c).
- **Neither day nor line.** When the facts read in the results' statement show the window covered and no line waiting
  (an import or a booking another session committed between the booked branch's statement and the results'), the alert
  is still raised — the row is not written yet — and says the run is judged again at the next check.
- **The texts** (`apps/web/src/lib/payments/debits.ts`, `CHECK_LABEL.remittance_breach_held`, `breachHeldHelp`): label «
  Dépassement de délai non encore enregistré »; help: according to the imported statements the run paid some collections
  after their latest execution date (art. R124-6 CPCE), but another transfer issued for it (the one cancelled after
  download, or its replacement) may have paid them on time, so the overrun is not recorded yet; it will be, if it
  stands, at the next check once the statements cover every business day in question and no line that may be that
  transfer's debit waits in « Débits et retours » — then the alert stops. With the row's details: « Importez les relevés
  du compte de fonds de tiers des jours ouvrés suivants : … » (ten named, then « et N autres »), the balances' break and «
  importez le relevé manquant entre eux », or « Classez dans « Débits et retours » la ligne du … de …, qui peut être le
  débit du virement … » (three named), « comptabilisez-la (« Comptabiliser… ») si c'est le débit de ce virement, sinon
  classez-la pour ce qu'elle est », and that a line « Comptabiliser… » does not propose as that transfer stops holding
  the record `bound_days` business days after its date (then « bloqué : débit possible non comptabilisé »). The same
  text whichever the switch (the alert exists only for a chain). No deadline of its own: the alert names no legal date.
- **PR #38's known limit, the booking guard.** `private.bank_line_booking_guard()` runs under `enable_seqscan = off` (its
  own `SET`, beside hash and merge joins off), as `private.bank_booking_recheck` since PR #38's CI round. That alone was
  not enough: its one join — the run of the reversed booking's transfer, `bank_line_booking` joined to `bank_transfer` —
  read `bank_line_booking` whole through `bank_line_booking_transfer_idx` once per new row (a full index scan is no
  sequential scan), so that read is keyed too: the reversed booking's transfer by its entry (`entry_id` is unique), then
  that transfer's run by its key — the same row, null when the booking has no transfer. The same rows read and the same
  verdict; only the plans change.

### Deviations from the task

- The guard got both treatments the task allowed (« enable_seqscan off in its SET clause, or keyed reads »): the first
  alone left 12 million rows under the test's statistics.
- The guard's test forgets the statistics of the nine tables the guard reads, inside its own transaction (rolled back
  with it), beside `random_page_cost` 1,000: with the statistics a run happened to leave, the joined read chose the
  entry's index (the guard passed at 48,001 rows with the join back), so the test was not deterministic for that mutant.
  *(Corrected in review round 1, tests-ui-1: forgetting the tables' statistics did not make it deterministic either —
  the planner sized each table from its blocks, and the indexes kept the stack's own statistics; the test now stores a
  first batch line and forges the indexes' row counts in its transaction: « M2c-6b-3b part 2 review fixes », round 1.)*
- The E2E's held state dates the run's collections back to the last business day before today through psql (as pgTAP's
  `pg_temp.hold_to` and the spec's own file backdating): the spec's late predecessor is booked today, before its
  collections' month ends.

## M2c-6b-3b part 3: the alert at volume, the last switch-on prerequisites, the switch still off (2026-11-21)

Plan: founder question 3 of « M2c-6b-3b part 2 » (its default: the three dedups round 1's fixer named and a 2,000-payout
volume case, before the switch flips; round 1's « Left open » cost-breach-held-linear-recompute), PR #39's two known
limits (the alert's CSV hint, « Contrôles »' 200 results), and plan §3.7's switch-on screenshots carried since 6b-3a-2.
Migration `20261121120000_switch_on_prerequisites_5.sql`: one internal helper is new — `private.remittance_chain_judged`
(EXECUTE revoked from every role); `private.remittance_chain_holds` is dropped and created again (its result gains
`lines`, which CREATE OR REPLACE cannot add; its body copied from its latest definition, `20261119090000:209`, with that
one change, its settings and grants restated); two functions are redefined whole from their latest definitions across
all the migration files (settings, `search_path ''` and grants restated, SECURITY DEFINER where it was):
`private.remittance_chain_rows` (`20261119090000:275`) and `private.run_remittance_runs_checks` (`20261121090000:208`);
`private.remittance_breach_held`'s comment is set. No public signature changed (`database.types.ts` regenerated:
unchanged); no Python product code changed. **The switch stays off**: no statement writes `private.feature_switch`;
`033` is byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`042` unchanged (no assertion changed; `041` 25/25, `042` 20/20).

### Decisions

- **The three dedups (founder question 3's default; behaviour unchanged).** The nightly checks read the booked chained
  runs once (`private.remittance_booked_chain_runs` into `pg_temp._rc_runs`), then every line due at each run's date
  with what its hold found, once (`private.remittance_chain_judged` into `pg_temp._rc_lines`: `private.remittance_chain_rows`'
  lines, unfiltered, each with its date's `covered`, `waiting`, `expired` and — new — the possible debits the hold
  judged on, `lines`, from the first of its one-snapshot reads). The booked branch writes the rows of the lines whose
  holds pass, as before; « remittance_breach_held » reads the same two tables in the results' statement: its held lines
  (those still without a row), per run its account and e0 (once per run), per account and window [least(e0, L), L] the
  coverage and the uncovered days (once, not once per run), and the waiting lines from the findings. No second reading
  of the runs, their late lines, the chain's paid date, its events, nor the holds' facts. `private.remittance_chain_rows`
  now returns `private.remittance_chain_judged`'s lines whose holds pass (its body moved there verbatim): one rule for
  the booking, its sheet's late flag and the nightly check.
- **The holds keep their name.** `private.remittance_chain_holds` itself records the lines (dropped and created again
  with the extra column) rather than a new function beside it: 041's race harness (`pg_temp.wrap('remittance_chain_holds')`,
  chain-holds-snapshot-race A, C, D) injects another session's commit as the holds start, by that function's name — a
  copy under another name left it never called (041 #20 failed: fired 0) and would have kept two bodies of one rule.
- **The standalone reading stays.** `private.remittance_breach_held` (part 2's, one snapshot) is kept unchanged and no
  longer called by the checks; the tests compare the checks' alert with it run by run (at 6 and 2,000 runs). Its comment
  says so.
- **The facts' snapshot (race only).** Part 2 read the alert's facts again in the results' statement. Now the window's
  coverage and its days are still read there (once per window), but the waiting lines are those the booked branch's
  holds judged on — named only when the window is covered now and was so then, and never a line booked or linked since
  (review round 1's guard, pinned by 042 RD and RL); otherwise neither day nor line is named and the text says the run is
  judged again at the next check (part 2's « neither day nor line » case). In a race (another session's import or booking
  between the two statements) the alert can be raised for a run the statements already show paid on time — part 2's
  second reading raised none there; the next check corrects it and no R124-6 row is written or missed (« M2c-6b-3b part 3
  review fixes », dt3-race-alert-for-run-paid-on-time). Outside a race the alert is the standalone reading's, row for row.
- **The CSV hint (PR #39's known limit).** A CSV statement's period is its lines' first and last booking dates
  (`private.ingest_statement`), and `private.statement_covers` counts a day of it only from its first operation's day to
  the day before its last one's (and uploaded after the day). « exportez jusqu'au jour suivant » was not enough when that
  day had no operation, nor when the export's first operation came after the day. The sentence now reads « … un relevé
  établi pendant l'un d'eux ne compte pas pour ce jour, ni le jour de la dernière opération d'un export CSV, ni un jour
  avant sa première : exportez une période qui contient une opération datée au plus tard du <premier jour> (le premier de
  ces jours) et une opération postérieure au <dernier jour> (le dernier). » — dated since review round 1
  (dt3-csv-hint-last-day-not-named: the details carry `last_uncovered_day`); true of the rule, no legal rule invented.
- **« Contrôles » beyond 200 results (PR #39's known limit).** The page still reads 200 results, now in one total order
  (`CHECK_RESULT_ORDER`: anomalies first, then by code, then within a code the oldest first, an undated one last, then by
  subject, then by the result's id), and says what it leaves out: above the list « Seuls les 200 premiers résultats sont
  affichés, sur N : le nombre de résultats non affichés est indiqué pour chaque contrôle. », under a code's last row « N
  autres résultats de ce contrôle ne sont pas affichés. », and a code none of whose results is read is listed with « N
  résultats de ce contrôle ne sont pas affichés. » The counts are the run's own by code (`payment_check_run.summary`,
  written by `private.run_payment_checks` when it finishes) minus the rows read — counts only, no amount said for the
  results not read; a run in progress (no summary yet) says nothing is cut. No SQL change (`lib/payments/check-results.ts`).
- **Plan §3.7's switch-on screenshots.** The switch-on E2E project has built the late predecessor through the pages
  since 6b-3a-2's review round 1 (tests-5: a payout cancelled out of a downloaded file by two people on the statements'
  evidence, executed late under its own reference, booked from « Débits et retours » as its run's payout) and
  screenshots the pages it changes: the file page before (`m2c-virement-telecharge`, `m2c-annulation-fichier`), the
  booking sheet (`m2c-debit-reversement-annule`), the run page (`m2c-reversement-debite-en-retard`) and, since part 2,

  request) and the `scale-payouts` job at 2,000 (`test_breach_held_scale_integration.py`). Each compares the
  checks' alert with the standalone reading run by run, two windows on one account (half the runs' x dated a business
  day earlier, W: their window starts there), writes every row the next night once W and M are imported, and counts the
  work by function (`track_functions`: calls are deterministic whatever the machine). A pgTAP file would have needed
  041's 1,200-line fixture for one more chain; `041` and `042` already pin every behaviour, unchanged.

- **The volume case is a new scale file**, `test_breach_held_scale_integration.py`, beside the cancellation file (the
  task allowed either): its fixture is the 5,000-payout file's (`_file_payouts`, given a `day` for the collections;
  the default unchanged), sized 2,000, and its scenario is shared with the db job's small twin.
- **It runs in CI's `scale-payouts` job, not `scale`.** The `scale` job took 27.6 of its 30 minutes on `main` (the run
  of 2026-11-21 08:13 UTC); this file adds about 6 (its 2,000 runs through the jobs about 4); `scale-payouts` took 12.4
  of its 40. The payouts' bookings run first in that job, on the database they were tuned on; the held runs after them.

  dedups and take 12.8–13.0 s after (one fixture, committed and measured again); the scale file alone right after a

  date and its events, twice per run: once for the runs, once in the holds' one-snapshot facts — 4,000 calls of

### Left open (low), with its default

- **The booked branch's own cost at volume.** After the dedups, 2,000 held chained runs still take 12.8–13.0 s of

  payouts was cancelled and re-issued; the worker's nightly call has no statement timeout. Default: keep (above plan
  §1.4's 5 s, which is for 5,000 booked payouts without chains); passing the chain's events from the selection into the
  holds would trade part 1's snapshot guarantee for it.

  contrôle »), or raised for a run the statements already show paid on time; it never names a line booked or linked since

## M2c-6b-3b part 3 review fixes (2026-11-21)

### Round 1

The review of `8a369c3` raised seven lows and no high or medium: the alert in a race (dt3-race-alert-for-run-paid-on-time),
the held-rows screenshots left at part 2's (dt3-held-alert-screenshot-shows-old-csv-hint), the CSV hint's last day
(dt3-csv-hint-last-day-not-named), three test gaps (tests-ui-1 … tests-ui-3) and the alert's own per-run scans (cost-1).
Each was reproduced first on the main stack (the switch on inside rolled-back transactions only). The migration
`20261121120000` is unmerged and was edited in place: one function more is redefined, `private.remittance_breach_held`
(copied from its latest definition, `20261121090000:114`, with one key added, its settings and grants restated).
Building cost-1's volume case found one medium more, pre-existing (below: the options' locks), fixed at the root:
`private.transfer_line_offers` is redefined too (from `20261117110000:405`). **The switch stays off**; `033` byte for
byte unchanged; `034`–`041` keep every assertion, no expected value changed (`038` #1's runs read in their numbers'
order besides their shared `created_at`, below); `042` keeps its 20 assertions, each unchanged, and gains 9 (below:
#18 … #26) and a guard in its `pg_temp.nightly` helper.

- **dt3-race-alert-for-run-paid-on-time (kept, pinned, and the booked line never named).** The alert takes its runs,
  their held lines and the holds' findings from what the booked branch recorded; the rows written, the days and (new)
  the waiting lines' bookings and links are read again in the results' statement. A commit by another session between
  the two — an import showing the chain paid on time, or ops booking the very line that waited — leaves that check's
  alert stale until the next one, which part 2's second reading, made after the commit, did not raise in those shapes
  (a commit landing just after part 2's results' statement left its alert stale alike). The review's option 1 (each
  alerted run's paid date read again in the results' statement) was measured, not built: one more
  `private.remittance_chain_paid` per alerted run, 4.21 and 4.71 s at 2,000 held runs (the night: 14.7 and 15.5 s;
  close to a third of what the dedups saved) — for a race that only delays a correct reading by one night.
  **Default: keep** (the alert is the booked branch's reading of each run; the next check judges it again), and one cheap guard: a waiting line booked
  or linked since the booked branch judged it is no longer named (two lookups by key per waiting line, as
  `private.transfer_debit_lines` reads them) — never « comptabilisez-la » for a booked line. Pinned in `042`: RC (041's
  race C: the import as the holds start) — the racing check's alert names neither day nor line, no row, the standalone
  reading and the next check none; RD (041's race D2: ops book x's line « Virement hors reversement » as the holds ask
  its options) — the alert no longer names the line (it did: failed first on `8a369c3`), no row, the standalone reading
  and the next check none; RL (H2l's shape: ops classify the line not ours as the holds ask its options) — the alert
  names no line, as the standalone reading at that state does (the guard on), the next check writes the row at y's
  date. The ADR's « Left open » sentence (« as part 2's race ») is corrected in place.
- **dt3-held-alert-screenshot-shows-old-csv-hint.** `m2c-controles-depassement-en-attente` (desktop, mobile) retaken
  by the switch-on project and committed, with the new hint (their date and id diffs are the page's own); the two
  sentences of « M2c-6b-3b part 3 » that said otherwise are corrected in place.
- **dt3-csv-hint-last-day-not-named.** The alert's details gain `last_uncovered_day`, the last business day no imported
  statement covers (null when none), in the checks and in the standalone reading alike; the hint names both ends: «
  exportez une période qui contient une opération datée au plus tard du JJ/MM/AAAA (le premier de ces jours) et une
  opération postérieure au JJ/MM/AAAA (le dernier). » — the last the row's own, else the last of its days when they are
  all there; an older row whose days were cut keeps the rule without a date (no day the page cannot know). True of
  `private.statement_covers`' rule for a CSV (its period is its lines' first and last booking dates,
  `private.ingest_statement`); no legal rule. `042` #21/#22 (EA's two days: d3; HL, HD's 41 days: d15 beyond the 31
  named); vitest `breach-held.test.ts` (12 → 13; the CSV test's expected sentence now dated — this slice's own test).
- **tests-ui-1 (the alert's equivalence on one shape).** `042`'s `pg_temp.nightly` now holds every check it runs to the
  standalone reading (`private.remittance_breach_held`, part 2's correlated reads, kept independent on purpose: the
  review's suggestion to give it the checks' new aggregates too would have let one mistake pass both), run by run and
  field by field, the scenario dying otherwise — every scenario of `042` (H1 … HU, the waiting lines, the break, the
  caps, two dates) — off only inside RC and RD. And three shapes no scenario had: EA (#18, forged: the held line beside a
  released copy of itself), EB (#19: x first filed in a file nobody downloaded, cancelled and dated earlier), EC (#20: a
  chain of three, a line that may be the debit of x or of y, named once as the one with the smaller id). The review's
  three mutants are killed by them (each by its own assertion with the guard off, by the guard with it on). The scale
  scenario adds the waiting lines' shape at volume (below), its alert held to the standalone reading too.
- **tests-ui-2 (a code none of whose results is listed).** `checks-cap.spec.ts`: the statement is dated a month back
  and also holds a credit nobody's file claims — « Paiements sans dossier depuis 20 jours ou plus » (`unmatched_ageing`,
  sorting after the unknown references): the 200 results read end inside the unknown references, so that check is
  listed with none of its results — « 1 résultat de ce contrôle n'est pas affiché. » —, asserted, and the end-of-list
  screenshots (mobile, desktop) show it. The page without its unlisted rows now fails the spec (it passed before).
- **tests-ui-3 (the rows' order where the page uses it).** The query's order is `orderCheckResults(query)`
  (`lib/payments/check-results.ts`, CHECK_RESULT_ORDER key by key), called by the page and unit-tested with a builder
  that records each `.order` (column, ascending, nullsFirst); `groupCheckResults` lists the rows read in
  `compareCheckResults`' order, so the rows of a code come in one order whatever order the database returns them in
  (unit-tested from every rotation). `compareCheckResults` is now the page's (kept with its test).
- **cost-1 (the alert's per-run scans).** The alert's days and waiting lines are aggregated once per run (`hd`: the days
  in order, their count, the last, the break; `hwr`/`hwa`: the lines numbered per run, the first 10 named — their
  amounts and transfers read by key for those only —, all counted) and joined to each run by key, instead of five
  correlated subqueries scanning the per-run facts once per run. Its rows are unchanged (the guard and the scale
  scenario hold them to the standalone reading). The scale scenario adds the waiting lines' variant, rolled back to a
  savepoint after the first night: x requested from W (as pgTAP's `chain_prefix`), W's statement holding two debits
  without our references of x's amount for each run of the half dated back (and one credit of their total, the balances
  following), M's: every window covered, those runs alerted with their two lines each and no day, the others' rows
  written — timed under its own bound (110 s: twice its first measure, 52.8 s; 55.3 s on the final run).
- **The options' locks (medium, pre-existing; found by cost-1's volume case).** The waiting lines' variant at 2,000 runs
  failed the whole nightly check: « out of shared memory — You might need to increase max_locks_per_transaction », in
  `private.transfer_line_check`'s `create temp table _tl_drafts`, reached from `private.remittance_chain_holds` through
  `private.transfer_line_offers`. The options of a line build working tables, dropped and created again at each call,
  and a dropped table's lock is held to the end of the transaction; the nightly checks ask the options of every possible
  debit past the bound days, in one transaction — the booked branch's holds (switch on) and, since 6b-2c, the in-flight
  branch (`private.remittance_inflight_judge`, `private.transfer_debit_suppression`: production, switch off). About a
  hundred such lines in one servicer's check (6,400 lock slots at the default `max_locks_per_transaction`, 60 per call) (a CSV bank's statement without our references, its payouts' debits left
  unbooked past the bound days) failed the check every night: no R124-6 row written, no alert, no other check. Fixed at
  the root: `private.transfer_line_offers` reads its answer in a subtransaction rolled back once read — the working
  tables and their locks go with it (the options only read; the same answer from the same reads); 041's race harness,
  which wraps that function by name, still injects before it. Pinned: `042` #26 (OL: asked once, then three times more —
  the same answer, the transaction's relation locks unchanged; 60 more per call before: failed first), and the scale
  scenario's waiting variant (52.8 and 55.3 s at 2,000 runs; failed before).
- **`038` #1 (« Suivi », a flaky order, pre-existing).** The full suite failed it once: its runs were listed `order by
  created_at`, which they share (one transaction's `now()`), so the plan decided their order. Read now `order by
  created_at, number` (numbers drawn from one sequence as the runs are requested): the expected value unchanged (house
  rule R3: no expectation changed); 038 passed alone and in the next full run.

## M2c-6b-3b part 3 — CI round (PR #40) (2026-11-21)

**The failure.** CI run 44909449352 (dispatched on the PR's branch), job « Scale runs (50k boarding, statement,
matching, allocation; 5k receipts) »: `test_transfers_cancelled_out_of_a_downloaded_file_and_reissued_beside_a_large_file`
read **486,480** rows of `bank_transfer` in its nightly checks, its bound 183,008 (12 × (SIZE + 2 × CANCELLED) + 24 ×
(SIZE + 2) + 2,000); every other assertion passed (the checks 3.41 s; main's last scale run, 417fe36: 86,521 rows,
0.88 s, the same breaches). Part 3's build ran the file alone after a reset: it passed.

**Root cause: not this PR's bodies — an arm of `private.run_transfer_checks` that reads every waiting refund once per
cancelled refund, cheap only while the plan happens to stop early.** Reproduced on the main stack in the scale job's
order (`supabase db reset`, CI's logging settings, the six scale files before this one, then this file's world with
its nightly checks measured per statement under auto_explain, in its rolled-back transaction): **486,480** rows — CI's
figure to the row; with main's bodies (417fe36's `run_remittance_runs_checks`, `remittance_chain_holds`,
`remittance_chain_rows`, `remittance_breach_held`, `transfer_line_offers`) applied over the PR's in the same
transaction, 486,521 (the 41 more: main reads the servicer's cancelled filed transfers twice). Named: the statement
`insert into public.payment_check_result … with flight …, cx …` of `private.run_transfer_checks` (as 20261118100000
left it: this arm unchanged since M2c-6b-3a, PR #36), its arm « transfer_already_debited » over `cx` (the cancelled
transfers of a downloaded file debited late) and its exclusion of a refund whose chain's live end is still waiting —
`not exists (select 1 from public.refund_request q … where q.organization_id = … and q.status = 'requested' … and exists
(select 1 from private.transfer_chain(q.transfer_id) c where c.transfer_id = t.id))`: a Bitmap Heap Scan of
`refund_request` by `refund_request_waiting_idx` (the servicer's 10,012 waiting requests) 21 times, each request's
transfer probed by `bank_transfer_pkey` (**210,250** loops) and its chain read (SubPlan, `private.transfer_chain`:
**200,210** calls, their statement 200,424 rows). Which plan it got rested on `refund_request`'s statistics, that is on
autovacuum: the scale test asks 10,040 refunds in its set-up and autovacuum analyses the table within the minute. Once
analysed (the PR's run), the bitmap read every waiting refund before reaching a cancelled refund's own (its row
rewritten by the re-issue, so last); not yet (main's run, the build's), the waiting index read in `requested_at` order
met the cancelled refunds' requests among the first, after 488 requests each: 86,480 rows. The same state with only
`refund_request`'s statistics forgotten in the transaction: 86,480; analysed: 486,480. « Flake » was the timing of
autovacuum; the cause, a read whose cost is the servicer's waiting refunds per cancelled refund, by construction (a
servicer whose cancelled refunds were asked after its other waiting refunds pays it under any plan).

**Fix** (in place in the unmerged `20261121120000`, a new last section; behaviour unchanged):
`private.transfer_reissues(t)` (new; SQL, stable, `search_path ''`, `enable_seqscan off`; EXECUTE revoked from every
role) — a transfer and the transfers re-issuing it, forward by key (`bank_transfer_replaces_transfer_id_key`, unique:
each transfer is re-issued at most once), with `private.transfer_chain`'s depth bound: y is in `transfer_reissues(t)`
exactly when t is in `transfer_chain(y)`. `private.run_transfer_checks` redefined from 20261118100000 (line 2905;
SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path ''`, `enable_seqscan off` and its grants restated), changed only in that exclusion: the
same refund requests (requested, the servicer's, their transfer ordered or in a file) read from the cancelled refund
forward — each re-issue by key, its request by `refund_request_transfer_id_key`, its transfer's status by key, the
other conditions outside the probes (as `transfer_sibling_debited_late`'s). The same rows: in every state measured the
checks raise the same results (CI's six codes and counts), pgTAP 039 (C4: a cancelled refund whose request was
cancelled, executed late, alerted; L3) passes unchanged. `bank_transfer` rows read by the scale world's nightly checks
(the same committed state, each variant in the same transaction, rolled back between them):

| statistics in the transaction | PR's bodies (main's) | fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refund_request` analysed (CI's PR run) | 486,480 (486,521) | **75,850** |
| `refund_request` never analysed (main's CI run) | 86,480 | 75,850 |
| `bank_transfer`, `transfer_file_item`, `refund_request`, `transfer_cancellation_request` analysed | 276,294 | 65,874 |
| eight tables' statistics forgotten (their indexes recorded empty), probes priced at 1,000 pages | 86,482 (86,523) | 115,980 |

(The last: three once-per-check reads of the servicer's cancelled filed transfers — `remittance_booked_chain_runs`,
the paying account's, `transfer_sibling_debited_late`'s payouts — took `bank_transfer_file_idx` whole under those forged
index statistics, 10,063 rows each, once: linear, below.)

**Test** (`worker/tests/test_transfer_cancellation_reads_integration.py`, in the `db` job, about 6 s): the
transfer-cancellation world at 300 + 300 refunds and 40 cancelled out of their own downloaded file (20 debited late),
the cancelled refunds' requests asked after 300 others still waiting — so whatever plan reads the waiting refunds meets

It holds the rows (each late refund's re-issue alerted, never the cancelled refund; each late line once),
`private.transfer_chain`'s calls (track_functions: deterministic, whatever the plan or the stack) ≤ 4 × 40 + 100, and

body (applied over the fixed one): **6,210** calls of `transfer_chain` and 21,410 rows — it fails; fixed: none (20 of
`transfer_reissues`), 7,500 to 9,460 rows as the stack's other servicers' rows grow (the once-per-check reading).

**Suites** (the main stack alone): `supabase test db` after `supabase db reset` — **Files=44, Tests=2,911, PASS**; then,
without a reset (CI's order), the integration tests but the scale files — **245 passed** (244 and the new test);

`scale` job's command as `ci.yml` runs it (its nine files): **15 passed** (1,421.5 s) — this file's nightly checks

round (PR #40) ». Then `supabase db reset` (the stack left running). No web code changed.

## M2c-7a: remitted reversals covered everywhere, and the backstop (2026-11-21)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0 (D1–D4, D12, D13), §1.4 (7a row), §2, §3 and their [critic] / [check 1–3]
marks; founder questions §10 none answered, every default built and left open. Migration
`20261122090000_remitted_reversals_covered.sql` (one file, forward-only). New: `private.run_settled_at` /
`run_settled_on`, `private.item_settled_at` (review round 2), `private.entry_remitted`, `private.remitted_cover_fact` / `_held` / `_target` / `_gap`,
`private.remitted_cover_begin` / `_post`, `private.cover_remitted_reversals` (at the reversal),
`private.cover_booked_run_reversals` (at the booking), `private.advance_in_flight_run`, `private.remitted_cover_release`
(the unplanned return), the deferred constraint triggers `ledger_entry_remitted_cover` and `remittance_run_booked_cover`
(SQLSTATE `LG009`), `private.run_advance_checks`, the table `private.advance_full_check_request` (RLS on, no grant to any
client role, its guard, append-only for deletes, change log) with `private.advance_full_check_take` and
`public.request_full_advance_check`, `public.cover_remitted_reversal` (« Couvrir »), `public.allocation_remitted` (the
« Désimputer » read), three indexes for the nightly's keyed reads. Redefined, each copied whole from its latest
definition across every migration file (the change only; settings, `search_path ''`, SECURITY DEFINER where it was and
grants restated): `private.ledger_check_now` (`20261111090000:1335`), `public.reverse_allocation`
(`20261109190000:1079`), `private.debit_post_rows` (`20261110120000:549`), `private.approve_remittance_run`
(`20261114090000:786`), `private.run_remittance_checks` (`20261115090000:3710`), `private.transfer_line_post`
(`20261118100000:2163`), `private.bank_booking_post_rows` (`20261121090000:808`), `public.remittance_run_payout`
(`20261118100000:4380`). Worker: `RemittedReversalUncoveredError` (`LG009`; a debit-job link refused so is
`posting_failed`, as `LG008`). Web: « Désimputer » and « Débits et retours » say what was remitted, the toast says the
advance, the run page words each advance by cause, « Contrôles » gains the three checks, « Couvrir » and « Vérification
complète des avances ». **The switch stays off**: nothing writes `private.feature_switch`; the rules reachable only with
it on are tested with it on inside rolled-back subtransactions (043 `pg_temp.iso(name, true)`); `033` byte for byte
unchanged.

### Decisions

- **D1 — remitted, and what is covered (plan §2.1).** An allocation or forward E is remitted when its live line is in a
  booked run that does not also hold its reversal R ([critic] M7-MONEY-1: a same-run pair nets to 0 in that run and was
  never paid out; 5a–5c). T(R) = E's line then; otherwise what the live unplanned payouts paid of E (switch on; an
  attribution whose booking is not reversed); otherwise 0. C(R) = R's live covers (`client_advance`, cause
  `remitted_reversal`, `cause_entry_id` = R, entry not reversed). I23: C(R) = T(R) for every reversal.
- **D2 — where the cover is posted.** In the transaction of the reversal: `reverse_allocation` (« Désimputer »), the M2b
  return in both modes and « Retour au-delà du paiement » (`private.debit_post_rows`, step 1 collects the reversals it
  posts and covers them before step 2), set-based (`pg_temp._rcv`, at most 2,000 entries per `ledger_post_set`). At the
  booking, for a line reversed while its run was in flight: `private.bank_booking_post_rows` step 3b (the payout's
  transfer and debit line on the advance, [critic] F5) and the N = 0 branch of `private.approve_remittance_run` (no
  transfer). The overrun cover (step 4) then reads the balances after these covers: `payout_overrun` remains `LG008`'s
  backstop for a debit no reversed line explains (043 #39, a planted raw 4670 debit).
- **Its date** is greatest(R's date, the date of the payout it covers) ([critic] F3: a back-dated « Désimputer » never
  puts the advance before the payout; 043 #1 reads 4670, 4679 and 4112 the day before the payout).
- **D3 — the backstop.** Two deferred constraint triggers check I23 at every commit — on each reversal (its own gap; a
  reversal of an unplanned booking: the gap of every item that booking paid; a reversal of a cover: its reversal's gap,
  [critic] F6) and on a run set booked (each live allocation or forward line's reversal, never a same-run pair) — SQLSTATE
  `LG009`. `private.ledger_check_now()` fires them with `LG008`'s, so every command that calls it fails at once.
- **D4 — the release (switch on).** An unplanned payout's return reverses the covers of the items it paid that were
  reversed since, down to what the other live bookings still pay (re-posted under `adv:<R>:rel:<line>:<booking>`);
  refused « transfer line booking refused: advance_settled » while the advance is settled and « advance_in_flight »
  while an approved or sent run's plan takes it back ([critic] M7-MONEY-2), nothing booked.
- **D12 — what the client received, and when (`private.run_settled_at`, plan §3.2.1 [check 1] [check 2]).** A run's
  transfer chain paid and stayed paid → its paid date, « paid »; came back → followed through the re-queued item's live
  line in a booked run (the chain's returns read from its `payout_returned` bookings, never `return_entry_id`, which a
  late predecessor's return leaves null); an N = 0 run → its `booked_on`, « set_off » when it set something off, else
  « netted »; recursion bounded at 10 (`settled_on_depth` on `advance_open`). The « Désimputer » sheet follows `paid_how`.
- **D13 — the nightly (`private.run_advance_checks`, called by `private.run_remittance_checks`).**
  `remitted_reversal_uncovered` (violation, the gap) reads a delta: the reversals posted since the last finished run
  less one day, the runs booked since, the attributions and covers since, and the reversals the last run listed
  ([critic] F9); the whole history on the 1st of the month (Paris) or when the run takes an admin's request
  (`public.request_full_advance_check`, aal2; one open request per servicer; taken by the next check run, its `run_id`
  set; a run that fails rolls the take back). `advance_ledger` (violation: per client, the open advances against
  4112) and `advance_open` (alert: an advance open more than 30 days). « Couvrir » (`public.cover_remitted_reversal`,
  admins at aal2, compare-and-set on the gap the page showed) posts a missing cover under `adv:<R>:cov:<md5 of the key>`.
- **Locks.** Row locks, then `payments:<org>` (taken by the ledger's posting before any cover reads a line), then
  `remit:<org>`, then a counter (plan §2.2). `reverse_allocation`'s `lock_timeout` (2 s) may now be reached on the remit
  lock a file generation holds: « Opération en cours sur les virements : réessayez dans un instant. » (55P03).

### Deviations from the plan

- **The migration's name** is the task's, `20261122090000_remitted_reversals_covered.sql`.
- **`private.cover_remitted_reversals(p_reversal_ids uuid[], p_line_ids uuid[] default null)`**: a second, parallel
  array — the bank line each reversal was posted at (the M2b return), kept on the advance (`bank_transaction_id`).
- **Keys.** « Couvrir » posts under `adv:<R>:cov:<md5 of its idempotency key>` (the plan's `adv:<R>:cov:<key>`: a key
  of any length in an entry's key); the release's re-post under `adv:<R>:rel:<line>:<booking>` (the plan's
  `adv:<R>:rel:<line>`: one return line can reverse several bookings — an unsplit lot — each releasing its own items).
- **`private.run_settled_at` rule 2 fallback.** A booked run whose chain has no counted execution and no return (the
  chain rule, `private.remittance_chain_paid`, does not count a debit dated before its transfer's requested execution
  date — a booking the debit job and the tests make) gives the run's `booked_on`, « paid »: without it « Désimputer »
  said « revenu, à verser de nouveau » of a payout that never came back.
- **043 holds 44 assertions, not ≈ 70**: each scenario returns one `jsonb` of every fact it checks (the advance, its
  key, date, books, the queue, the gap, the check), compared whole.
- **Pins flipped beyond the plan's list (house rule R3; each keeps its purpose):**
  - `037` `p_draft_partial` (« P (review 6b-2c money-4) »): the same raw reversal of a booked run's line as `d_f5`; reworked
    as `d_f5` (the bounced collection in the run in flight R2, covered at R2's booking): `held` gains
    `client_advance:10000` (the cover); `draft_unplanned` unchanged (31 000).
  - `037` `d_queue_call`: its bounced collection is now e7 in R2 in flight (c7, remitted in the booked R0, would be
    covered); the expectation is unchanged (the queue nets the same 39 200).
  - `038` `d_queue`, `f_partial`, `d_twice` (the Suivi of a bounce): they stand for a bank's return of a remitted
    collection by a raw `private.ledger_reverse`, which now fails `LG009` at commit; the setup switches the cover trigger
    off around those three scenarios (`pg_temp.cover_check(false)`, then `(true)`), every assertion unchanged.
  - `017` (three check-code sets, l.845–878): + `advance_ledger` — the fixtures post raw `client_advance` entries
    (4112) with no advance row, which I18's new advance half flags.
  - `023` r5 (l.518, l.580): « Désimputer » of file 01's collection remitted in the booked r1 posts its cover: r5's plan
    gross 100 000 → 300 000 and its lines 2 → 3 (the plan named this flip); its `prepare` helper left-joins the file of
    an item (an advance item has none).
  - `024` (l.472): the runs booked above queue their deferred cover check; it is fired before the test's `ALTER TABLE`

  - `035` §5 (r8, l.1435ff), `036` #14 (`c_overrun`), `037b` `d_ml1_cover`, `040` F5b: cause `payout_overrun` →
    `remitted_reversal`, same amount, same payout and line (the plan named 035, 037b, 040); 035's `payout_overrun`
    alert → none (the advance is the reversal's cover; `advance_open` takes it after 30 days).
  - Named by the plan and flipped so: `037` `d_f5` and `d_ml1_signed`; the worker's RV-3
    (`test_remittance_runs_integration.py::test_the_worked_example_continues_a_credit_note_on_a_settled_invoice`: gross
    300 000, refund 36 000, net 282 000, its docstring saying why).
- **Not done:** `tests/ledger_machine.py`'s 7a part (the `reverse` rule marking an entry remitted; the oracle expecting

### Round 2

The review of `756dc1b` raised one medium, `run-settled-transfer-run-unplanned-return`. Checked against the code first
(reproduced on the main stack inside rolled-back transactions on `043`'s preamble, the switch off and on), it holds:
`private.run_settled_at` rule 2 answered « paid » on a run's own debit date for every run whose transfer chain paid,
whatever an unplanned payout had paid of its items. Rule 4 followed an unplanned payout that came back only for an N = 0
run, and for the whole run. So a collection that an unplanned payout had paid, netted in a run with a transfer of its own
(the payout's −P row beside it), still read « Déjà reversé au client (reversement RV-Y, débité le …) » once that payout
came back and its money was waiting in the queue. The same held for an earlier run settled through such a run (switch
off, S03r: « … RV-Y, débité le …, après le retour du virement du reversement RV-X »). The « Désimputer » sheet and the
« Débits et retours » note stated a dated payment that had not happened, and the plan's « `paid_on` null ⇔ the client
has not received the item », which 7c-2's `payout_not_received` will rely on, did not hold. The plan's rule 2 (§3.2.1)
has the same gap: a departure from the plan, recorded here. No money moves through this read in 7a: no cover, release,
check amount or posting reads it.

The migration `20261122090000_remitted_reversals_covered.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place. It adds one function,
`private.item_settled_at`, and changes `run_settled_at`, `run_settled_on`, `entry_remitted`, `run_advance_checks`
(`advance_open`'s depth detail) and `allocation_remitted` (one key more). No function is redefined beyond the eight of the
slice and no public signature changes (`allocation_remitted` returns `jsonb`), so `database.types.ts` is unchanged.
**The switch stays off.** `033` is unchanged byte for byte, and `034`–`042` are untouched. `043` keeps its 49 assertions:
three are extended (17 e, f, g also read `returned_via`) and two are new (#48, #49; round 1's #48 and #49 are now #50
and #51), so 51 in all.

- **`run-settled-transfer-run-unplanned-return` (fixed, at the item: the remaining fix's alternative).**
  `private.item_settled_at(entry, run, depth)` says when an item of a booked run reached the client and stayed with it.
  It starts from its run's own settlement (`run_settled_at`). Then, for each unplanned payout whose P paid this item
  (`private.unplanned_paid_item` by `unplanned_paid_item_entry_idx`; with the switch off, S03r's re-executed payout
  attributes the returned item; with it on, it also attributes the items a cancelled run released) and whose booking was
  reversed (`ledger_entry_reversed_once_uq`: it came back, its return re-queued +P), it follows that return's live line
  in a booked run, as an item. No such line means the item is not with the client. A line of the run itself is netted
  there and settled with the run, as round 1's M7A-MONEY-1 netted it. When the run and every followed return are
  settled, the row is the latest of those followed, with its `how` and run number; with nothing followed, it is the
  run's own row; otherwise `on_date` is null. `run_settled_at` now says only what a run itself paid out. Rule 3 follows
  the chain's returns through `item_settled_at`, so a re-queued item that an unplanned payout paid and that came back
  stays unsettled: this fixes the switch-off case. Rule 4 is now just « an N = 0 run → its `booked_on`, `set_off` or
  `netted` »: what an unplanned payout paid of it is each item's own, so the run's other items, set off or netted, stay
  settled (before, one returned payout unsettled the whole run). `private.entry_remitted` and `advance_open`'s
  `settled_on_depth` read the item. `run_settled_on` stays the run's read, with no row while the run is not settled.
  Same bound (depth 10) and keyed reads, `enable_seqscan` off.
- **`returned_via` (new key of `public.allocation_remitted`).** It says what came back first of what had paid the
  entry: `run` (the remitted run's own payout), `unplanned` (a payout outside any run whose P had paid it, with or
  without a transfer of the run's own) or null. The texts now name the payout that came back by this key. `run_transfer`
  (round 1) wrongly said « du reversement RV-Y » for a run that had a transfer but whose payout was not the one that came
  back. It stays in the read; the texts no longer use it. The sheet and the return note while the money waits, for the
  `unplanned` case: « Compris dans le reversement RV-… (le virement hors reversement qui l'avait payé est revenu, à
  verser de nouveau) » and « Paiement compris dans le reversement RV-… (le virement hors reversement qui l'avait payé
  est revenu, à verser de nouveau) : … ». The `run` case is unchanged: « (revenu, à verser de nouveau) ». Once a later
  run has paid: « … après le retour du virement hors reversement qui l'avait payé » or « … du virement du reversement
  RV-X », as before. COMPLIANCE OQ-97 quotes the second path's new text; DOMAIN's I23 paragraph says the read is per
  item.
- **Pinned.** `043` #48 is 17 h (switch off). In S03r, run Y is debited between the two returns, holding E2 (150 000),

### Round 3

The review of `3a91b47` raised one medium, `item-paid-by-live-unplanned-payout-run-payout-returned`, the converse of
round 2's fix (the switch on). Checked against the code first, it holds: the reviewer's probe, rerun on the main stack

`private.item_settled_at` gated every item on its run's own settlement (`v_all := s.on_date is not null`). It did so
even for an item that a live (unreversed) unplanned payout had paid in full, which the run's own payout therefore never
carried. The scenario: `late_cancel` (E 40 000 released), U booked on 19/11 and never back; run Y with E, F (25 000)
and U's −40 000 row, net 25 000, debited on 20/11 and returned on 21/11 (the queue holds `payout_returned:25000`, F's
money); W pays it, debited on 22/11. While the money waited, « Désimputer » said of E « Compris dans le reversement RV-Y
(revenu, à verser de nouveau) ». Once W was debited it said « Déjà reversé au client (reversement RV-W, débité le
22/11/2026, après le retour du virement du reversement RV-Y) ». That run and that date are false for E: W never carried
it, and the client had it from U on 19/11. This broke the ⇐ direction of the plan's « `paid_on` null ⇔ the client has
not received the item », which 7c-2's `payout_not_received` will rely on. The plan's §3.2.1 takes `paid_on` from the
run, so this is a departure from the plan, recorded here. It is not round 2's second open low: that low assumes the
run's own settlement stands, and here Y's payout came back. No money moves through this read: no cover, release, check
amount or posting reads `paid_on`, and E's cover is its line (T(R) unchanged).

- **`item-paid-by-live-unplanned-payout-run-payout-returned` (fixed, at the item, as the remaining fix proposed).**
  Before applying its run's gate, `private.item_settled_at` now reads what the unplanned payouts that stayed paid paid
  of the item: the sum of its `unplanned_paid_item` rows whose booking is not reversed (`unplanned_paid_item_entry_idx`,
  each booking by its key, its reversal by `ledger_entry_reversed_once_uq`), against the item's live line
  (`remittance_line_live_uq`). Two conditions must hold: that sum reaches the line, and nothing the item follows came
  back (no return of a payout that had paid it, waiting or paid outside its run). Then two cases:
  - While the run's own settlement stands (rules 2 and 4: `returned` null), the run's row is kept (round 2's default).

  An item those payouts paid only in part keeps the run's reading (conservative; below). Rule 3 of `run_settled_at`
  carries the new row as it carries any followed item's. So a run whose re-queued item such a payout paid in full is
  settled on that payout's date, « unplanned », with no run number and `returned` « run ». It is keyed as before and
