### Left open (low), with its default

- **A collection an unplanned payout paid only in part, in a run whose own payout came back** reads `paid_on` null as
  a whole (« revenu, à verser de nouveau »). That is true when the rest came back with the run's payout (17 l: the next
  run carries it). It is only conservative when the run set the rest off, for example the commission the cancelled run
  had set off, taken by the next run's invoice: the item is then with the client in full. A set-off is per run, not per
  item, so 7a has no exact per-item split. Default: keep it. 7c-2 asks no repayment of an advance whose item reads not
  received. Proposed as a question for the plan's §10 at 7c-2: should a run's set-off be shared out over its items for
  this read?
- **A collection paid in full by an unplanned payout that stayed paid and by one that came back**, whose return waits
  or was paid outside its run, also reads not settled (the « nothing it follows came back » guard). It needs two late
  executions that each paid the item, the first having come back before the second paid it: the attribution rule
  (M2c-6b-3a-2 J) leaves out an item that a live one paid. `043` #50 plants it. Default: keep it (conservative).
- **The delta pass's generic plan for a `remittance_run` believed empty** may read every booked run through the
  primary key (above). Default: keep it. It lasts only until autovacuum first analyses the table, and the window's
  bound still filters what the pass reads next (the lines of runs outside the window are never read).
- Round 2's second open low stands: while the run's own settlement stands, an item an unplanned payout paid and kept is
  dated by its run.
- **The return named for an item its run never carried** (found by round 3's verification, already on round 2's
  ordering of `returned_via`). Collection E paid in full by an unplanned payout U; E's run Y's payout comes back; then U
  itself comes back and its re-queued 40 000 is paid by a later run W. E reads `returned_via` 'run' (« revenu, à verser
  de nouveau », then « …après le retour du virement du reversement RV-Y ») instead of 'unplanned': the run, the date and
  the « paid » state are true, the payout named as come back is not (Y's payout never carried E; U's return is not
  named). No money moves and the nightly is clean: no money path reads `returned_via`. Fix proposed for 7b (which
  reworks 038's Suivi scenarios anyway): when the item's attributions not netted in the run cover its line, take
  'unplanned' instead of the run's `returned`, with a `043` case (17 j, then U back, then W). Default until then: keep.
- Everything rounds 1 and 2 leave open stays open.

## M2c-7a — CI round (main) (2026-11-23)

**The failure.** CI run 45206756541 (the push of 245296d, PR #41's squash, to `main`), job « Scale runs (50k boarding,
statement, matching, allocation; 5k receipts) », `test_transfer_line_scale_integration.py` in the job's order (after the
50,000-line files): `test_the_command_reads_a_lot_by_key` — the 500-member lot short of one, in its rolled-back
transaction, read **25,202,495** rows of `remittance_line` (its bound 10 × 500; every other per-member table within its
own, no sequential scan), `book_transfer_line` 6.18 s; `test_a_lot_at_the_cap_short_of_one_member_is_booked_within_budget`
— the same booking through the API 6.16 s (budget 4 s), the allocation lock held 5.99 s. The same commit's run
dispatched on the PR's branch (45201431943) passed that job, and so did `main` before 7a (70bfa8f).

**Root cause: a read 7a added, `private.cover_booked_run_reversals`.** Step 3b of `private.bank_booking_post_rows` calls
it once per booking with every payout row's run; it read each run's live allocation and forward lines through
`cross join lateral (select … from public.remittance_line q where q.run_id = u.run_id and not q.released and q.kind in
('allocation', 'forward') offset 0)`. Reproduced on a second local stack (project `collectoo-cifix`, ports 553xx, the
main stack untouched) in the scale job's order: `supabase db reset`, CI's logging settings, the job's nine files in one
pytest call as `ci.yml` runs them — the same two tests failed (here both past the API's 8 s, at that statement: this VM,
shared with another stack's suites, is slower than CI's runner). `remittance_line` had last been analysed by autovacuum
when it held exactly the two runs of `test_remittance_scale_integration.py` — the cancelled 50,000-line run (every line
released) and its re-run (every line live): `n_distinct(run_id)` 2 (MCV 0.500 / 0.500), `released` 0.5 / 0.5,
`correlation(run_id)` 0.9999. The lateral's key is a parameter (the outer row's run), so its estimate is 1 / n_distinct:
half the table, 50,000 rows. A probe of `remittance_line_pkey` for that many (a two-column index: its first column's
correlation weighted down) was priced above a bitmap of the whole partial index `remittance_line_live_uq`, whose
predicate `not released` the subquery's filter implies (49,997 entries, 271 pages; cost 16,173). EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the
statement on the failing state, for the lot's 499 runs: `Bitmap Index Scan on remittance_line_live_uq (actual
rows=51004 loops=499)`, then `Filter: … run_id = y.run_id`, `Rows Removed by Filter: 51003` — **8.7 s**. CI's figure is
the same read: 25,202,495 = 499 × 50,506 + 1 (CI's table then held 50,506 live lines). Which plan the statement got
rested on when autovacuum last analysed `remittance_line` — a matter of seconds in the job's order: with its statistics
forgotten in the transaction (as before any analyse), the same statement took a BitmapAnd of the key and the live index
(one row fetched per run, but still 51,004 index entries read per run: 1.0 s), within the test's row bound; the PR
branch's run, whose log does not show the analyse, did not meet the bitmap. The same read in two other 7a bodies: `private.run_booked_cover_check`
(the deferred LG009 check of a run set booked, which `private.ledger_check_now` fires inside the same booking: its custom
plans keep the key — not what CI hit —, its generic plan of `new.id` takes the same bitmap, 20 ms per run on that state),
and the nightly's runs booked since in `private.run_advance_checks` (a lateral like the cover's: the lot's 500 runs
booked, **8.9 s** on that state). None of the three existed on 70bfa8f.

**Fix** (`20261123080000_cover_reads_by_run_key.sql`, forward-only, sorted before 7b's `20261123090000`; behaviour
unchanged): the three bodies copied whole from `20261122090000` (lines 547, 731 and 895; SECURITY DEFINER,
`search_path ''`, `enable_seqscan off` and their grants restated), changed only in these reads. Each run's lines are read
by the run's key alone inside the `offset 0` fence — no partial index's predicate is implied there, so
`remittance_line_pkey`'s prefix is the only index the planner can use — and `not released` and the kinds are applied
outside it. « R is itself a live line of that run » ([critic] M7-MONEY-1's same-run pair, the `not exists`) reads R's
own live line by `remittance_line_live_uq` (unique) inside a fence, its run compared outside: under the same statistics
its old shape hashed every live line once per statement (the cover) or once per run (the check's generic plan) as soon as
a reversed line was met. The same rows: a live allocation or forward line of the run, and R's live line in that run —
the same predicates, only where the planner may apply them moved; pgTAP `043` (the covers at the booking and at an
N = 0 approval, LG009 at every commit, the nightly's codes) passes unchanged. On the failing state the statement took
**5.8 ms** (a bitmap of `remittance_line_pkey` by run: one row per run).

**Test** (`worker/tests/test_remitted_cover_reads_integration.py`, in the `db` job, about 7 s): a lot of 12 payouts made
through the jobs (the scale file's fixture at 12 members); in each test's rolled-back transaction, 2 × 10,000 lines
planted in two runs, one of them released (written without the insert guard and foreign keys: they belong to no run,
entry or client), and `remittance_line` analysed with `run_id`'s `n_distinct` pinned at 2 (the column's attribute
option, rolled back with the rest) — the statistics CI's scale order left. (1) The lot short of one booked as the API's
session books it (`transfer_line_options`, then `book_transfer_line`): ≤ 10 `remittance_line` rows read per member
(`pg_stat_xact_user_tables`). (2) One member's collection reversed while its run is in flight (« Désimputer »), the
booking under `plan_cache_mode = force_generic_plan` (the check's generic plan), its cover posted at the booking, the
night's checks free of violations (I23 holds), then `private.run_advance_checks` again on that check run (the
servicer's first night: the full pass over its booked runs): the booking ≤ 10 rows per member, the advance checks
≤ 5 per run + 100. On 245296d's bodies: **111,761** rows (1), **243,779** (2) and **111,717** for the advance checks — it
fails; fixed: 56, 57 and 12.

### A second read: the double payout's advance (`private.transfer_line_post`)

**What it was.** 7a ([critic] F10) gave the double payout's advance the single mandate of its transfer's run's lines:
in `private.transfer_line_post` (`20261122090000` line 1602) the insert into `public.client_advance` reads, once per
`unplanned_payout` part with an advance, `count(distinct q.mandate_id) … from public.remittance_line q where q.run_id =
(select x.run_id from public.bank_transfer x where x.id = t.transfer_id)`. Neither that function nor its caller
`public.book_transfer_line` sets `enable_seqscan = off`, so under the scale job's statistics (`n_distinct(run_id)` 2:
the run's key estimated at half the table) each part read `remittance_line` by a sequential scan. Found by this round's
verifier (VF-7A-TLP-MANDATE, medium).

**How it is reached.** The bank debits a PmtInf twice (the cancellation-after-download switch off): the second line's
options propose the lot as `unplanned_payout` parts of the booked transfers (P = 0), each with its advance. The
verifier, a 500-member lot debited twice on the state the scale files leave: **51,502,500** rows in 500 sequential
scans, **14.28 s** — cancelled at the API's 8 s.

**Why not the fenced read alone.** The shape used above (the run by `bank_transfer`'s key, then its lines by `run_id`
alone inside an `offset 0` fence, the aggregate outside) changes nothing here: under the test's planted statistics
EXPLAIN still gives `Seq Scan on remittance_line` (cost 706, 10,000 rows estimated), below the bitmap of
`remittance_line_pkey` (cost 2,574; no partial index's predicate is implied by the key) — a key estimated at half the
table is cheaper by a sequential scan whatever the statement's shape. The three functions above already had
`enable_seqscan = off`; their fence only kept a partial index from standing for the key.

**Fix** (in `20261123080000`, the same unmerged migration): `private.transfer_line_post` redefined, copied whole from
`20261122090000` line 1602 (nothing later redefines it; 7b's `20261123090000` does not), with `set enable_seqscan = off`
beside `search_path ''` and the body unchanged — the same mandate or none in every case (several mandates, a line
without one, no run, released lines counted). SECURITY DEFINER and the grants restated (EXECUTE revoked from public,
anon, authenticated and service_role; the catalog's ACL `{postgres=X/postgres}` before and after). The setting also
holds for the callees that set none of their own (`private.ledger_post_set_begin`, `private.ledger_post_set`,
`private.ledger_reverse`, `private.transfer_file_release`, `private.bank_booking_begin`, `private.ledger_check_now`):
measured below.

**Test** (the same file, its third test, about 2 s): the 12-payout lot and the same planted statistics; the PmtInf
debited whole and booked (the payouts), then debited again and booked as the API's session books it (the options'
single proposal, every part an `unplanned_payout` with its advance): no sequential scan of `remittance_line` and
≤ 10 rows read per member by the command, and each `double_payout` advance on the mandate its run's lines hold
(computed from the lines in the test, so a fix that changed the result fails). On 7a's body: **240,588** rows, **12**
sequential scans — it fails; fixed: **24**, none. Mutants: the two last rows of the table above.

**At 500 members** (a probe, not a repo test: the scale file's fixture at 500, each command in a rolled-back
transaction; 2 × 50,000 lines planted with `n_distinct(run_id)` 2 — about the table CI's scale order leaves — or the
statistics as left; both bodies, two repeats in alternating order; every nested statement through `pg_stat_statements`,
`track = all`):

| Command (500 members) | 7a's body | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| second debit, planted: `remittance_line` rows / sequential scans | 50,286,500 / 500 | 1,000 / 0 |
| — the command | 5.58 s, 18.54 s | 2.69 s, 2.79 s |
| — `transfer_line_post` / its advance insert | 3.63 s, 16.69 s / 2.83 s, 15.76 s | 0.84 s, 0.90 s / 44 ms, 47 ms |
| second debit, as left | 2.81 s, 2.74 s | 2.81 s, 2.67 s |
| first debit (the payouts), planted / as left | 1.69 s, 1.84 s / 1.73 s, 1.98 s | 1.81 s, 1.83 s / 1.73 s, 1.79 s |
| the lot short of one, planted / as left | 1.90 s, 2.00 s / 1.83 s, 1.83 s | 1.85 s, 1.83 s / 1.87 s, 1.85 s |

Statement by statement (156 to 195 nested statements per command), none of `transfer_line_post`'s or its callees' is

### Left open (low), with its default

- **`private.inflight_overdue_lines`** (20261112090000, not 7a) reads each run in flight's lines with the same shape
  (`x.run_id = r.id and not x.released and …` inside its fence): under the test's planted statistics, the night's checks
  read the planted live lines once per run approved or sent and not booked (10,048 rows for test 2's one run in flight).
  The scale files' nights pass their bounds and budgets with it (above). Default: keep; give it the same shape in a
  later slice, with the nightly's scale run measured.
- **7b** (`20261123090000_advance_recovery.sql`, built in parallel) redefines `private.run_advance_checks` from
  `20261122090000`: it must be re-copied from this migration's body (the booked runs' lateral), or the new test's
  advance-check bound fails in the `db` job.
- **The double payout advance's mandate is tested on one line per run only** (the second read's verifier). Two mutants of
  `transfer_line_post`'s mandate expression survive every test: one drops `count(q.mandate_id) = count(*)`, the other
  drops `count(distinct q.mandate_id) = 1`. The new test's lot has one line per run, and no other test books a twice-debited
  lot. The code is right: an equivalence probe over 12 cases gave 7a's body and the fix the same mandate or none in each
  (several mandates, a null `mandate_id`, released lines, no run). Default: 7c-1 adds the two cases to the new test, a run
  holding a second mandate and a line with no mandate, both expecting no mandate. **Closed by 7c-1** (ADR « M2c-7c-1 »,
  carried low 1).
- **`private.ledger_post_set`'s pooled-dimension lookup** (pre-existing since `20261111090000`; outside 7a). Each
  dimension is found by the `(organization_id, book, currency)` prefix of `ledger_account_pooled_uq`, and the other
  columns only filter. Its cost therefore grows with the lot's members × the servicer's clients: 500 dimensions with 500
  clients read 218,500 buffers in 62–87 ms. That is bounded by the 500-member lot cap and far from the 8 s timeout.
  Default: keep; make it an index-equality lookup in a later slice, with LG006 checked again.

## M2c-7b: claw-back and write-off (2026-11-23)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0 #4, §1.3, §1.4 (7b row and « Order, and why »), §2, §4 (4.1.1–4.1.11, 4.2–4.6) and
their [critic] / [check 1–3] marks; founder questions §10 none answered — Q2 (an advance of no single mandate: a request
only) and Q5 (a write-off: an admin's, with a motif and its evidence, nothing sent to the client) built as their defaults
and left open, the others later slices'. Migration `20261123090000_advance_recovery.sql` (one file, forward-only). New:
`private.advance_open`, `private.advance_mandate`, `private.advance_born_on`, `private.mandate_recovery`,
`private.advance_recovery`, `private.advance_row`, `private.commission_settlement_advance_guard` (its statement trigger),
`public.write_off_advance` (« Passer en perte »), `public.client_advances` (« Avances »), `public.client_space_advances`
(the client space). Redefined, each copied whole from its latest definition across every migration file (verified by
indexing every `create or replace function` / `create function` of the 47 files, the last one wins; the change only;
settings, `search_path ''`, SECURITY DEFINER where it was and grants restated): `private.document_open`
(`20261112090000:1715`), `private.item_settled_at` (`20261122090000:172`, 7a's), `private.run_advance_checks`
(`20261122090000:895`, 7a's), `private.remittance_line_insert_guard` (`20261113090000:1860`),
`private.transfer_line_check` (`20261119090000:739`, 801 lines), `public.register_client_document`
(`20261111120000:579`), `private.can_read_client_document_object` (`20261111120000:555`) with the policy
`document_client_money_scope` (`20261111120000:571`, dropped and created), `public.allocation_remitted`
(`20261122090000:1111`) and `public.remittance_run_payout` (`20261122090000:2085`); the label of the entry type
`advance_write_off` (`20261111090000:102`: « Abandon d'avance » → « Avance passée en perte », LEX-28). Worker: the
prepare's facts and `run._plan`. Web: « Avances », the « Passer une avance en perte » sheet, the client space, the chip
on the Reversements cards, the run page note, the « Désimputer » sentence, the texts made true. **The switch stays
off**: nothing writes `private.feature_switch`; the rules reachable only with it on are tested with it on inside
rolled-back scenarios (`044` `pg_temp.iso(name, true)`); `033` byte for byte unchanged.

### Decisions

- **D1 — what is open of an advance (plan §4.1.1–§4.1.3).** `private.advance_open`: 0 once its entry is reversed (a
  cover released, 7a), else its amount less Σ its settlements of every kind (compensation, payment_own,
  payment_dedicated, write_off); null for an id that is no advance. Its mandate is the one 7a sets at its insert
  (`private.advance_mandate`, [critic] F10: never derived from the run's lines on each read); its claim is born on its
  entry's date (`private.advance_born_on`: 7a dates a cover no earlier than the payout it covers).
- **D2 — the claw-back in the plan (plan §4.2, §4.1.9 [critic] M7-MONEY-7).** The prepare reads the client's open
  advances (`client_advance_client_idx`, each open by `private.advance_open`, its birth) and `run._plan` passes them to
  `settlement.plan` (M2c-4's take_adv): after the invoices, oldest born first (then the order they were recorded), each
  on its own mandate — never one of no mandate (NO_MANDATE: founder Q2's default, a repayment request, 7c) —, under the
  claw-back clause of that mandate's terms in force today only, from that mandate's money only; one born before the
  client's proceeding is not set off (L622-7 I, as an invoice issued before it; 7d changes the rule). An advance's own
  queue item (`client_advance`, or its reversal's `client_advance_reversal`) has no file: the facts read its advance's
  mandate (`client_advance` by its entry) and the line counts in that mandate's gross — in NO_MANDATE's, §7.2's RV-3
  would give N 200 000 / D 100 000 with 118 000 left open instead of the design's 82 000 / 218 000. The terms of the
  advances' mandates are loaded with the files' (a run whose only item of a mandate is an advance's). The inputs hash
  names the open advances (id, open, mandate).
- **D3 — re-checked at the approval (plan §4.1.4).** `private.document_open` reads an advance when no invoice has the
  id, so `remittance_approval_refusal`'s `documents_changed` sends back a run whose planned advance settle no longer
  matches (it read null and never refused). Posted at the payout's debit by `private.post_run_settlements`, unchanged
  (compensation, −4112 Da), or at the approval for N = 0.
- **D4 — the settlement guard (plan §4.1.5).** A statement trigger after insert on `public.commission_settlement`
  (`enable always`): a row of document_kind advance names an advance of its servicer and client whose entry is not
  reversed (« not an advance of its client, or its advance reversed »), and Σ its settlements stays within its amount
  (« an advance settled beyond its amount »), for every poster (a run's settlements, 7c's payments, write-offs). One
  keyed lookup per advance of the statement.
- **D5 — « Passer en perte » (plan §4.1.6; founder Q5's default; D8).** `public.write_off_advance`: an admin of the
  advance's servicer at aal2; replay + request hash; the amount in euros (`private.euros_to_minor`), within what is open,
  compare and set on the open the page showed; under the allocation and remit locks; never while a run takes it back
  (`in_flight`); its evidence an uploaded document of that client (kind `advance_write_off_evidence`); posts
  `advance_write_off` (+6780 / −4112[c], its document the evidence, key `awo:<md5 of the idempotency key>`, reason
  « Avance passée en perte (décision du JJ/MM/AAAA) ») and a `write_off` settlement; never reversed (`LG003`). Nothing
  is sent to the client: not a remission of the debt.
- **D6 — nothing reverses an advance a run is taking back ([critic] M7-MONEY-2, F2; plan §4.1.10).**
  `private.transfer_line_check`'s `double_payout` rule refuses `advance_in_flight` while an approved or sent run's plan
  names the advance (`private.advance_in_flight_run`); after the run's debit the same return is `advance_settled` (6b-2's
  rule, now reachable). 7a's release of a remitted reversal's cover already refuses so (switch on); the write-off too
  (`in_flight`).
- **D7 — an advance's line on its mandate ([check 1]; plan §4.1.9).** `private.remittance_line_insert_guard` refuses a
  line of kind client_advance or client_advance_reversal whose mandate is not its advance's (none with none).
- **D8 — the evidence kind ([critic] F11; plan §4.1.11).** `advance_write_off_evidence`: registered by money staff
  (`public.register_client_document`), read — row and file — by money staff only (the restrictive policy
  `document_client_money_scope` and `private.can_read_client_document_object` list it; `private.can_read_client_document`
  already gives every kind but the RIB and the mandate to money staff only).
- **D9 — the pages and texts (plan §4.3).** « Avances » (Reversements): client, recording date, origin (« Paiement
  repris après reversement (dossier …) », « Reversement au-delà du dû », « Virement hors reversement »), advanced,
  recovered (with what was passed as a loss), left, recovery (« Reprise sur les prochains reversements (art. … du
  mandat) », « Demande de remboursement (pas de clause de reprise) », « Demande de remboursement (avance rattachée à
  aucun mandat unique) », « Reprise par RV-… en cours »), keyset-paged, « Passer en perte » for an admin; the sheet
  states « Le cabinet enregistre une perte de X € (compte 6780). Collectoo ne réclame plus cette somme au client (ni
  reprise, ni demande de remboursement) ; rien ne lui est envoyé : ce n'est pas une remise de dette. Irréversible. »; the
  client space « Avances du cabinet à rembourser : X € » with each advance's date, origin, what is left and how it is
  recovered (never what was passed as a loss); the chip « Avance à récupérer X » on the Reversements cards; the run page
  note per advance and how it is recovered; the « Désimputer » sentence « Elle sera reprise sur ses prochains
  reversements (art. … du mandat) » or « Une demande de remboursement pourra lui être adressée »; `advance_open`,
  `payout_overrun` and `double_payout_open` gain « Avec une clause de reprise, elle est déduite des prochains
  reversements du client ; sinon elle reste à récupérer (page « Avances »). Un administrateur peut la passer en
  perte. »; `advance_settled` « Cette avance a déjà été en partie récupérée : ce retour ne peut pas être comptabilisé
  dans Collectoo ; prévenez le support. »; the unplanned payout's effect sentence (`NOT_YET_RECOVERED`) « reprise sur les
  prochains reversements du client si son mandat a une clause de reprise, sinon à récupérer (page « Avances ») ».
  `terms.ts` (« Avances du cabinet reprises sur les reversements suivants ») is now true, unchanged.
- **D10 — the 7a carry-over (ADR-0014 7a round 3 « Left open », « The return named for an item its run never
  carried »).** `private.item_settled_at`: when the item's attributions not netted in its run (those of the unplanned
  payouts that paid it, live or come back, whose return is not a line of the run itself) cover its line, the run's own
  payout never carried it, so what came back on its way is « unplanned » once one of those payouts came back (it said
  « run » while the money waited and once a later run paid it). `044` k (17 j, then U back, then W), seen failing first.
- **`advance_open`'s detail (plan §4.1.8).** `run_advance_checks` adds `recovery` (the mandate's terms in force on the
  day the checks hold the books to); its codes are unchanged (`044` h pins them, as `043` #33).

### Deviations from the plan

- **The migration's name** is the task's, `20261123090000_advance_recovery.sql`.
- **The recovery of an advance of no mandate is `request_no_mandate`**, worded « Demande de remboursement (avance
  rattachée à aucun mandat unique) » (the plan's `request_several_mandates`, « (plusieurs mandats) »): a null mandate
  is also a forward on no file (a remitted reversal's cover) or a client part with no transfer (S13), never only a run
  of several mandates.
- **`private.can_read_client_document` is not redefined** (the plan names three functions): its body already gives
  every kind but the RIB and the mandate to money staff only, so the new kind needs no change there; the two others
  and the restrictive policy are redefined.
- **The client space reads `public.client_space_advances`** (new; the plan: the page reads `client_advance` through its
  RLS): what is open of an advance is SQL's (`private.advance_open`), never the page's subtraction; it is readable by
  the client's whole-client members and by money staff, and never says what was passed as a loss.
- **Helpers beyond the plan:** `private.mandate_recovery` (one rule for the page, the client space, the nightly, the
  run page and « Désimputer »), `private.advance_recovery`, `private.advance_row` (one row of « Avances »).
- **Two more redefinitions** than the plan's 7b list: `public.allocation_remitted` (each entry's `recovery` and
  `clause_ref`, for the « Désimputer » sentence the plan asks back, [critic] L19 (d)) and `public.remittance_run_payout`
  (each advance's id, open part from `private.advance_open`, `reversed`, `written_off_minor`, `recovery`, `clause_ref`,
  for the run page note).
- **The run page note is not « … déduite de ce reversement par compensation »** (plan §4.3): the advances it lists are
  those recorded at this payout's debit (7a's `remittance_run_payout.advances`), which a later run takes back, never this
  one. It reads « Avance du cabinet enregistrée le JJ/MM/AAAA (<cause>) : X €, » then « à reprendre sur les prochains
  reversements du client (clause de reprise, art. … du mandat) », « à récupérer par une demande de remboursement (pas
  de clause de reprise) » (or « (avance rattachée à aucun mandat unique) »), « reste Y € … » in part, « récupérée »,
  « soldée (dont Z € passés en perte) », or « annulée (le virement hors reversement qui avait payé l'encaissement est
  revenu) ». What this run itself recovered is still « Avances du cabinet récupérées par compensation le … » (M2c-6b).
- **The client space says « une demande de remboursement pourra vous être adressée »** (plan « vous sera adressée »):
  7c sends it; « pourra » is true now. The « Avances » intro and the checks' help say « elle reste à récupérer ».
- **`advance_in_flight` keeps 7a's text** (review round 1, tests-ui-2: « … ne peut pas être comptabilisé tant que ce
  reversement n'est pas débité ; après son débit, prévenez le support. »): the plan's « sera comptabilisable après son
  débit (il sera alors refusé …) » contradicts itself; the refusal carries no run number.
- **The write-off's key is `awo:<md5 of the idempotency key>`** (the plan's `awo:<key>`), as 7a's « Couvrir »: an entry's
  key bounds its length. Two refusals more than the plan's: `bad_request` (the open text the page sent is not minor
  units) and `reason_required` (the motif, 1–2,000 characters).
- **Screenshots:** `m2c7-avances`, `m2c7-avance-perte` as planned; the Reversements page with the chip is
  `m2c7-reversements-avance` (the plan retakes `m2c-reversements` and `m2c-reversement`: those files belong to
  `remittances.spec.ts`, whose tenant holds no advance; `m2c-reversements` is retaken for its new « Avances » link,
  `m2c-reversement` differs only by dates and ids and is kept; the run page's note shows in 7a's flow, which the 7b
  steps extend, and `m2c7-desimputer-deja-reverse` is retaken for the sheet's recovery sentence).
- **The E2E steps extend 7a's `remitted-reversal.spec.ts`** (its flow builds the remitted collection and its advance)

  run's own settlement: if U's return is paid by a later run while the run's own payout's return still waits, the item
  reads `paid_on` null though the client has it again. Default: keep (conservative for 7c-2's `payout_not_received`; no
  money path reads `paid_on`).

  (`commission_settlement_read`, M2c-4, unchanged); the client space shows only what is still claimed and never words a

  `private.advance_open`** (no partial index on what is open): the page reads every closed advance it passes over.
  Default: keep at today's volumes (advances are rare); an index on what is open needs a column the settlements update.

  failure between the two leaves an unregistered object, as « Joindre un document ». Default: keep (a retry reuses the
  same key).

## M2c-7b review fixes (2026-11-23)

### Round 1

The review of `70796ea` raised thirteen items: one high and one medium of the money lens (M7B-MONEY-1, M7B-MONEY-2),
the same medium twice more (tests-ui-1, CCS-1: one item, fixed once), seven lows of tests and pages (tests-ui-2 … 8) and
one of cost (CCS-2). Each was checked against the code first (the worker's real prepare and the SQL on the main stack,
inside rolled-back transactions, the switch on only where the item needs it); all hold. The migration
`20261123090000_advance_recovery.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place: no function is redefined beyond the
slice's nine, two helpers are new (`private.client_opening_on`, `private.advance_recovery_of`), no public signature
changes (`recovery` is a value inside the reads' `jsonb`), `database.types.ts` is unchanged (regenerated, identical).
**The switch stays off**; `033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`043` keep every assertion and expected value (`037`,
`037b`, `038`, `043` change only their emulated prepares' trigger, below).

- **M7B-MONEY-1 (high; fixed at the root: each pair of queue rows in one bucket).** 7b put every advance's queue row on
  its advance's mandate. A remitted reversal's cover pairs with R(E), on E's file (the same mandate): right. A double
  payout's advance (on the payout's run's single mandate M) pairs with its unplanned payout's −U row, which has no file
  (NO_MANDATE): M's room grew by A and `settlement._cap_to_pool` then charged NO_MANDATE's −U to the whole client pool,
  so M's claw-back took the advance out of another mandate's collections (no claw-back clause there) or out of a
  re-queued `payout_returned` (never netted: Q17 / OQ-97), and M's netting set its invoices off against them too.
  Reproduced through `run.prepare_run` with the facts as loaded: the review's M/M2 case (a double payout of 50 000 on
  M, claw-back art. 7.4; a collection of 70 000 on M2, netting only) gave advances 50 000, N 7 400 — now 0 and 57 400.
  Reached with the switch off (S03r: a returned payout paid again by a later run, then executed again by the bank).
  The same root with the switch on: a cancelled run's released items its late execution paid stay on their mandate
  while that payout's −U row sits in NO_MANDATE (M's room inflated by what the client already had). Fix:
  - `run._advance_item_mandate`: an advance's row counts in its advance's mandate only for a remitted reversal's cover
    (its release too); a double payout's or an overrun's counts in none, with the rows of no file it pairs with (as
    before 7b). The facts carry the advance's cause (`jobs/remittances.py`: `ca.cause`), the rule is pure.
    `private.remittance_line_insert_guard` expects the same (none for every other cause).
  - `run._unplanned_paid_out`: what an unplanned payout of the run already paid of a line of the run — its live
    attributions (`private.unplanned_paid_item` by its key, the booking not reversed: the prepare's new read, only when
    the run holds an `unplanned_payout` row) — counts with that payout's row, outside every mandate; Σ gross unchanged.
    With the switch off an attribution is always of a `payout_returned` item (NO_MANDATE already): a no-op; with it on,
    a released item's mandate brings only what the late payout did not pay (`test_transfer_line_ops_more_integration`:
    {M: 200 000 − A, none: 0}, was {M: 200 000, none: −A}). The inputs hash names the attributions.
  - Pinned: pytest `test_a_double_payout_s_advance_is_never_taken_from_another_mandate_s_money` (the review's case),
    `…_never_taken_from_a_re_queued_payout` and `test_a_mandate_s_netting_never_reaches_another_mandate_s_money_through_a_double_payout`
    (its two variants), `test_a_double_payout_s_advance_is_taken_from_its_own_mandate_s_collections`,
    `test_an_overrun_advance_s_item_counts_outside_every_mandate`, `test_what_an_unplanned_payout_paid_of_a_line_is_no_mandate_s_money`
    (switch on); the Hypothesis property `test_a_mandate_takes_only_from_its_own_money_whatever_the_run_s_other_rows`
    (500 examples: covers with their reversals, double payouts with attributions, returned payouts, earlier advances of
    either mandate or none; each mandate's money in the plan equals its collections less what the run's unplanned
    payouts paid of them, its takes stay within it); integration `test_an_overrun_advance_s_row_is_no_mandate_s_money`
    (the real prepare and approval, a second mandate's collection: advance 0, N 127 400, the row on no mandate, the
    approval's guard accepts it) and the switch-on assertion above; pgTAP `044` l (the insert guard: a double payout's
    and an overrun's row, and the double payout's reversal's, on none; on the advance's mandate refused). All failed first

- **M7B-MONEY-2 = tests-ui-1 = CCS-1 (medium; fixed).** `private.mandate_recovery` named the claw-back whenever the

### Left open (low), with its default

- **CCS-2: what is open of an advance is computed per row** (`private.advance_open`), so « Avances »' totals, its
  open-only page, the client space and the prepare's open advances read every advance the servicer (or the client) ever
  recorded, settled ones included (about 30 µs each: 5,000 settled advances, 147 ms for the chip's call). Default: keep
  at today's volumes (advances are rare; no real remittance before M2c-7) — the 7b « Left open » on « Avances »' read
  stands; 7f's hardening takes the chip's totals from the 4112[c] balances (the nightly `advance_ledger` proves them
  equal) or a keyed set of open advances, and moves the chip read out of the page's auto-refresh.
- **A portfolio moved to another mandate between E's run and R(E)** puts a cover's row (its advance's mandate: E's
  line's) and R(E)'s (the file's mandate today) in two buckets. Default: keep (no command moves a portfolio's mandate in
  M2c; 7f's property machine adds the case if one appears).
- **A cover's release re-queued in a later run than the collection it covered** (switch on: the late payout that paid
  E comes back after E, R(E) and the cover were remitted): the release's −A counts in the cover's mandate and the
  unplanned return's +A outside every mandate (never netted, as any returned payout, Q17): that mandate's room is the
  lower — less is set off, never more. Default: keep (conservative).
- Founder questions Q2 and Q5 (plan §10) keep their defaults, open. Q18 stays 7d's: an advance born since the opening
  is still taken back under its clause (the plan's 7b rule, as invoices), and the pages say so; only one born before
  it is `barred_proceeding`. The switch stays off.

### Round 2

Round 2 raised three items: one high (REBASE-7B) and two mediums (advance-date-contradicts-barred, SWEEP-7B-STATS).
Each was checked against the code first, on the main stack, inside rolled-back transactions. Since round 1, 7a was
squash-merged to `main` as `245296d` (the same tree as `36a662d`, 7b's base), and main's scale job went red: the CI
round `349fc3b` (« M2c-7a — CI round (main) » above, `20261123080000_cover_reads_by_run_key.sql`) is not merged yet.
7b is rebuilt on it: branch `m2c7b-r2` from `349fc3b`, then `70796ea` and `78942f4` cherry-picked. Only the docs
conflicted (this ADR and `docs/benchmarks/remittances.md`), and both sides were kept, with the 7a CI round's sections
before 7b's. The migration `20261123090000_advance_recovery.sql` is still unmerged and was edited in place. It now has
two new internal functions (`private.client_open_advances`, `private.unplanned_paid_live`). No public signature changes
(`born_on` is a key inside the reads' `jsonb`), and `database.types.ts` was regenerated identical. **The switch stays
off**; `033` is unchanged byte for byte; `034`–`043` keep every assertion and expected value.

- **REBASE-7B (high; fixed).** The item holds. 7b's `private.run_advance_checks` was copied whole from
  `20261122090000` line 895, with round 1 adding the details' `recovery`. Applied after `20261123080000`, it put back the
  nightly's read of the booked runs' lines that the CI round removed: « run_id = r.id and not released and kind in
  (…) » inside the fence, a bitmap of `remittance_line_live_uq` read whole once per run booked (VF-7B-RECOPY). Measured
  with `test_remitted_cover_reads_integration.py` on 7b's old body: the advance checks read **110,265** rows for a
  12-run lot, against a bound of 160. The function is now `20261123080000` line 138's body plus 7b's single hunk (the
  `recovery` key of `advance_open`'s details). The diffs confirm it: diff(the CI body, 7b's new body) is exactly
  diff(`20261122090000`'s body, 7b's old body), and diff(7b's old body, its new one) is exactly the CI round's hunk.
  Its header now cites `20261123080000:138`. On 7b the cover-reads test passes 2/2: the booking reads 56 rows, the
  booking under generic plans 57, and the advance checks **12** (the CI round's own number, the bound 160).
  `20261123080000` redefines `private.cover_booked_run_reversals`, `private.run_booked_cover_check` and
  `private.run_advance_checks`. 7b's other redefined functions are `private.document_open`, `private.item_settled_at`,
  `private.remittance_line_insert_guard`, `private.transfer_line_check`, `public.register_client_document`,
  `private.can_read_client_document_object`, `public.allocation_remitted` and `public.remittance_run_payout`. None of
  them is redefined there, and each is still copied from its latest definition across every migration (checked file by
  file). The CI round's second commit on `ci-fix-7a` (`245ce62`, `private.transfer_line_post` with `enable_seqscan`
  off) redefines none of 7b's functions either. Rebasing onto it will conflict only in the docs.
- **advance-date-contradicts-barred (medium; fixed).** The item holds. In `044` m's own case, the cover is born d − 2
  (`private.advance_born_on`: its payout's debit, the date the barred rule reads) and recorded today, and the client's
  proceeding opened d − 1. The client space then read « Avance du <today> (…) — antérieure à l'ouverture de votre
  procédure collective … », a date after the opening beside a statement that the advance predates it. « Avances »
  dated the row by its recording too (column « Date »). And the client space said « Avances du cabinet à rembourser »
  over a list of `barred_proceeding` advances only: pre-opening claims the client may not pay outside the proceeding.
  The fix:
  - `private.advance_row` (hence `public.client_advances`) and `public.client_space_advances` return `born_on`
    (`private.advance_born_on`, read once per advance and passed to the recovery).
  - The client reads « Avance née le JJ/MM/AAAA (…) ».
  - « Avances »' column is « Née le » (`born_on`); the recording date appears under it as « enregistrée le … », only
    when it falls on another day (`advanceDates`).
  - The client space heading says « à rembourser » only when no open advance is `barred_proceeding`. Otherwise it reads
    « Avances du cabinet : <total> », and each line states its own fact. No rule is invented; the lines' wording is
    unchanged.
  - The rows' order is unchanged (by recording).
  - Pinned by `044` m (round 2), a new assertion (plan 17 → 18), seen failing (`born_on` null): `born_on` = d − 2 =
    `advance_born_on` < the opening (d − 1) < the recording (d), on both reads, both `barred_proceeding`.
  - Pinned by vitest: the dates (born ≠ recorded, and the same day), the client lines « née le » with a fixture born
    before its recording, the heading neutral for a barred-only list and for a mixed one, and both parsers refusing a
    row without `born_on`.
  - Pinned by the E2E: « Avance née le … » in the client space and the « Née le » cell on « Avances ».
- **SWEEP-7B-STATS (medium as raised; the SQL is not exposed, the worker's loader was; fixed).** Every statement 7b
  adds or redefines that reads `remittance_line`, `private.remittance_pending`, `ledger_entry`, `ledger_posting`,
  `allocation`, `client_advance`, `commission_settlement`, `bank_transfer`, `private.unplanned_paid_item`,
  `client_status_event` or `mandate_terms` by a parameter or a correlated key is listed below, with the rows it read
  from the planted tables. The measurement is `worker/tests/test_advance_reads_integration.py` (db job, two tests,
  about 8 s). Planting: `remittance_line` as the cover-reads test plants it (2 × 10,000 lines, one run released,
  `n_distinct(run_id)` 2, and `remittance_line_live_uq` rebuilt); 10,000 rows each over two values of every key read
  below (`commission_settlement`: `document_id`, client; `client_advance`: servicer, client, `cause_entry_id`;
  `unplanned_paid_item`: `booking_entry_id`, `ledger_entry_id`, servicer; `remittance_pending`: `draft_run_id`, client;
  `client_status_event`: client; `mandate_terms`: mandate). Each table is analysed with those columns' `n_distinct`
  pinned at 2, and every plan is forced generic (`plan_cache_mode`). Then a 6-payout lot, its line booked short of
  one, and three collections taken back (« Désimputer »: three covers). The rows counted are each table's sequential
  reads plus the index entries its indexes returned (`pg_stat_get_xact_tuples_returned`), so an index-only or bitmap
  read of a whole index counts. `ledger_entry` and `ledger_posting` are read only by unique keys (`id`,
  `ledger_entry_reversed_once_uq`, `entry_id`); `allocation` and `bank_transfer` are not read by 7b's new statements.
  None of them is planted.

  | 7b statement (`20261123090000` line, or the worker) | table: key (index) | rows read |
  |---|---|---|
  | `advance_open` (51) | `client_advance`: id (pkey); its entry's reversal (unique); `commission_settlement`: `document_id` (`_document_idx`) | 1 |
  | `advance_mandate` (69), `advance_born_on` (82) | `client_advance`: id; `ledger_entry`: id | 1, 1 |
  | `advance_recovery` (154) → `advance_recovery_of` (138), `client_opening_on` (121), `mandate_recovery` (98) | `client_status_event`: client (`_client_idx`); `mandate_terms`: mandate (its exclusion index) | 3 |
  | `document_open` (214), its advance branch | `commission_invoice`: id; then `advance_open` | 1 |
  | `advance_row` (383) | `client_advance`: id; settlements by `document_id`; the recovery | 6 |
  | `client_advances` (429), all three advances / one client | `client_advance`: servicer (`_org_idx`) or client; `advance_open` per row; the totals | 27 / 14 |
  | `client_space_advances` (493) | `client_advance`: client and servicer (`_client_idx`) | 6 |
  | `item_settled_at` (544; its 7b hunk) | `remittance_line`: `ledger_entry_id`, live (`_live_uq`, unique); `unplanned_paid_item`: `ledger_entry_id` (`_entry_idx`) | 0 |
  | `run_advance_checks` (668; the CI body + the recovery) | the booked runs' lines by the run's key (CI's fence); `client_advance`: servicer; settlements by `document_id` | 17 |
  | `commission_settlement_advance_guard` (242), in `write_off_advance` (296) | `new_rows`; `client_advance`: id; settlements by `document_id` | 6 |
  | `remittance_line_insert_guard` (825; its 7b hunk), in the approval job | `client_advance`: `entry_id` (unique) | 1 (+ 2 settlements, `document_open`) |
  | `transfer_line_check` (883; `advance_in_flight`), its statement prepared generic, seq scans off | `client_advance`: `cause_entry_id` (`_cause_idx`); `advance_in_flight_run` (`remittance_run_pending_uq`, unique) | 0 |
  | `allocation_remitted` (1779), `remittance_run_payout` (1820) | the recovery; `client_advance`: transfer; settlements by `document_id` | 0, 4 |
  | worker `load_facts`: the items' advances (7b's join) | `client_advance`: `entry_id` | **10,003** (a hash of the whole table) → 1 per item |
  | worker `_open_advances` (7b) | `client_advance`: client, currency | **10,005** (a sequential scan) → 5 |
  | worker `_unplanned_paid` (round 1), eight bookings | `unplanned_paid_item`: `booking_entry_id = any(…)` | **10,000** (a sequential scan) → 0 |

  Every SQL function reads by key under these statistics. Most of them already have `enable_seqscan` off, and the rest
  read by primary or unique keys only. The PostgreSQL 17 generic plan prices each non-unique probe at half the table,
  and none of these tables' other indexes offers a cheaper read of the whole table. The worker's three 7b statements were
  exposed: its session has sequential scans on, so the generic plan of the items' join hashed the whole of
  `client_advance` (the queue's draft priced at half of `remittance_pending`), and the open advances and the
  attributions were sequential scans. `load_facts` read **20,008** `client_advance` rows before the fix (WIP `521d9a3`,
  seen failing). The fix:
  - the items' advance is a fenced lateral probe by its entry (`client_advance_entry_id_key`, unique);
  - the open advances go through `private.client_open_advances(client, currency)` (`client_advance_client_idx`, the
    conditions outside the fence, `advance_open` once per advance, seq scans off);
  - the attributions go through `private.unplanned_paid_live(bookings)` (the primary key's prefix, seq scans off).
  - Both functions are internal: revoked from `public`, `anon` and `authenticated`, granted to `service_role` like
    `advance_open`.
  - After the fix, `load_facts` reads 6 `client_advance` rows, `_open_advances` 5 and `_unplanned_paid` 0.

  By the severity rule this is low today. At the scale files' volumes, `client_advance` and `unplanned_paid_item` hold
  a few rows (no scale file records an advance: `draft50k`'s 50,000 entries are of type `client_advance`, not
  `client_advance` rows). The worker's statements also run custom plans: psycopg prepares a statement after five
  executions, and the plan cache keeps the custom plan while the generic is priced higher, as it is under these
  statistics. It is fixed anyway because the three statements are 7b's own and the fixes are small. The earlier
  slices' reads that the same test sees are printed apart and not bounded (« Left open » below).

## M2c-7c-1: client payments and refunds (2026-11-24)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0 #5, §1.3, §1.4 (7c-1 row and « Order, and why »), §2 (2.1–2.4, with 7c-1's widened
shapes), §5.0, §5.1 (`client_credit` and the recovery table), §5.2.1–§5.2.6, the checks of §5.2.8 that concern them,
§5.5 but the request, §5.7's `045` (b)–(f), (i), (j)–(l), §5.8 (7c-1's part), and their [critic] / [check 1–3] marks.
The request (7c-2: its tables, `request_advance_repayment`, the letter, `045b`) is not in this slice. Founder questions
(plan §10), none answered: Q4 (a: the client designates with its evidence, else invoices due, advances, the other
invoices; the surplus a credit owed back; a client in a proceeding never pays a pre-opening claim), Q5's recovery part
(a: a later repayment of a written-off advance booked as income) and Q7 (a: the servicer's own transfer, recorded after
the fact with its proof) built as their defaults and left open. Migration `20261124090000_client_payments.sql` (one
file, forward-only). New: the books 419 (`client_credit_owed`, per client) and 7714 (`written_off_recovered`, pooled),
Collectoo's labels; the tables `public.client_credit` and `public.advance_write_off_recovery` (RLS, change log,
append-only, a statement guard each) and the settlements' guard of a credit's refunds
(`private.commission_settlement_credit_guard`); the reads `public.client_open_documents` (« Ce que le client doit au
cabinet »), `public.client_payment_preview` (the sheet's live effect), `public.client_payment_line` (a dedicated-account
line), `public.client_space_credits` (the client space); the commands `public.record_client_payment`,
`public.book_client_payment_line`, `public.record_client_refund`; the plan (`private.client_payment_order`,
`private.client_payment_plan`, `private.client_settlement_plan`) and its helpers. Redefined, each copied whole from its
latest definition across every migration file (verified by indexing every `create or replace function` /
`create function` of the 43 files, the last one wins, and diffing each copy against it: only the change; settings,
`search_path ''`, SECURITY DEFINER where it was and grants restated): `private.ledger_post_set` (`20261111090000:889`),
`private.ledger_entry_verify` (`20261111090000:295`), `public.ledger_balance` (`20261111090000:1416`),
`public.accounting_export_entries` (`20261116090000:4494`), `private.run_advance_checks` (`20261123090000:674`, 7b's:
PR #42's body and 7b's recovery), `public.register_client_document` (`20261123090000:1701`, 7b's),
`private.can_read_client_document_object` (`20261123090000:1757`, 7b's), `public.client_space_advances`
(`20261123090000:497`, carried low 3); the constraint `ledger_account_shape` (`20261111090000:161`), the policies
`ledger_account_read` (`20261111090000:1394`) and `document_client_money_scope` (`20261123090000:1776`), the check
`commission_settlement_document_kind_check` (`20261112090000:435`); the three client-money types' allowed books

the chart (`ledger/model.py`: the two books, the allowed books, the three widened shapes, a client's payment naming
its client; `test_ledger_integration.py` compares it with the database). Web: « Ce que le client doit au cabinet » on
the client's « Reversement » page with « Enregistrer un règlement » and « Enregistrer le remboursement »,
« Règlement d'une facture ou d'une avance du cabinet » on a client's line of « Débits et retours », « Enregistrer le
remboursement » on a credit note, the client space's « Sommes que le cabinet vous doit », the texts made true. **The
switch stays off**: nothing writes `private.feature_switch`. The commands read approved and sent runs' plans (plan

reachable only with it on — a run cancelled after download no longer holds them, and the client's payment settles

asserts the switch is off at the end; `033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`044` unchanged.

### Decisions

- **D1 — the books and the shapes ([check 1] gap 2; plan §5.0).** Two rows of `public.ledger_book`: `419`
  « Mandants — sommes à leur rembourser » (`client_credit_owed`, dimension client, the servicer's fund, normal side
  credit, not client-visible) and `7714` « Rentrées sur avances passées en perte » (`written_off_recovered`, pooled) —
  the numbers are Collectoo's labels (`account_number` is NOT NULL unique), the accountant maps them (OQ-88, OQ-98).
  `client_payment_own` and `client_payment_dedicated` may post both, `client_refund_own` 419; no other type touches
  either (their allowed books refuse it, `LG002`). The account shape puts 419 with the per-client books (the client
  set, nothing else) and 7714 with the pooled ones. `ledger_post_set`: 419 joins the per-client lists (the line's
  client, the given-client rule, the client check) and both books the servicer fund's closure list. I3′
  (`ledger_entry_verify`): two counts each (`n_cco`/`d_cco`, `n_rec`/`d_rec`); a client payment has at most one credit
  line on each of 4111, 4112, 419, 7714 and none in debit, at least one of the four, the VAT pair as before, and
  `n = 1 (or 3 on the dedicated account) + n_com + n_adv + n_cco + n_rec + n_vatp + n_vatc`; `client_refund_own` is two
  lines, −5122 and exactly one of +4111 or +419. The read policy `ledger_account_read` and `public.ledger_balance` give
  both books to money staff only; `accounting_export_entries` lists them with the servicer's fund (a payment with a
  surplus, a recovery or a credit's refund balances in the export).
- **D2 — what a payment settles (plan §5.2.3; founder Q4; [critic] L16, M7-MONEY-10, L21; [check 1] gap 11).**
  `private.client_payment_plan` (pure, plpgsql; twin `remittance.client_payments.plan_client_payment`, Hypothesis
  parity through the database): with the client's designation, the documents it names in its order, each up to its open
  part — one it may not pay (`private.document_client_payable` false: born before its proceeding opened, L622-7 I al. 1)
  becomes a credit of cause `procedure` naming it (`details`), never a settlement —, then the written-off advances it
  names, each up to what is left to recover; without a designation, the default order (`private.client_payment_order`:
  invoices due on or before the payment's date by (due date, year, number), advances by (birth, recording, id), the
  other invoices by (due date nulls last, year, number)) over what the client may pay — a pre-opening document is
  skipped, never paid. What is left is one credit owed back, of cause `procedure` while a `proceeding_opened` or a
  `liquidation` of the client stands on the payment's date (`private.client_proceeding_stands`), else `overpayment`:
  never refused. Documents an approved or sent run settles are never planned (`private.client_payment_free`, from
  `private.document_in_flight_run`, the twin of `advance_in_flight_run` for every document); named, they are refused
  `in_flight` with the run's number. VAT moved per invoice part: `private.vat_part` = R(pending × part / open), all of
  it when the part closes the invoice (the run plan's rule). The client's documents are read once
  (`private.client_payment_docs`: its invoices by `commission_invoice_client_idx`, its open advances by
  `private.client_open_advances`, each one's open part, pending VAT, payability and run in flight).
- **D3 — « Règlement du client » on the own account (plan §5.2.4).** `public.record_client_payment`: admins and ops
  managers at aal2; replay and request hash; the amount in euros (`bad_amount`), its value date not in the future
  (`bad_date`), the evidence a `client_payment_evidence` of that client (`evidence_required`), the own account active,
  purpose own, in the currency (`no_own_account`), the designation (documents or recoveries named) only with a
  `payment_designation_evidence` of that client (`designation_evidence_required`: ops never choose, C. civ. 1342-10
  al. 1); under the allocation and remit locks (`remittance_command_locks(org, true)`: the plans of approved runs read
  under the locks approvals take) — a named document with nothing open, of another client or currency, or a named
  written-off advance with nothing left to recover → `not_open`; in flight → `in_flight`; what it may settle ≠ what the
  page showed → `open_changed`. Posts `client_payment_own` (+5122[own] P / −4111 Σ invoice parts / −4112 Σ advance parts
  / −419 Σ credits / −7714 Σ recoveries ‖ +44574 v / −44571 v), dated the value date, its document the evidence, key
  `cpay:<md5 of the idempotency key>`, reason « Règlement du client par virement sur le compte du cabinet (valeur
  JJ/MM/AAAA) »; one `commission_settlement` per document part (`payment_own`, its VAT moved), one `client_credit` per
  cause (their sum the −419 line), one `advance_write_off_recovery` per recovery; then `ledger_check_now()`. No R124-6
  receipt: not a debtor's payment (CPCE-07).
- **D4 — the dedicated account (plan §5.2.5; [critic] F7, M7-MONEY-12, L16).** `public.book_client_payment_line`: the
  funds pass's lock order — the allocation lock, the line `for no key update`, then the remit lock — and the line's facts
  read under them (`private.client_line_facts`): a credit of kind `client_transfer_in` (or released as one) on an active
  `client_funds` account, not a held duplicate (`not_a_client_credit`), carrying none of our references (our transfers,
  our lots, an unsplit part of ours, a `TOP` id, an RMT/SWP/TOP id in its label: `our_reference`), neither linked, booked,
  released nor a payment (`line_booked`), from the IBAN of exactly one client's **confirmed** payout account (active,
  returned or retired; never a proposed or rejected one: `not_a_client_credit`, `ambiguous_client`). The whole line is
  the amount; a designation as D3, or a label naming each designated invoice's number. Posts
  `client_payment_dedicated` (+5120[b] P / −4679 P ‖ +4689 P / −4111 / −4112 / −419 / −7714 ‖ VAT), dated the line's
  booking date, key `cpayd:<line>`, one `bank_line_booking` (`client_payment`, method ops, the motif) — the booking
  guard's `client_payment` arm already admits it (`20261121090000:784-787`, not redefined; `045` d) —, the line's
  review deleted, the settlements (`payment_dedicated`), credits and recoveries, `ledger_check_now()` and the line's
  booking check. The servicer's share on 4679 grows by P; the next file's sweep takes it (S unchanged).
- **D5 — refunds (plan §5.2.6; founder Q7).** `public.record_client_refund`: a credit note's refund still owed
  (`private.document_open`) or a credit owed back (its amount less its refunds, `private.client_credit_open`); admins and
  ops managers at aal2; replay and hash; `bad_amount`, `bad_date`, `bad_request`, `evidence_required` (a
  `client_refund_evidence` of that client), `no_own_account`, then under the locks `nothing_owed`, `in_flight` (a credit
  note an approved or sent run refunds; a credit is never in a run's plan), `owed_changed`, `amount_exceeds_owed`. Posts
  `client_refund_own` (+4111 or +419 / −5122), key `crfd:<md5>`, and a `refund` settlement (`document_kind`
  `credit_note` or `client_credit`): `credit_refund_owed` stops; a credit's refunds never exceed it (the guard).
- **D6 — what the servicer owes back ([critic] M7-MONEY-10, L21; [check 1] gap 8).** `public.client_credit` (cause
  `overpayment` or `procedure`, `details` for a designated pre-opening document, `entry_id` the payment that posted its
  −419 line, unique (entry_id, cause)); its statement guard: each payment's rows sum to minus its 419 posting, for its
  client, and only a client payment holds them. `public.advance_write_off_recovery` (primary key (entry_id,
  advance_id)): its guard keeps Σ per advance ≤ what was passed as a loss and the payment's −7714 line = Σ its rows. Both
  append-only (`refuse_change`, `enable always`), change-logged, RLS on with every privilege revoked but the read
  policies: credits for money staff and the client's whole-client members (never a restricted member, a collector or
  another tenant), recoveries for money staff only.
- **D7 — the nightly (plan §5.2.8, §5.0 (7)).** `run_advance_checks` adds `client_credit_owed` (alert: a credit with an
  open part more than 15 days after its recording; at once and `p0` for cause `procedure`), `client_credit_ledger`
  (violation, per client and currency: Σ the credits' open parts = −Σ 419) and `written_off_recovery_ledger` (violation,
  the servicer: Σ recoveries = −Σ 7714). `045` x asserts the full list of codes (043 #33, 044 h's, extended).
- **D8 — the evidence kinds ([critic] L16; plan §5.1).** `client_payment_evidence`, `client_refund_evidence`,
  `payment_designation_evidence`: registered by money staff (`register_client_document`), read — row and file — by money
  staff only (`document_client_money_scope`, `can_read_client_document_object`; `can_read_client_document` already
  gives every kind but the RIB and the mandate to money staff only). The web uploads to the client's key, then registers
  (`lib/remittance/evidence.ts`), as « Joindre un document ».
- **D9 — the pages and texts (plan §5.5 but the request).** « Ce que le client doit au cabinet »: invoices (open, VAT
  pending, « Créance antérieure à l'ouverture de la procédure du client » when it is), advances (and how each is
  recovered), written-off advances with something left to recover, refunds owed, credits owed back, the default order;
  « Enregistrer un règlement » (« Montant reçu (€) », « Date de valeur », « Preuve du virement », « Le client a-t-il
  désigné ce qu'il règle ? » with « Pièce de la désignation » and the documents in the client's order) and its live
  effect from SQL (« FC-… : X € réglés (dont TVA Y € devenue exigible) ; avance du JJ/MM/AAAA : X € remboursés ;
  trop-perçu de X € à rembourser au client »; a pre-opening part, a procedure's surplus and a recovery worded as plan
  §5.5 says); « Enregistrer le remboursement » on a credit owed back and on a credit note; on « Débits et retours », a
  client's credit gets « Règlement d'une facture ou d'une avance du cabinet » beside « Paiement relayé par le client »
  (« La somme revient au cabinet : elle sera virée sur son compte propre avec la prochaine quote-part. »); the review
  text `client_credit` and `credit_refund_owed`'s help reworded as the plan says; the three checks worded; the client
  space « Trop-perçu du JJ/MM/AAAA : X € que le cabinet vous doit » (or « Somme reçue le …, mise de côté pour votre
  procédure collective »). Refusals in French per code (`lib/remittance/settlements.ts`). No text words a write-off
  « abandon » or « remise » (LEX-28).

### Deviations from the plan

- **The migration's name** is the task's, `20261124090000_client_payments.sql`; pgTAP `045_client_payments.test.sql`
  (the plan's `045_client_settlements`; `045b` is 7c-2's).
- **`client_credit` has no `payment_entry_id`**: its `entry_id` is the payment's own entry (the payment posts the −419
  line), so the second column would always equal it.
- **`advance_write_off_recovery` is keyed (entry_id, advance_id)**, not `entry_id unique`: one payment may repay several
  written-off advances. It carries the servicer, client and currency (the guard and RLS read them).
- **`private.client_settlement_plan` takes the written-off advances named** (`p_recover uuid[]`, one argument more than
  the plan's) — the recoveries are part of what the payment settles.
- **The keys are `cpay:<md5 of the idempotency key>` and `crfd:<md5>`** (plan: the key itself), as 7b's `awo:`: an
  entry's key bounds its length. `cpayd:<line>` as planned.
- **More refusals than the plan's**: `bad_request` (the open the page sent is not minor units, a document named twice,
  a null in a list), `reason_required` on the dedicated line (its booking's motif, 1–2,000 characters).
- **A client's payment names its client whatever it settles** (`ledger_post_set`'s given-client rule): a payment that
  only recovers a written-off advance posts 5122 and 7714, a pooled book, and the rule (a client given only for an entry
  with a client line) would have refused it.
- **(k) through the command is unreachable in 7c-1**: a designated pre-opening document implies a standing proceeding,
  whose surplus is `procedure` too (plan §5.2.3), so one payment makes one row. The key (entry_id, cause) and the guard
  are tested with planted rows (two causes on one entry summing to its −419 line accepted; a second row of a cause, one
  short of the line, another client's or no payment's refused); a replay creates none (`045` b). 7d's closure events
  make the two-cause payment reachable.
- **A label designates invoices only** (« FC-… »): the `DRA-…` numbers are 7c-2's.
- **`client_open_documents` lists no « Demandé le »** and no « Demander le remboursement »: 7c-2's.
- **Reads beyond the plan**: `public.client_payment_preview` (the sheet's live effect from SQL, never computed by the
  page), `public.client_payment_line` (the line's client, its label's invoices, the preview), `public.client_space_credits`
  (the client space reads its credits through SQL, as 7b's `client_space_advances`). Helpers beyond the plan:
  `private.client_credit_open`, `written_off_available`, `document_in_flight_run`, `client_proceeding_stands`,
  `vat_part`, `client_payment_considered`, `client_payment_docs`, `client_payment_free`, `client_payment_recoveries`,
  `client_payment_named_refusal`, `client_line_facts`, `client_payment_post`, `client_payment_rows`.
- **`advance_write_off`'s label** was already « Avance passée en perte » (7b, LEX-28): §5.0 (2)'s last item needs no
  change.
- **Screenshots**: `m2c7-reglement-client`, `m2c7-reglement-compte-dedie`, `m2c7-remboursement-avoir` (mobile and
  desktop); `m2c7-demande-remboursement` and `m2c7-client-documents` are 7c-2's. `m2c-client-credit-relay` (mobile and
  desktop, `funds-own-credits.spec.ts`) is retaken: a client's line now shows « Règlement d'une facture ou d'une avance
  du cabinet » and the reworded review text. The E2E steps extend `credit-notes.spec.ts` (its tenant has a paid invoice
  and its credit note).
- **Carried low 4 goes beyond the scale files**: `remittance_helpers.approve()` records each run it queues with its
  default execution date, and `drain()` validates again, as ops would the next morning, those a Paris date change alone
  sent back to draft — so every integration test's `approve()`/`drain()` is covered, not only the three scale fixtures
  that call `approve_remittance_runs` themselves (they call `revalidate_after_date_change` after their own « Valider »).
  A run approved for an explicit day is the test's own and never re-validated.

### Carried lows closed

1. **The double payout advance's mandate on a twice-debited lot** (7a CI round « Left open »).
   `test_remitted_cover_reads_integration.py::test_a_lot_debited_twice_reads_each_advances_run_by_key`: one member's run
   gets a second line on another mandate, another member's run a line with a null `mandate_id`; those two double-payout
   advances have no mandate, the others keep their run's. Both mutants of `transfer_line_post`'s mandate expression (drop
   `count(q.mandate_id) = count(*)`; drop `count(distinct q.mandate_id) = 1`) are killed by it.
2. **The E2E import race** (PR #42's red e2e). One shared helper, `apps/web/e2e/support/statements.ts`
   `expectOwnImport`: after « Importer le relevé », that statement's own page (`/backoffice/encaissements/releves/<id>`,
   never « Encaissements » with the previous statement's « Importé »), its `bank_statement.status` `imported` in the
   database, then « Importé » on its page. Used by every spec that imports a statement (`checks-cap`, `credit-notes`,
   `funds-own-credits`, `payments-allocation`, `payments-debits`, `payments-queue`, `payments-receipts`, `remittances`,
   `remitted-reversal` — its 7b `importStatement` now calls it —, `statements`, `switch-on`); `statements.spec.ts`'s
   duplicate (`?deja=1`) keeps its own assertion.
3. **`client_space_advances`' unfenced read** (7b round 2 « Left open »): redefined, copied whole from
   `20261123090000:497`, its client's advances read on `client_advance_client_idx` alone (`offset 0`), the servicer
   outside. `test_advance_reads_integration.py::test_the_client_space_reads_its_client_s_advances_by_its_key` bounds it
   under 10,000 planted advances of the servicer's other clients (n_distinct 2, generic plans): seen failing on 7b's body
   (10,005 `client_advance` rows), passing on 7c-1's.
4. **The scale-payouts fixture across midnight in Paris** (PR #43's dispatched run: 1,755 of 5,050 runs refused
   `execution_date_after_cutoff`). `remittance_helpers.date_change_refusals` / `revalidate_after_date_change`: the runs
   of the fixture back in draft, refused at the approval with `execution_date_after_cutoff` or `execution_date_passed`
   on a Paris day after the command's while `private.paris_today()` is no longer it, validated again with a fresh
   « Valider » (200 a command), then drained; any other refusal is left to the fixture's own assertion. Used after every
   « Valider » of `test_debit_bookings_scale_integration.py`, `test_remittance_scale_integration.py` (both),
   `test_transfer_cancellation_scale_integration.py`, and by `drain()` for `approve()` (Deviations). Tested by
   `test_date_change_revalidation_integration.py` with the change simulated (the run's requested execution date moved to
   yesterday or today, committed on the test's own tenant with the run's guard set aside for that update — review
   round 1, TUI-9: not a rolled-back transaction; the command's day given as yesterday): validated again and approved;
   the same day, nothing; a run refused for its payout account, never — and through `drain()`.
5. **`transfer_line_check`'s `advance_settled` rule**: the default moves to **7e-3 fences it in its redefinition** (7b
   round 2 « Left open », updated): it is an 801-line copy that 7e-3 redefines anyway (plan §1.4), and 7c-1's scope does
   not touch it.

### Assertions whose expected value changed (house rule R3)

None. `033`–`044` are byte for byte unchanged. The E2E specs of carried low 2 replace their wait for « Importé » on
« Encaissements » with the shared helper, which asserts more (the statement's own page and status); no assertion was
removed or weakened. `debits.test.ts`'s and `transfer-line-*.test.ts`' expectations are unchanged (the reworded texts
are pinned in the new `settlements.test.ts`).

**Equivalent mutants, argued.** (1) `remit:` before the line lock with the allocation lock kept first: every path that
locks a dedicated-account line and then takes the remit lock (`post_debit_links` through `link_debit`,
`post_bank_bookings` through the debit job and `link_debit`) takes the allocation lock first, and so does
`book_client_payment_line`; under that lock no other session can hold the line while waiting for the remit lock, so the
order of the line and the remit lock is not observable (`release_own_credit` locks a line without the allocation lock
but takes no remit lock). The order the plan rules out (the line before the allocation lock, §2.2's « not
`remittance_command_locks` after the line ») deadlocks and is killed by the staged test. (2) `vat_part` without its
« all of it on the closing part » branch: the plan caps a part at the open part, and R(pending × open / open) = pending
exactly, so the closing part moves all the pending VAT either way (the branch states the rule). (3) The helper's
same-day guard dropped: `date_change_refusals` also requires the refusal's Paris day after the command's, which the
same day never is.

80 mutants: 77 killed (46 SQL — 42 through `045`, 4 through the worker's integration tests —, 12 of the twin, 5 of
the ledger model, 3 of the date-change helper, 11 web), 3 equivalent. Eight survived their first run and are killed by the cases added after it
(run again against the final files): 419's balance, the dedicated compare and set, the 15th day, a liquidation alone,
the recovery guard, the twin's birth order, `approve()`'s record, the refusal code. The tests the others ran were not
changed afterwards except by these additions.

### Left open (low), with its default

- Founder questions (plan §10): Q4 (a), Q5's recovery (a) and Q7 (a) — defaults built and open; the cancellation after
  download (6b-3 plan Q1) stays off.
- **A payment's surplus while a proceeding stands is always `procedure`**, so the plan's (k) (a designated pre-opening
  part and an `overpayment` surplus on one entry) is unreachable until 7d's closure events (Deviations). Default: keep;
  the key and the guard already take two causes.
- **What is open of a credit is computed per row** (`private.client_credit_open`), as 7b's CCS-2 for advances: the
  page, the client space and the nightly read every credit of the client (or the servicer) ever recorded. Default: keep
  at today's volumes (credits are rare); 7f's hardening with CCS-2.
- **A credit owed back has no expiry and no automatic refund**: ops refund it on proof (founder Q7 a); the alert
  repeats every night after 15 days. Default: keep.
- **A payment whose value date precedes an invoice's issue date settles that invoice** (the default order reads every
  open invoice): the entry posts −4111 and moves the VAT on its value date, so balances as of a day in between show the
  receivable in credit and the VAT due before the invoice — an advance payment, whose VAT is due at encaissement (CGI
  269 2 c, OQ-90). Default: keep (the money was received that day; today's balances and the nightly are exact).
- **Who receives a sum held for a procedure is not recorded** beyond the refund's evidence (the administrator, the
  mandataire or the liquidator, OQ-98). Default: keep until 7d-1's representatives.
- Everything 7a and 7b leave open stays open (CCS-2, the portfolio moved between E's run and R(E), the cover's release
  re-queued later, Q2, Q18; `transfer_line_check`'s `advance_settled` read now 7e-3's).

## M2c-7c-1 review fixes (2026-11-24)

### Round 1

The review of `7e987a7` raised thirteen items: one medium and two lows of the money lens (MONEY-1, MONEY-2, MONEY-3),
two mediums and seven lows of tests and pages (TUI-1 … TUI-9), and one medium of concurrency and cost (CC-1, the same
fault as TUI-2: one item, fixed once). Each was checked against the code first (the SQL on the main stack inside
rolled-back transactions, the sheets' code, vitest); all hold. The migration `20261124090000_client_payments.sql` is
unmerged and was edited in place: no function is redefined beyond the slice's own, no public signature changes (the
written-off rows' payability and the commands' `credits` are values inside their `jsonb`;
`private.client_payment_recoveries` gains `p_on`, a private helper of this file), `database.types.ts` is unchanged
(regenerated, identical). **The switch stays off** (no item depends on it: judged off and on, every fixed path is the
same with it on); `033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`044` byte for byte unchanged.

- **MONEY-1 (medium; fixed at the root: a loss the client may not repay is held for the procedure).** A client in a
  collective proceeding that named, for recovery, an advance passed as a loss born before the opening had that part
  booked as income on 7714 (`written_off_recovered`, an `advance_write_off_recovery`), while L622-7 I al. 1 forbids
  paying a pre-opening claim (HOLD-02; founder Q4 a: « jamais une créance d'avant le jugement »). The open part of the
  same advance was right (held, cause `procedure`); only the recovery loop of `private.client_payment_plan` never read
  any payability, and the twin did the same. Reproduced with `045`'s fixture (Dupont, the advance born before an
  opening of today): 300,00 € named for its recovery posted +5122 / −7714 30 000, no credit. Fix:
  - `private.client_payment_recoveries(…, p_on)` carries `payable` (`private.document_client_payable(advance, p_on)` —
    7c-1's « not born before the opening », and 7d-2's redefinition of that function applies here too), on the
    payment's date: the value date (own account), the line's booking date (dedicated account), the preview's day.
  - `private.client_payment_plan`'s recovery loop: a recovery the client may not repay is a `client_credit` part of
    cause `procedure` naming the advance, as a named document it may not pay; never `written_off`. Its loss stays to
    recover (`written_off_available` unchanged), the P0 alert follows (`client_credit_owed`), the credit's `details`
    name the advance (`document_kind` `advance` when it is no longer open: `client_payment_post` reads it so).
  - The twin: `WrittenOff.payable` and the same branch (`_recovery`); Hypothesis: the parity property draws it, the
    plan's properties assert income only for what may be repaid and the recoveries in the client's order after its
    documents.
  - « Ce que le client doit au cabinet »: its written-off rows carry `before_opening` / `payable`; the row, the sheet's
    choice and the live effect say « créance antérieure à l'ouverture de la procédure du client : … n'est pas encaissée
    en recette, … mise de côté pour la procédure » (OQ-98), never « 7714 ».
  - Tests: `045` c (`sl5`: the own account and the dedicated one, the page, the preview, the books, the credit and its
    details, no recovery, the loss still to recover, the P0 alert; the line booked today, the proceeding open on its
    date; a line booked the day before the opening is still a recovery, 7714), the twin's unit case, the parity
    property, vitest.
  - Reads: the payability is one keyed call per named loss and per written-off row of the page (the advance and its
    entry by their keys, the client's opening by `client_status_event_client_idx`). `test_advance_reads_integration.py`
    reads the written-off branch of `client_open_documents`, `client_payment_recoveries` and a recovery's preview under
    its planted statistics (10,000 rows per table, n_distinct 2, generic plans): 23, 7 and 16 rows (bounds 84, 72, 84).
- **TUI-1 (medium; fixed).** The client space drew one section « Sommes que le cabinet vous doit » over every credit,
  so a client in redressement or liquidation read that the servicer owed it the sums held for its procedure — a false
  statement on a client page (plan §5.2.6: they go to the administrator, mandataire or liquidator; OQ-98).
