### Left open (low), with its default

- **MONEY-2: the same proof recorded twice is not refused.** `record_client_payment` checks that its evidence is a
  `client_payment_evidence` of the client; its ledger key is per request. A second recording of one transfer (two
  staff, or after a reload: the sheet uploads the proof again, a new document) posts a second +5122 and settles more,
  or credits the client more, for money received once; own-account statements are not imported (design R12), so no
  bank line catches it. Default: keep for now (ops record a transfer once, on its proof; the client's credit owed back
  is then refunded only on a proof of the servicer's own transfer, and the nightly `client_credit_owed` lists it);
  7f's hardening (plan §8.1) adds `evidence_already_used`, keyed on the proof's content (its sha256 among the client's
  payment evidence, as two uploads of one file are two documents) with a partial unique index on the entries' source,
  and a stale-statistics bound for that read. `record_client_refund` the same, bounded by what is owed; one transfer
  refunding two documents is then two recordings of one proof, which the guard must still allow.
- **7d-2 redefines `private.client_payment_docs`' payability with `private.document_client_payable`**: the docs read
  it inline as « not before the opening » (one read per document), while the losses' payability (MONEY-1) calls the
  function. Default: 7d-2, when it widens `document_client_payable` (an advance while a proceeding stands), redefines
  both reads with it.
- Everything 7c-1's « Left open » lists stays open; founder Q4 (a), Q5's recovery (a) and Q7 (a) keep their defaults,
  open; the switch stays off.

### Round 2

The review of `fb82136` raised one item, a medium of the legal and money lenses (« a liquidation alone: the
pre-judgment claim paid »). It was checked against the code first and holds: on the main stack, inside `045`'s harness
in a rolled-back transaction, Roux (`a5`) with an invoice issued d − 5 and a `liquidation` event recorded alone at
d − 3 (« a liquidation opened at once », as `045`'s own `sl4` says): `client_open_documents` returned `procedure` true
— the page's note « Une procédure collective du client est en cours : une somme reçue pour une créance antérieure à son
ouverture n'est pas imputée » — and the invoice `before_opening` false, `payable` true; 360,00 € with no designation
settled it in full (−4111 36 000, VAT 6 000 moved, open 0, no credit); designated, 100,00 € settled 10 000. The
migration `20261124090000_client_payments.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place; no public signature changes
(`database.types.ts` regenerated, identical); **the switch stays off** (judged off and on: what the client may pay
reads no switch); `033`–`044` byte for byte unchanged.

- **The cause.** `private.document_before_opening` and `private.client_payment_docs`' inline advance test read 7b's
  `private.client_opening_on`, which reads `proceeding_opened` only, while `private.client_proceeding_stands` counts a
  `liquidation` too: 7c-1 held a surplus for the procedure but paid the pre-judgment claim. C. com.
  [L641-3](https://librejustice.fr/norm/fr/code-de-commerce/l641-3) al. 1 (read 2026-11-24, version in force since
  2019-05-24): « Le jugement qui ouvre la liquidation judiciaire a les mêmes effets que ceux qui sont prévus en cas de
  sauvegarde par les premier et troisième alinéas du I et par le III de l'article L. 622-7 … » — L622-7 I al. 1:
  « interdiction de payer toute créance née antérieurement au jugement d'ouverture » (COMPLIANCE HOLD-02, OQ-17). The plan
  defers the reading to 7d-2 (§6.2.2), which would have left the law broken and the page's note false until then.
- **The fix (the item's first option, at the root).** `private.client_opening_date(p_client uuid, p_on date)`: plan
  §6.2.2's function brought forward from 7d-2, with its signature and its rule — the earliest effective date of a
  `proceeding_opened` or `liquidation` event on or before `p_on`, null without one (`client_status_event_client_idx`:
  the client and the day in the index, the kind outside; SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path ''`, `enable_seqscan` off;
  revoked from public, anon, authenticated and service_role). `document_before_opening` (its comment: 7d-2 redefines
  it with `document_born_on`) and `client_payment_docs`' advance test read it; through them `document_client_payable`,
  `client_payment_recoveries`' `payable` (round 1's MONEY-1), « Ce que le client doit au cabinet » (invoices, advances,
  written-off rows), the preview, `record_client_payment`, `client_payment_line` and `book_client_payment_line` (on the
  line's booking date). Untouched, as the item asks: 7b's `private.client_opening_on` and
  `private.advance_recovery_of` (the claw-back's `barred_proceeding`), the prepare (`load_facts`' `proceeding_opened_on`)
  and `client_proceeding_stands`. 7d-2's §6.2.2 becomes a `create or replace` of the same body, and its §6.2.5
  (`document_born_on(doc) < client_opening_date(client, p_on)`) stands as planned. No web change: the page reads
  `procedure`, `before_opening` and `payable` from SQL, so its note and its « Créance antérieure à l'ouverture de la
  procédure du client » are now true of a liquidation recorded alone.
- **Tests (seen failing on `fb82136`'s bodies).** `045` l, c (27 tests):
  - `sl6`: Roux, FC-R1 issued d − 5 and an advance born d − 2, both before its liquidation at d − 1, and FC-R2 issued
    d. The page marks FC-R1 and the advance « antérieure à l'ouverture », not payable, and FC-R2 payable. 740,00 € with
    no designation pays FC-R2 only (18 000), and holds 56 000 for the procedure (P0 at once). FC-R1 has no settlement,
    the advance is still open, and nothing is dirty. On `fb82136`, the advance (20 000) and FC-R1 (36 000) were settled

  - `sl7`: FC-R1 and the advance designated (400,00 €) are all held for the procedure (+5122 / −419 40 000), each

  - `sl8`: `client_opening_date` takes the judgment's own day, is null before it, and takes the earliest of a
    redressement and a liquidation; a client with none has null. On `fb82136`, the function was missing.
- **Reads.** `client_opening_date` is one keyed read per call (per document of the client's open documents, per named

### Left open (low), with its default

- **The servicer's own set-off and claw-back still read `proceeding_opened` only.** For a client whose liquidation is
  recorded alone, a run still sets off its invoices and claws back its advances, whenever they were born: the prepare
  reads `proceeding_opened_on`, and `advance_recovery_of` reads `client_opening_on`. Both were so before 7c-1. A
  set-off of connected claims is L622-7 I al. 1's own exception (whether the runs' are connected is OQ-41); that
  nothing is set off in liquidation is founder Q11's default (LEX-09, plan §6.2.6). The client space and the staff
  pages state what those runs do. Default: 7d-2, as planned, moves the prepare's facts and `advance_recovery_of` to
  `client_opening_date` (§6.2.2, LEX-07 (2)) and adds `client_set_off_barred` (`liquidation`, §6.2.6).
- Everything round 1's « Left open » lists stays open; founder Q4 (a), Q5's recovery (a), Q7 (a) and Q11 keep their
  defaults, open; the switch stays off.

### Round 3

The review of `b181d65` raised two mediums. Each was checked against the code first, on the main stack inside `045`'s
harness in rolled-back transactions; both hold. The migration `20261124090000_client_payments.sql` is unmerged and was
edited in place. **The switch stays off**: judged off and on, neither path reads it. `033`–`044` are byte for byte
unchanged, and `044` passes against the redefined `private.advance_recovery_of` with no expectation changed.

- **A pre-judgment advance of a liquidation said « à rembourser » (medium; fixed at the root, the item's first
  option).**
  - Reproduced with `045`'s `roux()`. Roux's advance (20 000) was born d − 2 under a mandate with no claw-back clause.
    Its liquidation is recorded alone at d − 1.
  - Every page read `request`: `client_space_advances` (the client's « Avances du cabinet à rembourser : 200,00 € » and
    « … une demande de remboursement pourra vous être adressée »), the staff « Avances », and `client_open_documents`.
    The same page also said `before_opening` true, `payable` false.
  - Paid as designated (200,00 €), the money was held for the procedure (`client_credit` 20 000) and the advance stayed
    open and said to be repaid. The cause: 7b's `private.advance_recovery_of` reads `client_opening_on`
    (`proceeding_opened` only).
  - The law: under C. com. [L641-3](https://librejustice.fr/norm/fr/code-de-commerce/l641-3) al. 1 (read 2026-11-24,
    version in force since 2019-05-24) → L622-7 I al. 1, the client may not pay this claim. Al. 4: « Les créanciers
    déclarent leurs créances au liquidateur … ». No run takes such an advance (claw-back only), and 7c-2's request
    refuses `before_opening`. So the page stated a legal falsehood, and round 2's payability contradicted it.
  - Fix: `private.advance_recovery_of` is redefined, copied from `20261123090000:142` (same signature and settings,
    its revoke restated). An advance whose recovery would be `request` or `request_no_mandate` is now
    `barred_proceeding` when born before `private.client_opening_date(client, p_on)`, the opening 7c-1's payments read.
  - A `clawback` keeps 7b's rule (born before `client_opening_on`), as the item asks and round 2 recorded. The runs
    still take it until 7d-2, so the pages stay true of the runs. One keyed read of the opening either way.
  - Through the one function, every reader follows: the client space, « Avances » (`advance_row`), « Ce que le client
    doit au cabinet », the run page, « Désimputer » (`allocation_remitted`'s cover) and the nightly's `advance_open`
    details.
  - The web's wordings of `barred_proceeding` are already true of a liquidation: « Avances du cabinet : … » with no
    « à rembourser »; « antérieure à l'ouverture de votre procédure collective, elle n'est pas déduite de vos
    reversements »; « Pas de reprise : avance née avant l'ouverture de la procédure collective du client ». The web
    changes only a type comment.

    `effective_date` 22/11) and a dedicated-account line booked d − 1 (23/11) were both recorded today.
    `client_space_credits` and `client_open_documents.credits` gave `created_on` 24/11 (`client_credit.created_at`).
  - The pages then read « Somme reçue le 24/11/2026 … » (the client space and staff), and an overpayment value-dated

### Left open (low), with its default

- **A loss written off in parts on different days is recoverable from its last write-off only.** A payment dated
  between two write-offs designating the recovery is refused, though the first part was already a loss. Conservative
  (never more income than was lost on any day) and rare. Default: keep.
- **A payment received before an invoice existed stays a trop-perçu.** 7c-1 refunds a credit; it does not apply it to a
  later invoice (the M2c-7 plan has no such command). The invoice stays open: a run may set it off, the client may pay
  it, and the credit is refunded. Default: keep; whether to add « imputer un trop-perçu » is the founder's.
- **The payment sheet's value date has no `min`.** Its floor depends on what is designated, and the preview names
  the day before the sheet can record. Default: keep.
- **A `bad_date` names the first refused designation's day, not the latest** (round 4's verifier, probe q6).
  `private.client_payment_named_refusal` returns the first refusal in the client's order. An advance born d−2 and an
  invoice issued today, both designated at d−5, are refused with « … pas être daté avant le 22/11 ». Redated d−2, the
  payment is refused a second time with the invoice's day. Nothing is booked wrongly; it costs ops a second try.
  Default: keep; 7f's hardening names the greatest day among the refused designations.
- Everything rounds 1 to 3 list stays open; founder Q4 (a), Q5's recovery (a), Q7 (a) and Q11 keep their defaults,
  open; the switch stays off.

## M2c-7c-2: repayment requests (2026-11-24)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0, §1.3 D1, §1.4 (7c-2 row), §2, §5.1 (the request tables, the PDF's RLS and key),
§5.2.7 (the request, the withdrawal, the payload), §5.2.8 (`repayment_request_document_missing`, `requested_on`), §5.3
(the letter `demande-remboursement-avance-fr-1`), §5.4 (the letter and its job), §5.5 (the request's web), §5.6, §5.7
`045b` (a), (g), (h), (m), (n), the letter's goldens and design §7.3 variant (i), §5.8, with their [critic] / [check
1–3] marks. Founder questions (plan §10), none answered: Q6 (a: no due date, no formal notice, no legal article on
the letter), Q20 (a: no expiry; « Retirer la demande ») and the new Q22 (below) built as their defaults and left open.
Migration `20261125090000_repayment_requests.sql` (one file, forward-only). New: the tables
`public.advance_repayment_request` (DRA-AAAA-NNNNNN, its total, its frozen payload and hash, the template, its
letter's document once drawn, its withdrawal) and `public.advance_repayment_request_item` (the advances it names, each
with its open part then) — RLS, change log, append-only but for the request's document and withdrawal, each set
once —; the commands `public.request_advance_repayment` and `public.withdraw_advance_repayment_request`; the reads
`public.advance_repayment_preview` (the sheet) and `public.client_repayment_requests` (the client's requests, staff
and client space); the worker's `private.client_requested_advances`, `private.repayment_request_job`,
`private.repayment_request_document_done`; their helpers (`advance_live_request`, `advance_payout_not_received`,
`advance_repayment_refusal`, `advance_repayment_client_refusal`, `advance_reversal_origin`, `advance_repayment_row`,
`advance_repayment_payload`). Redefined, each copied whole from its latest definition across every migration file
(indexed: the last `create or replace function` of each name wins; each copy diffed against the live `prosrc` before
the change; only the change; settings, `search_path ''`, SECURITY DEFINER and grants restated):
`private.remittance_approval_refusal` (`20261114090000:688`), `private.run_advance_checks` (`20261124090000:2281`,
7c-1's), `private.advance_row` (`20261123090000:387`), `private.can_read_remittance_document_object`
(`20261113090000:1552`), the policies `remittance_document_object_read` and `document_remittance_scope`
(`20261113090000:1565`, `:1569`). Worker: the letter (`remittance/repayment_request.py`, its PDF
`remittance/repayment_request_pdf.py`), its job (`jobs/repayment_requests.py`, handler `repayment_request` on the
`remittances` queue), the prepare's requested flag (`jobs/remittances.py` `_open_advances`, `remittance/run.py`).
Web: « Demander le remboursement », « Retirer la demande » and the column « Demandé le » on « Avances »; the request
sheet and the client's requests on « Ce que le client doit au cabinet »; the client's requests and their letters in
the client space (`/client/reversements`); the nightly's new label. **The switch stays off**: nothing writes
`private.feature_switch`; the rules reachable only with it on (a run cancelled after download no longer holds its
advances; 043's cases 5f, 11 and 17 (d) whose request halves are `045b` n) run inside rolled-back scenarios with it on
(`pg_temp.iso(…, true)`); `045b`'s guard asserts it is off at the end; `033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`045`
unchanged.

### Decisions

- **D1 — a request is a letter, not a movement.** `request_advance_repayment` inserts the request and its items and
  queues the letter's job; it posts nothing, settles nothing and changes no advance. The client's repayment is 7c-1's
  « Règlement du client » (design §7.3 (i): `test_the_first_variant_of_7_3_…` pays the request's 200 000 that way:
  4112[Martin] = 0, `advance_open` silent). The number is unique per servicer, not gapless (design §3.2 #4: the run
  numbers' sequence). The letter states what the payload froze when the request was made; the PDF is a function of
  that payload alone (`test_the_pdf_depends_on_the_payload_only`), stored once by its bytes' hash.
- **D2 — who and under which locks.** Admins and ops managers of the client's servicer at aal2; replay and request
  hash (`command_replay` / `command_record`); 1–200 advances of one client and currency, none twice, none null, and the
  total the sheet showed (`bad_request` otherwise). Under `private.remittance_command_locks(org, true)` — the locks an
  approval takes — so a request and an approval reading the same advance never interleave (`lock_timeout` 2 s).
- **D3 — the refusals and their order.** Per advance (`private.advance_repayment_refusal`): `not_open` (unknown, another
  client's or currency's, nothing open), `in_flight` (an approved or sent run's plan takes it: the run's number),
  `before_opening` (born before the client's proceeding opened: 7c-1's `document_before_opening`, a liquidation alone
  opening it), `recently_requested` (a request not withdrawn issued less than 30 days ago: its day; day 29 refused,
  day 30 accepted — a reminder after 30 days is a new request), `clawback_applies` ([critic] M7-MONEY-3, L7: the
  mandate's terms in force that day hold a claw-back clause and set-off is not barred — the next run takes it; the
  clause), `payout_not_received` (D5); then `total_changed`, then the client's
  (`private.advance_repayment_client_refusal`): `no_own_account` (none active in the currency), `identity_incomplete`
  (`billing_identity_gaps`), `recipient_unknown` ([critic] L12: a death, guardianship, liquidation or mandate end in
  effect — 7c-2 sends nothing then; 7d-1 names who receives). Each is French on the page (`requests.ts`).
- **D4 — a requested advance is never also clawed back ([critic] M7-MONEY-3, L7).** An advance is *requested* while it
  is open and an item of a request not withdrawn names it (`private.advance_live_request`: the latest such request).
  The prepare reads them (`private.client_requested_advances`, keyed) and `_plan` leaves each to its request (it stays
  in its mandate's money, as an advance no clause recovers); the inputs hash names the flag only when set (the hashes
  of drafts that name no requested advance are unchanged). A request made after a prepare that planned the advance is
  caught by the approval: `remittance_approval_refusal` returns `documents_changed` when a planned advance settle names
  a requested advance (`045b` a; approved once the request is withdrawn). Under a clause the request itself is refused
  (`clawback_applies`), so the two meet only when the terms change after the request (`045b` a: the prepare's read
  still marks it requested).
- **D5 — never ask for what the client did not receive ([critic] M7-MONEY-8, L5; [check 1]).** For a remitted
  reversal's cover, `payout_not_received` exactly while `private.entry_remitted(E, R).paid_on` is null — a payout come
  back and not paid again, or an unplanned payout that had paid it come back —, not while the run's own payout is
  merely unpaid (the plan's mutant: read from `remittance_run_paid_on`). An N = 0 run (set off, netted) is received; a
  returned payout a later run paid is received (« … après le retour du virement du relevé RV-… »). The detail is
  « RV-…:run » or « RV-…:unplanned » (what came back: the run's payout, or a payout outside any run). (Beyond the
  plan) a `payout_overrun` advance whose run's payout came back and is not paid again is refused the same way
  (`private.run_settled_on`: no row) — asking the client to repay more than it was paid by a payout it never kept
  would be false.
- **D6 — the letter (plan §5.3).** Deterministic (reportlab pinned, invariant, DejaVu, no clock, no model, no LLM);
  every amount and date is the payload's, built in SQL from the ledger and the advances. Issuer: the servicer's billing
  identity (`private.receipt_issuer`); recipient: the client's name and billing address, else its registered office;
  « Objet : Demande de remboursement — référence DRA-… »; the rows by recording, each with its recording date, its
  mandate, its origin in the real order of events, « Versé », « Déjà remboursé », « Demandé »; « Total à rembourser »;
  the own account (holder, IBAN, BIC) and the reference; « Ce document n'est pas une facture. ». Origins per cause, as
  the plan words them: « versé le … (relevé RV-…) » only when `paid_how` is `paid`; « réglé par compensation dans le
  relevé RV-… du … » (`set_off`), « compris dans le relevé RV-… du … (montant net nul) » (`netted`) — never « versé »
  for an N = 0 run (house rule 26); the reversal first when it was recorded while the run was in flight (the cover
  posted at the booking, `adv:<R>:<run>`) or before the client was paid; a partial bank return « paiement repris en
  partie par la banque (X) ; imputation annulée en entier (Y) »; a payout outside any run « par un virement hors
  reversement » (no run named). Never a payer's name or IBAN, never an RMT, SWP or TOP id, no legal article, interest, penalty,
  due date or formal notice (founder Q6; OQ-95). The renderer refuses a payload whose rows do not add up to its total,
  an unknown template or cause, or a « versé » without its day.
- **D7 — the letter's job.** `{type: repayment_request}` on `remittances`, in the queue's transaction:
  `private.repayment_request_job` holds the request's row (two jobs never draw it at once; a request already drawn is
  left as it is); the PDF uploaded to `documents` at `repayment-requests/<servicer>/<request>.pdf`;
  `private.repayment_request_document_done` records the document (kind `advance_repayment_request_pdf`) only once the
  object is stored at its key, with the bytes' hash — again with the same bytes the same document, with other bytes
  refused. A failed attempt removes what it uploaded and fails the job (the queue retries it); the nightly raises
  `repayment_request_document_missing` (alert) for a letter still not drawn one hour after its request.
- **D8 — who reads the letter ([critic] F11).** The remittance documents' rule: money staff of the servicer and the
  client's whole-client members (`document_remittance_scope`, `remittance_document_object_read` with the letters'
  keys); never another tenant, a portfolio-restricted member or a collector (`045b` h, row and file). The request and
  item rows follow the same rule (their RLS); they are written only by the SECURITY DEFINER commands and the worker's
  functions.
- **D9 — the pages.** Every amount and date is SQL's (the preview's total, the requests' totals and days), the pages
  only word them. « Avances »: « Demander le remboursement » on a requestable advance (open, not in flight, recovered
  by a request — no claw-back clause, not born before the client's proceeding —, not requested in the last 30 days;
  the command decides), the sheet listing the requestable advances of its client and currency on
  the page with the preview's live total and refusals; « Demandé le JJ/MM/AAAA (DRA-…) » and « Retirer la demande »
  (sheet with its motif). « Ce que le client doit au cabinet »: the same sheet over the client's advances and the
  client's requests. The client space: « Demande de remboursement d'avances DRA-… du JJ/MM/AAAA : X € » with its letter
  (PDF), « — demande retirée le … » once withdrawn; an advance requested reads « demande de remboursement DRA-…
  adressée le … ». LEX-28: no text says « abandon » or « remise » (`requests.test.ts`).
- **D10 — reads keyed whatever the statistics.** Every new read is by a key with `enable_seqscan = off` and `offset 0`
  fences (the request by its client, by its servicer and document, the items by request and by advance); the night's
  undrawn letters by a plain index read with the literal predicate (never a partial index a parameter's filter would
  have to imply). `test_repayment_request_reads_integration.py` (Tests) bounds them under planted statistics.
- **The carried default (ADR-0014 « M2c-7a review fixes » Left open).** A collection an unplanned payout paid only in
  part, the rest in a run whose own payout came back, reads « not received » in full (7a's `entry_remitted`: the
  run's set-off is per run, not per item). 7c-2 asks no repayment of such an advance (`payout_not_received`) until the
  returned sum is paid again — `045b` cd (switch on). Plan §10 Q22 asks whether a run's set-off should be shared out
  over its items. Default (a): no.

### Deviations from the plan

- **The letter's last column is « Demandé », not « Reste dû »**: a part of an advance passed as a loss is no longer
  claimed (7b) but is not repaid either; « Reste dû » would state it owed, and « Déjà remboursé » counts only what was
  repaid (a compensation, a payment to the own or the dedicated account), never a write-off.
- **« Mandat »**: the advance's mandate; « plusieurs mandats » only for an overrun or a double payout of a run (a run
  pays several mandates); « — » for an advance with no mandate and no run (a payout outside any run): « plusieurs
  mandats » would be false there.
- **`recipient_unknown`'s text** says what the code does (« … aucune demande ne lui est adressée tant que la personne
  qui agit pour lui n'est pas enregistrée »): the plan's « indiquez d'abord qui agit pour le client » names an action
  that does not exist before 7d-1.
- **`payout_not_received` for an overrun** (D5) is beyond the plan's list; the detail `RV-…:run|unplanned` lets the
  page say which payout came back.
- **The request's columns**: `withdrawal_reason` (the motif the sheet asks for); the items carry the servicer and the
  client (their RLS reads them without a join to the request); `issued_by` without a foreign key (as the earlier
  slices' `*_by` columns).
- **`repayment_request_document_done(request, sha256, renderer)`**, not the plan's `(request, document_id, sha256,
  renderer)`: the function inserts the document itself, once it has checked the object is stored at its key, and
  returns it — the worker never writes `public.document`, and a document row never exists without its file.
- **`register_client_document` and `can_read_client_document(_object)` are not redefined**: the letter is a document
  the worker draws, read under the remittance documents' rule (D8), not a client document staff register.
- **The client space shows the requests on « Reversements » (`/client/reversements`, section « Demandes de
  remboursement d'avances »)**: the client space has no « Documents » page (only `/client/documents/[id]`, the
  download route of a client's RIB or mandate); the section sits beside « Sommes que le cabinet vous doit » and the
  advances the requests name. The screenshot keeps the plan's name `m2c7-client-documents`.
- **Beyond the plan**: `public.advance_repayment_preview` (the sheet's total and refusals from SQL, so the browser
  computes no amount; it states no open part of another client's advance) and `public.client_repayment_requests` (the
  pages' list). `private.advance_live_request` serves the approval's re-check, the prepare's read, « Avances » and the
  nightly's `requested_on`.

are added; `remitted-reversal.spec.ts` gains steps at its end).

## M2c-7c-2 review fixes (2026-11-24)

### Round 1

The review of `f0a8da0` raised thirteen items: two mediums and two lows of the money lens (MONEY-1, MONEY-2; NIGHT-1,
UI-1), three mediums and three lows of tests and pages (TUI-1 … TUI-3; TUI-4 … TUI-6), and three lows of concurrency
and cost (CC-1 … CC-3). NIGHT-1, TUI-4 and CC-1 are one fault (a withdrawn request's letter and alert),
TUI-3 and CC-2 another (the motif readable by the client): each fixed once. Each item was checked against the code
first — MONEY-1 and MONEY-2 reproduced on the main stack inside rolled-back transactions with `045b`'s fixture (switch
off and on), the others read in the migration, the worker's letter and the pages; all hold. The migration
`20261125090000_repayment_requests.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place. **The switch stays off** (nothing writes
`private.feature_switch`; MONEY-1's release path, reachable only with it on, is tested with it on in a rolled-back
scenario, and the double payout's return off and on); `033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`045` byte for byte
unchanged.

- **MONEY-1 (medium; fixed at the root: refused while a request names the advance, option (a)).** The two paths that
  reverse an advance's entry — the double payout's return (`return:adv:`, gated by `private.transfer_line_check`) and
  the release of an unplanned payout's covers when it comes back (`return:rr:`, `private.remitted_cover_release`) —
  refused while a run takes the advance back (`advance_in_flight`) or after it was settled (`advance_settled`), never
  while a repayment request names it. The advance was then reversed (its open part 0) while the request stayed live
  and the client space kept the letter asking for a payout the client never kept (plan §0 #1, D5); a client paying as
  asked would have had a credit owed back to refund. Reproduced: the double payout's return (switch off and on) and
  `045b` sn3's path without its withdrawal (switch on): 50 000 → 0 and 40 000 → 0, the request not withdrawn. Fix: both
  refuse **`advance_requested`** while `private.advance_live_request(advance)` returns a row — `transfer_line_check`
  (redefined whole from `20261123090000:889`, one rule after `advance_in_flight`: the preview and the booking) and
  `remitted_cover_release` (redefined whole from `20261122090000:614`, raised as the command's refusal, SQLSTATE
  55000, as `advance_in_flight`). Both run under the transfer line's locks (… → `remit:`), the lock the request takes:
  a request and such a return never interleave. The page says « L'avance liée à ce virement fait l'objet d'une demande
  de remboursement adressée au client : retirez d'abord cette demande (« Avances », « Retirer la demande »), puis
  comptabilisez ce retour ; l'avance sera alors annulée. » (`transfer-lines.ts`). `045b` v ×3: refused (preview and
  booking, nothing booked, the advance open), then booked once the request is withdrawn (the advance reversed), the
  nightly's ledger checks clean. Every `ledger_reverse` of the migrations was read: no third path reverses an
  advance's entry (below, Left open, the reviewer's backstop alert).
- **MONEY-2 (medium; fixed: plan §5.2.5, [critic] L16, the 7c-1 ADR's « the DRA-… numbers are 7c-2's »).** A
  dedicated-account line labelled with the client's DRA number designated nothing: the page named no document, naming

  (`advance_repayment_request_number_uq`), its items by the primary key's prefix, each advance by its key.

### Left open (low), with its default

- **No backstop nightly alert for a request naming a reversed advance** (MONEY-1's « in both cases »): both paths
  that reverse an advance's entry refuse while a request names it, under the lock the request takes, and a request is
  refused `not_open` for an advance already reversed; an alert would read every request not withdrawn each night for
  a state the refusals rule out. Default: none; 7f's hardening may add it with the other invariants.
- **A request made, then the payout that had paid its collection comes back** (found while fixing MONEY-1; plan §10
  Q23, new): the letter said true (« versé le … »), the advance stays open and owed again once a later run pays the
  re-queued sum, but meanwhile the client does not hold it; the request stays live. Default (Q23 a): keep; ops may
  withdraw it. Alternative b: refuse that return's booking while a request names an advance of its run, as
  `advance_requested`.
- **The withdrawal notice can overstate what stays requested** (round 1's verifier, `requests.ts` `withdrawEffect`).
  A reminder names A (also in an earlier live request) and B (only in the reminder); withdrawing the reminder returns
  `still_requested_by = [the earlier request]` and the notice says « … nomme encore ses avances : elles restent
  demandées », which is false for B (B may be requested anew, and is). Staff page only; no amount, date or legal
  mention. Default: 7f's hardening returns which advances stay requested and words the notice per advance.
- Founder questions Q6, Q20, Q22 and Q23 (plan §10): defaults built, open. The cancellation after download stays off.
- Everything M2c-7c-2's « Left open » lists stays open (the dead job's re-queue: ops withdraw and request again — now
  with no alert left behind).

## M2c-7d-1: client events, payees and recipients (2026-11-24)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0, §1.3, §1.4 (7d-1 row) and « Order, and why », §2, §6.1 but the withheld kind and
the disposition table (`claims_declared_item` is 7d-1's, with the kind `claims_declared` and `p_declared`), §6.2.1,
§6.2.3, §6.2.7, §6.2.8's gate and forward, §6.2.10's 7d-1 part, §6.2.12, §6.2.13, §6.3's `protection_event_to_qualify`
and `seizure_standing`, the request's recipient (7c-2's `recipient_unknown` narrowed, `advance_repayment_payload` with
two addressees for a curatelle), §6.3–§6.4, §6.6's `046a`, §6.7's 7d-1 part, with their [critic] / [check 1–3] marks.
Founder questions (plan §10), none answered: Q8 (a), Q10 (a), Q12 (a), Q21 (a) built as their defaults and left open;
counsel's OQ-41, OQ-91, OQ-93, OQ-94 stay open (COMPLIANCE). Migration `20261126090000_client_events.sql` (one file,
forward-only). **The switch stays off**: nothing writes `private.feature_switch` and no 7d-1 rule reads it; the
switch-on scenarios of `046a` (sp1, sp5, sp7, sp8, sg1, sa1) run in rolled-back subtransactions
(`pg_temp.iso(…, true)`) and equal their switch-off twins; `046a`'s last test asserts it is off; `033` byte for byte
unchanged.

What it builds:
- **The events** (§6.1): `client_status_event` gains `curatorship`, `claims_declared`, `seizure`, `seizure_released`;
  `refers_to_event_id` (a release names its seizure; `client_status_event_release_uq`, one release per seizure),
  `publication_date` (a proceeding's or a liquidation's BODACC publication), `qualified_at` (added without a default,
  so the rows from before keep null, then `default now()`; the guard refuses a null). The event table stays
  append-only: who acts for the client (`client_status_event_representative`) and the qualification of an old
  « Tutelle ou curatelle » row (`client_status_event_qualification`) are side tables, and a declaration's documents
  and amounts are `claims_declared_item` — each with RLS (money staff of the servicer), an insert guard, the change
  log and `refuse_change`. `record_client_status_event` dropped and recreated once (four parameters more:
  `p_publication_date`, `p_representative`, `p_refers_to`, `p_declared`); new commands `set_client_representative`
  and `qualify_protection_event` (admins at aal2, replayed by key).
- **What an event counts as** (`private.client_event_effective`): an old row not qualified is
  `guardianship_to_qualify` (payouts held, no mandate end, no addressee); qualified as a tutelle it is a
  `guardianship`; qualified as a curatelle it counts as nothing and its new `curatorship` event counts.
- **The payee** (§6.2.7; [critic] F16, L2, L10): `private.client_payee_rule` — the strictest of the events in effect
  (liquidation → `court_appointed`, death → `estate`, tutelle or curatelle → `protected_adult`, mandate end →
  `client`), the event that requires it and the latest recording among them. `private.remittance_payout_blockers`
  blocks `client_status:<that event's kind>` unless the client's current account is of that kind, confirmed via
  `second_admin` after that latest recording and, but for `client`, with its authority evidence; a standing seizure
  blocks `client_status:seizure` whatever the account. `propose_payout_account` (dropped and recreated: two
  parameters more, `p_authority_document_id`, `p_holder_attestation`) takes the kinds `estate` and
  `protected_adult` (a death, a measure recorded; the authority evidence; a protected adult's holder equal to the
  client's name by `private.epc_name_key`, or explained); `payout_court_appointed` keeps the client's users from
  every account after any of these events.
- **After the end of the mandate** (§6.2.3, §6.2.8; founder Q10): `private.client_end_event` (the earliest death,
  tutelle or mandate end on or before the day). `private.gate_assignments` holds a payment of the client's file
  booked on or after it `client_mandate_ended`; so does the allocation job's own gate (below, D6). « Reverser au
  client » (`forward_payment`) takes it with the reason `mandate_ended`: no schedule key, so no commission; the client
  reads « Reversement sans imputation : paiement reçu après la fin du mandat ».
- **Who receives the letters** (§6.2.12; [critic] L12, [check 1] gap 7): `private.client_addressee`. The repayment
  request refuses `recipient_unknown` only while it returns nothing (7c-2 refused every death, tutelle, liquidation
  or mandate end); its payload's `recipient` names the addressee's role, name and address lines, and a curatelle's
  payload adds `copies` (the curator). The letter (template `demande-remboursement-avance-fr-1`, no new template:
  none was issued with a role) prints « Tuteur de … », « Notaire — succession de … », « Héritiers — succession de … »,
  « Liquidateur de … » and « Copie : …, curateur, … », and words the opening in the third person when someone acts
  for the client.
- **The nightly** (§6.3): `protection_event_to_qualify` (alert) and `seizure_standing` (alert, `p0` while fewer than
  15 days since its recording), in `run_advance_checks` redefined from 7c-2's body.
- **The client's events page** (`public.client_events_view`, money staff): every event with what it counts as, a
  seizure standing or its release date, a row to qualify and its qualification, the representative in force and how
  many were recorded, a declaration's documents; the payee required today; whether a seizure stands; the letters'

  tutelle ou curatelle », « Compte exigé : … », « Demandes de remboursement d'avance adressées à : »; names corrected
  in review round 1, TUI-8), proposes the new kinds with the
  authority evidence and the explanation, and names each new blocker with what lifts it.
- Columns for 7d-2 only (§6.1): `private.remittance_draft.set_off_barred`, `opening_on`, and the index
  `remittance_line_repricing_invoice_idx` — written and read from 7d-2.

### Decisions

- **D1 — the strictest payee, and only after every event was recorded.** The plan's mapping, read over every event
  in effect, not the latest (F16: a mandate end recorded after a tutelle must not let the client's own account
  through). The account lifts the block only when confirmed by a second admin after the latest recording among the
  events in effect (C. civ. 2008: what was done before is valid; what is done after must follow the event), so a
  death recorded after a liquidation asks the liquidator's account confirmed again. The code is the requiring
  event's (`client_status:death`, `…:guardianship`, `…:curatorship`, `…:liquidation`, `…:mandate_ended`), so the
  page says which payee it waits for.
- **D2 — the authority evidence is required for every non-client payee, `court_appointed` included.** A liquidator's
  account confirmed before 7d-1 without it no longer lifts the block (L641-9 I: the payee is the one the judgment
  names; the evidence is how the second admin checks it). `019`'s court-appointed proposal now carries one (R3,
  below).
- **D3 — the holder's name for a protected adult** (427 al. 5; Q21 a): compared as the pain.001 writer spells it
  (`private.epc_name_key`, twin `pain001.name_key`: the writer's spellings, accents dropped, upper-cased, every run of
  other characters one space; null when a character outside Basic Latin is left, so never a false match); different
  → refused `holder_not_client` unless explained (`holder_attestation`, 1–500 characters, shown to the confirming
  admin with both names). The tutor's or curator's own account is refused `holder_not_client` (`046a` sp2) unless
  explained; Q21 a's « jamais le compte du tuteur ou du curateur » then rests on the confirming admin, who reads the
  explanation (OQ-94).
- **D4 — an old « Tutelle ou curatelle » row holds payouts and ends nothing until qualified** ([critic] L17): it
  cannot be told apart from a curatelle, so it is not treated as a tutelle (no mandate end, no payment held after it);
  the nightly lists it until an admin qualifies it with the judgment. (Review round 1, MONEY-LAW-1: as built, a
  protected adult's account confirmed after it lifted its hold — a deviation from §6.1 and §6.2.13 « until then the
  row keeps today's effect (payouts held) »; now no account lifts it before it is qualified,
  `client_status:guardianship_to_qualify`.) Qualified as a curatelle, a `curatorship` event is recorded with the old row's date and
  evidence (its `recorded_at` today, so an account confirmed before is confirmed again: conservative).
- **D5 — a seizure stands from its effective date until a release naming it is effective** ([check 2] gap 6; Q12 a):
  `private.client_seizures_standing` is the one place that reads it (blockers, the client's users' rights, the
  nightly, the page). A release is refused unless the seizure is the client's, effective on or before it and not
  released (checked under the `payout_accounts:` lock; the unique index is the backstop, its violation the same
  refusal).
- **D6 — the allocation job's gate twin holds `client_mandate_ended` too** (beyond the plan's list, which names
  `gate_assignments` only): the job gates again in Python (`jobs.allocation.gate`) before it allocates, so an end
  recorded after a payment was gated ready, before the job ran, would have let it be allocated and priced.
  `FileFacts.ended_on` is read once per client of the job's files (`private.client_end_event`), the rule comes first
  as in SQL, no release opens it; `private.allocation_begin` admits the outcome. `post_allocations`' backstop is not
  redefined (Left open).
- **D7 — who receives the letters**: the governing event in our order (liquidation, death, tutelle, curatelle; the
  earliest of its kind) and its representative in force; a curatelle's letter goes to the client at its billing
  address with the curator in copy (our rule by analogy with 467 al. 3, OQ-94). A mandate end or a proceeding keeps
  the client as addressee. No addressee while the person is unknown or the row is to qualify: the request is refused
  rather than sent to the wrong person.
- **D8 — what representatives store**: role, name (1–140) and 1–4 address lines (1–70), nothing else
  (`private.representative_clean`; personal data — no birth date, no phone, no email), with the evidence; read by
  money staff only (`046a` i).

### Deviations from the plan

- **`client_events_view`** (beyond the plan): the page's one read, so every rule (what counts, standing, the payee,
  the addressees, the name comparison) stays in SQL and the page only words it.
- **`private.client_payout_account_guard` redefined** (not in the plan's list): the two new columns are immutable once
  proposed, as the other columns are; the guard also checks the authority document is the client's
  `payout_authority_evidence`.
- **Two refusals beyond the plan's list**: `bad_attestation` (an explanation over 500 characters; a blank one is
  none) and `qualify_protection_event`'s `bad_kind`. `holder_not_client`'s text is static (the page shows both names
  where the admin confirms, never in an error).
- **`forward_payment` re-reads the end** to choose the reason: a payment held for the cut-off and booked after an end
  recorded since is forwarded with `mandate_ended`, not the cut-off's reason, so it earns no commission either. The
  copy also closes a hole of the merged body: `p.review_reason in (…)` on a null reason let a payment ready for
  allocation be forwarded; it is now `coalesce(…, false)` (`046a` sg2's last key).
- **A client-keyed partial index for seizures** (`client_status_event_client_seizure_idx`, beyond §6.1's servicer
  index): under stale statistics the per-client read chose the servicer's partial index read whole (5,008 planted rows
  per blocker check in the reads test); keyed by the client it reads the client's seizures only.
- **The « no release naming it » and « no qualification » checks are fenced** (`not exists (… offset 0)`, in
  `client_seizures_standing` and the nightly's two statements): in CI's order (the reads test after the earlier db-job
  files) the nightly's `seizure_standing` ran its NOT EXISTS as an anti-join reading `client_status_event_release_uq`
  whole (8,302 planted rows in the suite, 1,075 in the reproduction); the fence keeps it a correlated probe by key (3).
- **`portfolio_confirmation_blockers` is not redefined**: an old row qualified as a curatelle still keeps the client's
  portfolios from being confirmed (`client_mandate_ended`, as before 7d-1) — Left open. (Superseded in review round 1,
  TUI-2: redefined, it reads what each event counts as.)
- **No new letter template**: `demande-remboursement-avance-fr-1` gains the addressee and copy lines; no letter was
  issued with a role before, so the template's earlier bytes are unchanged (`GOLDEN_REQUEST_PDF` and
  `GOLDEN_EVERY_ORIGIN_PDF` unchanged; `GOLDEN_CURATELLE_PDF` new).

### Mutants

## M2c-7d-1 review fixes (2026-11-25)

### Round 1

The review of `a7489f2` raised thirteen items: two mediums and one low of the money and law lens (MONEY-LAW-1,
MONEY-LAW-2; MONEY-LAW-3), three mediums and five lows of tests and pages (TUI-1 … TUI-3; TUI-4 … TUI-8), and four
lows of concurrency and cost (CC-1 … CC-4). MONEY-LAW-2 and TUI-3 are one fault (a letter naming the person who acts
for the client, read by the client's members), MONEY-LAW-3 and TUI-1 another (a seizure's texts claiming a set-off
bar 7d-1 does not have): each fixed once. Each item was checked against the code first — read in the migration, the
pages and the worker, then seen failing as a test (046a's new cases, the vitest texts, the two integration tests) on
`a7489f2`'s bodies; all hold. The migration `20261126090000_client_events.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place.
**The switch stays off**: nothing writes `private.feature_switch` and no rule here reads it; the new scenarios that
touch payouts (`046a` sq3, sp9) also run with it on in a rolled-back subtransaction and equal their switch-off twins;
`033` byte for byte unchanged; `034`–`045b` unchanged.

- **MONEY-LAW-1 (medium; fixed at the root, the plan's rule).** An old « Tutelle ou curatelle » row not yet qualified
  counted, in `private.client_payee_rule`, as a `guardianship` requiring a `protected_adult` account: once ops proposed
  one in the client's name and a second admin confirmed it, `client_status:guardianship` lifted while the row was
  still to qualify. The plan keeps « today's payout hold until ops qualify them » (§6.1) — before 7d-1 no account
  lifted such a row's hold — and « until then the row keeps today's effect (payouts held) » (§6.2.13): if the row was a
  tutelle the mandate ended at its date (C. civ. 2003, « la tutelle des majeurs »), and the payments booked since,
  allocated by design (the gate ignores a row to qualify: no end stated), would have been paid out before anyone
  qualified it. Reproduced (`046a` sq3 on `a7489f2`: `[]` after the confirmation). Fix: the row to qualify requires
  `to_qualify`, a kind no payout account has, ranked above every other (its code `client_status:guardianship_to_qualify`,
  shown first whatever else is in effect); qualified as a tutelle, the protected adult's account confirmed after the
  old row lifts it; qualified as a curatelle, only an account confirmed after its curatorship event (recorded at the
  qualification) does. The texts that said the hold — the qualification form's « les reversements restent bloqués
  jusqu'à ce que vous précisiez » and the nightly's `protection_event_to_qualify` help — are now true; the blocker
  says « « Tutelle ou curatelle » enregistrée avant leur distinction : précisez-la avec le jugement (« Événements du
  client ») ; aucun compte ne lève ce blocage avant (règle du cabinet) », the page's payee line « Reversements bloqués
  tant que la « Tutelle ou curatelle » enregistrée n'est pas précisée … ». D4 above is corrected. `046a` sq3 (switch
  off and on), sq1's expected code.
- **MONEY-LAW-2 / TUI-3 (medium; fixed at the root, the plan's rule).** Plan §6.1: the names and addresses of who acts
  for the client are « never the client's users, restricted viewers or collectors »; the side table kept that rule,
  but the repayment request's letter addressed to that person (its payload's `recipient`: role, name, address lines;
  its PDF printing them) was the client's whole-client members' to read — the request's row over PostgREST (7c-2's
  policy), the letter's document row and its stored object (the remittance documents' rule), and its `document_id` in
  `client_repayment_requests`. Reproduced (`046a` si2: the client's admin read `[1, 1, 1]`). Fix:

## M2c-7d-2: set-off bars (2026-11-25)

Plan: `docs/design/m2c-7-plan.md` §0, §1.3, §1.4 (7d-2 row) and « Order, and why », §2, §6.2.2, §6.2.4–§6.2.6, §6.2.9,
§6.2.11 with the withheld kind and every redefinition it needs, the worker's `_plan` / `_documents`,
`document_client_payable`, `in_proceeding`, `set_off_after_bar`, `remittance_schedule_candidates` and the trigger
`settlement_withheld`, §6.3–§6.4 where they concern 7d-2, §6.6's `046b`, §6.7's 7d-2 part, with their [critic] /
[check 1–3] marks. Founder questions (plan §10), none answered: Q9 (a), Q11 (a), Q12 (a), Q17 (a), Q18 (a), Q19 (a)
built as their defaults and left open; counsel's OQ-41, OQ-91, OQ-92 (new in COMPLIANCE), OQ-93, OQ-94, OQ-97 stay
open. Texts read on LibreJustice on 2026-11-25, the versions in force: C. com. L622-7 (2021-10-01), L622-17
(2021-10-01), L641-3 (2019-05-24), CPCE L211-2 (2012-06-01), C. civ. 1347, 1347-7, 1348, 1348-1 (2016-10-01); only
what they say is quoted (COMPLIANCE PROC-01, SAISIE-01, OQ-41, OQ-91, OQ-92). Migration
`20261127090000_set_off_bars.sql` (one file, forward-only). **The switch stays off**: nothing writes
`private.feature_switch` and no 7d-2 rule reads it; every `046b` scenario that touches a payout runs a second time
with it on in a rolled-back subtransaction (`pg_temp.iso(…, true)`) and equals its switch-off twin; `046b`'s last
test asserts it is off; `033` byte for byte unchanged.

What it builds:
- **The opening, the births, the bars** (§6.2.2, §6.2.4–§6.2.6): the prepare, the approval and the claw-back read the
  opening through `private.client_opening_date` (7c-1's: the earliest `proceeding_opened` or `liquidation` in effect;
  `private.client_opening_on`, 7b's, now returns it). `private.document_born_on`: an invoice is born at the earliest
  collection it charges (its lines by `remittance_line_invoice_idx` and the lines later runs repriced onto it by
  `remittance_line_repricing_invoice_idx`, 7d-1's index), a corrective invoice with no line at its period's start, an
  advance at `advance_born_on`. `private.document_before_opening` reads that birth (never the issue date).
  `private.client_set_off_barred(client, day, kind)`: `liquidation` (founder Q11), `mandate_ended` (Q9,
  `client_end_event`), `seizure` (Q12, `client_seizures_standing`), and for advances `proceeding` (Q18), in that
  order; `private.document_nettable`: no bar of its kind and born on or after the opening; a credit note always.
- **What the client may pay** (gap 11; carried item 2): `private.document_client_payable` also refuses an advance while
  a proceeding (or a liquidation) stands, whatever its birth; `private.client_payment_docs` reads payability from it
  (7c-1's inline « before the opening » of the advances goes), so the default order skips such an advance and a
  designated payment of it is a `procedure` credit.
- **How an advance is recovered** (carried item 1): `private.advance_recovery_of` answers `barred_proceeding` while a
  proceeding or a liquidation stands (a liquidation recorded alone included, any birth), and `request` for a claw-back
  clause after a mandate end or while a seizure stands; the prepare's facts take the advances' bar the same way. The
  repayment request refuses `in_proceeding` after `before_opening` (L4).
- **The prepare** (§6.4): `private.prepare_set_off_facts` (one call: the opening, the draft's text of the bars, each
  kind's bar and its day); each open invoice's birth (`document_born_on`) when the client has an opening. `run._plan`
  sets off a document only when `_nettable` (the twin of `document_nettable`) holds; the run's own invoice ([critic]
  L1) is born at the earliest collection of its mandate's lines it charges — one it may not set off is issued `due`
  with the terms' `invoice_payment_days` and, born before the opening, in liquidation or under a seizure, a
  `payment_note` the invoice prints instead of (or, for a seizure, before) its payment line (`invoice._payment_line`);
  after a mandate end no note (due by its term to the own account). The draft records `opening_on` and
  `set_off_barred` (`private.remittance_record_draft`); the inputs hash names the bars and births only when the
  client has any (the other drafts' hashes are unchanged).
- **The approval** (§6.2.9; carried item 3): `private.remittance_approval_refusal` (from 7c-2's body, its
  `enable_seqscan = off` kept; 7d-1 did not redefine it) refuses a standing seizure whatever N
  (`payout_blocked:client_status:seizure`), and `client_status_changed` when the opening or the bars differ from the
  draft's or the plan sets off a document barred today (the run's own invoice included: `private.run_set_off_changed`,
  `private.plan_sets_off_barred`).
- **The hold before download** (§6.2.11 (b)): `private.transfer_hold_reason` holds such a payout
  `client_status_changed` (no file carries it; ops cancel the run and prepare again), whatever the switch.
- **The debit** (§6.2.11 (a); [critic] M7-MONEY-5, [check 1] gap 1): `private.post_run_settlements` reads, for the
  runs of a client with an event in effect by the debit's date (`private.runs_with_client_events`), the plan's settles
  barred that day (`private.run_barred_settles`: invoices and advances only — a refund settle is the servicer paying),
  posts the allowed part as `settle:<run>` with its `commission_settlement` rows and the barred part W as
  `settle:<run>:barred` (the shape of any settlement, no settlement row), reversed at once as `return:barred:<run>`
  with the reason « Compensation retenue : <procédure collective | liquidation judiciaire | fin du mandat | saisie
  entre les mains du cabinet> depuis le JJ/MM/AAAA (règle du cabinet) » (`private.set_off_bar_reason`). When the
  allowed part would be zero or less while settles remain (a refund at least as large as the allowed invoices), the
  whole plan is withheld (W = D). `private.ledger_entry_guard` (from M2c-1's body) lets through LG003 only a reversal
  keyed `return:barred:x` of a `client_settlement` keyed `settle:x:barred` whose source is the run x, same
  organization — read off the reversed entry by its primary key, a null in any of them being no exception;
  `ledger_entry_barred_reversed` (deferrable, initially deferred, `enable always`) fails the commit of a barred
  settlement without its reversal, and joins `private.ledger_check_now` (from 7a's body). The 4670 trigger
  (`private.ledger_posting_client_payable`) queues the reversal as a `settlement_withheld` item (kinds of
  `remittance_pending` and `remittance_line` widened; the line insert guard unchanged); `private.pending_item_deadlines`
  holds it to the withheld run's R124-6 date (that run's positive, live, dated line with the earliest latest execution
  date) — the worker's twin `HELD_TO_SQL` alike; a breach after it carries no blocked reason.
- **The schedule** ([check 2] gap 3): `private.remittance_schedule_candidates` (dropped and recreated) adds
  `settlement_withheld`; `_schedule_trigger` returns `payout_returned`, then `settlement_withheld` (any day), then
  `schedule`, then `deadline`; the run's trigger `settlement_withheld` (« Compensation retenue à rendre »).
- **The worker's kinds**: `LineKind.SETTLEMENT_WITHHELD` (never commissioned, outside every mandate's money, its
  deadline held like a returned payout's: `HELD_ITEMS`); the statement's nature « Compensation retenue au débit,
  rendue » (fr-3; 7d-3's fr-4 adds the explaining row).
- **The nightly** (§6.3): `set_off_after_bar` (alert, P0) in `run_advance_checks` (from 7d-1's body): a run's
  settlement posted on or after a bar's day that set off a document barred that day, its amount the barred documents'
  settlement rows (`private.set_off_after_bar_rows`); the codes list of `046b` sn2 extended.
- **The pages**: the run page's « Compensation retenue au débit » (`public.remittance_run_withheld`, money staff at
  aal2: W, its parts, the reason, the run that gave it back; « Compensation prévue à la validation » beside the plan's
  figure, the payout notes no longer stating the plan's set-off as made); the line kind « Compensation retenue au
  débit, rendue »; the hold's and the check's labels; the seizure's blocker « ni reversement ni compensation jusqu'à la
  mainlevée »; « Ce que le client doit au cabinet » marks an advance the client may not pay; the client's page lists
  what is never set off (« règle du cabinet »); the advances' texts say « client en procédure collective : avance à
  déclarer » (any birth) instead of « née avant l'ouverture ». Carried item 4: every 7c-1, 7c-2 and 7d-1 text that said
  « 7d-2 » would bar something is now true (the seizure's help and labels, the events' note, `046a` sp9).

### Decisions
- **D1 Mechanism (i), as planned**: the barred part posted and reversed in one transaction, never a pending row keyed
  on the remittance entry (plan Appendix B); the exception to LG003 is one conjunct in one rule, both keys read off the
  one reversed row by its key (`coalesce(…, false)`: a settlement with a null key or source is never excepted).
- **D2 The bars' order** (liquidation › mandate end › seizure › proceeding): the reason a withheld set-off names is the
  invoices' bar when there is one, else « procédure collective » (an advance while the proceeding stands, or a claim
  born before the opening).
- **D3 No new index on `client_status_event`.** A partial index of the servicer's events by kind (first written for the
  nightly) is implied by every per-client read filtering on a kind; under stale statistics a generic plan read it whole
  (40 010 tuples per `client_set_off_barred` call, 180 075 per prepare's facts in the reads test). The per-client reads
  stay on `client_status_event_client_idx` (the bars read the client's events once, materialized), and the nightly
  reaches the servicer's clients by `organization_servicer_idx`. For the same reason **7d-1's
  `client_status_event_seizure_idx` (the servicer's seizures) is dropped**: every per-client seizure read implies its
  predicate, and in the db job's order (after `supabase test db` and the earlier integration files) 7d-1's own reads
  test read it whole — 5,005 planted seizures per blocker check, 10,006 per approval (which 7d-2 makes read the
  seizures whatever N), 5,010 per « Événements du client » — while the same test alone read 5. The per-client reads keep
  7d-1's `client_status_event_client_seizure_idx`; `seizure_standing` reaches the servicer's seizures through its
  clients (`run_advance_checks`). The flip depends on the database's state, so no single test kills its mutant (the index
  restored) deterministically: the db job's run is the evidence.
- **D4 `private.approve_remittance_run` gains `set enable_seqscan = off`** (whole copy from 7a's body, nothing else
  changed): the reads test found its « their items leave the pending queue » delete reading the servicer's whole queue
  under a generic plan (10 008 tuples of `remittance_pending` with `draft_run_id` analysed at two values). A full copy,
  not an `alter function … set`, so a later slice copying the latest definition keeps the setting.
- **D5 `public.remittance_run_withheld`** (new, money staff): the run page states what the ledger did, not the plan.

### Deviations from the plan
- **`advance_open` keeps the advances of a client in a proceeding** (plan §6.2.10 [critic] L4 « leaves out every advance
  of a client in a proceeding or liquidation (they are listed to declare) »): `claims_to_declare`, which lists them, is
  7d-3's; dropping them now would leave such an advance in no alert until 7d-3 merges. Its `recovery` says
  `barred_proceeding`, which the page words « à déclarer ». Default: 7d-3 drops them when it adds `claims_to_declare`.
- **A negative D** (a refund larger than every take): W cannot be D; the barred takes are withheld and the rest posts
  as such a run's negative settlement always did (plan §6.2.11 (a) 1 covers D > 0 only).
- **A barred settle of 0** (a closed invoice's VAT left pending) is dropped with its VAT, moved by the next settlement.
- **The run page's read** (`remittance_run_withheld`) and the « Compensation prévue à la validation » label: not named
  by the plan; without them the page stated the plan's set-off as made.
- **D3, D4 above** (an index not built, a setting added to a function the plan does not name).

## M2c-7d-2 review fixes (2026-11-25)

### Round 1

The review of `a9a6e65` raised nineteen items: one high, one medium and two lows of the money and law lens (MLAW-1;
MLAW-2; MLAW-3, MLAW-4), two mediums and seven lows of tests and pages (TUI-1, TUI-2; TUI-3 … TUI-9), and six lows of
concurrency and cost (CC-1 … CC-6). MLAW-4 and TUI-3 are one fault (the run giving a withheld set-off back named before
it paid it), fixed once. Each item was checked against the code first — the reviewer's scripts re-run on this stack
(MLAW-1's `r1.sql`: the N = 0 run booked with its 10 000 set-off, `set_off_after_bar` raised the next night), the
rest read in the migration, the worker and the pages — then seen failing as a test on `a9a6e65`'s bodies (`046b`'s new
and extended cases: 6 of 29 failed; the worker's three new tests; the stale-statistics test's new calls); all hold.
The migration `20261127090000_set_off_bars.sql` is unmerged and was edited in place. **The switch stays off**: nothing
writes `private.feature_switch` and no rule here reads it; the new scenarios that touch payouts (`046b` sa3, sw5) also
run with it on in a rolled-back subtransaction and equal their switch-off twins; `033` byte for byte unchanged;
`034`–`046a` keep every assertion (only texts changed: TUI-6).

- **MLAW-1 (high; fixed at the root, the plan's rule).** The run's own invoice was dated (born) from this run's draft
  lines only — in the worker (`_new_invoice_born`) and in the approval's re-check (`private.plan_sets_off_barred`) —
  while it also charges the earlier runs' lines whose commission was left pending and which it reprices
  (`Draft.repricing`, invoiced), and `private.document_born_on` (the debit, the hold, the nightly) counts those lines
  (`remittance_line_repricing.invoice_id`). A client whose redressement opened between an earlier run (a commission
  left pending on a collection before the opening) and this one: the prepare netted the invoice, the approval accepted
  it, and an N = 0 run set off at once a claim born before the opening (L622-7 I al. 1; OQ-92's default birth) — the
  next night's P0; with N > 0 the invoice was frozen « À régler par compensation sur le reversement RV-… » (false)
  and the payout held `client_status_changed` for a change that never happened, again after each re-prepare.
  Reproduced (`r1.sql`, `046b` sa3 on `a9a6e65`: `booked:booked`, `[["invoice", -1, "compensation", 10000, 1666]]`).
  Fix: the worker builds once each charged entry's collection date, this run's lines and the repriced lines
  (`_births`, CC-6), and the invoice is born at the earliest of those it charges; the SQL's `new:` branch takes the
  earliest of the draft's invoiced lines of the mandate and of the draft's invoiced repricings
  (`private.remittance_draft_repricing` → `public.remittance_line` by its key, on the line's mandate — the approval
  files a repricing under `new:<line's mandate>`, `document_born_on` then counts it). Such an invoice is now issued due
  with the procedure's payment line (« Créance née avant l'ouverture … ni payée ni compensée hors de la procédure »)
  and nothing of it set off; a draft that nets it is sent back `client_status_changed` whatever N (`046b` sa3 a, b),
  the prepare's draft is approved, its invoice issued due with that note and no set-off reference, born d − 12, its
  payout not held (sa3 c). Worker: `test_the_run_s_own_invoice_is_born_at_the_earliest_line_it_reprices_too`; the
  Hypothesis property draws earlier runs' pending lines too and computes the invoice's birth from the draft's lines
  and repricings (found the fault in its first example).
- **MLAW-2 (medium; fixed at the root).** The « Lier » preview of a payout's debit said « ses factures sont réglées par
  compensation (D) », the plan's figure, while the booking of that same line withholds the barred part W
  (`settle:<run>:barred`, reversed at once) and sets off D − W. Fix: `private.run_settlement_split(run, day)` —
  `post_run_settlements`' rule for one run (the event gate, `run_barred_settles`, the whole plan withheld when the
  allowed part would be ≤ 0 while D > 0) — and `private.transfer_line_preview_of` redefined (from

  D − W and `withheld_minor` = W on the line's booking date; the sheet says « ; ses factures sont réglées par
  compensation (X) ; Y de compensation retenus (règle du cabinet : la situation du client ne la permet plus), rendus au
  client par son prochain reversement » (`payoutSetOff`). `046b` sw5 (switch off and on): sw1's plan → 36 000 and
  30 000, the booking's two entries the same amounts; a death (the whole plan) → 0 and 20 000; sw2 (iii)'s refund
  larger than the allowed invoice → 0 and D = 23 000; no event → D and 0. Vitest.
- **TUI-1 (medium; text).** The P0 `set_off_after_bar`'s help said the set-off was barred when « procédure collective
  ouverte avant la naissance de la créance » — the reverse of the code (a claim born before the opening is barred) and

## Founder decisions (2026-11-09, all defaults; design §24)
Twice-monthly runs with a deadline guard (#1); the shorter of the mandate's delay and one calendar month (#2); netting only under a clause (#3); commission on allocations only (#4); the supported grids (#5); credit notes for undone collections (#6); advances, claw-back only by clause, no hold-back (#7); **the servicer bears a return beyond its payment (#8)**; **the commission swept the day payouts are debited, bank fees on the dedicated account the servicer's cost (#9)**; IBAN changes confirmed by a second person (#10); one approver (#11); one yearly invoice series (#12); mainland-France professional clients in EUR (#13); **one dedicated account per currency (#14)**; pain.001 files uploaded by ops, the payee check kept (#15).
